whyPoints.description: If the slot is full, we say so. If the specialist for a niche Higher Level subject is based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening, we say that too. Availability invented to hold an enquiry costs a family a term.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, never borrowed
whyPoints.description: KHDA inspects Dubai's private schools and sets the mandatory-subject rules; MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit. We explain what each one does and link you to its own pages. IB Gram holds no accreditation from either, and no page here will suggest otherwise.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start for a child living in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school direction rather than on the tutor. Families on these streets report buses back between about 14:40 for Al Quoz 1 schools and 16:45 for Al Barsha and Nad Al Sheba routes, with an extra ninety minutes when there is an after-school club. Add thirty to forty-five minutes for food and decompression and the earliest workable start runs from roughly 15:45 to 18:45. Track the actual arrival time for a fortnight before fixing a slot, then book fifteen minutes later than the earliest workable time so a late bus does not eat the first part of the lesson.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Al Quoz 4 children attend?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside Al Quoz 4, so children travel in several directions. The inland run reaches schools in Al Quoz 1 and Al Barsha, including Indian-curriculum, British and IB continuum options. The coastal run reaches Al Safa, Umm Al Sheif and Jumeirah, which is why a large share of this community sits Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at sixteen. Because the community has no dominant school, it has no dominant curriculum either, and a tutor recommendation from a neighbour often does not transfer. Check the board and syllabus code on your child's statement of entry first.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to Al Quoz 4 for lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video. We do not send anyone to a residential address anywhere in the Emirates; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. We state that before a parent asks, because this market has a habit of implying a visit and explaining later. The practical trade is a larger pool of subject specialists, no travel priced into the hour, and a lesson whose full length survives a late school bus, against the loss of a tutor physically in the room.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Quoz 4 family expect to pay per hour in this market?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates run from AED 45-150 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik lists AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, where Unitors lists AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, to AED 200-450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270. Visiting tutors run AED 180-500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are the market's figures with their sources, not ours. Ask any provider whether marking between sessions is included before comparing numbers.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute session long enough to be worth booking?
faqs.answer: For the right job, yes. Forty-five minutes can teach and rehearse one technique properly, which is often exactly what a weekday after a long commute can hold. It cannot accommodate a full paper section sat under timed conditions and then marked line by line, which needs ninety minutes. The usual design for a Year 11 or Diploma student in Al Quoz 4 is a short weekday session for technique and a longer weekend session for timed practice. Schools themselves think in KHDA's 40-minute lesson unit, so many students find the shorter format familiar.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge IGCSE in the March series — when does the entry actually close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge's published key dates for the March series put final entries on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read backwards, the subject and tier decision has to be settled in October or early November, and the December break becomes the last substantial revision block. Take the exact timetable from your school: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the zone version matters.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IGCSE Physics and IGCSE Chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor with a physical-sciences background can often carry both at Core and Extended level, which simplifies scheduling in a household with one usable evening slot. At IB Higher Level the answer is usually no: the depth in each subject is enough that a specialist in one rarely marks to examiner standard in the other. Where we can cover two subjects with one tutor, we say so; where splitting them produces better teaching, we say that instead, even though it is harder to timetable.

faqs.question: How do we fit tuition around a school bus that leaves before seven in the morning?
faqs.answer: Early departures mean early tiredness, so the slot matters more than the number of sessions. For primary children the best answer is usually short and early: thirty to forty-five minutes shortly after the bus returns, two or three times a week, before extracurriculars take the evening. For secondary students the weekday evening is better spent on one focused technique session, with the longer timed-practice work moved to the weekend when the commute is not in the way. Sessions that run past a child's natural limit teach very little, whatever the invoice says.

faqs.question: What happens if the Al Khail Road drive runs late and we miss the start of a lesson?
faqs.answer: Tell us as it happens and the tutor holds the slot. Because the lesson is delivered online, the start can slide fifteen or twenty minutes and the full session still runs; there is no next household expecting the tutor at a door. That is one of the structural differences between formats worth pricing. A visiting arrangement in the same situation usually loses the time, because the end is fixed by the tutor's route. If a session is genuinely missed rather than delayed, we reschedule inside the same week wherever a slot exists.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Anyone providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Internal Assessment without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter, test whether a proposed research question is narrow enough to produce usable data, read a draft your daughter has produced and give feedback on structure, reasoning and use of evidence, and teach the underlying skills using a different example. What a tutor must never do is author text that appears in the submission or supply a model answer to her own question. Some Dubai schools also limit external feedback to one draft, and the school's rule takes precedence.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions do Al Quoz 4 families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week in one subject is the commonest start, and for most students it is the right one. A single subject taught properly for two terms produces more movement than three subjects covered thinly for six weeks, and it leaves room in a commuting household's evening. Diploma students in the final year often add a second slot for an internally assessed component or a Higher Level subject in the run-up to mocks. We review at six weeks against the original diagnostic and change the plan if the gap has not moved.

faqs.question: Will Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the Ministry of Education's five-subject requirement?
faqs.answer: No. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They remain mandatory in Dubai private schools and still appear on the report, so they matter for school progression. Verify current requirements on the Ministry's own channels before relying on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth planning in advance rather than improvising. Dubai schools run shortened days during Ramadan, so the afternoon returns earlier and the usual late-afternoon slot often becomes unusable because the household's rhythm has shifted. Many families move to a later evening session after Iftar, or to a mid-morning weekend slot. Because lessons are online, a change of time is a change of one line in a calendar rather than a renegotiation of someone's driving route. Tell us a fortnight ahead and the slot is held in the new pattern.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first session?
faqs.answer: Four things make the trial far more useful: the board and syllabus code, the most recent school report or criterion-level summary, one marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it, and a sentence saying what you want to be true in twelve weeks. The marked script is the single most valuable item, because it shows where marks actually went rather than where anyone thinks they went. If a school has set an internally assessed task, the task brief and the school's own deadline schedule help as well.

dubai/al-quoz-4.closingBody: Al Quoz 4 gives a family two usable evenings a week, maybe three, and the first decision is which subject earns one of them. Tell us the board and the syllabus code, the real time the bus gets back, and what you want to be true by the end of the term. We will set a diagnostic in the trial, send you a written read on what we found, and say plainly if tutoring is not the right purchase. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video; the hour starts when your child sits down and finishes a full hour later.

dubai/al-qusais.tutorsIntro: Tutors for this corridor teach Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE and the IB Diploma at both levels. The match is made on subject and component first and on availability second, because an excellent tutor in the wrong hour is no use to a household that gets home at half past six.

intro.heading: In Al Qusais the clock decides everything
paragraphs: Ask a parent in Al Qusais what went wrong with the last tutoring arrangement and the answer is rarely about teaching. It is about Wednesday. The tutor was good, the subject was right, and then a school event moved, the drive back from Mirdif took fifty minutes instead of twenty-five, and three sessions in a row were either cancelled or run with a tired child at eight in the evening. By half-term the slot had quietly died. The teaching was never the variable.

This district makes that outcome likely. Al Qusais sits along Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road with the Red Line running through it, close enough to the Sharjah boundary that a large share of households cross an emirate line at least once a day. Schools used by families here are scattered rather than clustered: some in Al Qusais itself, some in Mirdif and Al Warqa, some back towards Deira and Al Garhoud. A single household can have two children on two different buses with two different return times.

The consequence for tuition is specific. A 16:00 slot does not work on a weekday for most secondary students here, because they are still on the road. A 17:00 slot works for children at a school inside Al Qusais and not for those coming from Mirdif. A 19:00 slot works almost universally and costs concentration. The useful planning move is to pick the latest slot the child can still think in, and then protect it.

Online delivery is what makes protecting it possible. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; the in-home service runs only in India. A session with no journey attached starts when the student sits down. A session with a tutor driving in from Barsha or across the Sharjah border starts when the traffic allows, and in this part of the city the traffic frequently does not.

The second thing the clock decides is what a session should contain. An hour at 17:30 with a fresh student can carry new content. An hour at 19:30 after a long day cannot, and is better spent on marked papers, worked examples and command-term drilling, where the cognitive load is lower and the mark yield is higher. Matching the task to the hour is the part most tutoring plans skip.

The sections below map the week properly: when a lesson can start from each school direction, what to put in each kind of slot, how the UAE academic calendar and Ramadan reshape the term, what the market charges for both formats, and what to do when the hour you need has gone. Every figure here is attributed to whoever published it, and every scheduling claim is written from how the afternoon in this corridor actually behaves rather than from a map.

dubai/al-qusais.programmesIntro: Three routes matter in this corridor, and each one puts its pressure on a different part of the week. The notes below describe that timing pressure rather than restating what the programme is.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal written papers, with a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, which caps the grade on Core entry. Pearson runs single-tier papers in most subjects. Eight or nine subjects is normal, and the volume is the difficulty rather than any single topic.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 11 week in Al Qusais is already full: school until mid-afternoon, a slow return, and homework across nine subjects. Adding three tuition hours rarely works. Two protected hours, one on mathematics and one rotating across the sciences, is the pattern that survives from October to the spring series.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment the student designs outside lesson time, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The final score runs to 45 points. Higher Level adds content and usually an extra paper, not just harder questions on the same material.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this district are often travelling furthest, because the nearest IB Diploma provision is a drive away rather than on the street. That makes weekday evenings short and weekend mornings valuable. Coursework sessions are best placed on a Saturday, when a ninety-minute block is possible and a weekday hour is not.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and reported as a grade from 1 to 7. The programme rewards investigation and reflection, and does not drill procedure, so strong criterion grades can mask weak fluency in algebra or written accuracy.
programmes.countryNote: MYP families here usually arrive in Year 9 rather than earlier, when a child begins to look slow under timed conditions. One short weekly slot in the earlier years is far cheaper in both money and family time than a crisis block in Year 11, and it fits an afternoon that is not yet full.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth and examined in a June or November series, with little or no coursework in the sciences beyond a practical component. The narrowing of choice happens at sixteen, which suits a student who already knows the direction they want.
programmes.countryNote: For the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency route on the British track, the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary level at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the count of five.

dubai/al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Qusais concentrate on the subjects where a missed week compounds and where timed practice decides the grade. The list below is ordered by how often families in this corridor ask for it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this district by a wide margin. Extended reaches grade 9 while Core caps at C or 5, so a tier review in Year 10 can matter more than extra teaching. Algebraic manipulation and multi-step problem solving carry most of the available marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and proof decide the grade, and marks go on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. The 20-mark exploration is graded across five criteria, and the use-of-mathematics criterion carries the largest allocation, so working at course level rather than above it caps the mark.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest losses at IGCSE; fields and thermodynamics at Diploma level. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper rewards method detail that students who have only read experiments cannot supply, which makes it a good target for a late-evening session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis at IGCSE; energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms at HL. Observation questions need both colour and state to score. Significant figures and units quietly cost a mark a paper, and that habit fixes faster than any topic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty is the obstacle. Command terms decide marks: outline wants a list, explain wants a mechanism. Scheduling matters here more than in most subjects, because retention of a large content base depends on spaced review rather than a single long session.

subjects.name: English First Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Summary questions are the fastest marks available and the most commonly thrown away, because students paraphrase instead of selecting discrete points. Directed writing rewards register and audience. Both improve inside four marked sessions, which suits a short block.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers need the numbers used inside the argument rather than quoted beside it. Evaluation marks want a judgement with a reason from the stimulus. At Diploma level, Economics requires three commentaries of 800 words built on news articles, which needs early article selection.

subjects.name: Accounting and Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Both appear often in this corridor because several schools here offer them. Accounting rewards layout discipline, and marks are lost to presentation rather than arithmetic. Additional Mathematics is a step beyond Extended and needs fluency already in place before it is attempted.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and a frequent source of a weak line on an otherwise strong report. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so the stream your child is in determines which content applies.

dubai/al-qusais.regionsTitle: Al Qusais and the roads that feed it
dubai/al-qusais.regionsIntro: Session timing in this part of Dubai depends on which direction the school bus comes from. The notes below are route notes rather than descriptions, because the route is what sets the earliest workable hour.

regions.name: Al Qusais 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Residential blocks either side of Damascus Street with Red Line stations within walking distance for many households. Students at schools inside Al Qusais are home by around 15:30 and can take a 17:00 slot comfortably.

regions.name: Al Qusais Industrial Area
regions.note: Mixed commercial and residential towards the Sharjah boundary. Household commutes here often end later than the school run, so an evening slot that does not depend on a parent being home works better.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Immediately east, pressed against the emirate line, with the heaviest cross-border congestion in the late afternoon. A 17:00 start is optimistic on a weekday; 18:00 is the dependable hour for most students coming from this side.

regions.name: Hor Al Anz and Al Muteena
regions.note: Older Deira districts to the west along the Red Line, with a strong Indian and British curriculum presence. Transfers into IGCSE in Year 9 or 10 from another board are the most common request from these blocks.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: South-east, and the direction many Al Qusais children travel for school. The return is the slowest leg of the day in term time, which pushes those students to 18:00 or later on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: West across the airport road, holding British and IB provision. Off-peak the run is short; between 15:00 and 16:30 it is not. Students here usually settle on 17:30.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: South along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, a longer run with fewer stops, so the arrival time is more predictable even when it is late. A fixed 18:30 slot holds well for this group.

regions.name: Al Mamzar
regions.note: North towards the coast, a short hop from Al Qusais outside peak hours. Families here often want two children taught back to back, which works online because no travel sits between the sessions.

schoolClusters.city: Inside Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: The schools on the doorstep, running British and Indian curricula with IGCSE at sixteen in the British stream. Children at these schools have the earliest realistic tuition slot in the district because the journey home is short. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: The south-eastern direction many Al Qusais families travel for school, including IB continuum provision. This is the slowest return leg of the day, and the reason a fixed evening slot works better than an afternoon one for these students.

dubai/al-qusais.modesIntro: Three arrangements cover almost every request from this corridor, and each one is defined by when it sits in the week as much as by what it teaches. All run online, one-to-one, over live video.

modes.title: The protected weekday hour
modes.description: One fixed slot in one subject, placed at the latest time the student can still concentrate, and defended against everything except school exams. Most households in Al Qusais can hold one of these reliably and two with effort. The point of a fixed hour is that it stops being negotiated every week, which is what kills most arrangements by half-term.
bullets: Same tutor, same hour, reviewed at each half-term
Moves for school exam weeks instead of running on top of them
Written note to the parent afterwards, so nobody has to debrief a teenager
Content work early in the week, paper work later

modes.title: The weekend coursework block
modes.description: Ninety minutes on a Saturday or Sunday morning for the work that cannot be done in a tired weekday hour: internal assessment design, Extended Essay structure, a full timed paper with the clock running. For Diploma students travelling a distance to school, this block does more than two weekday hours and costs the family less disruption.
bullets: Long enough for a full past paper under timed conditions
Used for coursework scoping and criterion-based feedback in writing
Survives a week when every weekday slot has collapsed
Student arrives rested, which changes what can be attempted

modes.title: The pre-assessment short block
modes.description: Six to ten sessions clustered around a mock window or the final series, compressed into two or three weeks. Content teaching stops; marked scripts, pacing and command terms take over. Families in this district buy these in January and again in March, and the compressed shape fits a term that has no spare weekday hours left.
bullets: Starts from a marked mock rather than a fresh diagnostic

sections.heading: What time can a lesson in Al Qusais actually start?
paragraphs: The direct answer: between 17:00 and 19:00 on a weekday, and which end of that range depends entirely on where your child goes to school. Students at schools inside Al Qusais can hold 17:00. Students travelling back from Mirdif, Al Warqa or Academic City are realistically at 18:00 or later. Students crossing from the Sharjah side of Al Nahda should assume 18:30. Weekend mornings are open from around 09:00 and are the most productive hours available.

This matters because a slot chosen optimistically fails slowly and expensively. A family books 16:30 because it sounds reasonable, the child arrives at 16:45 twice, misses it entirely once, and by the fourth week the arrangement is being renegotiated every Sunday. The teaching never gets a chance to compound. Choosing a later hour that nobody has to fight for produces more learning than an earlier hour that keeps collapsing.

The second variable is what the student can do at that hour. Concentration is not flat across the evening, and pretending it is produces wasted money. New content, abstract reasoning and anything requiring sustained working memory belong earlier. Marked-script review, worked examples, command-term drilling and vocabulary consolidation hold up much later, because the cognitive load is lower and the structure comes from the paper rather than from the student.

The table below sets out the pattern by school direction. It is built from how long the inbound leg actually takes in term time rather than from map distance, which in this part of Dubai understates the afternoon by a wide margin.

sections.heading: The Damascus Street afternoon, and why it ends tutoring arrangements
paragraphs: Al Qusais is shaped by three pressures that all peak together. The Red Line carries commuters out towards Rashidiya and Centrepoint through the late afternoon. Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road carry cross-border traffic towards Sharjah from around 16:00. School buses from Mirdif and Al Warqa are moving against both. The result is an afternoon window where travel time stops being predictable, and unpredictability is far worse for a tutoring schedule than slowness.

A slow but reliable journey can be planned around. A journey that takes twenty-five minutes on Monday and fifty on Wednesday cannot, and that is the Al Qusais afternoon. Families here are not disorganised; they are working with variance. The right response is to build the schedule around the worst realistic case rather than the average, and then accept that the student sometimes starts a session early.

This is where a session with travel attached becomes structurally fragile. If a tutor is driving in, the same variance applies to them, and now two uncertain journeys have to coincide. A tutor crossing from Barsha, Mirdif or the Sharjah side is exposed to exactly the roads your child is on. One of the quietly persuasive arguments for online delivery in this district has nothing to do with teaching quality: the lesson only needs one party to arrive.

There is a knock-on effect on frequency. Families in this corridor who try three weekday sessions usually end the term doing one, because the third was always the one sacrificed. Families who commit to one protected weekday hour and one weekend block almost always still have both in March. The second pattern teaches more, and the difference is scheduling rather than effort.
bullets: Plan the slot against the worst realistic journey, not the average one
Two reliable sessions beat three that get renegotiated weekly
An online session needs only the student to arrive on time
Put the weekend block in the diary before the weekday hour

sections.heading: Mapping a week that survives to March
paragraphs: A workable tuition week in Al Qusais has four properties. It respects the inbound journey. It puts hard cognitive work at the best available hour. It leaves one evening completely free, because a teenager with no free evening stops cooperating by November. And it has a defined pause rule for school exam weeks, agreed in advance rather than argued about in the moment.

The pause rule is the part most families skip and the part that saves the arrangement. School assessment weeks arrive several times a year and a tuition session on top of three school exams is counterproductive. Agreeing at the outset that the slot pauses, with the sessions used later rather than lost, removes the conversation entirely. It also means nobody has to decide under pressure whether this particular week counts.

Subject rotation deserves a decision too. Two subjects at alternate weeks sounds efficient and usually is not, because a fortnightly gap is long enough for the thread to break. One subject weekly, taken to a stable position and then replaced by another, produces better results than two subjects each half-attended. Where a household genuinely needs two subjects running, the weekend block is the right place for the second.

The table sets out the shape that holds most reliably in this district. It is a template rather than a prescription, and the detail changes with which school the child attends, but the proportions are the point: one protected weekday hour, one weekend block, one untouched evening, and a pause rule in writing.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar reshapes tuition twice a year in ways a generic revision plan ignores. Ramadan shortens the school day, moves the family's evening around iftar and suhoor, and lands in a different part of the academic year each time because it follows the lunar calendar. Winter and spring breaks interrupt the run into the examination series. Eid can remove a week at short notice. None of this is an obstacle, but a plan that does not anticipate it loses several weeks of momentum.

During Ramadan the practical answer in this district is a post-iftar slot. Families who try to hold a late-afternoon session through the month usually lose it, because the hours before iftar are the least productive of the day for a fasting student and the household is occupied. A session at 20:30 or 21:00 with a student who has eaten works considerably better, and for non-fasting students the shortened school day actually opens an afternoon that is normally unavailable.

The planning point that matters most is the relationship between these interruptions and the examination series. Cambridge and Pearson run their main series in the first half of the year and again in the autumn, and the entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers. Cambridge's March 2027 series, as published in its key dates document, has an exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable ending on 19 November 2026.

For IB dates, treat anything published secondhand with caution, including on this page. The IB revises session timetables and the authoritative source is ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator. What can be planned on without any date at all is the internal calendar: the school's own deadlines for internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sit well before the external ones, and those are the dates a tuition plan should actually be built backwards from.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this corridor, and what the hour buys
paragraphs: Published rates in this market vary by a factor of ten, and the spread is explained mostly by format and seniority rather than by subject. The table below gives the bands in dirhams with the provider who published each one named, because a figure a parent can trace is worth more than a figure they have to trust. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list.

Reading the bands against the clock is the useful exercise for an Al Qusais family. If a household can genuinely hold two sessions a week, the budget question is monthly rather than hourly, and monthly packages published in this market sit at roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a single weekly hour run from AED 240 to 600 at the budget end up to AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Travel is the component worth examining in this district specifically. In-home bands run above online bands for a comparable tutor, and the gap pays for a journey. A tutor coming into Al Qusais between 16:00 and 19:00 is pricing in the same unpredictable afternoon your child is sitting in. That is money spent on a car rather than on teaching, and in a corridor with this much variance it buys a journey that sometimes fails anyway.

What a specialist hour actually buys is worth stating plainly, because the cheap end of the market and the specialist end do different jobs. At the budget band a tutor supervises homework and revises content. At the specialist band a tutor diagnoses from a marked script, knows what a particular paper's mark scheme rewards and can tell inside one session whether an internal assessment question will survive. Both are legitimate purchases. Buying the first while expecting the second is where families feel let down.

sections.heading: Online or a tutor in the room, when the drive is the problem
paragraphs: In-home tutoring has genuine advantages and a parent asking about it is asking a sensible question. Someone in the room can read a child's face, pick up the exercise book, and keep a restless thirteen-year-old on task more easily than a video call does. For younger students in particular that is worth paying for, and pretending otherwise would be a sales pitch rather than an answer.

The Al Qusais complication is that the advantage is bought with a journey through the worst hours on Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road. The fee carries that travel. The schedule carries the risk that the tutor is late or cancels. And the pool narrows to tutors who are willing to make the drive, which for a specific Diploma component can mean no suitable candidate at all. These are not small effects in this district; they are the main effects.

IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai, so the comparison here is a disclosure rather than a neutral survey. Our delivery is one-to-one over live video, in the UAE only. The in-home option exists in India, where the service model is different. A family that specifically wants someone in the room should know that is not what we sell before they spend time on an enquiry.

What closes the gap in practice is session design. A shared document both tutor and student type into, a visible clock on timed sections, the actual paper on screen with annotation, and a written note to the parent afterwards together do most of what physical presence was doing. The part that cannot be replicated is supervision of a child who will not work unless watched, and for that case a family is better served by a tuition centre or an in-home tutor, which is a straightforward thing to say.

sections.heading: What the metro changes for an Al Qusais teenager
paragraphs: Al Qusais is one of the few Dubai districts where a secondary student has a realistic independent travel option. Red Line stations serve the area, and an older teenager who can take the metro rather than wait for a parent changes the shape of the family's week. For tutoring this matters in two directions, and both are worth thinking through before setting a slot.

The first is arrival certainty. Metro timing is predictable in a way road timing here is not, so a student who travels independently can hold an earlier slot than a sibling who waits for a lift. Families with two children often discover they can place one at 17:00 and the other at 18:30 without either session being at risk, which is more teaching in the same evening than a single compromise hour.

The second is the trap. A session timed to start the moment a student walks through the door does not work. Teenagers need twenty minutes between arriving and thinking, and a session that begins in that window produces a tired, resentful half-hour. Build in the gap. An 18:00 arrival means an 18:30 start, not an 18:05 one, and the lesson that results is worth more than the extra twenty-five minutes.

There is a third consideration for exam terms. During a series, students sitting afternoon papers are not available in the early evening at all, and the useful session shifts to the morning of a free day or the evening before a paper, kept deliberately short. Arrangements that assume a fixed weekly hour through the series tend to waste the sessions that matter most.
bullets: Independent metro travel can buy an earlier, more reliable slot

sections.heading: The permit question, and what a parent should ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the application through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why any page quoting a specific amount should be read with suspicion. The useful question for a parent is not what the penalty is but whether the person teaching your child holds the permit, and because it costs nothing to obtain, a tutor who has not bothered has told you something about how they operate.

A second check applies in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing even from Dubai, because families move. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff there are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Anyone marketing your child's own class teacher for paid private lessons is operating against that, and the exposure falls on the teacher.

The organisational layer is different again. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence with initial approval, a completion window and annual renewal. That permit applies to centres with premises. It is not something an online matching service holds, and any provider implying regulator endorsement it does not have is a provider to leave alone.

sections.heading: If the hour you need has gone
paragraphs: Evening slots between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf time are the most requested hours in the whole UAE network, and in a mock or exam term they genuinely run out. Saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise. When the exact combination a family wants, a particular subject, a particular level and a particular hour, is not available, there are four honest options and they are worth knowing before you enquire.

The first is a different hour with the right tutor. A specialist at 19:30 usually beats a generalist at 17:30, particularly for coursework and technique work where the student is reading and responding rather than absorbing new content. The second is the weekend block, which for most Diploma students is the better slot anyway and is less contested than weekday evenings.

The third is a short wait with a date attached. If a specialist frees up a Tuesday in three weeks, that is often worth waiting for, especially outside the exam term. The fourth is a different tutor profile, taken deliberately: a strong subject teacher rather than a component specialist, for work that genuinely does not need the specialism. Content catch-up after an absence rarely needs an examiner's eye. An internal assessment three weeks from a deadline does.

What we do not do is take the booking and sort it out later. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and that silence is informative. Al Qusais families asking for a mainstream IGCSE subject at a mainstream hour will almost always be matched quickly. Families asking for Further Mathematics, Computer Science solution development or Arabic as a first language at Diploma level should expect a few days and a conversation rather than an instant answer.
bullets: A specialist at a later hour usually beats a generalist at the hour you wanted
Weekend blocks are less contested and suit coursework better

process.title: Start with the timetable, not the subject
process.description: Tell us which school, which direction the bus comes from and roughly when your child walks through the door. That single piece of information rules out half the possible slots and stops us proposing an hour that was never going to hold past October.

process.title: Send the board and the component
process.description: Subject, level and the exam board from the entry slip, plus what triggered the call: a mock grade, an internal assessment with no start, a fortnight missed. Syllabus codes are the most useful detail, because 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers and need different preparation.

process.title: Trial session in the real slot
process.description: The trial runs at the hour you actually intend to use, not at a convenient time for us. If 18:30 is the dependable hour, that is when the trial happens, because a slot that works once at 16:00 tells you nothing about a term.

process.title: Agree the pause rule before week one
process.description: School exam weeks, Eid, travel and Ramadan timing all get decided at the start rather than argued about later. Sessions pause and are used afterwards rather than being lost, which removes the weekly negotiation that ends most arrangements.

process.title: Half-term review against the school's marks
process.description: Progress is judged on the school's own assessment points, not on how the sessions felt. If the slot has stopped fitting, it moves. If the subject is stable, we say so and the hour goes to something else rather than running on out of habit.

whyPoints.title: The slot is designed before the teaching
whyPoints.description: We ask which school and which direction the journey comes from before proposing an hour, because in this corridor an optimistic slot fails by half-term. A dependable 18:30 session delivers more across a year than a 16:30 one that is renegotiated every week.

whyPoints.title: No journey inside the fee
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run above online rates for a comparable tutor, and the difference pays for travel through the same unpredictable afternoon your child is in. Online delivery removes that cost and the cancellation risk that comes with it.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the paper on the entry slip
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are different assessments, and tiered entry changes what is worth teaching. A tutor is assigned against the actual board and tier rather than against a year group, which is the difference between useful and merely competent.

whyPoints.title: Calendar-aware planning
whyPoints.description: Ramadan timing, school exam weeks, mock season and entry deadlines months ahead of papers are all built into the plan. Cambridge's March 2027 entries close in November 2026, and a family that learns that in January has already lost the option.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated upfront
whyPoints.description: Where a component is thinly covered or an hour is full, we say so and offer a dated alternative. No competing page in this market publishes a coverage limit, and a provider who never admits one is a provider who fills slots with whoever is free.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay support is teaching, question scoping and written feedback on the student's own draft. Operators in this market sell finished coursework; the consequence of that lands on the student's diploma, not on the seller.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: For a student at a school inside Al Qusais, 17:00 holds comfortably, because the journey home is short. For a child travelling back from Mirdif, Al Warqa or Academic City, 18:00 is the dependable hour. For families crossing from the Sharjah side, assume 18:30. Weekend mornings are available from around 09:00 and are the most productive hours of the week. The important thing is to pick a time nobody has to fight for: an optimistic 16:30 slot that gets renegotiated every Sunday teaches less across a term than a later one that always happens.

faqs.question: We get home from Sharjah at 18:30. Is that too late for a weekday lesson?
faqs.answer: It is late for new content and fine for everything else. At that hour the sensible work is marked-script review, worked examples, command-term drilling and short timed sections, where the structure comes from the paper rather than from the student's own concentration. Leave twenty minutes between walking through the door and starting, so an 18:30 arrival means a 19:00 session. If your child needs new abstract material taught, put that in a weekend morning block instead and keep the weekday hour for consolidation. That split produces better results than trying to do everything in one tired evening.

faqs.question: How many tuition sessions a week fit around a Year 11 timetable here?
faqs.answer: One protected weekday hour and one weekend block is the pattern that survives from October to the spring series in this district. Families who try three weekday sessions generally end the term doing one, because the third was always the session sacrificed when a school event or a slow return intervened. Two reliable sessions teach more than three contested ones. If a household genuinely needs two subjects running, put the second in the weekend block rather than adding another weekday evening, and keep at least one evening in the week completely free.

faqs.question: Do you run lessons after iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families in this corridor that is the slot that works. The hours before iftar are the least productive of the day for a fasting student and the household is occupied, so a late-afternoon session usually collapses within a fortnight. A session at around 20:30 or 21:00 with a student who has eaten works considerably better. For students who are not fasting, the shortened school day opens an afternoon that is normally unavailable, and that window is worth using for content work while it exists.

faqs.question: How long does the school run from Al Qusais to Mirdif take in term time?
faqs.answer: Longer than the map suggests, and more importantly it varies. The afternoon leg is squeezed between cross-border traffic heading towards Sharjah along Al Nahda Road, Red Line commuter flows and school buses moving against both. Arrival home between 16:15 and 16:45 is the realistic range for students travelling that direction, with worse days beyond it. Variance matters more than the average for scheduling: a journey that takes twenty-five minutes one day and fifty the next cannot be planned around, so build the slot against the worse case and accept an occasional early start.

faqs.question: My daughter's bus leaves at 06:40. Does a morning tutoring session ever work?
faqs.answer: Not on a school day, and the attempt usually costs more than it gains in lost sleep. Where morning sessions do work is on weekends and during school holidays, and they work very well there. A rested student at 09:00 on a Saturday can sustain a ninety-minute block, attempt a full timed paper or make real progress on an internal assessment, none of which is possible in a weekday evening hour. For a Diploma student travelling a distance to school, that weekend morning is often the single most valuable slot in the week.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost for a family in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: The market in Dubai splits by format and seniority rather than by neighbourhood. Published bands run from AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; and AED 200 to 450 or more for an exam specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the fee. These are the providers' own published figures rather than an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is a weekend block better value than two weekday hours for us?
faqs.answer: For Diploma students and for anyone doing coursework, usually yes. A ninety-minute weekend block is long enough to attempt a full past paper under timed conditions or to make genuine progress on an internal assessment, and the student arrives rested rather than after a long return journey. Two tired weekday hours cannot do either. The exception is subjects where spaced repetition matters more than depth, such as a large biology content base or vocabulary work, where shorter and more frequent beats longer and less often. Most families in this corridor end up with one of each.

faqs.question: Do sessions pause during school exam weeks?
faqs.answer: They should, and we agree the rule before the first session rather than arguing about it later. A tuition hour stacked on top of three school exams in a week is counterproductive, and the sessions are better used afterwards when the marked scripts come back, which is when they are genuinely diagnostic. Having the pause rule in writing from the start removes a weekly negotiation that quietly ends most tutoring arrangements by half-term. It also means nobody has to judge, under pressure, whether a particular week qualifies.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot if we travel over Eid or the winter break?
faqs.answer: The slot is held and the sessions are used after you return rather than being lost. Travel is normal in this part of the world and a scheme that punishes it ends up punishing the student. Tell us as far ahead as you can, because a gap of two or three weeks changes what the tutor should do in the session before you leave: a consolidation session with a short written task to take away works better than starting a new topic that will go cold. Longer absences are better handled by shifting to a holiday block.

faqs.question: Does a tutor driving into Al Qusais cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Published in-home bands in this market run above online bands for a comparable tutor, roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300, and part of that gap is travel. In this corridor specifically the journey is through the slowest and least predictable hours of the day along Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road, so the money buys a car journey rather than teaching, and the session carries a cancellation risk from the tutor's side as well as yours. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, so for us the comparison is a disclosure rather than a choice we sell both sides of.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book a slot for mock season?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. Evening hours between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf time are the most requested in the whole network, and in January and March they genuinely run out. Families who arrange a January block in November get the hour and the tutor they want. Families who call in the second week of January are choosing from what is left, which often means a later hour or a different tutor profile. If your child's school runs mocks in a known window, put the block in the diary when the school publishes the dates.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Qusais families use for IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The schools inside Al Qusais run British and Indian curricula, with IGCSE at sixteen in the British stream, and those students have the shortest journey home and the earliest workable tuition slot. For IB continuum and Diploma provision, families here commonly travel south-east towards Mirdif and Al Warqa or west towards Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City. Named schools on this page are neighbourhood context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. Check the KHDA listing for current programmes at a specific school, since provision changes between academic years.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time through its own app and e-services. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since it costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained it has told you something useful.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge entries actually close for a spring series?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, which catches families out every year. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series give an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May to June and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable ending on 19 November 2026. Always check the live official timetable, because provisional dates can be revised, and confirm any IB date with your school's coordinator.

The trial session runs at the hour you actually intend to use. If the hour you want is full, we will say so and give you a dated alternative instead of a maybe. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, so the only person who has to arrive on time is your child.

intro.heading: Tutoring that survives a roster, not just a term
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya sits immediately south of Dubai International Airport, between Airport Road and the Rashidiya interchange, with the Red Line terminus at its edge. The geography has shaped who lives here. A large share of households include somebody working to an aviation, logistics, hospitality or healthcare roster: cabin crew, engineers, ground operations, hotel managers, nurses at the nearby hospitals. In those homes the working week is a pattern that repeats every three or four weeks rather than every seven days.

That single fact breaks most tutoring arrangements, and it does so quietly. The session is booked for Tuesday at five. In week one the parent is home and the session is excellent. In week three the parent is on a long-haul pattern, nobody reminds the student, the laptop is not set up, and the hour is lost. In week five the same thing happens. By week eight the family concludes that tutoring did not work, when what actually failed was the assumption that an adult would be present to make it happen.

The fix is not more supervision. It is designing the arrangement so that no adult is required for it to run. That means the student holds the login, the task list and the calendar reminder; the tutor sends a short written note after every session that a parent can read from a hotel in another country; and the slot is fixed at a time that works on every week of the roster rather than on the easy weeks. None of that is complicated and almost nobody sets it up in advance.

The second Al Rashidiya factor is the school run. No private secondary school sits inside the district, so children travel: north and west towards Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, or east towards Mirdif and the suburbs beyond. Both directions cross roads that carry airport traffic as well as school traffic, and the afternoon pinch is correspondingly worse than the distance suggests. A realistic first slot here is 4:15pm or later, and for the Mirdif direction later still.

The third is travel by the whole family. Staff travel concessions mean many households in this district are away more often and for longer than the Dubai average, including term-time trips and long summers in another country. A tutoring plan that stops whenever the family moves is a plan that runs for half the year. One delivered over live video follows the student, which is the reason most parents here give for choosing it.

What follows is organised around those three. Roster patterns and the scheduling that survives them; the afternoon roads either side of the airport; what the market charges in dirhams; the examination calendar counted backwards so a travelling family can see the fixed points; and what a tutor may and may not do with assessed work when no adult is in the room. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video.

dubai/al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover most Al Rashidiya enquiries, and for each the relevant detail is how it behaves when the family is not all in one place.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers at sixteen. Cambridge examines in June and November series and tiers many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel examines in May/June and November and reports 9 to 1 on most specifications. Both boards publish their timetables in advance, and Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series so families can plan around them.

Entry deadlines, the examination window and the results date are the dates to put in a shared calendar first, because a family that books flights before checking them occasionally discovers the problem in the week of a paper.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The internally assessed components are the part most affected by a disrupted household, because they run on school-set internal deadlines across months rather than on a single examination day.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this district travel to school and often travel with the family too. The component that suffers is the Extended Essay, which depends on sustained independent work between supervisor meetings. Where a family is away for a month in DP1, the honest move is to agree what gets done before departure rather than afterwards.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria using task-specific descriptors. Because assessment is continuous rather than terminal, absence has a more diffuse effect: a student misses tasks rather than an examination, and the consequence appears in a report two months later.
programmes.countryNote: Families here benefit from asking the school early which tasks fall in which weeks. A term-time trip that crosses two criterion-assessed tasks costs more than one that crosses none, and the school can usually say which is which if asked before the flights are booked.

dubai/al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: Subject demand in this corridor leans towards mathematics and the sciences, with steady work on English for students in households where the language at home is not English and a parent is frequently away.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1
subjects.levels: Cambridge IGCSE Extended and Pearson Edexcel
subjects.description: The most requested subject here and the one that suffers most from inconsistent weeks, because fluency decays without practice. Two shorter sessions a week with set independent work between them hold up better across a roster than one long block.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves hold the marks. The practical paper credits a method described precisely enough to repeat, which a student can practise alone from a marked example if the tutor sets it properly before a family trip.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and quantitative questions. This is the subject where students most often need the tutor present to start a calculation, which makes it a poor candidate for a long unsupervised gap in the schedule.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The most self-studiable science at this level, because the losses are mark-scheme vocabulary and that can be drilled from flashcards and a marked script. Useful to park here when a travel month disrupts everything else.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic Diploma route, unforgiving of gaps. Higher Level assumes automaticity built over months, so a four-week break mid-course costs more here than in any other subject on this list.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with heavy calculator use. Marks leak on interpretation rather than computation: a question asking what a figure means in context gets answered with the figure.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to a real organisation. Students in aviation and hospitality households often have unusually good access to a genuine organisation for the research project, which is worth using while the family contact is available.

subjects.name: English B and English A
subjects.description: Two different courses often confused at enrolment. English B is a language-acquisition course; English A treats literature and language analytically. A tutor matched to the wrong one costs a term, and the distinction is on the school's course sheet.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy first: labelled axes, correct curves, clear shifts. Higher Level adds quantitative questions. The diagrams can be drilled independently, which makes this a good subject to set work in before a trip.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in every Dubai private school, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the expectations and language of instruction differ. Continuity matters here more than in most subjects, since vocabulary retention drops quickly over a long absence.

sections.heading: A roster is not a routine: what breaks and how to fix it
paragraphs: Scheduling around shift and duty patterns is a known problem in every industry and almost nobody applies it to tutoring. The mistake families make is to book the slot that suits the week they happen to be in when they enquire. If that is a week the parent is home, the slot gets chosen on availability that does not exist for three weeks out of four, and the arrangement unravels without anybody deciding to end it.

The correct method is to find the hour that works on the worst week. Lay out the full roster cycle, three or four weeks, and look for the slot that is viable in every one of them. It will usually be earlier or later than the obvious choice and it may be a weekend morning. That slot is worth more than a better hour that only exists some of the time, because consistency is most of what makes tutoring work.

The second move is to remove the adult from the critical path. A student of fourteen can hold a login, a calendar reminder and a notebook with the week's tasks in it. Where the parent is the one who opens the laptop and reminds the child, the session has a single point of failure that fails predictably. Where the student owns it, the parent's role shrinks to reading a note, which can be done from anywhere.

The third is the handover. In households with two working parents on different patterns, the person who knows what the tutor said last week is sometimes not the person at home this week. A short written note after each session, naming what was covered and what was set, solves that without a conversation. It is the single most appreciated thing we do for families in this district, and it takes the tutor three minutes.

sections.heading: The roads either side of the airport in the afternoon
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya's position has an obvious benefit and a less obvious cost. The benefit is access: Airport Road, Sheikh Rashid Road, the Ras Al Khor road and the Red Line terminus are all on the doorstep. The cost is that those roads carry airport and logistics traffic in addition to school traffic, so the afternoon congestion is not confined to the school-closing window and does not clear as quickly as it does in a purely residential district.

For families whose school lies north-west, towards Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, the journey is short in distance and the delay is concentrated at the interchange. For families heading east into Mirdif the journey is longer and the congestion along Algeria Street and Tripoli Street builds from before three. For the villa communities further east, Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej, the bus routes are longer still and a child can be on the road for forty minutes.

The practical consequence is that a 4:00pm start is optimistic for most of this district and 4:30pm is honest for the eastern direction. Families who want an earlier session are almost always better served by moving it to a weekend morning rather than compressing the gap between arrival and lesson, which produces a tired student and a frustrated tutor.

There is one local advantage worth using. Because the Red Line terminates here, older students who travel to school by metro arrive on a predictable schedule rather than a traffic-dependent one. For a Year 11 or Diploma student that predictability can be worth more than a shorter journey, and it allows a slot to be set with a smaller buffer.

sections.heading: What a student has to own when a parent is away
paragraphs: In households where an adult is frequently absent, the students who do well are not the cleverest ones. They are the ones who have been handed a small number of concrete responsibilities and understood that nobody else will pick them up. That transfer can be done deliberately, over a few weeks, and it is worth more to a teenager than any individual lesson.

The list is short. Hold the login and join the session two minutes early. Keep a single notebook with the week's set tasks written down, not a memory of what was said. Send the tutor a photograph of attempted work before the session if asked. Say when something was not done, rather than arriving and discovering it in the first five minutes. Know the date of the next school assessment.

Parents reasonably worry that this is too much to ask of a fourteen-year-old, and for some it is. The honest test is to try it for three weeks and watch. Students who cannot sustain it need the weekly format with a parent-facing reminder rather than the fortnightly one, and that is useful information rather than a failure. Students who can sustain it have acquired something that matters more at eighteen than at fourteen.

The tutor's side of this is equally concrete. A written note after each session, naming what was covered and what was set, so any adult in the household can pick up the thread. A clear statement when work has not been done, rather than a polite summary that hides it. And a refusal to use the session to do the work the student was supposed to do alone, because that converts a tutoring hour into a supervised homework hour at a specialist rate.

sections.heading: What the hour costs in this corridor, in dirhams
paragraphs: Published pricing in this market is scarce and inconsistent. Several of the most visible pages give no figure, and two of the ones that do quote US dollars. The figures below are dirham market rates attributed to the providers that published them. They describe the market and are not an IB Gram price list.

Budget online tutoring from university students and generalists is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, with one platform quoting from about AED 33. Qualified subject tutors online sit between about AED 150 and AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on one published index and AED 200 to AED 500 among independent tutors, because travel sits inside the rate. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one agency at AED 270, and one premium provider at AED 650.

There is a specific premium that matters in this district and nobody publishes it: the cost of inconsistency. A family paying AED 200 an hour who loses one session in four to a roster clash is effectively paying AED 267 for the sessions that happen, and losing the continuity that makes the subject work. Fixing the schedule is the cheapest rate reduction available, and it costs nothing.

Monthly figures seen in this market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. One published index estimates weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. We quote only after seeing a marked script and knowing the roster.

sections.heading: Online against a tutor who has to drive to Al Rashidiya
paragraphs: The in-home option is real in this market and deserves a fair hearing. A tutor at the table sees written working without being asked, can annotate a page, and gives a younger child a presence that a screen does not. If that matters most for your child, it is a legitimate choice and other providers offer it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. In this district the argument is sharper than usual for two reasons. The first is the roads: a tutor driving into Al Rashidiya in the late afternoon is crossing airport traffic, and the scheduled hour becomes an estimate. The second is the roster: an in-home visit needs somebody to admit the tutor, which is precisely the thing a roster household cannot guarantee.

There is a third reason specific to the travel patterns here. A family that spends six weeks away in the summer, or three weeks away at a term break, cannot take an in-home tutor with them. An online slot continues from wherever the student is, with the same tutor and the same plan. For households with staff travel concessions, that is not a marginal consideration; it is most of the value.

What we lose, and will say plainly: immediate unprompted sight of the page, which we replace with a phone or tablet camera angled over the working, and the social presence of an adult in the room, which for some younger students genuinely matters more than match precision.

sections.heading: The examination calendar counted backwards for a travelling family
paragraphs: A household that books flights months ahead needs the fixed dates before the revision plan, and this is the information no competitor page in this market provides. The two IGCSE boards publish their series and timetables in advance, and the lesson from their published dates is consistent: the deadlines that matter most sit long before the papers.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for International GCSE November 2027, which is the document to check before booking anything.

Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series make the same point more starkly: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 while final entries were due on 27 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A family revising from a timetable found online rather than the school's own is carrying a real risk.

For the IB May session, which is the one Dubai schools sit, we plan backwards from the school's internal deadlines. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, so we do not print one. The school's IB coordinator holds the internal dates for every assessed component, and those are the fixed points a travelling family should put in the calendar first.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when nobody is in the room
paragraphs: Households where an adult is frequently away are exactly the households most exposed to the worst offers in this market, because there is less oversight of what a student agrees to. One provider in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A student under deadline pressure, with a parent in another country, is the intended customer for that offer, and the consequence under board malpractice rules falls on the student.

The boundary is worth reading once so that a student can recognise it unaided. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on, explain each criterion and what its marks reward, say whether a research question is viable, warn that a method will not generate usable data, read a draft and name the criterion that is weak, and ask the questions that make a student see their own gap. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, pick the question, or edit a draft into a finished state.

The practical test we teach students here is simple enough to apply at eleven at night with a deadline the next day: if the help would still work with you absent, it is not help, it is substitution. Everything legitimate requires the student to be present and doing the thinking.

We also do not redistribute board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them, name the official source and work with what the school has issued. A provider offering a downloadable library of board material has told you how it operates, and it is worth noticing before a deadline rather than after one.

sections.heading: Starting, and the fallback when the slot you want is gone
paragraphs: Three things before the first session: a recent marked script or report, the board and syllabus code, and the full roster cycle rather than this week's availability. The third is the one families forget and the one that determines whether the arrangement survives to March.

The first session is a diagnostic. The tutor works through the script with your child and then writes a short note describing the actual gap, which is frequently not the one the school report named. Occasionally the note says a fortnight of structured independent practice would do more than a tutor, and we would rather write that than take a term's fee.

On availability, the honest position. The weekday window between 4:00pm and 6:00pm is contested across the whole city, and for scarce Higher Level subjects it fills. When your preferred hour is unavailable there are three options: a different hour with the specialist you want, your preferred hour with a tutor whose subject fit is good rather than ideal, or a weekend morning. In a roster household the weekend morning is very often the strongest choice anyway, because it is the slot least affected by the pattern.

Where we cannot match properly we say so at the enquiry. A narrow Higher Level subject with a coursework deadline inside six weeks, or an unusual language pairing, can take over a week to fill with the right person. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, and families keep finding one after paying for it.
