sections.heading: When the diagnosis says the problem is not technique
paragraphs: Diagnostic honesty cuts both ways. Sometimes the classification comes back overwhelmingly C - content the student genuinely did not know - and in that case no amount of command-term work or mechanical drilling will help. Saying so is more useful than selling a technique package, and it is the part of this approach that keeps it credible.

A content-dominated diagnosis usually points to one of three situations. There is a gap further back: a Year 11 chemistry problem that is really a Year 9 moles problem, which means the teaching has to start earlier than the current topic. The subject or level is a poor fit, which is a conversation about choices rather than about tutoring. Or the student has disengaged from the subject, in which case technique work is noise.

There are also diagnoses that are not academic at all. A consistent pattern of unfinished papers combined with strong untimed performance can indicate something worth discussing with the school rather than with a tutor, including whether access arrangements have been considered. Schools handle that process, not tutoring providers, and a family seeing that pattern should raise it with the school directly.

The last honest limit: tutoring is not required for anything. Not for Ministry of Education equivalency, not for university admission, not for progression through a school. Where a diagnosis shows a narrow execution problem, a handful of hours fixes it. Where it shows something else, the right answer may be a conversation with the school, a change of level, or simply time - and a provider that cannot say that is not diagnosing, it is selling.

sections.heading: Starting from the last paper somebody marked
paragraphs: The process here is deliberately short, because the first session has to produce evidence rather than rapport. A consultation establishes the school, the board, the subject and what the family already holds: mock scripts, returned assessments, a marked internal assessment draft. If nothing has been marked recently, the first session produces something by sitting a timed section under conditions.

The diagnostic session itself follows the classification method, with a written output: lost marks counted by cause, a note of the clusters, and a recommendation that may well be shorter than the family expected. Where the diagnosis shows execution rather than content, the plan is a fortnight of drills and two checking sessions rather than a weekly subscription, and we say so.

From there, a written plan with the school's own mock dates on it, reviewed fortnightly against something marked. The measure of progress is marks recovered per question type rather than a sense that sessions are going well, because the first is checkable and the second is not. Error counts from each diagnostic are kept so the family can see whether the mechanical losses are actually falling.

Two disclosures. Availability: mainstream requests are usually matched in a day or two, while scarce Higher Level subjects and coursework supervision close to a deadline are not, and in that case you get a date rather than a generalist. And the regulatory position: private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years, with tutoring without one subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. IB Gram has no UAE centre, office or branch and holds no regulator approval or accreditation.

process.title: Collect the evidence first
process.description: Before anything is taught, we ask what has been marked recently: mock scripts, class assessments, a returned internal assessment draft. Evidence beats description, and a parent's account of the problem is almost always broader than the script shows it to be.

process.title: Classify every lost mark by cause
process.description: Each lost mark is labelled content, command term, mechanical, sequencing or time. The counts are written down. Almost always the distribution is lopsided in a way the total mark concealed, and the lopsidedness is the plan.

process.title: Fix the cheapest losses first
process.description: Mechanical errors and command terms are drilled before content is touched, because they recover marks in a fortnight rather than a term. A student losing twenty marks to content and four to mechanics gets the reverse order, decided by the counts.

process.title: Practise under an enforced clock
process.description: Where the diagnosis shows unfinished papers, timing is practised deliberately: a marks-per-minute budget, a halfway checkpoint, and explicit permission to abandon a question after ninety seconds without progress.

process.title: Re-diagnose after each mock
process.description: Every mock produces a fresh classification and a fresh count, compared with the last one. The question is whether the mechanical losses are falling, which is checkable, rather than whether the sessions feel productive, which is not.

process.title: Stop when the diagnosis says stop
process.description: Where the counts show the execution problem has closed and no content gap remains, the honest recommendation is to stop rather than to continue weekly. A plan with an end condition is the difference between tutoring and a subscription.

whyPoints.title: Evidence before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session reads what has already been marked rather than starting at chapter one. A returned script with the scheme beside it answers in an hour what a term of general revision never establishes: where the marks are actually going.

whyPoints.title: Losses sorted by cause, not topic
whyPoints.description: Content, command term, mechanical, sequencing and timing require completely different responses and are indistinguishable in a total mark. Counting them separately is why the resulting plan is short and specific rather than a tour of the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: A method published for families to run free
whyPoints.description: The thirty-minute script-reading method is set out on this page so a parent can run it without buying anything. It costs nothing, it works, and most families have never been shown it by anyone.

whyPoints.title: Progress measured in recovered marks
whyPoints.description: Reviews run on marks recovered per question type and on falling error counts rather than on how sessions felt. Both are written down after every mock, so a family can check the claim rather than take it.

whyPoints.title: An end condition, stated upfront
whyPoints.description: Where the diagnosis shows a narrow execution problem, the plan is a fortnight of drills and two checking sessions. We say that rather than converting it into a weekly booking, and we say when the diagnosis points somewhere tutoring cannot reach.

whyPoints.title: A format built for three documents at once
whyPoints.description: Script, mark scheme and running tally sit side by side on a shared screen, the annotated file is kept, and the counts compare across the year. Paper copies on a table retain none of that.

faqs.question: My child in Arabian Ranches 2 revises constantly and the grade will not move. Why?
faqs.answer: In most cases the lost marks are not knowledge. Four causes account for nearly all of it: a command term misread so the wrong kind of answer was given, mechanical losses like dropped units and working not shown, a sequencing failure on multi-step answers under time pressure, or time running out. Revision addresses none of those, which is why more of it changes nothing. All four are visible on a returned script with the published mark scheme beside it, and counting them takes about half an hour.

faqs.question: How do I classify my child's lost marks myself?
faqs.answer: Take the marked script, the published mark scheme and a pen in a different colour. For each lost mark write one letter in the margin: C for content not known, T for a command term misread, M for a mechanical loss, S for a sequencing failure, X for a question not attempted. Do not discuss whether the mark was fair - the moment it becomes a dispute, the exercise stops working. Then count the letters. The distribution is almost always lopsided in a way the total mark hid.

faqs.question: What exactly is a mechanical mark loss?
faqs.answer: A mark lost for something unrelated to understanding. Units omitted from a numerical answer. Working not shown on a multi-step calculation, so one slip costs every mark rather than one. Rounding partway through and carrying the error forward. Significant figures that do not match the data. Graph axes without quantity and unit. Chemical equations balanced but missing state symbols. Each is worth a handful of marks across a paper, and together they frequently account for a grade boundary. A fortnight of drilling closes most of them.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on explain questions in Biology?
faqs.answer: Because they are answering describe. Explain requires a causal link - because, by, therefore - and a description of what happens earns part marks at best however accurate it is. The first-sentence test fixes it quickly: take ten past-paper questions and write only the opening sentence of each answer, then check that the sentence does what the command term asked. Ten first sentences takes about fifteen minutes and teaches more than an hour of writing full answers that repeat the same error.

faqs.question: My child leaves the last questions blank. Is that a knowledge problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the most misdiagnosed loss in examinations. Blank final questions record as ignorance, so families respond by teaching those topics, which achieves nothing because the student could already answer them. The common cause is over-investment early: a four-mark question answered at nine-mark length, repeated three times, costs the last page. The drill is a marks-per-minute budget written at the top of the paper, a halfway checkpoint, and explicit permission to abandon a question after ninety seconds without progress.

faqs.question: Is an untimed past paper useful practice?
faqs.answer: It measures knowledge and teaches nothing about timing, and for a student whose script shows unfinished questions it can make matters worse by rewarding the instinct to write exhaustively. For that student one enforced timed paper a week is worth three leisurely ones. Untimed work has its place earlier in a course, when the aim is to find out whether content is secure. Once a student is within a year of papers, the clock should be on for most practice.

faqs.question: How should I read an MYP report that gives criterion scores rather than percentages?
faqs.answer: Do not convert them. A criterion B score of 5 out of 8 is not 62% and does not map onto a percentage or a grade - it is an achievement level with published descriptor wording. Read the descriptor for level 7 or 8 in that criterion and compare it with what your child actually produced; the difference is the specific thing they are not yet doing. Families in this community routinely compare criterion scores between siblings as though they were grades, which produces conclusions the data does not support.

faqs.question: Should I ask the school for the annotated mock script, not just the grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most schools hand it over without hesitation when asked. A grade tells a family nothing about cause. The annotated script shows whether the marks went on content, command terms, mechanics or timing, and those four demand completely different responses. If the script has already been returned and filed at home, that is enough to run a diagnostic. If a school keeps mock papers, ask whether they can be seen at a parents' meeting.

faqs.question: How many hours does fixing an execution problem actually take?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A diagnostic on existing scripts is one hour. A command-term correction is one to two sessions. A mechanical-error drill is two sessions of checking plus short tasks at home over a fortnight. Those three total four to five hours and often account for most of the available improvement. A timing problem adds four to six. A genuine content gap in one subject is a different scale - fifteen to twenty-five hours - which is exactly why the diagnosis comes before the plan.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Arabian Ranches 2, or is everything online?
faqs.answer: Everything here is online, one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For diagnostic work the online format is genuinely better: the script, the mark scheme and a running error tally sit side by side on one screen, the tutor's cursor points at the line that lost the mark, and the annotated file is saved and sent afterwards. Across a table that is three paper documents and nothing retained.

faqs.question: What is the earliest workable session time from this part of Dubailand?
faqs.answer: For most families off Al Qudra Road, 6.00pm or later on a school night. A long return journey means a child reaching home at 4.15pm needs food and a pause before anything useful happens, and a 4.30pm start competes with both. Online delivery means a 6.30pm or 7.00pm slot carries no travel premium and no risk of a tutor sitting in traffic while the hour runs. Households whose children attend school inside the community or at Motor City can start earlier.

faqs.question: What if the diagnosis shows my child genuinely does not know the content?
faqs.answer: Then technique work will not help, and we say so rather than selling it. A content-dominated classification usually points to one of three things: a gap further back in the subject, so teaching has to start earlier than the current topic; a level or subject that is a poor fit, which is a choices conversation rather than a tutoring one; or disengagement, where technique work is noise. Each needs a different response, and a provider that cannot distinguish between them is not diagnosing.

faqs.question: Can two short sessions a week work better than one long one for a Year 7?
faqs.answer: For most students at that age, yes. Attention rather than content is the limiting factor below about Year 9, and two 45-minute sessions produce two contacts, two tasks and two corrections rather than one of each. The work at that stage is fluency - number bonds, tables, written method, reading comprehension practised aloud with questioning - rather than examination technique. Check whether a quoted rate is per hour or per lesson before comparing, since a 45-minute lesson at an hourly-sounding figure costs around a third more per contact hour.

faqs.question: When should tutoring stop?
faqs.answer: When the diagnosis says the execution problem has closed and no content gap remains. A plan with an end condition is the difference between tutoring and a subscription, and the end condition should be stated at the start: these error counts falling to near zero, these question types scoring consistently. Reviews after each mock test that claim against fresh counts rather than against an impression. Where the counts have closed, continuing weekly is spending money on a problem that no longer exists.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a UAE permit to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat specific amounts you see quoted with caution.

dubai/arabian-ranches-2.closingHeading: Send the script, not the symptom
dubai/arabian-ranches-2.closingBody: The most useful thing an Arabian Ranches 2 family can bring is the last paper somebody marked. From that, in a single session, the lost marks can be counted by cause and the plan becomes specific: a fortnight of mechanical drills, one session on command terms, a timing strategy, or - where the evidence points that way - genuine teaching of content that was never secure. Sessions run one-to-one over live video at a time that sits after the commute rather than inside it. If the diagnosis says the problem is not one tutoring can reach, you will be told that too.

intro.heading: Who lives in Arabian Ranches 3, and what their children are actually sitting
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 3 is an Emaar villa and townhouse community on the Dubailand side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, built out from 2019 onward across clusters including Sun, Joy, Bliss, Ruba, Caya, Anya and Elie Saab. That build date matters more to a tutor than it sounds. A community finished in the last six years is dominated by families who moved in with young children, which is why the age profile here skews heavily towards primary and lower-secondary rather than towards exam years. Most households have at least one child in Key Stage 1 or 2, or in the IB Primary Years Programme, and a smaller number who have already crossed into IGCSE or Diploma.

The second thing that shapes the academic picture is that Arabian Ranches 3 has no mainstream private campus inside its own gates. Children travel out: to Jumeirah English Speaking School in the original Arabian Ranches, to Ranches Primary School in Arabian Ranches 2, to GEMS Metropole in Motor City, to Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, to South View School on the Remraam side, to Victory Heights Primary in Dubai Sports City, or to Dunecrest American School and GEMS FirstPoint in the wider Dubailand ring. A single household can easily have two children on two different buses to two different curricula.

That split is the real academic pressure point of this community, and it is not the one marketing copy usually names. It is not that the schools are weak. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the Dubailand ring contains some strongly inspected campuses. The problem is that a parent here is often running two curricula, two reporting formats and two assessment vocabularies in one house. One child brings home a Key Stage 2 teacher assessment against national-curriculum expectations; the other brings home a PYP report with no grades on it at all. Neither tells you where the maths is actually weak.

Villa life changes the timetable as well. School runs in this belt are long, the bus window is wide, and after-school activity in Arabian Ranches 3 tends to happen inside the community rather than on the other side of town, which pushes homework and tuition towards the 17:00 to 20:00 block. Families with three children in different stages cannot send three different tutors to one villa on one evening at a sane cost, and they usually discover this in the first term of trying. An online schedule gives you 17:30 for one child and 19:00 for another without anyone driving anywhere.

The last piece is what happens when the youngest children in this community reach MYP 4 and IGCSE. Dubai's private school sector added six new schools during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%, and seven more arrive for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places. A community of young families sitting next to a growing supply of new campuses means a high rate of mid-stage school changes, and a school change between Year 8 and Year 10 is the single most common cause of the content gaps we are asked to close here.

So this page is written around the household rather than around a subject. It covers which campuses this community feeds, what the PYP to MYP to Diploma ladder actually demands at each step, what the Dubai market charges in AED, and how lessons are delivered. Everything on it is one-to-one tuition over live video with a specialist in the exact programme your child sits.

dubai/arabian-ranches-3.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches 3 households are usually spread across three or four stages at once, so the programme that matters is rarely a single one. These are the four we are asked for most often from this community, with what each one actually demands of a child living here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subject textbooks, and it reports on approaches to learning instead of percentages. Children here are strong at explaining their thinking and sometimes thin on procedural fluency: column arithmetic, times tables to twelve, written division, fraction equivalence. Those are the exact skills MYP mathematics assumes are automatic.
programmes.countryNote: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City runs the PYP within easy reach of Arabian Ranches 3, and several Dubailand campuses offer it alongside a British early-years structure. A parent moving a PYP child into a Year 5 British classroom in this belt should expect a term of adjustment in written maths methods and spelling conventions rather than in confidence.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment runs on four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Criterion A is usually knowledge and understanding; the later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection. Students who have always been quick at answers lose marks in MYP for not showing method, not justifying a choice of model, and not evaluating their own work.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Arabian Ranches 3 families most often arrive asking for help, because MYP 4 and MYP 5 coincide with the Personal Project and with the first set of marks that will shape Diploma subject choices. A tutor here works on criterion language and on the gap between a correct answer and a well-evidenced one.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum campuses in the Dubailand ring enter Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and the two are not interchangeable. Cambridge Physics is 0625 with a Core and Extended tier; Pearson International GCSE Physics is 4PH1 with a single tier and different practical arrangements. The mark scheme language differs, and so does the way a question is cued.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school's exams officer for the board and the syllabus code before you book any tutoring in Year 10. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and warns that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, so the exam dates your child sits are centre-specific, not generic.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The internal assessment in each subject is marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Students lose points far more often on the independent components than on the examined papers, because nobody schedules those for them.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, which means the practical crunch for a Dubailand family falls in the preceding November to February window when internal deadlines for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and subject internal assessments stack up on top of mock examinations. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the IB does not publish a date you should take second-hand.

dubai/arabian-ranches-3.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Arabian Ranches 3 households request most, listed with what the assessment actually rewards. We match one tutor to one subject and level rather than offering a generalist who covers everything badly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the paper marks. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigative problem and is the component Dubailand students most often meet unprepared, because school time runs out before it is practised properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. Marks go on interpreting output in context rather than on manipulation, so a student who can run a regression but cannot say what the gradient means in the situation given loses the communication marks.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tier choice is the decision that matters here. Core and Foundation cap the attainable grade; Extended and Higher expose a student to algebraic fraction work, circle theorems and functions that the lower tier never asks for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Students lose marks in units, significant figures and the explanation questions that ask for a mechanism rather than a formula. Electricity and circuits is the reliable trouble spot at IGCSE; at Higher Level it is fields and rotational work.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the mole concept decide the grade. The internal assessment also demands a research question narrow enough to control, and that is where a Diploma student most needs coaching on their own design rather than on content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Command terms are the hidden syllabus. The difference between describe, explain, outline and evaluate is worth more at this level than extra content, and data-analysis questions reward reading the axes carefully before answering.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE First Language English
subjects.description: The Diploma individual oral and the paper one guided analysis both reward a line of argument about how a text works. For IGCSE, directed writing marks turn on register and audience, which is a teachable skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. An economics answer without a labelled diagram and a clear judgement sentence rarely reaches the top band, however much content it contains.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics and Sciences
subjects.description: Work here is criterion-led: investigating patterns, communicating method, reflecting on the impact of science. The marks a student is missing are usually in criteria C and D rather than in knowledge, which is why extra content practice does not move the grade.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Arabian Ranches 3 usually means
paragraphs: Families in Arabian Ranches 3 who type this search are almost never asking for proximity. They are asking two questions at once: can someone teach the exact programme my child sits, and can they do it in the narrow evening window a Dubailand school run leaves behind. IB Gram answers both with one-to-one tuition over live video, matched by subject and level. Tutors do not travel to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India.

The reason this distinction matters here more than in older parts of Dubai is supply. Arabian Ranches 3 is a recent community on the far side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. The pool of people who both live within a reasonable drive and happen to specialise in, say, Chemistry at Higher Level or Pearson International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 Higher tier is small, and gets smaller the more specific the need. Choosing from that pool means trading subject expertise for geography, which is a bad trade in an exam year.

The second reason is arithmetic. A villa family with three children at three stages who books three in-home tutors is paying travel time three times over, at market in-home rates that run materially above online rates, and is coordinating three arrivals in one evening. The same family booking online slots at 17:30, 18:45 and 20:00 pays only for teaching time and nobody leaves the house. The comparison table further down this page sets out the cost and logistics side by side.

What a parent should take from this section is simple. Use the search phrase, because it is how this market talks. Then judge a tutor on the syllabus code they teach, the components they can diagnose, and whether they are free at the hour your household can actually sit down.

sections.heading: The Dubailand school ring: where Arabian Ranches 3 children actually go
paragraphs: No mainstream private campus sits inside Arabian Ranches 3 itself, so every child here commutes. That single fact shapes the academic support this community needs, because it means the school day is bracketed by two bus journeys rather than one short walk, and because it means siblings are frequently split across campuses and curricula to fit available places.

The table below sets out the realistic daily options and what each one means for a tutoring schedule. Commute figures are indicative off-peak driving times from the Arabian Ranches 3 entrance and will be longer on a school bus making stops, which is precisely the point: a bus that leaves campus at 15:10 can deliver a child home closer to 16:30, and an activity after that pushes a workable lesson to 17:30 at the earliest.

Curriculum mix is the other variable worth planning around. A household with one child at a British-curriculum primary and another at an IB continuum school is handling two reporting systems that do not translate into each other. A Key Stage 2 report describes attainment against national-curriculum expectations; a PYP report describes approaches to learning and conceptual understanding. Parents reasonably conclude that both children are fine, and then find a numeracy gap in MYP 4.

Before booking anything, ask each school's exams officer for the examination board and syllabus code your child will be entered for. For IB schools, ask the programme coordinator which year groups sit which internal assessments and when the internal deadlines fall. Those two answers change what a tutor should be doing far more than any general level description.

sections.heading: The PYP to MYP to Diploma ladder, and the two points where it bites
paragraphs: A community full of primary-aged children is a community that will meet two specific transitions in the next few years, and both are predictable enough to plan for. The first is the move out of the Primary Years Programme into either MYP 1 or a British Year 6 or 7 classroom. The second is MYP 5 or Year 11 into the Diploma or into A Level. Neither transition is about intelligence; both are about a change in what the assessment rewards.

Leaving the PYP, the change is procedural. Inquiry-led primary teaching produces children who explain their reasoning well and who have sometimes not drilled written methods to automaticity. MYP mathematics and British Year 7 both assume that long multiplication, written division, fraction operations and negative-number arithmetic happen without conscious effort, because the new content sits on top of them. A child spending working memory on the arithmetic has none left for the algebra.

Entering the Diploma, the change is about independence. MYP and IGCSE are taught in lessons with deadlines set by a teacher. The Diploma adds four pieces of work that are substantially self-managed: the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, the subject internal assessments, and the CAS portfolio. Students who have never had to schedule their own three-month project do not fail these on ability. They run out of calendar.

The table maps each step with the specific symptom a parent sees at home. It is worth reading the middle column carefully, because the home symptom is almost always misread as a motivation problem when it is a skills or scheduling problem.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in the Dubailand belt, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. That is unhelpful to a family budgeting in dirhams, so the bands below are published openly. They are market rates gathered from published provider pricing and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost tables, not an IB Gram price list. IB Gram's own rate depends on the subject, level and tutor and is quoted after a consultation.

Read the bands as a function of scarcity rather than of quality. A university student teaching Key Stage 2 numeracy online sits at the bottom. A specialist teaching a single Higher Level science with internal assessment coaching sits near the top, because the pool of people who can do that competently is small. In-home rates carry travel inside them, which is why they sit above the equivalent online rate for the same tutor profile.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set those against school fees: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

One practical note for a villa household. Where two or three siblings need support, the sensible structure is usually one weekly slot each at the level they are actually at, rather than longer sessions for the eldest. The marginal value of a fourth hour with a Diploma student is lower than the value of a first hour with the Grade 4 child whose arithmetic is slowing everything down.

sections.heading: Online lessons versus a tutor in the villa: the comparison a Dubailand family should run
paragraphs: This is the decision most Arabian Ranches 3 parents are actually making, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. A tutor sitting at the kitchen table has real advantages: a younger child is easier to keep on task, the parent can see what is happening, and there is no dependence on a connection. Those advantages are strongest at primary age and weakest in an exam year.

Against them sit three costs that are easy to underestimate. The first is money: in-home market rates carry travel inside them. The second is time: a tutor crossing Dubailand in afternoon traffic will protect their own schedule by limiting how many addresses they serve, which narrows your choice to whoever is already nearby. The third is substitution risk. When an in-home tutor is ill or leaves the country, there is rarely a like-for-like replacement within driving distance of a Dubailand villa.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so this is a comparison between our online model and what the local market sells, not a choice we can fulfil both sides of. Home visits are available only through our India service. What the online model buys an Arabian Ranches 3 family is subject depth: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist, a Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier specialist, an MYP criterion specialist, each at the hour that suits your evening rather than their route.

The honest recommendation is mixed. For a Grade 2 or Grade 3 child who needs a reading or number-fluency habit built, proximity and a parent in the room matter and a local in-home tutor is a reasonable buy. From MYP 4 and Year 10 upwards, where the grade turns on component technique and mark-scheme behaviour, subject specialism beats proximity every time.

sections.heading: Three children, three stages, one evening: how a villa schedule actually works
paragraphs: The scheduling problem in this community is specific enough to deserve its own section. A typical Arabian Ranches 3 household has a primary child home by 16:15, a middle-school child home by 16:45 after a bus with more stops, and sometimes a Diploma student who gets back later still and then has three hours of their own work to do. Into that, a parent is trying to fit tuition, activities, dinner and a bedtime that leaves a nine-year-old functional the next day.

The pattern that holds up over a full term puts the youngest child first, at 17:00 or 17:30, for a shorter session of forty-five minutes while they are still alert. The middle child takes 18:30, after a break and some food, for a full hour. The Diploma student goes last at 20:00, because older students work better later and because their session is often reviewing work they produced that afternoon. Nobody drives anywhere, so the gaps between slots are usable.

Two further adjustments are worth making deliberately. Keep the same weekday for the same child rather than rotating, because a fixed habit survives a busy week and a floating appointment does not. And during Ramadan, move sessions after Iftar: school hours shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and a post-Iftar slot is far more productive than a 16:00 one. Our tutors schedule across time zones, so a later evening slot is straightforward to hold.

The last thing to plan is the end of the arrangement. Weekly tuition should have an exit: a target component, a mock paper, a set of criteria. When the student can do the thing unaided, the sessions should stop or drop to monthly maintenance. An open-ended weekly booking that nobody reviews is how families end up spending for three years on a problem that was fixed in four months.

sections.heading: Why a Grade 4 maths gap shows up in MYP 4, and how to catch it early
paragraphs: This matters disproportionately in Arabian Ranches 3 because the community's children are mostly young enough that the gap is still cheap to close. The mechanism is straightforward. Secondary mathematics is cumulative in a way that no other subject quite is. Every new topic assumes fluency in an earlier one, and fluency means automatic, not merely possible. A student who can do fraction arithmetic slowly and with effort is not fluent in it, and will struggle with algebraic fractions two years later even though nobody taught algebraic fractions badly.

The reason it surfaces at MYP 4 or Year 10 rather than earlier is that until then there is enough slack in the curriculum for effort to compensate. A diligent student can get good grades through Year 8 by working hard on each topic in isolation. From MYP 4, topics start combining: a question gives a quadratic that needs factorising inside a problem about area, with an answer required to three significant figures. Three partial fluencies in one question produce a wrong answer and a confident student who cannot see why.

The diagnostic is easy to run at home and does not require a tutor. Ask a child to do twenty questions of pure arithmetic and simple algebra with no calculator and no context: times tables beyond seven, division with a remainder, adding unlike fractions, ordering negative numbers, simplifying a ratio, substituting a negative value. Time it. Fluency looks like near-perfect accuracy at speed. Anything slow or hesitant is a gap worth closing now rather than in Year 10.

Where a gap exists, the work is unglamorous and short: targeted practice on three or four specific skills over six to ten weeks, with the tutor checking retention rather than reteaching. Parents consistently expect this to take a year. It usually does not, provided it is diagnosed specifically rather than treated as general weakness in maths.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do with MYP and Diploma coursework
paragraphs: This has to be stated plainly, because at least one provider ranking for Dubai tutoring queries sells finished internal assessments. That is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A Diploma candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own faces an investigation that can end the Diploma. No tutoring arrangement is worth that risk.

What a tutor legitimately does is teach the skills the task assesses and give feedback on work the student has produced. For an internal assessment, that means helping a student understand what each criterion rewards, discussing whether a research question is narrow enough to investigate, reviewing a method for controlled variables, explaining why a graph does not support the conclusion drawn from it, and pointing at a paragraph that asserts rather than evidences. The student then does the work again, themselves.

What a tutor must never do is supply content, restructure a draft into finished prose, dictate conclusions, or hand over a model answer for the student to adapt. The line is simpler than it sounds in practice: if the tutor's words would end up in the submission, it has been crossed. IB Gram tutors are briefed on this boundary, and a session that drifts towards content production is a session to stop. The same principle applies to the MYP Personal Project and to IGCSE coursework components.

Parents can hold a tutor to this with one question at the start of a coursework block: what will you do, and what will my child do? A good answer is specific about both. It also means asking the school's coordinator what external help is permitted and declared, because schools differ in how they record acknowledged support, and declaring it is always safer than not.

sections.heading: Getting started from Arabian Ranches 3, including what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The useful first step is not booking a tutor. It is collecting four pieces of information: the examination board and syllabus code for each subject, the most recent mock or internal assessment mark with the mark scheme if the school released it, the school's internal deadlines for coursework, and the hours your household can actually sit down. With those four, a match takes a short conversation. Without them, the first three sessions are spent discovering what the problem is.

From there the sequence is a consultation, a trial session with a named tutor, and then a weekly slot if the fit works. The trial exists to answer one question: does this student work well with this person. Subject knowledge can be checked on paper; working relationship cannot, and a tutor who is technically strong but does not hold a fourteen-year-old's attention is the wrong tutor however good the credentials.

On availability, the honest position: specialist cover is not uniform. A request for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry Higher Level or IGCSE Mathematics Higher tier is normally matched quickly. A request for a less commonly taught Diploma option, a specific second language, or a narrow internal assessment specialism may take longer, and in some cases the right specialist is in a different time zone and the available slots are earlier or later than ideal. We say so when it applies rather than placing a generalist and hoping.

On regulation, one thing is worth knowing before you hire anyone in this market, including independently. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. If you are engaging a tutor directly, it is reasonable to ask whether they hold one.

faqs.question: Is there a school inside Arabian Ranches 3, or do children have to commute?
faqs.answer: There is no mainstream private campus inside Arabian Ranches 3 itself, so children commute into the surrounding Dubailand ring. The common destinations are Jumeirah English Speaking School in the original Arabian Ranches, Ranches Primary School in Arabian Ranches 2, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Victory Heights Primary in Dubai Sports City and South View School towards Remraam. Journey times from the community entrance run roughly ten to twenty-five minutes off-peak and longer on a bus making stops. The practical effect is that a workable tuition slot for a secondary child in this community rarely starts before 17:00.

faqs.question: Can we book a tutor who visits our villa in Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: No. All tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The reason is not cost but choice: an online match lets an Arabian Ranches 3 family book a Chemistry Higher Level specialist or a Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier specialist rather than whoever already drives this part of Dubailand. It also means two or three siblings can each have a slot on the same evening without a second journey or a second travel charge.

faqs.question: My two children are in different curricula at different schools. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and it is better not to try. A tutor who is genuinely strong on MYP criterion marking is not automatically strong on Key Stage 2 written methods, and the reverse is equally true. What we do instead is match one tutor per child per subject and schedule the slots on the same evening at different times, which costs nothing extra online. The sessions are recorded in notes written against each school's own scheme of work, so you can see both children's progress without having to translate between two reporting systems.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Diploma tutor cost per hour for a Dubailand family?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for a Diploma specialist online run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, with Standard Level towards the lower end and Higher Level with internal assessment coaching towards the upper. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quotes around AED 270; Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home rates sit higher because travel is inside them, typically AED 280 to 500. Those are market figures rather than ours. IB Gram quotes its own rate after a consultation, because it depends on the subject, the level and the individual tutor.

faqs.question: At what age does tutoring actually pay off for a child in this community?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most parents assume, and for an unglamorous reason. Secondary mathematics assumes fluency in primary arithmetic, and fluency means automatic rather than merely possible. A Grade 4 child who can add unlike fractions slowly is not fluent, and that shows up as unexplained errors in MYP 4 algebra five years later. A short, specific block of six to ten weeks on three or four named skills at primary age is cheaper and faster than remediation in Year 10. The test is accuracy at speed, without a calculator and without context.

faqs.question: Which exam board will my child be entered for, and why does it change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ask your school's exams officer, because the answer is centre-specific and it matters. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is syllabus 0625 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1 with a single tier and different practical arrangements. The question styles, the mark scheme language and the tiering decisions differ. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers can be teaching accurate physics and still leave a student unprepared for the specific paper they will sit. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six timetable zones, so dates vary by centre.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a goal is specific enough to be achievable, review a process journal the student has kept, question whether the evidence supports a conclusion, and point out where a report asserts rather than demonstrates. What a tutor must not do is supply content, restructure a draft into finished prose, or provide a model for the student to adapt. The test is simple: if the tutor's words would end up in the submission, the line has been crossed. Ask your school what support must be declared.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted is unverified. If you hire a tutor directly, it is reasonable to ask.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start after the Dubailand school bus?
faqs.answer: For a primary child on a short route, 16:30 is achievable. For a secondary child on a bus with multiple stops from Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Remraam, plan for 17:15 to 17:45 and accept that an activity after school pushes it later. The pattern that survives a full term in Arabian Ranches 3 households puts the youngest child at 17:00 or 17:30 for forty-five minutes, the middle child at 18:30 for an hour, and a Diploma student at 20:00. Because nobody drives anywhere, the gaps between those slots are genuinely usable.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education need separate tutoring alongside a British or IB programme?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth understanding why. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For non-Arab families, Arabic as an additional language is frequently the subject with the least homework support available at home, which makes it a common request. We offer tutoring in these streams online alongside the main curriculum.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 10 IGCSE student in Arabian Ranches 3 have?
faqs.answer: For one subject that is genuinely behind, two sessions of sixty minutes a week for a term does more than one longer weekly session, because retention improves with spacing. For a subject that is sound but needs exam technique, one session a week from January is usually enough. What rarely works is three or four subjects at one session each: the student has no time left to do the work between sessions, and tutoring without independent practice in between produces understanding without fluency. Pick the one or two subjects where the marks are actually being lost.

faqs.question: Can sessions move after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we recommend it. School hours shorten during Ramadan, afternoons are low-energy for fasting students, and a 16:00 session is usually the least productive hour of the day. Moving to a post-Iftar slot typically produces better work in less time. Because our tutors are matched across time zones rather than from one city, holding a later evening slot for several weeks is straightforward. The same applies to the long summer break and to the weeks either side of Eid, where families often prefer a short intensive block to a weekly rhythm.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Common requests such as Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry Higher Level, Physics and IGCSE Mathematics Higher tier are normally matched quickly. A less commonly taught Diploma option, a specific second language or a narrow internal assessment specialism can take longer, and sometimes the right specialist is in a different time zone, which means the available slots are earlier or later than a Dubailand evening would prefer. In that case we set out the real options rather than placing a generalist and hoping the fit works out.

faqs.question: Is a KHDA inspection rating enough to judge whether my child needs extra support?
faqs.answer: It is useful context and a poor individual diagnostic. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports, which tell you about provision across a whole school. They do not tell you whether your child's set is being stretched, whether the option block put them in the wrong mathematics course, or whether they are losing marks on command terms. For that you need the last mock script and the mark scheme. Read the inspection report for the school decision, not the tutoring decision.

faqs.question: We are moving a child from an IB school to a British school in Dubailand mid-year. What breaks?
faqs.answer: Usually two things, and neither is ability. The first is written method: an IB primary education emphasises inquiry and reasoning, and a British Year 5 or 6 classroom assumes specific procedures for multiplication, division and fractions are automatic. The second is assessment vocabulary, because national curriculum expectations and PYP reporting describe different things. Plan a short diagnostic block in the first six weeks focused on procedural fluency and on the specific topics the new scheme of work already covered. A term of adjustment is normal and should not be read as a drop in ability.

intro.heading: The subject is the variable, not the location
paragraphs: Families comparing tutors in Dubai tend to compare the wrong attributes: how near, how experienced in general, how well reviewed. The attribute that moves a Diploma grade is narrower than any of those. It is whether the person teaching understands that a Chemistry Higher Level student losing marks on unfamiliar data needs different work from one losing marks on organic mechanisms, and can tell which of the two your child is from a marked script.

That is a subject-level question and it has a subject-level answer, which is what this page is for. Each of the Diploma's six groups assesses something specific, divides its marks in a particular way between examined papers and internally assessed work, and generates its own recurring failure. A tutor who knows the subject in general and not the assessment in particular will teach competently for eight weeks and move nothing, which is the most common disappointing outcome in this market.

The Higher Level and Standard Level distinction carries more weight than almost anything else on a shortlist. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra hours attached: the content extends, there are additional examined components, and the written demands rise. A tutor who is strong at Standard Level and has never taught above it is a reasonable hire for one of those students and a poor one for the other, and the only way to know is to ask which level they teach this academic year.

There is also a Dubai-specific dimension. The Dubai Media Office reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the IB on 7% of enrolment. A Higher Level cohort in a single subject at a single Dubai school is often a dozen students or fewer, which means the school's own specialist is one person and a student who does not get on with that one person has nowhere else inside the building to go.

On the phrase in the URL, the plain answer. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so a scanned script is marked up by tutor and student together. Nobody arrives at a Dubai address, and the comparison table in the first section sets out what that trades away and what it buys.

What it mostly buys is the subject match this page is about. Matching across the whole pool rather than within a twenty-minute drive is how a Higher Level Chemistry student gets a Higher Level Chemistry teacher instead of the nearest available science graduate, and for the tight combinations that is the whole difference.

That is the gap private subject teaching actually fills in this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D in most subjects, each on a 0-8 band, converted to a 1-7 grade by a boundary table the school holds. The content and the criteria are different things, and most tuition at this stage teaches the content to a student who already has it while the criteria go unread.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the continuum place the personal project in Year 11, which absorbs a term of evenings in the year before the Diploma. The subject gap that most reliably follows into DP1 is algebraic fluency, because the project year displaces practice. A diagnostic in the first six weeks of DP1 is cheaper than a rescue in DP2.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, no percentages and no papers, so there is no assessment architecture to teach to. Support here is about reading fluency, number sense or an additional language, measured on a repeated task three weeks apart rather than on a test. The risk is a tutor importing a different system's worksheets.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and combined classes explicitly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson — a reasonable benchmark for primary session length too.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses inside it are examined exactly as in the full Diploma, so the subject tables on this page apply to them directly. The career-related units are provider-assessed and sit outside them.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the programme, so no local tutoring supply has grown around it. The honest approach is to treat the Diploma courses as the tutorable part, apply the same Higher and Standard Level logic to them, and ask the school's coordinator what the reflective project criteria require rather than guessing.

dubai/best-ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject, what changes between Higher and Standard Level and where the additional Higher Level demand actually bites. This is the information a shortlist should be built on, because it decides whether a tutor's experience is relevant to your child or to somebody else's.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level extends into additional organic and energetics content and adds examined material that rewards handling unfamiliar data rather than recall. Standard Level students lose marks on equilibrium explanations; Higher Level students lose them on method evaluation and mechanism precision. Different work, different tutor brief.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension is mathematical in content and verbal in assessment: more demanding derivations, and extended-response questions asking for reasons rather than values. Dubai cohorts are typically comfortable with the first and thin on the second, which makes the Higher Level brief partly a writing brief.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth across the core and more data-heavy assessment. The recurring loss at both levels is application rather than recall: a process known in the abstract and not transferred to a named organism in an unfamiliar graph. Higher Level simply raises how unfamiliar the graph is.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level extends calculus substantially and adds proof, and includes an additional examined paper. A Standard Level specialist can genuinely struggle here. The honest question to a tutor is whether they have taught Higher Level proof to a full cohort, not whether they are good at maths.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Higher Level deepens the statistics and modelling and adds its own additional examined component. At both levels the marks are lost in the written interpretation that must follow a calculation, and in undocumented calculator work, which is a presentation problem rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds quantitative content and an additional examined paper built on unfamiliar data. At Standard Level the band boundary sits in the evaluation paragraph; at Higher Level it sits there too, plus in the accuracy of calculation. Two separate remedies, often in the same student.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level extends the content and raises the weight of extended analysis. The loss is identical at both levels and unusually consistent: answers written from theory without touching the stimulus material, which forfeits the application and evaluation marks the question was actually testing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an additional written component and raises the demand for sustained argument across texts. Both levels examine close analysis of a specific technique in a specific line, and both lose marks to summary. The Higher Level extension is about holding an argument together at length.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Higher Level works with literary texts and raises the register expected in writing and speech. Marks at both levels are lost on text-type conventions rather than vocabulary, which is why general English practice does little and a template per text type does a lot.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth-study content and an additional essay-based examined component. The band boundary at both levels is named detail: dates, figures, actors. Higher Level demands more of it and demands it sustained across longer essays under tighter time.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Higher Level adds resource management, abstract data structures and an additional examined component. Marks at both levels go on pseudocode precision rather than on conceptual understanding. Supply at Higher Level is thin across the region, so ask about availability a term ahead.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: No Higher or Standard Level split; the same essay and exhibition for every candidate. The loss is structural rather than informational: a topic treated as a knowledge question. The only legitimate help is criterion feedback on the student's own draft, never drafting or redrafting.

dubai/best-ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: What differs by Dubai district is less the subject than the depth of local provision. The notes below record which parts of the emirate have a thin Higher Level supply nearby, which is where matching across a wider pool matters most.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Dubai South
regions.note: A spread-out catchment with large schools on several curricula and a modest IB cohort. Higher Level science groups here are small, and a student needing a second explanation has few options inside their own school.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: Established villa communities where most pupils travel to Mirdif or Al Warqa schools. Local tutoring supply is largely generalist, so a Higher Level brief almost always needs to be matched from outside the area.

regions.name: Al Twar, Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A dense school population dominated by other curricula, with a small Diploma presence. Mathematics requests dominate here, and the Higher Level and Standard Level split is where most mismatches happen.

regions.name: The Greens and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Apartment communities beside the city's densest IB school cluster, so local provision is better than anywhere else in Dubai. Even here, the less common Higher Level options have no nearby specialist at all.

regions.name: Jumeirah Islands and Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Villa catchments feeding British and IB schools across Al Barsha and Emirates Hills. Families here often compare the Diploma with A Level in Year 11, which makes a tutor who has taught both unusually useful.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: A small residential catchment with almost no nearby tuition provision and long evening journeys in either direction. The practical effect is that any subject brief here has to be solved without reference to distance.

regions.name: Dubai Production City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Short internal road networks and early school returns make 4.30pm starts realistic, which matters for Higher Level work that needs a student still able to concentrate. Local specialist depth remains limited.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: Dense, affordable housing with pupils spread across many schools and curricula. The tutoring offers that reach this area are overwhelmingly at the budget end, which is a poor fit for Higher Level coursework.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali, Dubai South and Dubai Investments Park
schoolClusters.note: Large schools serving a wide southern catchment, with Diploma cohorts that are small relative to overall enrolment. Students we support here most often need Higher Level sciences, which is precisely where a single school's specialist supply is one person deep.

schoolClusters.city: Al Khawaneej, Al Mizhar and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: A mixed cluster where households frequently run two curricula across siblings. The subject requests we see here split cleanly: mathematics at both levels for the Diploma students, and English or science support for the others, which is two different briefs in one house.
schools: Al Mizhar American Academy for Girls

schoolClusters.city: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: One of the emirate's densest school districts, with the IB a minority provision inside it. Students we support in this cluster are often the only Diploma candidate among their immediate friends, which makes a subject-matched specialist more valuable than a locally recommended generalist.
schools: Our Own High School Al Warqa

modes.description: One 60-minute session a week on a single Higher Level subject, working through the extension content and the additional examined component rather than revisiting the core. Suits a student whose Standard Level peers are coping and who is finding the Higher Level demand itself to be the problem.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room against one-to-one over live video
paragraphs: Worth getting out of the way first, because it affects everything else on this page. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. If what you need is an adult physically present to make a reluctant 12-year-old sit down, that is a real need and this is not the service that meets it. For a Diploma student working on a named component, the comparison below is the honest one.

The market for visits is substantial and priced accordingly. Bestimate's Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is broadly a car in evening traffic. What it purchases is presence; what it does not purchase is a wider choice of specialist, because the pool shrinks to whoever will drive to your community at 6pm.

That shrinkage is the point of the comparison for a subject page. A Higher Level Computer Science student in Nad Al Hamar is choosing between a specialist somewhere in the wider pool and whoever is local and willing. The specialist has taught the additional examined component; the local option may be a competent programmer who has never read the syllabus. No amount of presence in the room closes that gap.

There are two smaller differences that matter more than families expect. Marking is the first: a visiting tutor typically reads a script during the lesson, costing ten to fifteen minutes of a paid hour, while an online arrangement can mark between sessions and open with the diagnosis already done. The second is switching cost. Changing a visiting tutor means renegotiating a journey; changing an online specialist is an administrative act, which makes a week-six review genuinely actionable.
The table sets the two side by side on the things that differ. It is not a sales table: the first two rows go against us.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what actually changes
paragraphs: Parents are told Higher Level is harder, which is true and not useful. What changes is specific: the content extends beyond the shared core, there is normally an additional examined component, the written demands rise, and the time pressure in the examination room increases because the questions expect more development per mark. Each of those four produces a different tutoring need.

The content extension is the part a tutor's experience either covers or does not. A teacher who has delivered Standard Level for years knows the shared core thoroughly and may never have taught the extension topics at all. That is not a criticism; it is a scope question, and it is answerable in one sentence by asking which level they have taught to a full cohort rather than in isolated revision sessions.

The written demand is the part families underestimate. In the sciences particularly, the Higher Level papers ask for sustained reasoning rather than longer calculations, and a student who was comfortable at Standard Level can find that the mathematics was never the obstacle. For those students the Higher Level brief is partly a writing brief inside a science subject, delivered by somebody who knows which words the mark scheme rewards.

The decision to move between levels belongs to the school and has a deadline. Schools set their own internal cut-off for level changes, and the IB has registration requirements behind it, so a family considering a move from Higher to Standard Level should ask the Diploma coordinator for the date before doing anything else. A tutor's view is input; the school's calendar is the constraint.

The table compares the two levels across the things that change rather than restating that one is harder. Confirm the exact component weightings for your child's subject in the current subject guide, which the school holds and which is revised between cohorts.

sections.heading: The sciences: where the papers actually put the marks
paragraphs: Chemistry, Physics and Biology share an assessment shape and lose marks in entirely different places, which is why a science generalist is a weaker hire than families assume. All three combine externally examined papers with an internally assessed investigation, and in all three the internal component is worth a substantial single slice of the grade — roughly a fifth to a quarter, depending on subject and cohort. Confirm the figure for your child's subject with the coordinator.

The failure patterns diverge sharply. Chemistry loses marks on sign conventions, equilibrium explanations that describe direction without naming a driver, and mechanism precision. Physics loses them on written explanation while the numerical work holds up, and on units and significant figures in a final line. Biology loses them on application: a process understood in the abstract and not transferred to an unfamiliar graph of a named organism.

The internal investigation is where the three converge, and where the most tutoring value sits. Marks there go on the quality of the research question, the control of variables, the treatment of uncertainty and the evaluation — not on the elegance of the result. A student whose investigation produced a disappointing result can still score well, and most do not know that. A tutor who says so early changes the whole shape of the student's work.

That is also where the academic-honesty boundary is tightest. A tutor may ask whether the data will answer the question, name the criterion a section is failing, and check that feedback was understood. A tutor may not design the method, write the evaluation or edit the document. IB Gram does not write, complete or supply internal assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays at any price, and the dated-draft record is built so that the student can demonstrate authorship.

sections.heading: Both mathematics routes, and the choice that sets two years
paragraphs: Mathematics is the only Diploma group where a family chooses between two different subjects rather than two levels of one, and the choice has consequences well beyond the Diploma. Analysis and Approaches is the calculus-and-proof route; Applications and Interpretation is the statistics-and-modelling route. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, which produces four distinct courses that are routinely discussed as though they were one.

University prerequisites are the part to get right, and they are not ours to assert. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while a wide range of other courses accept either. The only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific universities and courses your child is considering, including the UAE institutions, and to do it in DP1 rather than in DP2.

What a tutor can genuinely help with is the fit question. A student who enjoys structure, abstraction and proof will find Analysis and Approaches rewarding and Applications and Interpretation tedious. A student who thinks in contexts and data will find the reverse. Prior attainment matters less than that disposition, and a marked IGCSE paper read properly tells a specialist more about it than a preference expressed in a conversation.

Both routes lose marks in characteristic ways that a session fixes quickly. Analysis and Approaches students show method and drop accuracy: units, significant figures, exact forms. Applications and Interpretation students perform the test correctly and write the conclusion poorly, or use the calculator without documenting the screens that earn the marks. Neither of those is a mathematics problem, and neither takes long once named.

sections.heading: The essay subjects: what a band boundary actually looks like
paragraphs: English A, History, Economics, Business Management and Theory of Knowledge are all marked on the quality of an argument, and all five produce the same complaint from parents: the work looks fine and the grade does not move. The reason is nearly always structural rather than informational. The student knows enough; the answer is not doing the thing the band descriptor asks for.

The specific failures are remarkably consistent across Dubai cohorts. In English A, summary written where analysis was wanted. In History, a general process described with no named dates, figures or actors. In Economics, both sides of an evaluation listed with no judgement reached. In Business Management, theory applied without touching the stimulus. In Theory of Knowledge, a topic discussed rather than a knowledge question examined.

Each of those has a short, teachable remedy, and each is invisible to a tutor who only discusses content. The History remedy is a case-study bank built deliberately: named examples the student can deploy unaided under time. The Economics remedy is literally the final paragraph, written over and over until the judgement arrives naturally. The English A remedy is technique vocabulary, then a paragraph shape that earns marks.

The reason these subjects reward private teaching disproportionately is that classroom marking cannot be frequent enough. A teacher with a full timetable cannot mark and discuss one student's paragraph every week; a weekly session can. The marks here move through iteration on the student's own writing, and iteration is a time problem rather than a knowledge problem.

sections.heading: Internal assessment by subject: criteria, limits and the boundary
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and it is the single largest concentrated slice of the grade a student directly controls. It is also the part where a family is most likely to be offered help that would end a candidacy. Both facts argue for treating it as its own project with its own schedule rather than as homework that happens alongside everything else.

Word and page limits exist for most components, and they are published in the subject guides your school holds. They are revised between cohorts, which is why no tutoring site should present them as fixed facts — including this one. Ask the coordinator for the limits applying to your child's year, and then hold the student to them from the first draft rather than cutting 900 words out of a finished piece in the last fortnight.

The criteria are letters with mark allocations attached, and almost no competing page in this market names a single one. Reading them with the student is the highest-value hour available in coursework support, because it converts a vague instruction to improve into a specific instruction to address criterion C. It costs nothing and most students have never been walked through it line by line.

The boundary, stated once more because it matters: a tutor may ask whether the question is answerable with the available data, name the criterion a section is failing, and check that the feedback was understood. A tutor may not supply the question, write the method, rewrite sentences or proofread to completion. There are providers in this SERP selling completed internal assessments at a fixed price; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate.
