sections.heading: What cannot be taught remotely, and what can
paragraphs: An honest subject page has to name the limits of the format. Physical laboratory work cannot be done over video. A student standing at a bench measuring a reaction rate is doing something a screen cannot replicate, and the school owns that work, supervises it and assesses it. The same applies to a Visual Arts exhibition hung in a school space, and to any practical performance component.

What remains, however, is most of the marks. In the sciences, the investigation is marked on the research question, the control of variables, the treatment of uncertainty and the evaluation, not on manual technique. All four of those are desk work, and all four are easier to do on a shared screen where two people can annotate the same data table than leaning over one page.

In the arts, the assessed material is substantially documentation and critical commentary — the process portfolio, the comparative study, the artist's statement — and those respond to criterion feedback exactly as any written component does. A tutor cannot and should not touch the artwork; they can read the commentary against the criteria, which is where students most often lose marks.

Language orals are the case where video is arguably better than a room. The assessment is a recorded or live spoken interaction, frequently conducted through a screen in practice, and rehearsing it in the same medium removes a variable rather than adding one. The same is true of any component the school itself administers through a device.

The honest summary is that the format costs you the bench and gains you the specialist. For a student whose practical technique is the weak point, the school is the right source of help and the teacher is the right person to ask. For a student losing marks in the write-up, the design or the evaluation, the bench was never the problem.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for a visit against an online hour
paragraphs: The AED figures below were published by the providers named and read in October 2026. They are market rates rather than IB Gram's prices; our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and what a plan costs depends on subject, level and how many sessions it genuinely needs. The reason to publish any of this is that three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price and the two that do quote US dollars.

Read the table by subject brief rather than by band. For a Standard Level topic repair of three to five sessions, the middle band is appropriate and the premium band is a waste. For Higher Level coursework supervision across a term, the bottom band is a false economy, because a university student who has not read the subject guide will give confident feedback against criteria they have not seen.

The level premium is real and should be asked about directly. Several providers price Higher Level above Standard Level, and the justification is legitimate where the tutor has actually taught the extension content and the additional examined component. Where the same person teaches both at the same rate, that is also informative: it may mean honest pricing, or it may mean they treat the two as one course.

Four things to get in writing before any payment, at any band. Whether VAT is included. Whether marking and written feedback happen outside the session. The cancellation window. And whether the rate changes closer to the May session, which is asked surprisingly rarely and answered differently by different providers.

A final caution. A figure quoted with no currency, date or source is a sales number, not a market fact, and a self-asserted star rating is worth less than nothing. Every number in this table carries the name of whoever published it.

sections.heading: Choosing which subject to fund first
paragraphs: Almost no family can fund six subjects, and almost none should try. Six sessions a week leaves a Diploma student no evening in which to do the work that was set, which converts tuition into another timetable rather than a remedy. The realistic number is one or two subjects at a time, and choosing which is a decision worth making deliberately rather than by whichever report card was worst.

Three criteria usually settle it. First, distance from target in a Higher Level subject, because Higher Level marks are harder to recover late and carry more weight in a points total. Second, proximity of a coursework deadline, because an internal component is a fixed slice of the grade with a date attached and cannot be revisited afterwards. Third, whether the subject is a university prerequisite, which makes a grade there worth more than the same grade elsewhere.

What should not drive the choice is which subject the student dislikes most. Dislike is often a symptom of two identified gaps rather than a verdict on the subject, and a week-one diagnostic frequently shows that a student convinced they are hopeless at Chemistry is losing marks in exactly two places. That discovery does more for the following six weeks than a change of subject would.

Sequencing beats simultaneity. One subject supported properly for eight weeks, with marked work at each end, then a decision, then the next subject, uses the same money better than two subjects half-supported for sixteen. It also produces a cleaner answer at week eight, because only one variable changed.

If the honest conclusion is that two Higher Level subjects both need support now, say so and expect an honest answer about availability. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are genuinely tight, and we will give a date for the second subject rather than filling the slot with someone who teaches the subject group but not the level.

process.title: Name the subject and the level, separately
process.description: "Chemistry" and "Chemistry Higher Level" are different briefs with different specialists behind them. Say which level your child sits, and which examined component or internal piece of work the marks are going on, and the match gets considerably more accurate before anybody has been booked.

process.title: Send the marked script and the criterion list
process.description: One marked page shows a specialist where the marks went. If coursework is involved, the subject guide's criterion list — which your school holds — turns a general conversation into a specific one about which criterion the draft is not yet meeting. We do not distribute those documents ourselves.

process.title: Hear the honest level match
process.description: We will tell you whether the specialist has taught your child's level to a full cohort or only revision blocks, and what the real match time is. For Higher Level sciences and Computer Science in the Gulf evening window that figure is sometimes a week or two, and you get the figure rather than a reassurance.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the component
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details. Ask them to teach the component the script shows the loss in rather than a comfortable topic. You receive a written diagnosis naming the secure areas, the gaps and the first three sessions, and you keep it either way.

process.title: Fund one subject, measure it, then decide
process.description: Start with one subject at one session a week, with a baseline script at week one and a comparison on the same component at week six. Then decide whether to continue, change the plan, change the specialist, or move the budget to a second subject. Sequencing gives a cleaner answer than running two at once.

whyPoints.title: Level treated as a separate question from subject
whyPoints.description: Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra hours. We match on the level a tutor has actually taught to a full cohort, and we will say when the only honest answer is that nobody suitable is free this week.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from the student's own script
whyPoints.description: Chemistry loses marks on sign conventions and drivers, Physics on written reasoning, Biology on transfer to unfamiliar data. Those are different remedies with different session counts, and a marked page tells a specialist which one you have before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that is criterion feedback only
whyPoints.description: Feedback by criterion letter, on a separate sheet, with the student's dated drafts untouched. We do not write, complete, edit or proofread internal assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays at any price, and the record is built so authorship can be demonstrated.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the format cannot do
whyPoints.description: Bench practicals and arts exhibitions happen at school and belong to the school. We say so rather than implying otherwise, and we work on the design, the data treatment and the write-up, which is where most of those components' marks sit.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no school partnership, no star rating, no promise about a final grade. Every AED figure names the provider that published it and the month it was read.

whyPoints.title: Sequenced rather than stacked
whyPoints.description: One subject supported properly for eight weeks, with marked work at both ends, uses the same budget better than two subjects half-supported for sixteen. We will say so even when it means a smaller arrangement.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subject is the hardest to teach remotely?
faqs.answer: Visual Arts, by some distance, because the assessed work is physical and lives in a school space. Even there, the process portfolio and comparative study are written components that respond to criterion feedback like any other. The sciences are easier than families expect: the bench work belongs to the school, while the research question, variable control, uncertainty treatment and evaluation are desk work and are better done on a shared screen where two people can annotate the same data table.

faqs.question: How much of the Chemistry Higher Level grade sits in Paper 3?
faqs.answer: Confirm the exact weighting with your Diploma coordinator or the current subject guide, which your school holds and which is revised between cohorts — no tutoring site should state it as a fixed figure. What is stable is what the component rewards: handling unfamiliar data and evaluating a method rather than reproducing content. That makes it the part of the course where practice on seen material helps least, and where a session built around genuinely unfamiliar questions earns its fee fastest.

faqs.question: What does the Mathematics exploration get marked against?
faqs.answer: A set of criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, each with its own mark allocation. The exact letters and allocations are in the current subject guide your school holds. Reading them line by line with the student is the single highest-value hour in coursework support, because it converts a vague instruction to improve into a specific instruction to address one criterion. A tutor may give that feedback; a tutor may not write any part of the exploration.

faqs.question: Does English A Language and Literature need a different kind of tutor?
faqs.answer: It needs one who marks writing rather than discusses texts. The band boundary sits in close analysis of a specific technique in a specific line, and the usual shortfall is a well-written summary of what the passage is about. The remedy is technique vocabulary followed by a paragraph shape that earns marks, iterated on the student's own writing. That iteration is a time problem rather than a knowledge problem, which is exactly what a weekly one-to-one hour is good for.

faqs.question: How does a Physics practical write-up work if the lesson is online?
faqs.answer: The experiment happens at school, supervised and assessed there, and nobody should suggest otherwise. What a session works on is everything around it: whether the research question is answerable, whether the variables are genuinely controlled, how uncertainty is treated, and whether the evaluation identifies real limitations rather than generic ones. Those carry most of the available marks and are desk work. A shared annotation surface is better for them than two people leaning over one printed page.

faqs.question: Is Biology Higher Level mostly memory, or is that a myth?
faqs.answer: Largely a myth, and the belief itself causes the mark loss. Dubai cohorts typically arrive with recall intact and lose marks applying a known process to an unfamiliar context — a named organism in a graph nobody has seen. Higher Level raises how unfamiliar that context is. A student revising by re-reading notes is practising the half they can already do. The fix is unfamiliar data-based questions with the command term read aloud before the answer starts.

faqs.question: What separates a Higher Level History essay from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Sustained named detail across greater length under tighter time, plus the additional depth-study content and extra examined component at Higher Level. The band boundary at both levels is the same thing: an argument supported by dates, figures and actors rather than a general process described well. The remedy is a deliberately built case-study bank the student can deploy unaided, which takes five to eight sessions and outperforms more essay practice.

faqs.question: Which Economics Higher Level component carries the calculation marks?
faqs.answer: Higher Level adds quantitative content and an additional examined component built on unfamiliar data, so calculation appears in more than one place — check your child's subject guide for the current structure. The useful point is that calculation losses are accuracy losses rather than method losses, which is a two-to-four session fix. The harder and more valuable work is the evaluation paragraph, where both levels lose the top band by listing two sides and never reaching a judgement.

faqs.question: Does Visual Arts need a tutor at the table rather than on screen?
faqs.answer: For the artwork, yes, and the school is the right place for that. The assessed material also includes substantial written documentation and critical commentary, and those respond to criterion feedback exactly as any written component does. A tutor should never touch the artwork itself. Reading the commentary against the criteria is legitimate and is where students most often lose marks, because the writing is treated as an afterthought to the practical work.

faqs.question: How many taught hours does the IB expect at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: More than at Standard Level, with the figures set out in the IB's own programme documentation and the subject guides your school holds; ask the coordinator for the numbers applying to your child's cohort rather than taking them from a tutoring site. The practical consequence matters more than the figure: because Higher Level carries more taught content, a late start is harder to recover, which is why support that begins in DP1 does more per hour than the same support in DP2.

faqs.question: Can a student drop from Higher Level to Standard Level mid-course in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision belongs to the school rather than to a tutor or a parent. Schools set their own internal cut-off for level changes and there are registration requirements behind it, so the first step is asking the Diploma coordinator for the date. A tutor's input is useful on one narrow question: whether the difficulty is the extension content itself or two identifiable gaps in the shared core, because those point to different decisions.

faqs.question: Why is a home tutor search answered with an online lesson in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The phrase in the URL is what parents search, so it is answered honestly rather than avoided. What the format trades away is physical presence, which genuinely matters for a young or reluctant student. What it buys is a specialist matched on subject and level across the whole pool, and roughly sixty minutes of teaching in a 60-minute hour rather than thirty-five to forty.

faqs.question: What does a Language B Higher Level session work on each week?
faqs.answer: Text-type conventions for the writing paper, register and accuracy in speech, and the literary texts that Higher Level adds. The marks at both levels are lost on conventions rather than on vocabulary, which is why general conversation practice does less than a template per text type, practised against the criteria. The oral components are one of the few places where a pair genuinely helps, because another voice creates the unpredictability the assessment depends on.

faqs.question: Which subjects most often need help in the first term of DP1?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, overwhelmingly, in both routes and at both levels, because the step up from IGCSE algebra arrives immediately and nothing else in the timetable waits for it. After that, Chemistry, because equilibrium and energetics appear early and punish shallow understanding. Students arriving from the Middle Years Programme often have a specific algebraic fluency gap created by the Year 11 personal project, which is cheap to close in DP1 and expensive to ignore until DP2.

faqs.question: Does Computer Science Higher Level suit online teaching?
faqs.answer: Unusually well, since the work is already on a screen. Pseudocode can be written on a shared surface with both people editing, and the marks go on initialisation and loop boundaries rather than on conceptual understanding, which is easier to catch when the code is visible to both. The practical issue is supply rather than format: Higher Level Computer Science is among the thinnest specialisms across the region, so ask about availability a term before the component becomes urgent.

faqs.question: What if both of our child's weakest subjects are at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Sequence them rather than running both. One subject supported properly for eight weeks, with a baseline script and a comparison on the same component, produces a clean answer because only one variable changed. Two half-supported subjects over sixteen weeks produce an argument. If both genuinely cannot wait, expect an honest availability answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf window are tight, and we will give a date rather than a substitute.

dubai/best-ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the component, not the postcode
dubai/best-ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are searching for the best IB home tutor in Dubai, the useful first move is to write down the subject, the level and the component the last marked script shows the loss in. Send that script, book the free trial lesson with no card details taken, and ask the specialist to teach the difficult component rather than a comfortable topic. You keep the written diagnosis either way. Then fund one subject properly for eight weeks, compare two marked scripts on the same component, and decide from there.

intro.heading: Nobody can sell you the best tutor, so price the work instead
paragraphs: No platform can honestly claim to supply the best IB IGCSE tutor in Dubai, and any page that does is describing its marketing rather than its teaching. Best is a fit judgement: the right board, the right level, the right failure mode, at a time your child can concentrate, for a price that survives twenty sessions rather than two. What can be published honestly is the thing this market hides. Of six competitor pages fetched and read in October 2026, three published no price at all, and two of the remaining pages quoted US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in.

So the spine of this page is cost. Not our cost, because a rate quoted before the subject and level are known is a number pulled from the air. The market's cost, in dirhams, tier by tier, with the provider who published each figure named beside it and the date it was read. That gives you something a testimonial cannot: a range to test a quote against. If a tutor asks AED 500 an hour for IGCSE Core maths, the table further down tells you that sits two tiers above the published band for that work, and you can ask why.

The second half of the question is what moves a number inside those bands, and the answers are specific. Level moves it: Diploma Higher Level pays more than IGCSE Core everywhere in this market. Proximity to the series moves it, because January, April and the fortnight before a November sitting are the tightest weeks in the Dubai calendar. Session length moves it, usually in the buyer's favour, since a 90-minute slot rarely costs one and a half times a 60-minute one. Coursework supervision moves it, because reading an Internal Assessment against criterion descriptors is slower and more skilled work than teaching a topic.

Then there is the part of the price that is not teaching at all. Travel sits inside the hourly rate of any in-home visit, which is why that band starts higher and widens fastest. Platform fees and currency conversion sit inside a marketplace rate. Admin and materials charges sit outside some agency rates and are billed later. A tuition centre's per-student rate looks cheap until you notice it has removed the diagnostic that makes a session targeted. None of that is dishonest, but it is rarely on the page where the headline rate appears.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and does not send a tutor to any UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is relevant to cost as well as to logistics: with no travel to fund and no catchment to respect, the tutor is chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the drive, and the money buys teaching time instead of a car on Al Khail Road. The first lesson is free, with no card required, and it runs as a diagnostic on a real past paper.

dubai/best-ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Price in this market tracks programme and level more closely than it tracks anything else, including experience. Here is what each programme demands of a tutor, and why that shows up in a quote.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with no external examination, assessed continuously and reported against learner-profile attributes. Tutoring here is about literacy, numeracy fluency and English language support, and it sits at the bottom of every published rate band because the subject knowledge required is broad rather than deep. Session length is usually 45 to 60 minutes, because attention rather than content sets the limit.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP demand concentrates on English language acquisition for families arriving mid-year and on numeracy for children moving from a different curriculum. Published budget bands in the emirate start around AED 45 an hour online, and parents should expect the honest answer that weekly tutoring at this stage is often less useful than reading aloud at home for twenty minutes a day.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Because most MYP subjects carry no external paper, tutoring tends to be about criterion literacy: understanding what an achievement level 7-8 descriptor actually asks for, and producing work that meets it rather than work that is simply correct.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai continuum schools run MYP through to Year 11, and the pricing conversation here is usually about the Personal Project and the MYP 5 ePortfolios, which land in the same term. Mid-band rates apply. The expensive mistake families make is buying topic teaching when the problem is criterion interpretation, which takes fewer sessions and a different kind of tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level adds content and, in the sciences, a third paper. Internal Assessment is teacher-marked against criteria and moderated by the IB, which is why supervision work is priced above topic teaching almost everywhere in this market.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Higher Level sits at the top of the published Dubai bands, with specialist figures from AED 200 to 450 and above, and a premium tier beyond that. Demand concentrates in Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and Economics, and it peaks in the weeks before the May session Dubai schools enter candidates for. Confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE, both boards
programmes.description: Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry, and Pearson Edexcel codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C or 5; Pearson offers a modular route in some subjects. Tier and route both change how many sessions a plan needs, which is the real driver of total cost.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE is the volume market in Dubai, where British-curriculum schools dominate by enrolment and most students sit IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. Extended-tier work prices above Core in every published band. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so take dates from the school's exams officer.

dubai/best-ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates vary by subject as well as by level, and not always in the direction parents expect. These are the subjects Dubai families ask about most, with what makes each one cheap or expensive to support well.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most consistently expensive subject in this market at Higher Level, because the supply of tutors who can teach Paper 3 and supervise an Exploration is genuinely thin. Standard Level costs less and needs fewer sessions. A tutor who cannot talk about the Exploration criteria is quoting for half the job.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Priced slightly below Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and similarly at Standard Level. The hidden cost is calculator fluency: a student who cannot drive a graphic display calculator confidently burns sessions on button sequences rather than on statistics, and that is cheaper to fix early.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The highest-volume subject in Dubai tutoring, so supply is good and published rates sit in the middle bands. Extended prices above Core. Total cost depends mainly on whether the plan starts in Year 10 or in January of Year 11, because the second scenario needs twice the weekly contact for a smaller result.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level physics attracts specialist rates because the mathematics inside it defeats students who are coping with the concepts. Supervision of the Internal Assessment is the part that pushes a quote up, since a measurable research question with controlled uncertainty takes several reads to shape.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Cheaper than physics or chemistry to support, because the content is accessible and most lost marks come from command-term technique rather than from misunderstanding. A short block of six to eight sessions, built on marked papers, is usually a better buy here than a full year of weekly contact.

subjects.name: IB Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics is scarce in Dubai outside the central corridor, which raises the rate. The three commentaries and Paper 3 quantitative work are the specialist elements. Group formats work less badly here than in mathematics, since diagram technique can genuinely be taught to three students at once.

subjects.name: IB Business Management
subjects.description: Mid-band pricing, with the cost concentrated in the Higher Level business research project rather than in the taught content. Case-study technique and command-term discipline are the recoverable marks, and both respond to a short marked-paper block rather than to open-ended weekly support.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: One of the better-value subjects to tutor in Dubai, because supply is reasonable and the mark scheme is highly teachable. Students lose marks by writing general business sense instead of applying a named concept to the case, which is a technique problem with a short fix.

subjects.name: IB English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Priced in the middle, with the cost in marking time rather than in contact time. Paper 1 unseen analysis improves fastest with written feedback on timed responses, so ask whether marking is inside the hourly rate or billed separately, because practice in this subject is handled by different providers differently.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside any licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools, and consistently underpriced relative to how hard it is to staff well. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, so support must match the stream the school placed the child in.

sections.heading: What best can honestly mean, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages read for this market in October 2026 describe themselves in superlatives and publish no price. Two publish a self-asserted star rating. One asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. That combination is worth naming, because it tells you where the pressure in this market sits: on persuasion rather than on specification.

A tutor can be the right choice for your child on four grounds that are checkable before you pay. They have taught the exact board and syllabus code your child is entered for. They can describe the failure mode in your child's work after reading one marked paper, rather than after a term of acquaintance. They are available at a time your child can actually concentrate, which in Dubai means after the school run and before collapse. And the rate sits inside the published band for that level of work, so the plan survives twenty sessions rather than four.

None of those four is a claim about being the finest tutor in the emirate, and none of them needs a star rating to verify. They are specification, and specification is what this page substitutes for superlatives. A provider that will not give you a straight answer on board experience, availability and rate is not withholding a trade secret; it is managing a conversation it would rather you did not start.

The rest of this page is built to be used in that conversation. Market bands to test a quote against, the variables that legitimately move a number, the permit question in a form you can actually ask, and a scorecard for the first hour.

sections.heading: The Dubai rate card, in dirhams, with sources
paragraphs: Here is the thing this market does not publish. The bands below were assembled from competitor pages read in October 2026 and from a 2026 Dubai tutoring rate table, and each row names who published the figure. They are market rates and not an IB Gram price list, and they are hourly unless the row says otherwise.

Read them as tiers of work rather than as a quality ladder. The budget band is largely university students and generalists, and for homework supervision or consolidation at primary level that is a sensible purchase rather than a compromise. The qualified-subject-tutor band is where most IGCSE work sits. The specialist band is Diploma Higher Level, Extended-tier sciences and coursework supervision. The premium band is small, badge-driven, and the one where a parent should ask hardest what the extra money buys.

The in-home column behaves differently from the others and it is worth understanding why. Travel is inside that rate, not beside it, which is why the band both starts higher and runs wider. A tutor crossing Dubai at 4pm for a 60-minute session is selling ninety minutes of their day, and prices accordingly. That is a rational charge rather than a markup, and it is the mechanical reason in-home sits at AED 180 to 500 while a comparable online band sits at AED 150 to 300.

Monthly packages are the other shape visible in this market, and they need reading carefully. An advertised AED 799 per month for eight sessions works out near AED 100 a session, which places it in the budget band regardless of how it is described. In-home monthly packages seen in the emirate run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Dividing the package by the hours before comparing it is the whole trick.

sections.heading: What actually moves a quote inside those bands
paragraphs: Six variables explain almost every difference between two quotes for apparently the same work, and only one of them is the tutor's reputation. Knowing them turns a negotiation into a specification.

Level is the strongest. Diploma Higher Level prices above Standard Level, which prices above Extended-tier IGCSE, which prices above Core. That ordering holds across every published band in this market and it reflects supply rather than effort: the number of people in or reachable from Dubai who can teach Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3 is small, and the number who can also supervise an Exploration is smaller. Proximity to the exam series is the second. January, April and the fortnight before a November sitting are when demand peaks, and a slot booked in September costs what a slot booked in September costs.

Session length usually works in the buyer's favour, since a 90-minute booking rarely costs one and a half times the 60-minute rate, and for Higher Level work it wastes less time on re-entry to a topic. Coursework supervision works against it, because reading a draft against criterion descriptors and writing useful feedback takes longer than the session it is attached to. Group size reduces the per-student rate sharply and removes the individual diagnostic, which is a genuine trade rather than a free saving. And the badge, examiner status or a named qualification, moves the rate most and justifies it least, which the last section of this page deals with squarely.

What should not move a quote: how far the tutor lives from you, if the lesson is online; how urgent you sound; or how many subjects you buy, unless the provider says explicitly that a multi-subject rate exists. Any of those three appearing in a quote is worth one direct question.

sections.heading: Provider models compared on what the rate excludes
paragraphs: Every page in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms. That comparison is worthless because the straw man has no permit route, no replacement policy and no published exclusions. Comparing models instead of brands is both more useful and more honest, so the table below does that: agency, marketplace, freelance, centre, school support, and this platform.

The columns chosen are the ones that cost money later. The permit route matters because private tutoring in the UAE is regulated and an individual needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, while a centre with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different instrument entirely. The replacement policy matters because a mismatched tutor in week three is a predictable event, and whether you restart the search or inherit a swap with the diagnostic carried over is worth real money. Exclusions matter because travel, materials, admin and marking are inside some rates and outside others.

The marketplace row deserves a note. Marketplaces quote in dollars, convert at their own rate, and rarely verify a UAE permit, which leaves the parent holding both the currency risk and the compliance question. That is not an argument against marketplaces; it is an argument for reading the invoice before the review score.

IB Gram's own row is deliberately plain. Lessons are online and one-to-one, no UAE premises exist and none is claimed, no regulator approval is held or implied, the trial lesson carries no charge and no card, and the rate is quoted at consultation once board, level and subject are known.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated and most pages in this market never mention it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories named in the official guidance include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a parent comparing quotes. First, nobody can charge you for a permit, because the permit is free, so a fee presented as a licensing cost is not one. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears here.

A separate rule applies to school staff. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics framework for private and charter school staff has been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring service to students affiliated with the holder's school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but take the practical point: your child's own class teacher, privately and for a fee, is the arrangement most likely to create a problem for everyone involved.

IB Gram holds no regulator permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. The table gives you the question to ask of any provider, including this one.

sections.heading: Scoring the first hour, so the trial is evidence
paragraphs: A trial lesson is the cheapest due diligence available, and most families spend it being reassured. Treated as an assessment instead, one hour tells you more than any rating. The table gives five things to watch, what a weak version looks like, what a strong version looks like, and why each predicts whether the money will be well spent.

The single most informative moment is what the tutor does with a marked paper. A tutor who reads a script and says your child needs to work on chemistry has told you nothing you did not know. A tutor who says four of the lost marks came from explain questions answered as describe questions, and that the fix is a command-term drill rather than a content re-teach, has diagnosed something. That distinction appears inside ten minutes and it predicts the next twenty sessions.

The second is whether the tutor asks for the syllabus code before teaching anything. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called mathematics and differ in tiering, formula provision and paper structure. A tutor who begins without establishing which one your child sits is going to teach competently and miss the technique, which is where the recoverable marks are.

The third is the honest no. A tutor who says the Higher Level Mathematics Exploration is outside their experience and suggests a colleague has just saved you a term. Availability transparency is worth more than breadth, and no competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

sections.heading: Price per hour against price per mark
paragraphs: Hourly rate is the wrong unit for this purchase and everyone uses it anyway. What a family is actually buying is mark movement against a fixed deadline, and two quotes with the same hourly rate can differ by a factor of three on that measure.

Consider two plausible Dubai plans for the same IGCSE Extended student. Plan A is thirty weekly sessions across the year at the mid band, with no diagnostic, no marking and content covered in syllabus order. Plan B is twelve sessions: a timed paper first, six weeks on the two topics the paper exposed, command-term drills throughout, a second identical paper at week ten. Plan A costs roughly two and a half times as much and may move fewer marks, because syllabus order is not the order your child's marks are leaking in.

This is why the diagnostic, the marking and the retest are not extras in a tutoring plan; they are the measurement that makes the spend accountable. Without them you are buying attendance. With them, at week ten, you can read two marked papers side by side and make a decision that is not a feeling. Continue, change tutor, change tier expectation, or stop, and all four are legitimate.

The corollary is a budgeting rule that saves Dubai families real money. Buy a short, measured block first. If the block moves marks, extend it. If it does not, the information cost you twelve sessions rather than a year, and you still hold two marked papers that any other tutor can work from.

sections.heading: What a premium rate should buy, and what it should not
paragraphs: The top of this market is badge-driven. Examiner status is the most common badge, and it is the one that needs the most care, from the provider and from the parent. A tutor who currently marks for a board brings genuine familiarity with how a mark scheme is applied, and that is worth paying for where it can be evidenced. It does not bring access to papers, to boundaries or to marking in progress, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation rather than raise the rate.

IB Gram does not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners unless current status can be evidenced, and does not use examiner status to imply access to assessment material. The honest version of the claim is narrow: experience of applying a published mark scheme consistently, which shows up in how a script comes back annotated.

Two other things a premium rate legitimately buys. Scarcity, where the subject and level genuinely have few capable teachers, and Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3 with Exploration supervision is the clearest example in Dubai. And marking volume, where the provider is reading and annotating substantial written work between sessions, which is real labour sitting outside the contact hour.

What a premium rate never buys is an outcome. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place, and any refund promise tied to a score needs its exact terms on the same page as the promise. Equally, a self-published star rating is not evidence: competitor pages in this market show different ratings and review counts in the same document, which is a reason to discount both. Ask instead for the four checkable things at the top of this page, and for a number you can set against the bands in the rate table.

sections.heading: Tuition cost against the rest of a Dubai school budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought out of the same household budget as school fees, transport and activities, and it competes with them. Dubai gives that comparison an unusually clean anchor this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. A flat fee year is the context in which a weekly session is affordable or not.

The supply side is moving too. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. More Diploma places means more Diploma tutoring demand in the same labour market, which is the mechanism that tightens Higher Level availability in the weeks before a session.

Set against that, the arithmetic of a tutoring plan is straightforward once the hours are visible. One hour a week across a term is twelve hours. The mid band of the 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, and the specialist exam-year band at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. A twelve-session measured block at the qualified-tutor band sits well below a year of weekly attendance at the same rate, which is the budgeting point the per-hour framing hides.

One figure deliberately absent from this page is an IB Gram price. The trial lesson is free with no card required, and a rate is quoted in the consultation once the board, level, subject and session length are known. A number published without those four attached is a marketing figure, not a quote, and this market has enough of those.

A quote against a subject name is not, which is why most tutoring comparisons collapse at the second email.

process.description: Put the number beside the rate table above. If it sits two tiers above the band for that work, ask what the extra buys. If it sits below the band, ask who is teaching and at what level of experience. Either answer is useful; the absence of one is the most useful of all.

For a centre, ask for the KHDA Educational Services Permit number and check it against KHDA's own listing.

Read the two scripts side by side and choose: continue, change tutor, adjust the tier expectation, or stop. The information costs twelve sessions instead of a year, and the papers remain useful to anyone.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay a tutor in Dubai in dirhams?
faqs.answer: The published bands read in October 2026 run from AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 and above at the premium end. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with one provider publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE work sits at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are market figures from other providers, not an IB Gram price list, and a rate here is quoted once board, level and subject are known.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutors quote AED 150 and AED 450 for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually because the work is not actually the same. Level accounts for most of it: Diploma Higher Level prices above Standard Level, which prices above Extended-tier IGCSE, which prices above Core. Coursework supervision prices above topic teaching, because reading a draft against criterion descriptors is slower work. Travel sits inside any in-home rate. Marking may be inside the hour or billed separately. Beyond those, the gap is usually a badge rather than a difference in the teaching, and the right response is a direct question about what the extra money is buying.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate actually buy a better grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and no rate buys a grade at all. A premium rate legitimately covers two things: genuine scarcity, where few people can teach the level, and marking labour sitting outside the contact hour. It does not cover access to papers, boundaries or marking in progress, and any implication that it does should end the conversation. The measure that matters is mark movement on identical question types across a measured block, which costs the same to generate at AED 180 as at AED 500. Buy the short measured block first and let the two scripts decide.

faqs.question: What hidden costs should I check before booking a tutoring package in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Six. Whether marking and feedback time sit inside the hourly rate or are billed on top. Whether travel is inside an in-home rate or added per visit. Whether a minimum session length applies, which is common for the outer communities. How a cancelled or shortened session is charged, especially in apartment buildings with access procedures. Whether materials or administration fees exist. And whether the advertised monthly package divides out to the rate you think it does, since AED 799 for eight sessions is near AED 100 a session whatever the headline suggests.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class cheaper than one-to-one across a term?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly yes: centre group rates in this market run roughly AED 60 to 200 per student against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online one-to-one tutor. Across a term the comparison is less obvious, because the group format removes the individual diagnostic and the marked-paper cycle that make a session targeted. For diagram technique, command terms and shared content gaps, a group works genuinely well. For a student losing marks in a pattern nobody has identified yet, it buys attendance. A centre with premises also needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is worth asking to see.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who says they are an examiner?
faqs.answer: Only where the status can be evidenced and only for what it actually provides. Current marking experience brings real familiarity with how a mark scheme is applied, and that shows up in how a script comes back annotated. It does not bring access to papers, grade boundaries or marking in progress, and nobody should imply that it does. IB Gram does not describe a tutor as an IB or Cambridge examiner without evidence of current status. If a quote rests mainly on the badge, ask what the annotation on a marked script will look like, and judge that instead.

faqs.question: How do I check that a Dubai tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it, and ask when it was issued. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because the permit costs nothing, there is no commercial reason for vagueness. For a centre with premises, ask for the KHDA Educational Services Permit number instead and check KHDA's own listing.

faqs.question: Will I pay more if I start looking for a tutor in January?
faqs.answer: Rates in the published bands tend to hold, but availability collapses and that has the same effect on what a family ends up paying. January, April and the fortnight before a November sitting are the tightest weeks in this market. The 5pm to 7pm slots go first, Higher Level science and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches tutors go first within that, and what remains is either an inconvenient time or a more expensive tier. Booking a protected weekly slot in September costs the same as booking one in January and is materially easier to get.

faqs.question: Does a 90-minute session cost less per hour than a 60-minute one?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and for Higher Level work it is also better teaching. A 90-minute booking rarely costs one and a half times the hourly rate in this market, and it wastes less time re-entering a topic, which matters when the content is cumulative. The exception is younger students, where attention rather than content sets the limit and 45 to 60 minutes is the right length regardless of the arithmetic. For in-home arrangements in outer Dubai communities, a 90-minute minimum is often imposed anyway, because a tutor will not cross the city for an hour.

faqs.question: What does coursework supervision cost compared with topic teaching?
faqs.answer: More, across every model in this market, and for a defensible reason. Reading an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay draft against criterion descriptors and writing feedback that names the criterion letter and the current band takes longer than the session it attaches to, and the skill is narrower. Supervision is usually sold as a block rather than monthly. What you should not be paying for is text: the student is the sole author under IB rules, so no tutor supplies sentences, finishes a draft or provides a model answer to the same research question.

faqs.question: How many weeks should I commit to before judging value for money?
faqs.answer: Twelve, structured so the judgement is possible. A timed past paper in week one before any teaching, six weeks on whatever that paper exposed, command-term and arithmetic drills throughout, and an identical paper around week ten. Then read the two marked scripts side by side. Anything shorter cannot show movement on the same question types; anything longer delays a decision you could already have made. If nothing has moved by week ten, that is information worth having, and it cost twelve sessions rather than a year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children to bring the cost down?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on whether they are at the same board, level and stage. Two children sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended in the same year group can share sessions productively, and the per-student rate falls to something near the group band. A Year 10 IGCSE student and a Diploma Higher Level student cannot share anything useful, and paying one tutor for a combined hour means each child gets half a session. Ask for a split arrangement instead: separate shorter sessions with the same tutor, which keeps the diagnostic intact for both.

faqs.question: Does the quoted tutoring rate include VAT in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because the treatment is not something this page will state as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation. The practical questions are narrow and answerable: is the figure you were quoted the figure you will be charged, is any tax shown separately on the invoice, and does the provider hold a tax registration number. A provider who cannot answer those three about their own invoice is telling you something about their administration. IB Gram quotes a rate at consultation and the quoted figure is the figure invoiced.

faqs.question: What should I get in writing before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Five things, and all five are reasonable to ask for. The rate, the session length, and whether marking time sits inside or outside it. The cancellation and rescheduling terms, including how a shortened session is treated. Which board and syllabus code the tutor is teaching to. What the first three sessions will cover, based on the diagnostic. And the replacement position if the match does not work in week three. None of that requires a contract; an email is fine. What matters is that it exists before money moves, not after.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not publish its own price on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a number without the board, level, subject and session length attached is a marketing figure rather than a quote, and this market already has plenty of those. What is published here instead is the thing a parent can actually use: the market bands in dirhams with each publisher named, the variables that move a number inside them, and the questions worth asking. The trial lesson is free with no card required, and the rate is quoted in the consultation once the specification exists. That order round makes the quote mean something.

dubai/best-ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The specialists below each teach a named subject at a named level and work from your child's own marked papers. Ask for a trial on the component that is costing marks, and watch the screen mechanics described further down this page while it runs.

intro.heading: The format is the product, so examine the format
paragraphs: Online tutoring is described in brochures as though the delivery were incidental — the same lesson, through a screen. It is not incidental. A live lesson has a shared surface, a pointer, a scanned script, a calculator that either can or cannot be seen, an audio channel that either carries a sixteen-year-old's quiet voice or does not, and a recording policy. Each of those is a design decision, and the difference between a good online hour and a poor one lies almost entirely in them.

Most parents judge an online tutor on the same signals they would use for a visiting one: manner, qualifications, price. Those matter, and they do not distinguish between two providers whose lessons look identical in a brochure and completely different on screen. One has the student writing for forty minutes on a surface both people can annotate. The other has a tutor screen-sharing worked solutions while a muted teenager watches. The second is a video lecture with an audience of one.

So this page is about the mechanics. What is on screen minute by minute. What each Diploma subject specifically needs visible — a data booklet, a documented calculator screen, a scanned handwritten page, a diagram drawn live. How a handwritten script actually gets marked when nobody can hold the paper. What the Dubai household needs at its end, which is less than most providers imply and more specific than a fast connection.

It also covers two things the market tends to skip. The first is recording: whether sessions are recorded, who holds the file, and what happens to it. The second is data about a child, which in the UAE sits under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. A provider that cannot tell you what it collects, why, and how to have it deleted is asking for information about a minor without a stated purpose.

On what we are, plainly. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we have no premises in the UAE. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every session described here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

That last point is a limitation and should read as one. If your child needs an adult in the room to begin work at all, the format is wrong for them and no amount of good screen design fixes it. For a Diploma student who will sit down and work, the mechanics below are what separate an hour that moves marks from an hour that passes pleasantly.

dubai/best-ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: What needs to be visible on screen changes completely between IB programmes, because what is being assessed changes. The notes below describe the practical demand each one puts on an online lesson.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most screen-friendly of the four, because nearly everything assessed on paper can be reproduced on a shared surface: scanned scripts, annotated data, live diagrams, documented calculator screens. The exception is physical practical technique, which belongs to the school. Sessions here need two usable surfaces, one for the question and one for the student's working.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students sit the May session and are the group most likely to be travelling in term time, between emirates or abroad. A fixed online slot survives that in a way a visiting arrangement does not, which matters most in DP2 when the weeks before the papers cannot be rescheduled.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Works well on screen with one adjustment: criterion descriptors should be visible beside the student's own work rather than described. Having the band wording in one pane and the paragraph in another is the whole lesson for many MYP students, and it is easier on a screen than on a kitchen table covered in paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the continuum set the personal project in Year 11, and much of its documentation is already digital. That makes criterion feedback on a shared document natural, provided the student's file stays the student's own and the tutor's comments are kept separate from it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The hardest stage to deliver well on screen, and the one where an adult nearby matters most. Sessions need to be shorter, more visual, and built around a task the child physically does rather than watches. A primary session that becomes a video call with a talking adult has already failed.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any such lesson, which is a sensible frame for primary tuition length too. Arabic as an additional language, the commonest primary request in Dubai, needs handwriting practice on paper rather than on a screen.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma courses inside it behave exactly as they do in the full Diploma, so the screen requirements are identical. The career-related units are provider-assessed and frequently involve placement or project evidence that no tutor should be handling, so the honest scope of an online session is the Diploma subjects.
programmes.countryNote: With very few Dubai schools licensing the programme, online matching is often the only way to find anyone who has taught the relevant Diploma courses alongside it. The reflective project criteria should come from the school's coordinator rather than from a tutoring provider's interpretation.

dubai/best-ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below, what each subject actually needs visible during a session, and what goes wrong when it is missing. This is the most practical filter available for an online tutor, because a provider whose platform cannot show the thing the subject needs cannot teach the subject properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs a surface where the student writes line by line and the tutor annotates alongside. Without it the tutor writes the solution and the student copies, which produces the feeling of understanding and no method marks in the examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Needs the calculator screen visible, because documented screens earn marks and undocumented ones lose them. A second camera or a screenshot works; a tutor who never asks to see the calculator is not teaching this course's assessment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs the data booklet in one pane and a drawing surface in the other for mechanisms, with the student adding the next arrow rather than watching one appear. Energetics work needs the sign convention written out, not described aloud.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Needs the formula booklet visible and space for a diagram, plus a text pane for written answers. The written half of Paper 2 is where Dubai cohorts lose marks, and it cannot be practised by watching someone else's reasoning.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Needs graphs and data tables that both people can mark up at once. Annotating an unfamiliar graph together is the actual lesson; reading it aloud is not. A printer at the student's end helps, and a stylus does the same job.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Needs a blank drawing surface, because diagrams have to be drawn by the student repeatedly rather than displayed. The marks come from the diagram being referenced in the prose, so both have to be visible side by side.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Needs the case-study extract on screen with highlighting, because application marks come from touching the stimulus. A session conducted without the case material in front of both people teaches theory and loses the marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Needs the text visible with live annotation in the margins, and a pane for the student's paragraph. Close analysis of two lines is the skill; a scrolled text with no annotation turns the session into a discussion of themes.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Needs audio quality above everything else, because the oral components depend on hearing register and accuracy. Headphones with a microphone matter more here than screen resolution, and a quiet room matters more than either.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Needs the source extract on screen and a growing case-study document the student owns and adds to each week. The bank is the deliverable; a session that produces only discussion leaves nothing to revise from.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The most natural fit of any subject, since the work is already on a screen. Pseudocode can be edited by both people, which makes loop boundaries and initialisation visible exactly where the marks are lost.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Needs almost nothing technically and one uninterrupted hour, which is scarcer. The useful artefact is a shared document where knowledge questions are drafted and rewritten, with tutor comments kept separate from the student's own text.

sections.heading: What a live online IB lesson looks like, minute by minute
paragraphs: A good online hour has a shape, and watching for it during a trial lesson tells you more than any amount of discussion about teaching philosophy. The first few minutes should be the tutor stating what the marked script showed and what the hour will target, which is only possible if the script was read beforehand. If those minutes are spent finding out what your child is studying, the information you supplied in writing was not read.

The bulk of the hour should have the student writing. On a shared annotation surface this is visible and easy to check: whose cursor is moving, whose handwriting is appearing. The tutor's job during that stretch is to ask about what has just been written — why that line, what the next step assumes, what the command term was asking for. A tutor writing a worked solution for a muted student to copy has produced a video lecture.

The last ten minutes should produce two things: a numbered list of work for the week, in a stated order, and a note of what will be marked before the next session. The list is what converts intention into an appointment with the material. "Keep practising" is where a Dubai student's week disappears, because there are three internal deadlines competing for the same evening.

After the hour, a written note should arrive within a day, naming the syllabus statements touched, the marks earned per question, the error category behind each loss and the work set. That note is the only part of the lesson that still exists at week six, which is why its specificity matters more than how the session felt at the time.
The table below sets out that shape with the thing to watch at each stage. It works as a checklist during a trial lesson with any provider, including this one.

sections.heading: Marking a handwritten script when nobody can hold the paper
paragraphs: This is the single most practical question about online tuition in a subject where answers are written by hand, and most providers never address it. The workable method is dull and effective: the student completes a timed question on paper, photographs or scans each page with a phone, and sends it before the session. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, annotates the images, and returns them with the session note.

Three details make the difference between that working and not. The photograph must be taken straight on in reasonable light, because a skewed image of pencil working is genuinely unreadable and the student will conclude the method does not work. A free scanning app that flattens and sharpens the page solves it permanently. Second, pages must be numbered, because an unnumbered set of six images arrives in an unpredictable order.

Third and most importantly, the marking must happen before the session rather than during it. A tutor reading a script in silence while a sixteen-year-old watches is spending ten to fifteen minutes of a paid hour on something that could have been done the night before. Ask any provider directly where marking happens. The answer is a reliable signal, and it changes the useful cost of the hour more than the hourly rate does.

What comes back should be specific enough to act on without the tutor present. Marks shown per question with the scheme's own language, each loss labelled by category — method, accuracy, command term or concept — and a note of which of those the following week will target. A tick-and-cross script tells a student they were wrong, which they already knew.

Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are the copyright of the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and schools hold licences for them. We do not host or distribute any of those documents. The right route is your child's teacher or the school's own resource platform, and a provider offering them as downloads is doing something it should not.

sections.heading: What each subject needs visible, and what breaks without it
paragraphs: A platform that cannot display the thing a subject is assessed on cannot teach that subject properly, however good the tutor is. This is where online provision varies most and is discussed least, because it is easier to sell a general promise about interactive learning than to say whether a calculator screen can be seen.

The sharpest example is Applications and Interpretation. Marks there depend partly on documented calculator work, so a session in which the calculator is never visible is a session that cannot address a real source of lost marks. The fix is trivial — a phone propped as a second camera, or screenshots sent before the lesson — but it has to be somebody's deliberate decision.

The second sharp example is English A. The assessment is close analysis of a specific technique in a specific line, which requires the text on screen with live annotation in the margins and the student's paragraph visible beside it. A session where the text is scrolled through and discussed becomes a conversation about themes, which is pleasant and does not move Paper 1 marks.

Economics and Chemistry both need a blank drawing surface used by the student rather than by the tutor. A diagram the student has watched being drawn is not a diagram they can draw under time, and a mechanism arrow the tutor placed is not an arrow the student understands. The test in a trial lesson is simply whose hand draws it.

sections.heading: The Dubai household setup, in about fifteen minutes
paragraphs: Providers tend to ask for a fast connection and leave it there, which misses most of what actually goes wrong. In Dubai the recurring problems are router distance in large villas, evening contention in dense towers, west-facing glare between about four and six, hard-surfaced rooms that echo, and air-conditioning noise directly above the desk. None of those is a bandwidth problem and none needs a new package.

Audio matters more than video, and it is the one families underinvest in. A lesson works if the tutor can hear a quiet sixteen-year-old thinking aloud; it fails if the student has to raise their voice over a compressor, because they will stop talking instead. Headphones with a microphone cost very little and resolve echo, household noise and the self-consciousness of being overheard in one purchase.

Screen area is the second thing worth attention. A subject needing a question in one pane and working in another is cramped on a phone and uncomfortable on a small laptop. A second monitor, an external keyboard, or simply a tablet beside the laptop for the question paper makes a visible difference in subjects where two things must be read together.

Then the household rules, which are not technical. One device for the lesson, notifications off, the question paper on paper rather than in a tab behind the call, and a slot chosen when the adult who shares the bandwidth is not on a call. In Internet City, Media City and Business Bay households that last point is the single most common cause of a session that keeps being rescheduled.
The table is the checklist. It takes about fifteen minutes to work through once, and it prevents most of the problems that get blamed on the tutor or on online learning in general.

sections.heading: Recordings, and what is held about a child
paragraphs: Two questions worth asking before a first session, and worth getting answered in writing. Is the lesson recorded, and what personal information about your child is held. Both are reasonable, both are quick to answer honestly, and the quality of the answer is informative in itself.

Our position on recording is that it happens if you ask for it and not otherwise, and that the file belongs to the family. Recordings are genuinely useful for some students — a Language B oral rehearsal, a difficult derivation to revisit — and they are also a store of video of a minor, which is not something to create by default. A provider that records every session automatically should be able to say where the files are held and for how long.

On data, the relevant UAE framework is Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. What a matching service actually needs is narrow: the student's name, year group, school, subject, level, and whatever marked work you choose to send. What it does not need before a trial lesson is a photograph, a full academic history, a copy of a report card or a passport. A form asking for those without a stated purpose is collecting more than the job requires.

You should be able to ask what is held and ask for it to be deleted, and a privacy link should be on every page rather than buried in a sign-up flow. That applies to the lead form as much as to the lessons: a form that captures a child's school, grades and photograph without saying why is the pattern worth refusing, whoever is running it.

One further Dubai-specific point. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE, the data still concerns a child living in Dubai, so the useful question is not where the tutor sits but who holds the information and how it is removed on request. sections.heading: What the format does better, and what it does worse
paragraphs: An honest comparison has rows going both ways, and a page that only lists advantages is selling rather than explaining. The format is worse at three things and better at five, and which set matters depends entirely on the student rather than on the subject.

It is worse at presence. A reluctant twelve-year-old who needs an adult physically alongside to start work is not served by a screen, and no platform design changes that. It is worse at physical practical technique, which belongs at the school bench under supervision. And it is worse for a student with no usable space at home, where a tuition centre's quiet room is genuinely the better product even at a worse teaching ratio.

It is better at the specialist match, which is the big one for Diploma subjects: the pool is the whole pool rather than whoever will drive to your community at 6pm. It is better at the minutes, since a 60-minute session contains close to sixty minutes when travel is removed and marking happens beforehand. It is better at continuity through travel, exam weeks and Ramadan, because a slot that depends on nobody's journey survives disruption.

It is also better at two subtler things. Annotation history: everything written in a shared file stays there, so by week six a student has a reference built from their own errors rather than a set of downloaded notes. And switching cost: changing specialist is an administrative act, which is what makes a genuine week-six review possible rather than theoretical.
The table lists this task by task so the comparison can be made against your child's actual situation rather than in the abstract.
