sections.heading: The student who drifts, and what the format can do about it
paragraphs: The most common objection to online tuition is attention, and it is not a silly objection. A teenager at a laptop has a browser, a phone and a group chat within reach, and a tutor on a screen is easier to tune out than one in a chair beside them. Any provider claiming the format solves this on its own is not being straight.

What does work is structure rather than surveillance. A session in which the student is writing for most of the hour has very little room for drift, because the next thing required is always theirs to produce. The shape described earlier in this page exists partly for that reason: short spells of explanation, long spells of the student working, with questions about lines they have just written.

Three practical measures help more than any software. One device for the lesson, with notifications off and the phone out of the room. The question paper on paper rather than in a tab behind the call, so attention does not have to switch windows. And a slot earlier in the evening, because a student who is home by 3.15pm in Mirdif and works at 4pm is a different student from the same child at 8.30pm.

The fourth measure is to notice it in the record rather than argue about it in the moment. If session notes stop naming specifics or the work set is not being done, something has changed, and that is visible in writing within three weeks. A tutor who flags it early is doing their job; one who reports that everything is fine while nothing gets done is not reading the week.

If a student genuinely cannot work on a screen — and a few cannot — then the honest conclusion is that this format is wrong for them, and school support or a visiting arrangement is the better answer. We would rather say that than sell twelve sessions into a situation the format cannot fix.

sections.heading: What an online hour costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: The AED figures below were published by the providers named and read in October 2026. They are market rates rather than IB Gram's prices; our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and what a plan costs depends on subject, level and how many sessions it genuinely needs. Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars.

Online rates sit below in-person ones for a straightforward reason: no journey is being paid for. Bestimate's Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The saving is the car, not the teaching, and a provider charging an in-person premium for an online lesson should be asked what the premium is for.

Within the online band the spread is also explicable. The bottom is a university student working from a textbook, which is adequate for a Standard Level topic gap and not for Higher Level coursework. The middle is qualified subject teaching. The top is sold on a claim — examiner experience, a reputation — which may be real and should be asked to evidence itself with a board, a subject and a recent series.

What changes the real cost per useful hour more than any of this is where marking happens. A provider at AED 200 who marks between sessions delivers more teaching minutes than one at AED 170 who reads the script in front of the student. Ask the question, get the answer in writing, and compare on minutes rather than on the headline.

Four more things in writing before the first payment: whether VAT is included, whether written feedback sits outside the session, the cancellation window, and whether the rate moves closer to the May session.

sections.heading: Judging an online tutor from one trial lesson
paragraphs: One hour is enough, provided you watch the right things. The temptation is to judge on warmth, which is the easiest attribute to perform for sixty minutes and the least predictive of whether marks move. The mechanics in this page are observable in real time and much harder to fake, because they require preparation that either happened or did not.

Watch the opening. A tutor who read the marked script you sent will open with a diagnosis and a target for the hour. A tutor who did not will open with questions whose answers you already supplied in writing, which is a reliable indicator of whether anything happens outside the paid hour.

Watch the hands. The student should be writing on the shared surface for most of the session, with the tutor annotating alongside and asking about lines just written. If the tutor's working fills the screen while your child watches, you are buying a lecture, and a lecture produces the comfortable sensation of understanding with no transferable method.

Watch the close. A numbered list of specific questions in a stated order is a plan; a general exhortation is not. And then watch the following day: a written note naming statements, marks, error categories and work set is the only part of the hour that still exists in six weeks, which is when you will actually be making a decision.

Our trial is free, takes no card details, and produces that written diagnosis whether or not you continue. Use it on more than one provider and compare the two documents rather than the two impressions. If nobody suitable is free in your child's subject and level, we will give you a date instead of a substitute — Higher Level sciences in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest.

process.title: Test the device before the trial
process.description: Five minutes on the device your child will actually use, especially if it is school-issued: some managed builds block screen sharing or annotation. Check that headphones work, that two panes fit on the screen, and that the study corner is not facing a west window at 5pm.

process.title: Send a scanned marked script
process.description: Photograph each page straight on, in reasonable light, numbered in order — a free scanning app does it properly in a minute. The specialist marks it against the published scheme before the trial, which is what lets the hour open with a diagnosis instead of an introduction.

process.title: Free trial lesson, watching the mechanics
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details. Watch the opening, watch whose handwriting appears, watch what gets set at the end. You receive a written diagnosis naming secure topics, gaps and the first three sessions, and you keep it either way.

process.title: Agree the recording and data position in writing
process.description: Whether sessions are recorded, who holds any file, what information about your child is held and how to have it removed. These are quick questions with quick honest answers, and the quality of the answer tells you something before any money is involved.

process.title: Fix the slot around the household, not the map
process.description: Choose the hour from when your child is actually home and when the adult who shares the bandwidth is not on a call. Then set a week-six review date in the same message, so the comparison of two marked scripts is scheduled rather than requested.

whyPoints.title: The student writes, not the tutor
whyPoints.description: A shared surface both people annotate, with the student producing most of the handwriting and the tutor asking about lines just written. Copying a worked solution feels like learning and earns no method marks in the examination room.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens before the session
whyPoints.description: Scripts are scanned, marked against the published scheme and annotated between lessons, so the hour opens with the diagnosis done. That recovers the ten to fifteen minutes a tutor otherwise spends reading in silence while your child watches.

whyPoints.title: Recording only on request
whyPoints.description: Sessions are not recorded by default, and where you ask for one the file belongs to the family. Creating video of a minor is a decision, not a setting, and we would rather you made it than we did.

whyPoints.title: Only the data the match needs
whyPoints.description: Name, year group, school, subject, level and the marked work you choose to send. No photograph, no academic history, no report card before a trial. You can ask what is held and have it deleted, under the UAE's personal data protection framework.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where the format loses
whyPoints.description: Bench practicals belong at school. A reluctant young student usually needs an adult in the room. A household with no usable space is better served by a quiet room elsewhere. We say so rather than selling into situations the format cannot fix.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE premises, no star rating, no promise about a final grade. Every AED figure names the provider that published it and the month it was read.

faqs.question: What does a live online IB lesson actually look like on screen?
faqs.answer: Two panes and a shared annotation surface. The first few minutes show the marked script with the tutor's annotations and a stated target for the hour. The middle forty minutes should be mostly your child's handwriting appearing on the shared surface while the tutor asks about lines just written. The last five produce a numbered list of work in a stated order. A written note follows within 24 hours naming statements covered, marks earned, error categories and the work set.

faqs.question: How does a tutor annotate my child's handwritten script over video?
faqs.answer: The student completes a timed question on paper, photographs each page straight on and numbered, and sends it before the session. A free scanning app that flattens and sharpens the page makes the difference between readable pencil working and an unusable image. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme beforehand, annotates the images and returns them with the session note. The crucial detail is that the marking happens before the lesson, not inside the paid hour.

faqs.question: Does a graphic display calculator work in an online maths lesson?
faqs.answer: It has to, particularly for Applications and Interpretation, where documented calculator work earns marks and undocumented work loses them. The practical solutions are a phone propped as a second camera pointing at the calculator, or screenshots sent before the session. Neither is difficult, but it has to be a deliberate decision. A tutor who never asks to see the calculator screen is not addressing a real source of lost marks in that course.

faqs.question: What internet speed does a Dubai household need for a video lesson?
faqs.answer: Less than most providers imply, and the usual problems are not speed at all. In large villas the study is often far from the router, which looks like a connection fault and is a distance problem fixed by a mesh node or a wired run. In dense towers the issue is evening contention, fixed by using the 5GHz band or a cable for the study device. The genuinely important investment is audio: headphones with a microphone, not bandwidth.

faqs.question: Are lessons recorded, and who can see the recording?
faqs.answer: Not by default. Where you ask for a recording — useful for a Language B oral rehearsal or a difficult derivation — the file belongs to the family rather than being retained for marketing. Recording every session automatically creates a store of video of a minor, which is not something to do as a setting. Any provider that records by default should be able to tell you where the files are held, for how long, and who can access them.

faqs.question: What personal data about a child does an online tutoring platform hold?
faqs.answer: It should hold only what the match needs: first name, year group, school, subject, level, and whatever marked work you choose to send, plus a parent contact. Under the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection you can ask what is held and ask for it to be removed. Be cautious of any form requesting a photograph, a full academic history or a report card before a trial lesson, especially without a stated purpose.

faqs.question: Can a chemistry mechanism be taught on a shared whiteboard?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than on paper, provided the student draws it. Mechanisms get built one arrow at a time with your child adding the next step while the tutor asks why it goes there; a step can be rolled back and reconsidered, which is awkward with a pencil. The failure mode is a tutor drawing the full mechanism for the student to copy, which produces a diagram they recognise and cannot reproduce under examination conditions.

faqs.question: How does a tutor check working rather than just answers online?
faqs.answer: By watching it appear. On a shared annotation surface the student's lines arrive in real time, which is more visible than leaning over a page, and the tutor can question a line the moment it is written rather than after the answer is finished. That is where method marks are won: a student trained to write the method line before the answer keeps the mark even when the arithmetic then fails, which is what M1 in a mark scheme rewards.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops during a Dubai evening lesson?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in writing at the start, before it happens. Ours is that a session interrupted for more than a few minutes is made up, because the hour was bought and not delivered. More usefully, most drops are preventable and local: router distance in a villa, evening contention in a tower, or a device on a crowded 2.4GHz band. Fifteen minutes of setup work at the Dubai end removes the majority of them permanently.

faqs.question: Does an online lesson suit a student who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: It can, through structure rather than supervision. A session in which the student is writing for most of the hour leaves little room for drift, because the next thing required is always theirs to produce. Three practical measures help: one device with notifications off and the phone out of the room, the question paper on paper rather than in a tab, and an earlier slot. If a student genuinely cannot work on a screen, the honest answer is that this format is wrong for them.

faqs.question: Which device works best for a Diploma student's online lesson?
faqs.answer: Whatever gives two usable panes. Most subjects need the question visible beside the student's own working, which is cramped on a phone and tight on a small laptop. A tablet beside the laptop for the question paper, or a second monitor, makes a visible difference. If the device is school-issued, test it before the first session: some managed builds block screen sharing or annotation, which is ten minutes of session one otherwise wasted on diagnosis.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor see a Biology data table or a graph?
faqs.answer: It goes on the shared surface where both people can mark it up at the same time, which is the actual lesson for data-based questions. Annotating an unfamiliar graph together — reading the axes aloud, labelling the command term, marking what the question is really asking — is what the component rewards. A printer at your end helps because some students think better on paper, and a stylus on a tablet does the same job without the printing.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for the Individual Oral practice?
faqs.answer: Well, and sometimes better than a room. School oral components are frequently recorded or conducted through a device anyway, so rehearsing in the same medium removes a variable rather than adding one. What matters is audio quality rather than video: headphones with a microphone, a quiet room, and a willingness to speak aloud without being overheard by the household. That last point is often the real obstacle in a shared Dubai apartment.

faqs.question: Is a shared document needed between sessions?
faqs.answer: It is the most undervalued part of the format. Everything written during an hour stays in a file the student owns, so by week six they have a reference built from their own mistakes rather than a folder of downloaded notes. For History it becomes a case-study bank; for mathematics an error log by category; for Theory of Knowledge a set of redrafted knowledge questions. Tutor comments should sit in a separate document, especially where coursework is involved.

faqs.question: Why is there no option for a tutor to attend a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. There are no IB Gram premises in the country either. What that removes is physical presence, which genuinely matters for younger or reluctant students. What it adds is a specialist matched across the whole pool and close to sixty minutes of teaching in a 60-minute hour, against roughly thirty-five to forty once travel, settling and in-lesson marking are counted.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free in our subject and level this week?
faqs.answer: You get a date rather than a substitute. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest, with Higher Level Computer Science and less common Language B options thinner still. We would rather leave the slot empty for a fortnight than put a Higher Level student with somebody who teaches the subject group but not the level, and we will say what is worth doing unsupervised in the meantime.

dubai/best-ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Watch the mechanics, not the manner
dubai/best-ib-online-tutor.closingBody: If you are comparing online tutors for Dubai, book a free trial lesson with no card details and watch four things while it runs: whether the tutor opens with a diagnosis from the script you sent, whose handwriting appears on the shared surface, whether the thing your child's subject needs is actually visible, and whether the hour closes with a numbered list. Then look for the written note the next day. Those four observations separate providers more reliably than any price list or review score in this market.

dubai/best-ib-tuition.tutorsIntro: The specialists below teach named subjects at named levels. Before booking anything, use the budget tables on this page to decide how many hours you are actually buying and in which term. Then ask for a free trial in the subject that matters most.

intro.heading: Build the budget first, then choose the tutor
paragraphs: Most families choose a tutor and then discover the cost. The reverse order works better, because the number of hours available is what determines whether a plan is a remedy or a gesture. A Dubai family with AED 1,000 a month to spend on tuition has roughly four to six useful hours in it depending on who teaches them, and four hours a month spent on one identified component will do more than eight hours spread across three subjects.

Published AED rates make that arithmetic possible, and almost nobody in this market publishes them. Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search show no price at all; the two that do quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in; and one competitor's structured data contradicts the price on its own visible page. Every figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

Our own model is deliberately not a shelf price, and it is worth saying why rather than hiding it. What a plan costs depends on the subject, the level, how many sessions a week it genuinely needs and for how long. So the sequence we use is a free trial lesson with no card details, a written diagnosis, then a conversation about how many hours the diagnosis actually implies. A quoted rate before a diagnosis is a number attached to an unknown quantity.

The useful context for any Dubai tuition budget is the school fee sitting beside it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That leaves one large number fixed on one side of a family's ledger, which makes the tuition decision easier to make deliberately.

Supply is moving too, and in a direction that matters for cost. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB places arriving faster than experienced Diploma teachers do is the condition under which specialist tutoring rates stay firm, which is worth knowing before assuming prices will soften.

On delivery, plainly, because it changes the arithmetic. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The in-home premium in this market is substantial and it buys presence rather than teaching minutes, which is the single largest avoidable cost in a Dubai tuition plan.

dubai/best-ib-tuition.programmesIntro: Cost per useful hour differs sharply by programme, because what the hour has to achieve differs. The notes below say what a family is realistically buying at each stage of the IB continuum in Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive stage and the one where hours are worth most, because grades here are used for university entry and the internally assessed components cannot be revisited once submitted. The budget question is which one or two subjects to fund properly rather than how to cover six, and the answer is distance from target at Higher Level plus the nearest coursework deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session, which concentrates demand and therefore pricing in the eight weeks beforehand. Families who start in DP1 pay a lower effective rate for the same outcome, because availability is easier and the work can be spread. A DP2 rescue in the spring is the most expensive way to buy the same number of hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest place to fix a problem that would otherwise cost far more later. Algebraic fluency, writing structure and criterion literacy all respond to a small number of hours at 13 or 14 and become expensive to repair at 17. The budget logic here is preventative rather than remedial.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the highest-value MYP spend is usually mathematics in the two terms before DP1 begins, because the step up from criterion-marked work to a Diploma paper arrives immediately. Schools running the Year 11 personal project frequently displace algebra practice, and that specific gap is cheap to close in advance.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The band where paying specialist rates makes least sense. There are no examinations, no percentages and no assessment architecture to teach to, so what is being bought is reading fluency, number sense or an additional language. A competent generalist at the bottom of the market is usually the right purchase.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic as an additional language is the commonest primary request in Dubai, because KHDA requires Arabic in all private schools with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. It is a language-teaching brief rather than an IB one, and should be priced as such rather than at a Diploma specialist's rate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Budget only for the Diploma courses inside it, which are examined exactly as in the full Diploma. The career-related units are provider-assessed, and paying a tutoring provider to work on them is paying for guesswork about criteria they have not seen.
programmes.countryNote: With very few Dubai schools licensing the programme there is no local price benchmark at all, so quotes vary widely and unhelpfully. The practical approach is to price the Diploma subjects at the normal bands and take the reflective project criteria from the school's coordinator at no cost.

dubai/best-ib-tuition.subjectsIntro: Rough hours, not rates. For each subject below, how many sessions a typical identified problem actually takes, which is the number that turns an hourly rate into a budget.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: An accuracy problem is two to four sessions. A genuine Higher Level calculus or proof gap is a term. The expensive mistake is buying a term of sessions for a problem that was two sessions of units and significant figures, which a marked script identifies immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical interpretation and documented calculator work are each about two to three sessions. Modelling content at Higher Level is longer. Most spend here is wasted on re-teaching tests the student can already perform rather than on the written conclusion.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equilibrium and energetics repair is four to six sessions; the internal investigation is a separate block tied to the school's draft stages. Higher Level data-handling practice is ongoing rather than finite, which makes it the subject most worth starting in DP1.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Written-explanation work is four to six sessions and is where most Dubai cohorts' marks sit. Numerical content rarely needs paid hours at all for a student already coping, so a quote built around calculation practice is usually a quote for the wrong thing.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based question practice is three to five sessions. Content revision is close to limitless and close to pointless for a student whose recall is intact, which describes most Dubai students who ask for Biology help in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The evaluation paragraph is three to four sessions, and it is the cheapest band improvement available in the Diploma. Higher Level calculation accuracy adds two. Anything longer than that is a content course the school is already providing.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Building a usable case-study bank is five to eight sessions, the longest honest block on this list, because the deliverable is a body of named detail the student can deploy unaided. Essay practice without the bank is the expensive version.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Technique vocabulary plus paragraph structure is four to six sessions and moves Paper 1 reliably. Reading the set texts is not a tuition cost; the school covers it and a tutor charging for text discussion is selling reading time.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Three to five sessions on answering with the stimulus quoted. The content is not usually the problem, which means a long content course is the most common overspend in this subject across Dubai.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Three to five sessions on text-type conventions, plus oral rehearsal closer to the assessment. A pair or trio is genuinely as good here, which makes it one of the few places a group rate is the better buy.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Three to four sessions, timed to when the prescribed titles and exhibition prompts are issued rather than spread across two years. A standing weekly slot in this subject is almost always money better spent elsewhere.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A finite block tied to the school's own draft stages, typically four to five sessions across several months. Priced as a block rather than hourly, because the work happens in bursts around deadlines rather than weekly.

dubai/best-ib-tuition.regionsIntro: Spending patterns differ across Dubai more than rates do. The notes below record what families in each area typically buy, which is useful mostly as a check on whether your own plan is shaped by evidence or by what the neighbours are doing.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Beside the densest IB school cluster, so families here compare quotes constantly and tend to overbuy breadth: three subjects at one session each rather than one done properly. The local market is competitive, which helps on rate and not on plan.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Meydan
regions.note: Shortlists here are frequently sorted by price downwards from the top band, on the assumption that the premium is a quality signal. Sometimes it is. The question worth asking is whether the premium buys something the specific component needs.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2 and 3
regions.note: Established villa communities with long school runs, which historically made in-home visits the default and expensive. The travel element inside those rates is the single largest recoverable cost in a plan from this area.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Jumeirah Village Triangle
regions.note: High-turnover catchments where families are often new to the Diploma and buy monthly packages because they are easier to compare. Converting the package to minutes and contact points usually changes the decision.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Budget-conscious households where the realistic choice is between a generalist at the bottom band and a small number of specialist hours. For an identified Higher Level component, fewer specialist hours is the better purchase.

regions.name: Deira and Al Rigga
regions.note: Plenty of low-cost local supply aimed largely at other curricula. A Diploma family here can spend a full budget on hours that are cheap per unit and poorly matched, which is the most expensive outcome available.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Dubai Modern catchment
regions.note: Continuum IB families who often start support in DP1 rather than DP2. That timing lowers the effective cost of the same outcome, because availability is easier and the work can be spread across more weeks.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: The cheapest tutoring supply in the emirate advertises here, next to the university cluster. Appropriate for Standard Level topic gaps and a false economy for Higher Level coursework, where the feedback is given against criteria the tutor has not read.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Science Park
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where school fees sit at the upper end and tuition is frequently added without a budget being set. Students we support here most often need one or two Higher Level subjects rather than the broad coverage families initially ask for, which usually reduces the quote rather than raising it.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Dubai Sports City
schoolClusters.note: Long school runs made visiting tutors the historical default in this cluster, at published in-home rates of AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 online for a qualified subject tutor. Recovering the travel element is the clearest single saving available to families here.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Al Mamzar and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: A district with abundant low-cost tutoring supply oriented to other curricula, where the risk is not overpaying per hour but paying for poorly matched hours. Students we support in this cluster are often the only Diploma candidate in their immediate circle.

sections.heading: What two years of IB tuition costs a Dubai family
paragraphs: The table below is a model, not a price list, built from the AED bands published by other providers and read in October 2026. It exists because no competing page in this market will put a two-year total in front of a parent, and a parent cannot plan against an hourly rate alone. Adjust the rows to your own situation; the point is the shape of the number rather than the number itself.

The assumptions are stated so you can argue with them. One Higher Level subject supported weekly across both Diploma years, a second subject supported for one term in DP2, a finite coursework block for the internal assessment and another for the Extended Essay, and a revision block in the final twelve weeks. That is a fairly typical plan for a student who is not in difficulty and wants to move one or two grades.

Two things usually surprise families reading it. The first is how much of the total sits in the final twelve weeks if the plan is left until then — a concentration that raises the effective cost per useful hour, because availability tightens across the Gulf in the run-up to the May session. The second is how cheap the coursework blocks are relative to their weight in the grade, since internally assessed work carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades.

A plan built in DP1 costs less for the same result, and not only because the hours are spread. Starting early means a problem is diagnosed while it is two topics rather than a subject, availability in the tight Higher Level specialisms is easier, and the student has enough weeks for the work set between sessions to actually be done. A DP2 spring rescue buys the same hours at the worst moment in the calendar.

Nothing in the table is an IB Gram price. Our sequence is a free trial lesson, a written diagnosis, then a conversation about how many hours the diagnosis implies — which is the only honest basis for a total.

sections.heading: What moves a Dubai quote, and the question that tests it
paragraphs: The spread between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour in this market is not noise. Each band corresponds to a different product, and within a band the variation is driven by a small number of identifiable factors. Knowing which factor a quote is pricing lets you ask whether you need it, which is a more productive conversation than negotiating a rate.

Level is the most legitimate driver. Higher Level content extends beyond the shared core and most subjects add an examined component, so a tutor who has taught that level to a full cohort is scarcer and prices accordingly. Where the same person charges the same for Standard and Higher Level, that is worth noticing in either direction: it may be honest pricing, or it may mean they treat the two as one course.

Format is the largest avoidable driver. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-350 at Bestimate and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is a car in evening traffic. It buys presence in the room, which matters for a young or reluctant student and does not add teaching minutes for a Diploma student with a closed door.

Timing is the driver families notice last. Demand concentrates across the whole Gulf in the eight weeks before the May session, which is when availability in the tight Higher Level specialisms disappears and when a family has least room to negotiate anything. Starting a plan in DP1 is a pricing decision as much as a pedagogical one.

sections.heading: Tuition in context: school fees, the fee freeze and exam entry
paragraphs: A tuition budget makes more sense once it sits beside the other education numbers a Dubai family is already carrying. The most useful of those is now fixed: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

That matters practically rather than sentimentally. A family that had budgeted for a fee increase has a known amount of room, and the question becomes whether that room is better spent on tuition, on examination entry for an additional subject, or on nothing at all. The last option is legitimate and under-considered: a student with a sound diagnosis and a numbered list of work for the week does not always need paid hours.

Examination entry is the cost most often forgotten. A student sitting a paper outside their own school as a private candidate pays entry fees to a recognised examination centre, and those fees and deadlines are set by the centre and the board rather than by any tutoring provider. Cambridge's published March 2027 series shows how far ahead the deadlines sit: an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026.

Equivalency and attestation sit outside the tuition budget too, and outside any tutoring provider's remit. The Ministry of Education's documented British-track requirements include five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae; no IB points figure should be quoted by anyone without a Ministry source.

sections.heading: Where in the two years an hour does the most work
paragraphs: Hours are not interchangeable. The same AED 250 buys a different amount of grade movement depending on which week of the Diploma it is spent in, and the differences are large enough to reorganise a budget around. The pattern is consistent and almost nobody plans against it, because tuition tends to be bought in response to a bad result rather than in advance of a known pressure point.

The highest-value window is the first term of DP1. A problem diagnosed there is still two topics rather than a subject, there are enough weeks for work set between sessions to actually be done, and availability in the tight Higher Level specialisms is manageable. An hour spent in October of DP1 does more than an hour spent in March of DP2, and costs less because demand is lower.

The second highest-value window is whatever fortnight precedes a coursework draft deadline. Internally assessed work carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades, it cannot be revisited after submission, and criterion feedback at the right moment is cheap relative to its weight. Families consistently underbuy here and overbuy generic revision later.

The lowest-value windows are the two most popular. The first is the fortnight immediately after a disappointing mock, when the instinct is to buy as many hours as possible in as many subjects as possible; the result is breadth with no diagnosis. The second is the final fortnight before the papers, when nothing new can be learned and the only useful work is technique and timing.

sections.heading: Monthly package or hourly rate
paragraphs: Most tuition in Dubai is sold monthly, which makes comparison harder rather than easier because the unit is a month instead of an hour. Published figures read in October 2026 cluster at about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, with Bestimate's wider monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions running roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Convert everything to two numbers before comparing: total minutes and contact points. Eight 60-minute sessions and four two-hour sessions contain the same minutes, but eight contacts keep weekly pressure and produce eight written records, while four long visits concentrate the teaching and spend part of each one arriving and settling. For a student who needs steady accountability the first is better; for a single large coursework push the second may be.

Then look at the terms rather than the headline, because that is where the money actually goes. Rollover of unused sessions, the notice required to cancel, whether the rate changes closer to the May session, and whether VAT is included. A package that looks cheaper and expires monthly is more expensive than one that looks dearer and carries forward, for any family whose term includes a school trip.

Blocks are the third option and the one this page keeps recommending. A finite component block with a stated number of sessions, a start and an end date, and marked work at each end is the only shape in which the total is known before you commit and the outcome is measurable afterwards. It is also the shape providers are least keen to sell, because it does not renew by default.

sections.heading: The costs that never appear on a tutoring quote
paragraphs: Four costs sit around a Dubai IB plan and are almost never mentioned by anyone selling tuition, which means families meet them as surprises in the term when there is least room. None of them is a tuition cost, and none should be presented as something a tutoring provider handles on your behalf.

Examination entry as a private candidate is the first. If a student sits a paper outside their own school, entry runs through a recognised examination centre at the centre's and the board's prices, with deadlines months ahead of the papers. Cambridge's published March 2027 series had final entries due 27 November 2026 for an exam period beginning 3 February 2027. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones and states that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk.

Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation is the second. It is a documentary process run by the Ministry, with sourced requirements for the British track and no published IB points figure that anyone should be quoting without a moe.gov.ae source. Describe it, verify it on the official channel, and treat any provider offering to perform or guarantee it as overstating what it can do. Nobody should imply that tuition is required for equivalency, admission or progression.

The third is the mandatory UAE subject load. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and combined classes explicitly prohibited. Those lessons sit inside the school day and inside the fee, but any additional support for them is a separate line a Diploma budget rarely includes.

The fourth is resources the family ends up buying: a graphic display calculator the student actually owns, printing for data-based questions, the school's editions of set texts. Small individually and worth listing, because they land in the same month as the first tuition invoice. What should not be on that list is past papers, mark schemes or subject guides — those are the boards' copyright, the school holds the licence, and no provider should be selling them to you.

sections.heading: VAT, cancellation and the four lines to get in writing
paragraphs: Four questions, answered in writing before any money moves, prevent nearly every tuition billing dispute. They are ordinary questions and an honest provider answers each in a sentence. A provider who answers in paragraphs of reassurance has told you something useful at no cost.

The first is VAT. Ask whether the quoted AED figure includes it. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not in a position to give; what a provider can and should tell you is simply whether its own quoted price is inclusive. Get that in writing and the invoice will match the conversation.

The second is where marking happens. A provider at AED 200 an hour who marks between sessions delivers more teaching minutes than one at AED 170 who reads the script in front of your child, so this single answer changes the real cost per useful hour more than the rate does. The third is the cancellation window: how much notice, what happens to a session lost to a school event, and whether unused sessions carry forward.

The fourth is whether the rate changes closer to the May session. Answers differ across this market and the question is asked surprisingly rarely. A provider that raises rates in the peak eight weeks is not necessarily behaving badly, but a family planning a final revision block needs to know before building the budget around the current figure.

One more, specific to anything described as free. Caution in this market is warranted around conditions attached to free trials: card details taken, automatic enrolment into a package, or a trial that converts unless cancelled. Our trial takes no card details and books nothing afterwards, and any condition attached to the word free should be visible on the same screen as the word.

sections.heading: The cheapest honest plan that still works
paragraphs: If the budget is genuinely tight, there is a version of this that costs very little and is not a compromise so much as a different order of operations. It starts with the part that is free and ends with the smallest number of paid hours the diagnosis actually justifies.

Step one costs nothing: get the three documents the school already holds. The last marked script with the teacher's annotations, the assessment calendar with internal deadlines, and the criterion list for any coursework component. Most families have never asked for the second and third, and they turn a vague worry into a specific plan with dates attached.

Step two is a free trial lesson with a written diagnosis, which converts the worry into a number of hours. If the diagnosis says two sessions of accuracy drilling on units and significant figures, buy two sessions. That is a complete and honest plan and it costs a fraction of a monthly package. The temptation to round it up to a term is the single most common overspend in this market.

Step three is to spend the remaining budget on the highest-value window rather than the most anxious one: the fortnight before a coursework draft deadline, or the first term of DP1 if you are early enough to choose. Coursework support is cheap relative to its weight in the grade, and criterion feedback at the right moment is the best-value hour in the Diploma.

Step four is free again: use the student's own work as the record. A baseline script, a topic checklist and a numbered list of work each week cost nothing and do most of what a paid hour is often bought to do. Where the honest answer is that no paid hours are needed at all, we would rather say so than sell a package into a situation that does not need one.

sections.heading: Why online delivery changes the arithmetic in Dubai
paragraphs: Stated plainly, because it is the largest single line in this page's arithmetic. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. There are no IB Gram premises in the country. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

The money consequence is direct. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-350 at Bestimate and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is broadly a car in evening traffic. For a Diploma student who will sit at a desk and work, that premium buys presence and adds no teaching minutes, which makes it the clearest avoidable cost in a plan.

There is a second, larger saving that does not appear as a rate. A visiting hour contains roughly thirty-five to forty minutes of teaching once arrival, settling and in-lesson marking are counted; a video hour with marking done between sessions contains close to sixty. Priced per useful minute rather than per nominal hour, the difference is considerably bigger than the headline rate difference.

The third effect is on availability, which is a cost in disguise. Matching across the whole pool rather than within a twenty-minute drive is what makes the tight Higher Level specialisms available at all, and a family that cannot find a specialist ends up buying more hours from a generalist to reach the same place. That is the most expensive way to spend a tuition budget and it rarely shows up as overspending.

The honest limitation remains physical. Bench practicals and arts exhibitions happen at school and belong to the school, and a young or reluctant student who needs an adult present is better served by a different arrangement. For everybody else, the arithmetic on this page points one way.

process.title: Collect the three free documents
process.description: The last marked script with annotations, the school's assessment calendar with internal deadlines, and the criterion list for any coursework component. Your school holds all three at no cost, and together they turn an open worry into a plan with dates on it before any money is involved.

process.title: Take the free trial and get the hour count
process.description: Sixty minutes with a matched specialist, no charge and no card details, producing a written diagnosis you keep either way. The important output is not reassurance but a number: how many sessions the identified problem actually implies. That number is what makes any quote assessable.

process.title: Decide the window before the amount
process.description: An hour in DP1 term one, or in the fortnight before a coursework draft deadline, does more than an hour in the final fortnight before the papers. Move hours earlier rather than adding more of them, which usually lowers the total rather than raising it.

process.title: Get the four lines in writing
process.description: Whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, where marking happens, what the cancellation and rollover terms are, and whether the rate changes closer to the May session. Four sentences, answered by email, and the invoice will match the conversation in month three.

process.title: Buy a block, then review
process.description: A finite component block with a stated number of sessions and marked work at each end, rather than a monthly arrangement that renews by default. Review against the two scripts and then decide whether to continue, move to a second subject, or stop.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED number on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and none of them is an IB Gram price. In a market where three of six ranking pages publish no price and one contradicts its own structured data, attribution is the differentiator.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a quote
whyPoints.description: A rate quoted before anybody has read a marked script is a number attached to an unknown quantity. Our sequence is a free trial with no card details, a written diagnosis, then a conversation about how many hours that diagnosis implies.

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks, not default renewals
whyPoints.description: Most identified component problems are four to six sessions. We will say so even when a monthly package would be worth more to us, and a block has a stated end date rather than rolling over unless cancelled.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium removed
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 online for a qualified subject tutor. Teaching over video removes that premium and adds roughly twenty teaching minutes per nominal hour, because no journey or settling sits inside it.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what is not ours to charge for
whyPoints.description: Examination entry, resits, equivalency and attestation belong to the boards, the examination centres and the Ministry. We describe them, point you at the official channel, and never present them as a service we perform or guarantee.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE premises, no star rating and no promise about a final grade. We also do not state the VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact, only whether a quoted price is inclusive.

faqs.question: What does two years of IB tuition cost a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Using published market bands read in October 2026, a fairly typical plan — one Higher Level subject weekly across DP1, coursework blocks for the internal assessment and Extended Essay, a second subject for one term in DP2, and a twelve-week revision block — comes to roughly 74 hours and an indicative AED 12,800 to 27,300. That is an illustration from other providers' rates, not an IB Gram price. The variable you control is hours, and moving them earlier lowers the total more reliably than negotiating a rate.

faqs.question: How much of a tuition budget should go on the final six months?
faqs.answer: Less than most families spend there. Demand across the Gulf concentrates in the eight weeks before the May session, which raises rates and collapses availability in the tight Higher Level specialisms at exactly the moment you have least room to choose. An hour in DP1 term one buys more grade movement and costs less. If you are already in DP2, spend the first session on a diagnosis rather than on content, however counter-intuitive that feels with the calendar closing.

faqs.question: Did the KHDA fee freeze change what families spend on tuition?
faqs.answer: It changed the room available rather than the decision. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A family that had budgeted for an increase now has a known amount of flexibility. Whether it goes on tuition, on an additional examination entry, or on nothing at all is worth deciding deliberately rather than by default.

faqs.question: What does a private candidate pay to sit IGCSE papers in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Whatever the recognised examination centre charges, plus the board's own fees, and those vary by centre so the centre is the only reliable source. The deadlines matter as much as the cost: Cambridge's published March 2027 series had final entries due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones and states that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk. No tutoring provider can enter your child.

faqs.question: Which single decision moves a Dubai tuition bill the most?
faqs.answer: Whether a tutor travels. Published in-home rates run AED 180-350 at Bestimate and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The premium is a car in evening traffic, and for a Diploma student who will sit at a desk it buys presence rather than teaching minutes. The second largest is where marking happens, because that changes the useful minutes inside the hour you are already paying for.

faqs.question: Is one subject at two sessions a week better value than two subjects at one?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, provided there is a diagnosis. One subject at two sessions allows a diagnose-rebuild-retest cycle inside a fortnight, which is how a component actually moves. Two subjects at one session each gives neither enough contact to complete a cycle, and gives the student twice as much work set with no extra evening to do it in. The exception is where a coursework deadline in a second subject is imminent, since internal assessment work cannot be revisited later.

faqs.question: What does a coursework support block cost in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: It is usually priced as a block rather than hourly, because the work happens in bursts around the school's draft stages rather than weekly. Using the specialist band of AED 200-450 an hour published in this market, a five-session internal assessment block sits at roughly AED 1,000 to 2,250. Relative to the weight of internally assessed work — roughly a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades — that is the best-value spend in the Diploma, and families consistently underbuy it.

faqs.question: Should we budget for tuition in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, for three reasons that all reduce the total. A problem diagnosed in DP1 term one is still two topics rather than a whole subject. There are enough weeks for the work set between sessions to actually be done, which is where most of the learning happens. And availability in the tight Higher Level specialisms is manageable rather than scarce, so you are not paying peak-demand rates for a substitute. A DP2 spring rescue buys the same hours at the worst moment.

faqs.question: How do we compare a monthly package with an hourly rate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Convert both to total minutes and contact points, then read the terms. Published packages cluster at about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions — the same minutes with half the contacts and part of each visit spent arriving. Then check four things: rollover of unused sessions, notice to cancel, whether the rate changes before May, and whether VAT is included. A package that expires monthly is dearer than it looks for any family with a school trip in the term.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate rise as the May session approaches?
faqs.answer: Answers differ across this market, which is why the question is worth asking in writing before you build a budget on today's figure. What is consistent is that availability falls sharply in the eight weeks beforehand, because demand concentrates across the whole Gulf at once and the tight Higher Level specialisms disappear from early-evening slots first. A family that intends to buy a final revision block should secure the slot well before the term it is needed in.

faqs.question: Are there months in the Dubai calendar where tuition is wasted money?
faqs.answer: Two, in practice. The final fortnight before the papers, when nothing new can be absorbed and the only useful work is technique, timing and sleep — paying for new content there is paying for anxiety management. And the fortnight immediately after a disappointing mock, if the response is to buy breadth across four subjects with no diagnosis. Ramadan is not one of them: sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot and work perfectly well, provided the change is agreed a fortnight ahead.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support a Standard Level subject?
faqs.answer: Get the three free documents from the school, take a free trial to convert the worry into an hour count, then buy only the hours the diagnosis justifies. A Standard Level accuracy problem is often two to four sessions of units, significant figures and exact forms — a complete plan at a fraction of a monthly package. The temptation to round that up to a term is the commonest overspend in this market, and a provider who encourages it is selling continuity.

faqs.question: Does the quoted rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get it in writing, because the answer varies by provider. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, since that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation; what any provider can tell you is simply whether its own quoted figure is inclusive. That one sentence prevents the commonest billing dispute in private tuition, and a provider unwilling to put it in an email has told you something before you have spent anything.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive hour in Dubai the most useful hour?
faqs.answer: Only where the premium matches the need. The top band, published at AED 500-650 or more, is sold on a claim — examiner experience, a reputation — which may be real and should be asked to evidence itself with a board, a subject and a recent series. For a three-session Standard Level topic fix it is a waste. For a specific, identified Higher Level component need it may be exactly right. The band to avoid for Higher Level coursework is the bottom one, where feedback is given against criteria the tutor has not read.

faqs.question: Why does online delivery change the arithmetic for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Three ways. It removes the travel premium, which published figures put at roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour between in-home and online qualified teaching. It adds teaching minutes, because a video hour with marking done beforehand contains close to sixty against thirty-five to forty for a visit. And it widens the specialist pool, which matters because a family that cannot find a specialist buys more generalist hours to reach the same place. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: What if the budget only covers a handful of hours?
faqs.answer: Then buy a diagnosis and the single highest-value block, and use free resources for the rest. The diagnosis is free with our trial; the school's marked scripts, assessment calendar and criterion lists cost nothing; and a numbered list of work each week does much of what a paid hour is often bought for. Spend the paid hours in the fortnight before a coursework draft deadline, where criterion feedback is cheap relative to the weight of the component. Where no paid hours are needed, we will say so.

dubai/best-ib-tuition.closingHeading: Decide the hours before you choose the tutor
dubai/best-ib-tuition.closingBody: The useful version of best IB tuition in Dubai is the plan that converts the money you have into the largest number of hours spent in the right window. Start with the three documents your school already holds, take a free trial lesson with no card details and get the written diagnosis, then decide how many hours the diagnosis actually implies and which term they should sit in. Get VAT, marking, cancellation and peak-season pricing in writing, buy a finite block, and review it against two marked scripts.

dubai/best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each specialist below teaches a named subject at a named level. Use the scorecard further down this page during the trial lesson rather than after it, and compare two written diagnoses side by side before committing to anyone, including us.

intro.heading: There is no league table, so build the measurement yourself
paragraphs: No authority ranks private tutors in the UAE. KHDA inspects schools, not tutors. MoHRE issues a tutoring permit, which establishes permission rather than quality. The IB authorises schools and trains teachers; it does not rate individuals who teach its syllabuses privately. So a page claiming to list the best IB tutor in Dubai is listing whoever paid for the position, and a parent who treats that list as a ranking is reading an advertisement as data.

What exists instead is a set of things that can be measured, and most of them can be measured before any money changes hands. Whether a tutor teaches the specific level your child sits. Whether they read a marked script before the first lesson or during it. Whether they can name the criterion a coursework draft is failing. Whether the work they set is a numbered list or an instruction to keep practising. Whether, after six weeks, a second marked script on the same component scores differently from the first.

This page is built around those measurements rather than around adjectives. There is a scorecard you can fill in while a trial lesson happens, including a trial lesson with us. There is a four-checkpoint calendar so you can tell the difference between a tutor who is not working and eight weeks that were always going to feel slow. And there is a short list of questions whose answers reliably end a shortlist in one direction or the other.

Two warnings about the claims this market makes, because they come up in every shortlist. The first is accreditation: no tutoring provider in Dubai is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson in the way those words are usually implied. IB Gram holds none of them either, and says so. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises, and nobody without premises holds one.

The second is the review score. Competitors in this market publish self-asserted star ratings, sometimes two different ones on the same page, and ratings that cannot be traced to countable reviews are worth precisely nothing. The same applies to statistics without a sample size, a date and a method. If a figure on any tutoring site cannot tell you those three things, ignore it — including on this page, where every AED number names the provider that published it and the month it was read.

A plain word on how we deliver, since it bears on the comparison. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That removes presence in the room from what you are buying, and adds a match made on subject and level across the whole pool rather than within driving distance.

dubai/best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: What counts as a good tutor changes with the programme, because what the programme actually examines changes. The notes below say what to test for at each stage, which is a more useful filter than years of experience.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Test for level, not subject. Higher Level content runs deeper than Standard Level and the extra papers are the ones that separate grades, so a tutor comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically the right choice above it. Ask which level they teach this academic year and which paper they would start on; a specialist answers with a component in one sentence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session and apply to UK, North American and UAE universities in parallel, so a good tutor here knows the school's internal deadlines as well as the board's. Ask whether they have taught a full two-year cycle rather than isolated revision blocks, because the DP1 term-two coursework pile-up is where a plan is usually made or lost.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Test for criterion fluency. MYP work is marked on bands A to D rather than by percentage, and the common failure is a tutor who teaches content competently while the student keeps losing marks against a descriptor nobody has read to them. Ask what separates a 5-6 band from a 7-8 band in your child's subject; a vague answer is the answer.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that run MYP into the Diploma set the personal project in Year 11, and it is the student's own work. A tutor who offers to help produce it has failed the only test that matters. The right answer is process coaching and criterion feedback, and a willingness to say so without being asked.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Test for restraint. There are no examinations and no percentages at this stage, so the risk is a tutor who imports a British Year 5 worksheet scheme into an inquiry classroom and confuses a seven-year-old. Ask how they would measure progress without a test; the good answer is a repeated task, three weeks apart, compared side by side.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and combined classes explicitly prohibited. Most primary tuition requests in the emirate are Arabic as an additional language, and the right tutor for that is a language teacher rather than an IB specialist.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Test for scope honesty. The Diploma courses inside the Career-related Programme are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so those are tutorable on familiar terms. The career-related units are assessed by the provider, and a tutor claiming to know their criteria without naming the provider is guessing.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the programme, so there is no local peer group and very little tutoring supply built around it. A good tutor here will say plainly which parts they can help with and point you back to the school's coordinator for the reflective project criteria rather than improvising an answer.

dubai/best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: A trial lesson is more useful when you know what to ask the tutor to teach. Below, by subject, the single question type that separates somebody who knows the syllabus from somebody who knows the topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask them to teach a question where the method is worth more than the answer, and watch whether they insist on a written method line. A tutor who accepts a correct answer with no working has not taught anyone who lost an accuracy mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask for a statistical test and then ask what the conclusion sentence should say. A tutor who stops at the p-value is teaching mathematics and not the subject, because the marks sit in the interpretation written in plain words.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask them to explain a shift in an equilibrium and listen for whether they name what drives it rather than describing the direction. Then ask what Paper 3 actually tests; if the answer is "the options" and nothing about unfamiliar data, that is useful to know.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask for a question that requires a reason instead of a number. Dubai cohorts are usually strong numerically and thin on written explanation, and a tutor who only sets calculations will never touch the half of Paper 2 that is costing marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Hand over a data-based question on an unfamiliar context, not a recall question. Watch whether the tutor starts by reading the command term aloud. If the lesson becomes a content revision, you have learned what the next eight weeks would be.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask them to write the last paragraph of an evaluation answer. That paragraph carries the top band and is the single thing most tuition in this subject never reaches, because it is faster to draw another diagram.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Give them a case-study extract and ask for an answer that quotes it. A tutor who answers from theory without touching the stimulus is demonstrating exactly the error that costs application and evaluation marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask for an analysis of two lines rather than a reading of a whole text. The skill being examined is close analysis of a specific technique, and a tutor who paraphrases the passage is teaching comprehension instead.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Ask what named detail a strong answer on your child's topic would contain. A good answer arrives with dates, figures and actors; a weak one describes a process. The difference is the band boundary in both Higher and Standard Level essays.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask them to turn a topic into a knowledge question in front of you. If they offer to draft the essay instead, the shortlist has just got shorter, and for the right reason.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Ask which text type a given task requires and what its conventions are. Marks here are lost on conventions rather than on vocabulary, and a tutor treating it as general English practice will miss that entirely.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask for pseudocode with the loop boundaries stated explicitly. Marks go on initialisation and boundaries rather than on logic, and supply at Higher Level is thin enough across the region that this is worth asking about a term early.

dubai/best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: How Dubai families choose a tutor is partly geographic, because recommendations travel along school-gate and community lines. The notes below record what that does to a shortlist in each area, and where the local recommendation is least likely to fit.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Al Manara
regions.note: Dense school-gate networks where a single well-liked tutor can end up teaching a dozen families. That is a genuine signal about manner and an unreliable one about level, since most of those dozen are at different stages.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Lakes
regions.note: Small, well-connected communities where recommendations carry a lot of weight and are rarely tested against a marked script. Worth asking the recommender which subject and level their child was taught, because the answer is often not yours.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City and Motor City
regions.note: Several schools inside a short radius, so parent groups compare notes constantly and a shortlist arrives ready-made. The useful addition here is the scorecard, since the shortlist has already been filtered on popularity rather than on component fit.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Next to the university cluster, which means a steady supply of undergraduate tutors advertising locally at the bottom of the market. Fine for Standard Level topic gaps and usually wrong for Higher Level coursework.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Established villa communities feeding both British and IB schools, where families frequently compare an A Level route with the Diploma. A tutor who has taught both is genuinely more useful here than one who has taught either very well.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing catchments with high turnover, so recommendations are newer and shallower. This is the area where a written trial diagnosis does most of the work that word of mouth does elsewhere.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Garhoud
regions.note: A smaller IB cohort surrounded by schools on other curricula, so the local recommendation is often for a tutor who teaches a different system well. Ask which board and which level before anything else.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Meydan
regions.note: Newer, affluent catchments where the shortlist tends to be sorted by price upwards, on the assumption that the top of the market is the top of the quality range. The premium is sometimes real and should be asked to prove itself.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim, Al Manara and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: A long-established cluster with strong parent networks, where a tutor recommendation can travel across a dozen families in a term. Students we support here are split between the Diploma and A Level routes, and the most useful question in the cluster is which of the two the tutor has actually taught.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Dubailand
schoolClusters.note: Schools clustered inside a short internal road network, which keeps school runs short and makes 4.30pm sessions realistic. Requests we see here are heavily weighted towards mathematics at both levels, and towards the IGCSE-to-Diploma transition in Year 11.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Dubai Academic City
schoolClusters.note: Sitting beside the university cluster, this is where the cheapest tutoring supply in the emirate advertises. Students we support here benefit most from the scorecard, because the gap between a confident undergraduate and a Higher Level subject teacher is invisible in a listing and obvious in a trial lesson.

sections.heading: Five things parents mean by "best", and the test for each
paragraphs: The word hides five different requirements, and most disappointment in private tuition comes from buying one of them while needing another. A family that needs a diagnostician hires a motivator and reports that nothing changed. A family that needs somebody to make a 13-year-old sit down hires a Higher Level examiner and reports that the sessions were too advanced. Both tutors were competent and both hires were wrong.

Writing down which one you need takes about two minutes and it is worth doing before a single phone call. Does your child know the content and keep losing marks, or not know the content at all? Does the problem sit in the externally examined papers or in the coursework? Is the obstacle technique, or is it getting started at all? Each answer points at a different tutor and a different number of sessions.

The tests in the table are all things you can do before paying. None of them requires you to understand the subject, and all of them can be done inside a trial lesson or a single email exchange. The pattern worth noticing is that each test asks for something specific: a component, a criterion letter, a numbered list, a named level. Specificity is the measurable part of quality in this market.

A note on the fifth row, because it is the one families are least comfortable asking about. Availability is a quality attribute. A tutor who is genuinely strong but cannot offer a slot before 8pm in the eight weeks before the May session is, for a tired 17-year-old, not the right tutor. The honest version of best is best-available-at-the-hour-your-child-can-still-learn.
Use the table as a filter rather than a scorecard; the scorecard comes next. The purpose here is only to make sure you are shortlisting for the thing you actually need.

sections.heading: A trial-lesson scorecard you can fill in while it happens
paragraphs: A trial lesson usually gets judged on rapport, which is the one variable a tutor can perform. Rapport matters, and it is also the easiest thing in the world to fake for sixty minutes. The scorecard below moves the judgement onto things that can be observed rather than felt, and it works equally well on us and on anyone else you are considering.

Watch the first ten minutes especially. A tutor who has read the marked script you sent arrives with a hypothesis and tests it within the first few questions. A tutor who has not read it spends those minutes finding out what your child is studying, which is information you supplied in writing. That single observation separates a shortlist more cleanly than anything else on the list.

The second thing to watch is whose pen moves. In a good session the student is writing most of the time and the tutor is asking questions about what has just been written. In a weak session the tutor is writing a worked solution and the student is copying it, which is a lecture with an audience of one. Copying produces the comfortable feeling of having understood and no evidence that anything was learned.

The third is what gets set at the end. A numbered list of four specific questions, in a stated order, is a plan. "Keep practising past papers" is a wish. Dubai students are busy rather than idle, and the vague instruction is what loses the week between sessions.

Score it during the lesson rather than afterwards. Memory rearranges an hour into a general impression within about a day, which is why two providers seen a week apart become indistinguishable by the time you sit down to decide.
