sections.heading: The three documents to put in front of a new tutor
paragraphs: Families usually arrive at a first session with a description of the problem. A description is the least useful thing available, because it has already been filtered through a teenager's account of their own performance and a parent's reading of a report card. Three documents replace it entirely, and Dubai schools hold all three.

The first is the last marked script, with the teacher's annotations left on it. Not a clean copy and not a grade — the marked version, including the parts the student would rather not show. A single marked page tells a subject specialist which marks were lost and, usually, why, before anyone has spoken. If a tutor does not ask for one, ask yourself what they intend to base the first month on.

The second is the school's assessment calendar for the year, with the internal coursework deadlines on it. Dubai schools set their own internal dates for drafts, mock windows and moderation, and they do not coincide across the emirate. A tutor working to the wrong dates is useful in the wrong month, and that is a surprisingly common and entirely avoidable waste.

The third applies only where coursework is involved: the criterion list from the subject guide your school holds. It is the document that turns a vague conversation about an internal assessment into a specific one about which criterion the draft is not yet meeting. We do not publish or distribute subject guides, past papers or mark schemes — those are the boards' copyright and the school holds the licence — so the school is the route to them.

Hand all three over at the first contact rather than the first session. A tutor who has read them before the trial starts has already told you something about how they work, and the trial lesson can then be spent on the student rather than on an orientation.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, four checkpoints: when a judgement is fair
paragraphs: Two weeks is too early and a term is too late. Judged at two weeks, almost every arrangement looks promising, because a new person asking better questions produces an immediate lift in engagement that has nothing to do with marks. Judged at a term, a family has spent twelve or fourteen sessions before discovering the diagnosis was wrong. Eight weeks with four fixed checkpoints is the honest middle.

The checkpoints matter more than the length. Fixing them in advance, in writing, changes the conversation from a complaint into a scheduled review, which makes it far more likely to happen at all. Providers rarely propose this because a scheduled review is a scheduled opportunity to stop, and that is precisely why a parent should propose it.

The content of each checkpoint is different, and the table sets out what each one can and cannot tell you. Week one produces the baseline: a timed question marked against the published scheme, which must be kept however poor the result, because it is the only thing week six can be measured against. Families routinely throw it away for exactly the reason it is valuable.

Week three is about process rather than marks. Was work set, was it done, do the session notes name specifics. If three consecutive notes could have been written about any student, the tutor is not reading the scripts, and no amount of further weeks will change that. Week six is the comparison script. Week eight is the decision.

Three outcomes are all normal at week eight: continue, change the session plan, or change the tutor. A provider who treats the third as an insult has misunderstood the arrangement. We will change the specialist on request at any point, without a reason being required, and without restarting the block.

sections.heading: Questions that end a shortlist, and the answers that should worry you
paragraphs: Six questions, asked by email so the answers are in writing, will usually reduce a shortlist of five to one or two. None of them is hostile and all of them are things an honest provider answers in a sentence. The ones that produce a paragraph of reassurance instead of a sentence of fact are the informative ones.

The most useful question is about coursework, because it is where the market divides sharply. There are providers in this SERP selling completed internal assessments; one has been found advertising finished IAs at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller. A good provider states the boundary before being asked, as we do: feedback by criterion, delivered separately from the document, with the student's dated drafts untouched.

The second most useful is about accreditation, for the opposite reason. The right answer is a plain no. No tutoring provider in Dubai is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson in the sense that phrase implies. A provider who answers yes should be asked for the permit number and the issuing authority, and the answer will be interesting.

Examiner claims deserve the same treatment. Examiner status, where it exists, is current or it is nothing, and it does not confer access to marking, boundaries or paper content. A tutor describing themselves as an examiner should be able to say for which board, which subject and which recent series, and nobody should imply that the role gives them inside knowledge of unreleased material.

sections.heading: What no tutor can tell you, however good they are
paragraphs: A good tutor is honest about the edges of what they know, and there are four things on which the correct answer is a plain refusal. The first is a final grade. Nobody can promise a 7, a points total or a grade improvement, and no refund arrangement makes such a promise credible. A provider willing to attach a number to your child's final result has told you how they treat evidence.

The second is grade boundaries. Boundaries are set after the papers have been sat and marked, vary by session, and are published by the boards rather than estimated by tutors. An experienced teacher can say roughly what a mark has historically converted to and should say the word roughly. Anybody offering a precise conversion for a session that has not happened is guessing with confidence.

The third is unreleased material. No tutor has sight of papers before a session, and anybody implying otherwise is either lying or describing something that would end the student's candidacy. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are the boards' copyright and are available through the school, which holds the licence; we neither host nor distribute them.

The fourth is the equivalency and attestation process for UAE purposes. A tutor can describe it and should point you at the official channel. For the British track, the sourced requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB, no points threshold should be published by anyone without a Ministry of Education source, and one ranking competitor already publishes a wrong subject count for the British track.

Treat a tutor's willingness to say "I do not know, ask the coordinator" as a positive signal rather than a gap. In a market where several ranking pages publish figures with no source attached, a provider that draws a line around its own knowledge is the unusual one.

sections.heading: What the top of the Dubai market charges, and what the premium should prove
paragraphs: Price is the closest thing this market has to a published ranking, which is why parents use it as one. It is a poor proxy, but it is not a random one: the bands below correspond to genuinely different products. The AED figures are published by the providers named and were read in October 2026. They are market rates, not IB Gram's prices, and our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

The bottom band buys a university student working from a textbook. For a Standard Level topic gap at 15, that is often exactly the right purchase and a specialist would be a waste. For Higher Level coursework it is not, and the cost of discovering that is a term. The middle band is where qualified subject teaching sits and where most honest matching happens.

The top band is the interesting one because it is sold on a claim rather than a qualification. Examiner experience, a named reputation, a specific school's results — each may be real and each should be asked to evidence itself before the premium is paid. The question is not whether the tutor is good but whether the extra AED 300 an hour buys something your child's specific component needs.

Before paying at any band, get four things in writing: whether VAT is included, whether marking and written feedback sit outside the session, what the cancellation window is, and whether the rate changes closer to the May session. All four become arguments in month three otherwise, and the fourth is asked surprisingly rarely.

One caution that applies to the whole table. A provider quoting a figure without naming the currency, the date or the source is asking you to treat a sales number as a market fact. Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in.

sections.heading: Changing tutor without losing the term
paragraphs: Changing is normal and most families are too slow to do it, usually out of politeness. The cost of six extra weeks with the wrong match is six weeks, and in DP2 that is a material fraction of the time remaining. The reason to publish a checkpoint calendar is to make the change a scheduled option rather than a confrontation.

Three signals justify it without any further analysis. Session notes that could have been written about any student, for three weeks running, mean the scripts are not being read. A comparison script at week six that has not moved on the component worked on means the diagnosis was wrong, and if the tutor cannot say why, a second opinion is cheaper than a third month. And a student who stops attempting hard questions in sessions has usually decided the person is not safe to be wrong in front of, which no amount of subject expertise repairs.

What should carry over is the evidence, not the relationship. The baseline script, the topic checklist, the error log and the session notes belong to you and should be handed to the next specialist on day one. A new tutor starting from those documents is productive in the first session rather than the third, which recovers most of the time a change appears to cost.

What should not carry over is the diagnosis, at least not unchallenged. If the first six weeks did not move the marks, the hypothesis deserves re-testing rather than inheriting. Ask the new specialist to produce their own reading of the baseline script before they see the previous one; disagreement between two readings is itself informative.

We will change the specialist on request, at any point, without a reason being required and without restarting a block. That is a policy rather than a favour, and it is worth asking any provider in this market to state their equivalent in writing before the first payment.

sections.heading: Why our lessons happen over live video
paragraphs: Stated plainly, since it bears on any comparison you are making: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Nobody will arrive at a Dubai address. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so a scanned script can be marked up by tutor and student at the same moment.

The reason this matters to a page about choosing well is the size of the pool. Matching on subject and level across the whole pool rather than within a twenty-minute drive is the difference between a Higher Level Chemistry specialist and the nearest available science teacher. For the tight combinations — Higher Level sciences in the early-evening Gulf window, Higher Level Computer Science, less common Language B options — proximity and quality point in opposite directions.

The second reason is the hour itself. No journey, no arrival, no settling, and marking done between sessions rather than in front of the student. A 60-minute video session contains close to sixty minutes of teaching, where a visit of the same nominal length contains thirty-five to forty. Over a term of weekly sessions that is several additional hours at no extra cost.

The third is simply that a change of tutor costs nothing logistically. Nobody has to redraw a route or renegotiate a journey, so switching specialist at week six is an administrative act rather than an upheaval — which is what makes the checkpoint calendar above usable in practice rather than in theory.

The honest limitation is physical. Bench practicals and arts exhibitions happen at school and belong to the school. What a video session does with those components is the design, the data treatment and the write-up against the published criteria, which is where the bulk of their marks sit in any case.

process.title: Write down which kind of help you need
process.description: Diagnostician, content teacher, technique coach, coursework supervisor, or simply somebody available at the right hour. Two minutes on this question prevents the most common wrong hire in private tuition, which is a competent tutor bought for the wrong problem.

process.title: Send the three documents
process.description: The last marked script with the teacher's annotations, the school's assessment calendar with its internal deadlines, and the criterion list if coursework is involved. Send them before the trial, not at it, and notice whether the tutor has read them when the lesson starts.

process.title: Fill in the scorecard during the trial
process.description: Score the first ten minutes, who is writing, which question gets chosen, the language used about marks, and what is set at the end. Score it while it happens, because memory flattens an hour into a general impression inside a day. The trial is free and takes no card details.

process.title: Fix four checkpoints before the first paid session
process.description: Weeks one, three, six and eight, with dates written down and what each one will produce. Week one is the baseline script, which you keep however poor it looks. Week six is the comparison. Week eight is an explicit decision rather than an automatic renewal.

process.title: Decide at week eight, on the two scripts
process.description: Continue, change the session plan, or change the specialist. All three are normal. If you change, hand the next tutor the baseline script, the error log and the session notes, and ask for their own reading of the baseline before they see anyone else's.

whyPoints.title: A trial that produces evidence, not an impression
whyPoints.description: One timed question attempted unassisted, marked against the published scheme, and a written diagnosis naming secure topics, gaps and the first three sessions. Yours to keep whether you continue or not, and comparable side by side against any other provider's.

whyPoints.title: The measurement published, not just promised
whyPoints.description: The scorecard and the four-checkpoint calendar on this page are tools you can use on anyone, including us. We publish them because a provider that controls the measurement is not being measured.

whyPoints.title: A specialist change is a policy, not a favour
whyPoints.description: You can ask for a different specialist at any point, without giving a reason and without restarting a block. Your evidence file goes with you, which is why a change at week six costs a week rather than a term.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no board partnership, no star rating, no promise about a final grade and no statistic without its source. Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line stated before being asked
whyPoints.description: Criterion feedback delivered separately from the document, dated drafts left entirely the student's own, and no writing, editing or proofreading to completion at any price. In a market where completed internal assessments are openly sold, this is the question worth asking first.

whyPoints.title: Availability treated as a quality attribute
whyPoints.description: A strong tutor who can only offer 8.30pm is the wrong tutor for a tired Diploma student. We quote the actual slot and the real match time for your subject and level before anything else is discussed, and give a date rather than a substitute if nobody suitable is free.

faqs.question: How do we judge the best IB tutor in Dubai without a published ranking?
faqs.answer: By measuring instead of ranking. No authority rates private tutors in the UAE: KHDA inspects schools, MoHRE issues a permit that establishes permission rather than quality, and the IB authorises schools rather than individuals. What you can measure before paying is whether the tutor teaches your child's specific level, whether they read a marked script before the lesson or during it, whether they name criteria and command terms rather than confidence, and whether a second marked script moves at week six.

faqs.question: What should the first forty minutes of a trial lesson produce?
faqs.answer: A hypothesis, a hard question attempted, and a page of the student's own working. A tutor who read the script you sent arrives with a theory and tests it in the first few questions; one who did not spends those minutes collecting information you already supplied in writing. Watch whose pen is moving: in a strong session the student writes and the tutor asks about what has just been written. A tutor writing a model answer for the student to copy is lecturing to an audience of one.

faqs.question: Which three documents should a Dubai parent put in front of a new tutor?
faqs.answer: The last marked script with the teacher's annotations left on it, the school's assessment calendar including internal coursework deadlines, and the subject guide's criterion list where coursework is involved. Dubai schools hold all three. Send them before the trial rather than at it, and notice whether the tutor has read them. We do not publish or distribute subject guides, past papers or mark schemes, since those are the boards' copyright and the school holds the licence.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a tutoring decision can honestly be made?
faqs.answer: About eight, with checkpoints at weeks one, three, six and eight. Two weeks is too early, because a new person asking better questions lifts engagement immediately without touching marks. A full term is too late, because fourteen sessions have been bought before the diagnosis is tested. Week one produces the baseline script, week three shows whether the tutor reads the student's own work, week six produces the comparison, and week eight is the decision.

faqs.question: What does a diagnostic actually test that a conversation does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks went. A conversation produces a teenager's account of their own performance, filtered twice, and a report card grade with no component breakdown behind it. A diagnostic produces a timed attempt at a question the student would have avoided, marked against the published scheme, with each loss sorted into a category: method, accuracy, command term or concept. Those four categories have four different remedies and four different session counts, and guessing between them is the usual wasted month.

faqs.question: Should a tutor set work between sessions, and how much?
faqs.answer: Yes, and as a numbered list rather than an instruction. Four specific questions in a stated order, with the hardest third rather than last, is a plan a busy Dubai student can execute. "Keep practising past papers" is a wish and it is what loses the week. The amount matters less than the specificity: two well-chosen questions that get done beat ten that do not. The following session should open by checking the list, which is also how you know it mattered.

faqs.question: What does a credible answer about examiner experience sound like?
faqs.answer: A board, a subject, a level and a recent series, offered without being pressed. Examiner status is current or it is nothing, and it confers no access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries. A tutor who implies otherwise is either overstating or describing something that would end a candidacy. The useful follow-up is what the experience changes in a lesson: usually a sharper read of command terms and mark allocations, which is worth something but is not a different syllabus.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who asks for the school's assessment calendar a good sign?
faqs.answer: One of the better ones. Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines for drafts, their own mock windows and their own moderation timetable, and those dates do not coincide across the emirate. A tutor who asks for the calendar intends to work to your child's real year rather than a generic one. A tutor who never asks will eventually do useful work in the wrong month, which is a quiet and entirely avoidable waste.

faqs.question: How do we compare two tutors who both sound convincing?
faqs.answer: Put their written diagnoses side by side. Both will have been pleasant for an hour; only one may have named a component, an error category and four specific questions. Read for specificity: which paper, which criterion, which command term, which topic. Then compare the practical terms, in writing: where marking happens, what the cancellation window is, whether the rate changes near the May session, and what happens at week six if nothing has moved.

faqs.question: What should we do if progress stalls after eight weeks in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Look at which of three things stalled. If the comparison script has not moved on the component worked on, the diagnosis was wrong and deserves re-testing rather than more of the same. If the topic checklist moved but exam-condition scripts did not, the student can do the work slowly and not under time, which is a different fix. If session notes have stopped naming specifics, the scripts are not being read and the specialist should change. All three are ordinary.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai tutor tell us the grade our child will finish with?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers a number has told you how they handle evidence. Nobody can promise a 7, a points total or a grade improvement, and no refund arrangement makes such a promise credible. Grade boundaries are set after papers are sat and marked and vary by session. An experienced teacher can say roughly what a mark has historically converted to, and should say the word roughly. Predicted grades belong to the school, not to a private tutor.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge at the top of the range, and why?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 reach AED 500-650 or more an hour at the examiner-experienced end, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. The top band is sold on a claim rather than a qualification, which is why it should be asked to evidence itself: board, subject, recent series. The real question is whether the extra buys something your child's specific component needs.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to speak to our child's Diploma coordinator?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and not without you asking. Session notes go to the family, and what you share with the school is your decision and your child's. Some Dubai families forward a marked script and a diagnosis when a predicted grade is being set, and most coordinators read them with interest. What a tutor must never do is present private marking as carrying standing inside the school's own assessment process, because it carries none.

faqs.question: Is the trial lesson free, and what is attached to it?
faqs.answer: It is free, it takes no card details, and nothing is booked afterwards unless you come back. The condition worth stating is that it is one session with one matched specialist, sixty minutes, and it produces a written diagnosis rather than an open-ended assessment. You keep the diagnosis whether you continue or not. Where a provider's trial does require card details or auto-enrols you into a package, that condition should be visible on the same screen as the word free.

faqs.question: Why does the lesson happen over live video for Dubai families?
faqs.answer: Because it widens the pool and lengthens the hour. Matching on subject and level across the whole pool rather than within a twenty-minute drive is the difference between a Higher Level specialist and the nearest available science teacher. A video hour also contains close to sixty minutes of teaching against thirty-five to forty for a visit, since there is no journey, no settling and marking happens between sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody suitable is free for our subject and level?
faqs.answer: You get a date rather than a substitute. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest, along with Higher Level Computer Science and less common Language B options. Putting a Higher Level student with somebody who teaches the subject group but not the level costs six weeks, which is worse than a fortnight of waiting. We will also say what is worth working on unsupervised in the meantime without consolidating the same errors.

dubai/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Use the scorecard on us first
dubai/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: There is no ranking to win, so the useful thing this page can offer is the measurement. Send the three documents, book a free trial lesson with no card details, and fill in the scorecard while the hour runs rather than afterwards. Then fix four checkpoints at weeks one, three, six and eight before any payment, and keep the baseline script however poor it looks. If the comparison at week six has not moved, change the plan or change the specialist. Both are ordinary, and both are cheaper than politeness.

dubai/best-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below lists the syllabus codes they teach and the components they mark most often, because an IGCSE specialism is narrower than a subject. A tutor strong on Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 is not automatically the right match for 0607 investigation work, and the profiles are written so you can see the difference before booking.

intro.heading: Start from the component, not the subject
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is assembled from components, and a student is almost never equally weak across all of them. A child described at school as struggling in physics may be entirely sound on the mechanics questions in the main written paper and losing a quarter of the available marks on the practical-skills component, where the demands are reading a scale accurately, tabulating with units in the column heading and writing a conclusion that refers back to the data. Those are different problems with different fixes, and a tutor who starts with the subject rather than the component will spend six weeks on the wrong one.

So the first question we ask a Dubai family is not what grade your child is on. It is which board, which syllabus code, which tier, and which paper the lost marks sit on. Cambridge 0580 and Cambridge 0607 are both IGCSE mathematics and they assess different things with different equipment. Pearson 4PH1 and Cambridge 0625 are both IGCSE physics and only one of them has a separate practical paper. These distinctions sound administrative until you watch a student revise diligently for a paper structure they will not meet.

The tier decision deserves the same precision. Cambridge builds Core papers to award grades C to G and Extended papers to award A* to E, which means the tier a school enters a child for places a ceiling on the possible outcome long before the exam. A capable student sitting Core because they were quiet in Year 9 has their result capped, and a student placed on Extended who cannot yet complete a paper inside the time is answering questions pitched above their working speed. Both situations are common in large Dubai year groups and both are visible on one marked past paper.

There is a reason the phrase home tutor dominates this search. For a generation of parents in the UAE, private tuition meant somebody arriving after dinner with a folder of worksheets. That model still exists in Dubai and the market prices it accordingly, because the tutor is paid for the drive as well as the teaching. What has changed is the alternative: a one-to-one lesson over video, with a shared workspace, an annotated script that gets saved, and a tutor chosen for the component rather than for the postcode.

To be exact about what IB Gram provides: lessons for Dubai families are delivered one to one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, because sending a tutor to a residential address is a service we run only in India. The sections below answer the home-tutoring question honestly, including what the Dubai market charges and what the travel does to an evening, and then get on with the subject content, which is what the search was really about.

dubai/best-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Three tier and route decisions determine what an IGCSE student is actually sitting, and a fourth stage decides what the grades are for. Each has its own component structure, and each produces a different kind of tutoring brief.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: Core candidates sit a shorter, lower-demand set of papers, and Cambridge builds the tier to award grades C to G. The content is a subset rather than a different subject. Questions are more structured, with fewer multi-step problems and more single-mark recall, which rewards accuracy and punishes gaps in number work.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools with large year groups often use Year 9 data to allocate Core, then revisit the decision late. If your child is scoring in the top quarter of the Core mark range by the spring of Year 10, that is worth raising with the head of department, and a marked Extended paper is the evidence that moves the conversation along.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended papers are built to award A* to E and contain the multi-step questions, the extended-response writing and the quantitative work that a sixth form assumes. Most mark loss here is structural rather than topical: a first step unmarked because it was done mentally, a comparison written as two descriptions, a graph plotted accurately with unlabelled axes.
programmes.countryNote: The majority of British-curriculum schools in Dubai enter most of a year group for Extended in maths and the sciences. That makes timed practice on single papers more important than extra content delivery, because the constraint for many students is working speed under exam conditions rather than knowledge of the syllabus.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson tiers its International GCSE as Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and the component architecture differs subject by subject. Mathematics A allows a calculator in both papers. Physics, chemistry and biology assess practical skills inside the written papers instead of in a separate component.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools enter different departments with different boards, so a single student may sit Cambridge sciences and Pearson mathematics in the same series. That matters for revision: the formula provision and the question wording differ, and a student who has practised on the wrong board's papers will meet a structure they have not rehearsed.

programmes.name: What the grades are for: A Level, Diploma and equivalency
programmes.description: IGCSE grades function as entry criteria. Sixth forms set subject-specific thresholds, typically a grade 6 or B in the subject to be continued and often in mathematics and English as well. The gap between an IGCSE grade and the first term of an A Level or Diploma course is mostly about independent working rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One competing page in this market states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule through the Ministry before relying on it.

dubai/best-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where a Dubai family most often asks what a single session could fix. Each entry names the syllabus code, the component that carries the risk and the kind of mark that goes missing, because that is the level at which tutoring either works or does not.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A bridging qualification into A Level, taken alongside or after 0580 Extended. Calculus and trigonometric identities produce the losses, usually because students apply a differentiation rule correctly and then cannot interpret what the derivative means in the question's context. Expect to work on worded questions rather than on technique.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences in one award, so breadth with little depth. Students lose marks by giving a biology-style descriptive answer to a physics calculation question and by running out of time, because the paper moves between disciplines faster than revision habits do. Paper-order practice helps more than extra content.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Two practical components alongside the theory paper, assessed on documents produced to a brief. Marks go missing on specification detail: a field type set incorrectly, a required evidence document not saved, a mail merge that works but is not demonstrated. The fix is working through the brief's checklist until it becomes mechanical.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are where candidates concede most marks. Students who can write working Python often lose marks for not following the syllabus pseudocode conventions, and trace tables are abandoned halfway. Both are habit problems that respond quickly to marked practice.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall is necessary and not sufficient. The marks sit in using the figure, map or graph provided, and in questions asking for evaluation where candidates write description. Skills questions on cross-sections and population pyramids are reliably underpractised in Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge 0470)
subjects.description: Source utility questions are the discriminator. Candidates summarise a source's content when the question asks how useful it is and why, and essay answers narrate events rather than explaining causation. Two marked answers a week is worth more than another pass through the depth study.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Format discipline carries the marks. A correct figure in the wrong statement, a missing heading or an unbalanced trial balance costs marks that the candidate's understanding deserved. Students who learn the layouts to the point of boredom score well; those who understand the concepts and improvise do not.

subjects.name: French (Cambridge 0520)
subjects.description: Four skills, and the speaking component is where Dubai candidates are least rehearsed because practice requires a partner. Writing marks are lost on tense accuracy and on not answering every bullet in the task. Short, frequent spoken practice beats long written exercises here.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: A literary and analytical paper rather than a conversational one, demanding control of formal register and of extended written argument in Standard Arabic. Students fluent at home often lose marks on structure and on the summary task's word discipline rather than on language.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: A distinct qualification from 0508, built for learners rather than first-language speakers, with tighter and more predictable tasks. Mark loss clusters in reading comprehension where candidates lift whole lines and in writing where the register asked for is ignored.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (Cambridge 0457)
subjects.description: Assessed through a written exam and team and individual work, with marks given for research, reasoning and reflection rather than content recall. Candidates lose marks for unevidenced assertion and for reflection that describes what happened instead of what the student would change.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Included here for its practical-skills component, which is where online teaching has to be explicit. Reading a burette, identifying the control variable and explaining anomalies are taught through marking the student's own tables and conclusions rather than by watching a demonstration.

sections.heading: What a home tutor in Dubai means in practice, and what we do instead
paragraphs: The traditional arrangement is straightforward: a tutor drives to a community, teaches for an hour or ninety minutes, and leaves. Published Dubai rate guides for 2026 put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is accounted for, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The gap between the two columns is mostly the drive.

The drive is not only a price. Between four and seven in the evening, a trip from Jumeirah to Mirdif or from Marina to Nad Al Sheba can take longer than the lesson, which has three consequences a family feels. The tutor's realistic capacity is two or three sessions an evening, so the slots on offer are few and inflexible. A late arrival shortens the lesson rather than the drive. And rescheduling after a mock week or a school fixture is hard, because a round trip has to be refitted rather than a calendar entry moved.

The second consequence is subtler and matters more for IGCSE. The pool a family can reach is the set of tutors willing to drive to their community at that hour. For Mathematics 0580 at Core tier that pool is large enough. For a Cambridge 0607 investigation paper, for Arabic as a First Language 0508, for Additional Mathematics 0606 or for a practical-skills component in a specific science, it narrows to whoever is nearby, which is not the same as whoever is right.

IB Gram's answer is to keep the one-to-one teaching and drop the travel. Lessons run live over video with a shared workspace, the student photographs handwritten work, the tutor annotates it on screen, and the annotated version is saved so a parent can keep it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision and its grade ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the single most consequential decision in a Cambridge IGCSE and the one parents are least often consulted about. Cambridge builds Core papers to award grades C to G and Extended papers to award A* to E. The tier therefore sets a ceiling, and the ceiling is fixed at entry rather than at the exam. A student capable of a B who is entered for Core cannot be awarded one, however well they perform on the day.

Schools make the decision for sound operational reasons: set placement, Year 9 data, teaching groups that have to be taught one syllabus route. Those reasons are about the cohort. A family's question is about one child, and the two can diverge, particularly for a student who was quiet in Year 9, arrived mid-year from another curriculum, or had a weak term for reasons unrelated to ability.

The evidence that settles it is not an opinion. Set one Core paper and one Extended paper, both timed, both marked against the published scheme, and look at two things: the mark, and how far the student got. A child scoring near the top of the Core range has their ceiling in the wrong place. A child who scores respectably on Extended questions but completes only two-thirds of the paper has a working-speed problem that is fixable with practice, not a tier problem.

The decision is also time-bound, which is where families get caught. Cambridge's final entry deadline for its March 2027 series falls on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. A tier conversation in January is a conversation about the following series. Raise it a term before the deadline, with marked papers in hand, and it is a short discussion.

sections.heading: What each kind of component actually assesses
paragraphs: Components are not interchangeable slices of a subject. Each one assesses a different thing and each has its own failure mode, which is why a student's grade can be held down by one component while the rest are fine. Knowing which type of component is costing marks turns a vague brief into a short, finishable piece of work.

Short structured questions assess recall and precision. Candidates lose marks here for omissions rather than errors: a unit left off, an observation not stated, a named example missing. Extended-response questions assess organisation as much as knowledge, which is why a student can write everything true about a topic and still score in the middle band. Data and source questions assess use of the material provided, and the commonest failure is answering from memory while the figure sits unexamined on the page.

Practical and skills components assess process. In Cambridge sciences this is a separate alternative-to-practical paper; in Pearson International GCSE sciences the same skills are assessed inside the written papers. Either way the marks go to identifying variables, tabulating properly, plotting accurately and explaining anomalies, none of which is learnt by watching an experiment. Coursework and portfolio components assess sustained independent work, and must be the student's own throughout.

The table maps each component type to the marks at stake and to the kind of session that addresses it. Note that in four of the six rows, the work is marking the student's own attempts rather than teaching new content. That ratio is why a diagnostic paper before lesson one changes what a family buys.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: What follows is specific rather than general, and it comes from marking Dubai candidates' scripts in these syllabuses. Each row names the syllabus, the component carrying the risk, the loss we see most, and what one or two sessions can realistically do about it. No row says revise more, because that is advice rather than teaching.

A pattern runs through the list. In the humanities the loss is answering a different question from the one asked, usually description where evaluation or utility was wanted. In the quantitative subjects it is unshown method and lost precision. In the languages it is register and task completion rather than vocabulary. In the vocational and applied subjects it is format and specification compliance, where a student who understands the material loses marks on presentation requirements.

This is also why the number of subjects a family supports matters more than the number of hours. Two subjects taught by component specialists, with marked work every fortnight, produces visible movement. Five subjects at one session each a week produces busy evenings and a student who is slightly better at everything and measurably better at nothing, which is the commonest way a Dubai family spends a term without a result.

Where a subject is not on this list, ask. The honest answer sometimes is that the right specialist for a minority language or an unusual option block is not free in the slot a family needs, in which case we say so with a realistic date rather than putting a generalist in the gap.

sections.heading: What a single sixty-minute session can honestly fix
paragraphs: Parents often ask whether one session is worth booking. Sometimes it genuinely is, and it is useful to be specific about which problems fit in an hour and which do not. The distinguishing feature is whether the problem is a habit, a misconception or a gap. Habits and misconceptions can move inside a session. Gaps take as long as the content takes.

A habit is something the student does automatically and wrongly: writing final answers without working, starting an essay without reading the command word, drawing graphs without labelling axes. One session of marking their own scripts against the scheme makes the cost visible in marks, which is more persuasive than instruction, and the behaviour usually changes within a fortnight.

A misconception is a specific wrong model: that osmosis moves salt, that a parallel circuit divides current by the number of branches, that a derivative is a gradient of a straight line. These are identifiable in minutes and correctable in one session, and they frequently explain a cluster of lost marks that looked like several separate problems.

A gap is content never taught or never learnt, and it takes the time it takes, usually a session per significant topic plus practice. The honest answer to a family with four weeks and six topics is that we can cover three properly or six superficially, and that the first option moves marks. sections.heading: Practical science when the tutor is not in the room
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online science teaching and it deserves a direct answer rather than reassurance. Cambridge assesses practical skills for most IGCSE sciences through a written alternative-to-practical paper, and Pearson assesses the same skills inside its written papers. In both cases the marks are awarded for reading instruments, tabulating data, plotting, identifying variables, explaining anomalies and drawing conclusions that refer to the data. All of that is assessed on paper.

What this means in practice is that the examined practical skill is a paper skill, and it is taught by marking the student's own tables, graphs and conclusions. A student who has done an experiment in the school laboratory and never had their write-up marked against the scheme will still lose the marks. A student who has annotated ten of their own tables with a tutor will not, whether or not they enjoyed the laboratory.

Where a school offers a coursework practical route, the position is different and we say so: the school supervises and assesses that component, and the work is the student's own under their teacher's supervision. A tutor's contribution is process coaching, never the production of content for a submission, and we will not work on an assessed practical write-up in any way that makes the thinking ours.

The school laboratory remains important for understanding, and nothing here suggests otherwise. The point is narrower: the marks on the practical component are won on the page, and the page is exactly what can be marked over video with the script annotated and saved for the family to keep.

sections.heading: Following the school's scheme of work rather than the syllabus order
paragraphs: A syllabus lists content; a scheme of work decides the order a particular school teaches it in. Those two things diverge more than families expect, and a tutor who follows the syllabus order will regularly teach something three weeks after the class assessment on it. For an IGCSE student, the useful sequence is the school's, because that is what the next test and the next report are based on.

So the second question we ask, after the board and the code, is what the class is doing now and what the next assessment covers. In Dubai this matters more than in a single-system market, because schools here set internal assessment weeks on their own calendars and mid-year arrivals are common. A student who joined in January from another curriculum has a gap defined by the difference between two schemes of work, not by the syllabus.

Following the school also makes the tutoring visible to the teacher, which is worth having. A student who arrives in class having already marked two past-paper questions on the current topic is a different student in that lesson, and the classroom teacher's feedback becomes another source of evidence rather than a separate track. Where a school's order is unclear, a single email from the parent asking for the term's plan usually resolves it.

There is one exception. In the final months before a series, the syllabus order stops mattering and the paper order takes over. At that point sessions are organised around whole timed papers and the losses they reveal, which cuts across topics by design.

sections.heading: Timing a session in a Dubai school week
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the shape of the Dubai week fails quietly. School runs, bus routes, mock weeks, Ramadan timings and the long summer all move when a student can concentrate, and a slot that was fine in October is unusable in March. Because lessons are over video there is no drive to re-plan, so the sensible approach is to expect the timetable to change two or three times a year and to agree in advance how.

Term-time evenings are the default, with 17:00 and 18:00 the most-requested slots and 16:00 workable only for families whose child is not on a bus. During mock weeks, sessions shift to the morning or to the weekend, and the content shifts to whole papers. In Ramadan many Dubai schools run shortened days, and families frequently ask for post-Iftar sessions, which work well because the student is rested and the house is quiet.

The summer is the underused opportunity. Students on a Cambridge June series finish in late June and come back in late August, and a short block in that window is where tier repair and content gaps are cheapest to fix, because nothing else is competing for the evening. For a student heading into Year 11, four or five sessions in August is worth more than ten in May.

sections.heading: Mock scripts, coursework and the limits on a tutor
paragraphs: A mock script is the most useful document a family owns and it is usually filed unread. It has been marked by the class teacher, it is recent, and it shows exactly where the marks went under timed conditions. The first thing we ask for, where it exists, is a photograph of the whole script including the parts the student got right, because the pattern matters more than any single question.

What a tutor does with it is re-mark selectively and compare. Where the teacher's mark and the published scheme disagree, that is worth a conversation with the school rather than a complaint; more often they agree and the student has simply not read the annotations. Converting a marked mock into a list of four recurring losses takes twenty minutes and gives a six-week plan a target.

On assessed coursework the limits are firm. A tutor may read the mark descriptors with the student, discuss whether a paragraph meets a band, explain why an argument does not follow from the evidence, and help a student plan backwards from the school's deadline. A tutor may not supply sentences that appear in a submission, restructure a piece so the reasoning becomes theirs, or work on the document while the student watches. Boards treat breaches as malpractice and the consequence lands on the student.

Official material is referenced and linked rather than reproduced. Syllabuses, specimen papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites, and that is where a family should get them. A tutor offering a private archive of papers and schemes is not providing access to anything the official sites do not already provide legitimately.

sections.heading: Getting matched, and what we will not promise
paragraphs: The practical steps are few. Tell us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the year group, plus which component the marks are going missing on if you know. Send a photograph of a marked mock if there is one. We set a diagnostic paper where there is not, mark it against the published scheme, and propose a tutor whose marking experience matches the diagnosis. A thirty-minute trial lesson follows, with no card details taken.

Matching takes two to three working days for common subjects. Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a First Language 0508, minority languages and some ICT practical components take longer, and we give a date rather than a reassurance. If the right specialist is in a different time zone, that constrains which evening slots exist, and we tell a family before they plan around a slot that does not exist.

Two things we will not do. We will not promise a grade, because the examiner marks the student's script and no tutoring arrangement controls that. And we will not quote a single hourly rate on a page like this, because the number depends on the subject, the tier and the number of sessions, and a figure printed here would be wrong for most families reading it. The market bands above are published so you can calibrate any quote, including ours.

What we will commit to is the evidence: a marked script every fortnight, a short written note naming the next two targets, and a straight answer when the sessions have done what they can and the remaining gap is classroom work.

process.title: Name the board, the code and the component
process.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended, Year 11, losing marks on the alternative-to-practical paper is a brief a tutor can act on. Chemistry help is not. If you do not know which component is costing the marks, send a marked mock and we will work it out before proposing anybody.

process.title: Send the marked mock, or sit a diagnostic
process.description: A recent teacher-marked script is the fastest route to a plan. Where there is none, we set a full past paper under timed conditions and mark it against the published scheme, sorting losses into habit, misconception and gap, because each of those needs a different number of sessions.

process.title: Settle the tier question if it is open
process.description: Where Core or Extended is still in play, we mark one paper from each tier and write a short comparison for the school meeting. The school decides entry; the family's contribution is evidence. Do this at least a term before the board's final entry deadline.

process.title: Meet the tutor in a free trial lesson
process.description: Thirty minutes with the specific tutor proposed, no card details taken, no obligation. Ask them which component carries your child's lost marks and how they would mark it. The answer tells you more than any profile, and if the fit is wrong we propose somebody else.

process.title: Run weekly sessions against the school's plan
process.description: Sessions follow the school's scheme of work during the year and switch to whole timed papers as a series approaches. Marked work arrives every fortnight with a note naming two targets, and the slot moves when mock weeks or Ramadan timings require it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor who has marked hundreds of alternative-to-practical scripts is a different proposition from one who knows chemistry well. We match on the component where the marks are being lost, which is why the first conversation is about papers rather than about availability.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice backed by two marked papers
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended set different grade ceilings, and the decision is usually made on cohort data. We produce one marked paper from each tier and a written comparison, so a family can raise the question with the school before the entry deadline closes it.

whyPoints.title: The school's order, not the syllabus order
whyPoints.description: Sessions follow what the class is doing and what the next assessment covers, so the work is visible to the classroom teacher and useful in the next lesson. In the final months that flips deliberately to whole papers, because by then paper order is what matters.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught as paper skills
whyPoints.description: The examined practical marks are awarded for tabulating, plotting, identifying variables and explaining anomalies, all of which are assessed in writing. We teach them by marking the student's own tables and conclusions rather than by describing experiments.

whyPoints.title: A timetable that survives the year
whyPoints.description: Mock weeks, Ramadan and study leave all move when a student can work. With no drive to re-plan, sessions shift to mornings, weekends or post-Iftar slots as the term requires, and we agree that pattern at the start rather than improvising in March.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is process coaching on the student's own draft. Nothing is supplied for a submission, and official syllabus material is linked rather than redistributed. That boundary protects the student's result, which is the only reason any of this is being bought.

faqs.question: Can we book an IGCSE home tutor who comes to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor arriving at a residential address is a service we run only in India. For Dubai families the teaching is one to one over live video, at a time set on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's handwritten work photographed and marked on screen so the annotated version is saved. The honest case for that arrangement is the tutor pool: you can work with the specialist who marks the component your child is losing marks on, rather than the tutor who is willing to drive to your community at six in the evening.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor cost in Dubai once travel is counted?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 Dubai rate guides put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The difference is largely the drive, which the tutor has to price. There is a second, hidden cost: evening traffic shortens the lesson rather than the commute, so a family can pay for sixty minutes and receive forty-five. Ask any provider whether marked written feedback is included, because that is what makes two similar hourly rates incomparable.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai students lose the most marks in?
faqs.answer: By volume of requests, Mathematics 0580 Extended, the separate sciences and English First Language 0500. By severity of avoidable loss, the pattern is clearer than the subject list: unshown method in the quantitative subjects, description where evaluation was asked for in the humanities, and the practical-skills component across all three sciences. In our experience the practical component is the most consistently underprepared, because students associate it with laboratory work rather than with reading scales, tabulating with units and writing conclusions that refer to the data. All of those are marked on paper.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge IGCSE Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: They are different routes through the same syllabus with different papers and different grade ceilings. Cambridge builds Core papers to award grades C to G and Extended papers to award A* to E, so the tier a school enters a child for caps the possible result. Core questions are more structured with more single-mark recall; Extended carries multi-step problems and extended-response writing. Core covers a defined subset of the content. If your child is scoring near the top of the Core range, raise the tier question with the school, and do it a term before the board's final entry deadline rather than after it.

faqs.question: Can a single session fix a topic my child has never understood?
faqs.answer: If the problem is a misconception, often yes. A student who believes osmosis moves salt, or that a parallel circuit divides current by the number of branches, holds a specific wrong model that can be identified in minutes and corrected in one session, and it usually explains a cluster of lost marks that looked like several problems. If the problem is content never taught, no: expect roughly a session per significant topic plus practice. The useful first step is a marked paper, because it shows which of the two you are dealing with before you buy a term of lessons.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: For most Cambridge IGCSE sciences the practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper, and Pearson assesses the same skills inside its written papers. The marks go to reading instruments, tabulating data with units in the headings, plotting accurately, identifying variables, explaining anomalies and writing conclusions that refer to the data. Those are paper skills and they are taught by marking the student's own tables, graphs and conclusions. Where a school runs a supervised coursework practical route, the school assesses it, the work is the student's own, and a tutor's role is process coaching only.

faqs.question: My child writes long answers but still scores low marks - why?
faqs.answer: Almost always structure rather than knowledge. Extended-response questions award marks for development and comparison, not for the number of true statements present. A student who writes six accurate sentences about a topic without linking them to the question, or who describes two things when asked to compare them, collects the content marks and none of the rest. The fix is mechanical and fast: take one of their own paragraphs, read the mark descriptors beside it, and rebuild it so each sentence does a job the scheme pays for. Two fortnights of that usually moves the band.

faqs.question: Is it better to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, for two reasons. The tier decision is still open, which is the single most consequential variable in a Cambridge IGCSE, and there is time for habits to change before they are tested under pressure. Year 10 work can also be slower and more diagnostic: one session a week, a marked script every fortnight, and the content gaps closed as they appear. Year 11 tutoring is necessarily narrower, built around whole timed papers and two subjects at most. It still works, but it is repair rather than construction and the ceiling is lower.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does one IGCSE subject need?
faqs.answer: One sixty-minute session a week is the standard and it is enough for most students, provided the week also contains the practice the session sets. Two sessions a week makes sense in the final term, or where a student has a genuine content gap to close against a deadline. Beyond that, the limit is not the tutor but the student's capacity to practise between lessons, and more contact time with less independent work produces a dependent learner. Two subjects supported properly beats four supported thinly, which is the commonest spending mistake in this market.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a later slot during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Many Dubai schools run shortened days during Ramadan, routines shift, and an early-evening slot that worked in February stops working. Post-Iftar sessions are popular because the student is rested and the house is quiet, and shorter, more frequent sessions often suit the month better than a single long one. Because lessons are over video there is no drive to re-plan around, so moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a negotiation. We agree the Ramadan pattern in advance where the month falls inside a booking.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's school scheme of work or the syllabus?
faqs.answer: The school's scheme of work during the year, and the paper order in the final months. A syllabus lists content; a scheme of work decides the order one school teaches it in, and those diverge enough that a tutor following the syllabus will regularly cover a topic weeks after the class was assessed on it. We ask what the class is doing now and what the next assessment covers. That keeps the tutoring useful in the next lesson and makes the classroom teacher's feedback another source of evidence rather than a separate track.

faqs.question: What does the tutor do with a mock paper my child has already sat?
faqs.answer: Re-marks parts of it and reduces it to a short list. Send a photograph of the whole script, including the questions your child answered well, because the pattern matters more than any single answer. We compare the teacher's marking with the published scheme, identify the four losses that recur, and build the next six weeks around those. Most students have never read the annotations on their own mock, which makes a twenty-minute review of it the highest-value work available at the start of an arrangement, and it costs nothing to send.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do the students you support attend?
faqs.answer: Across the emirate: the long-established British-curriculum schools in Jumeirah and Al Safa, the large all-through schools in Al Barsha and Dubai Hills, the Mirdif and Deira clusters with their mixed British and Indian curriculum intakes, and the newer schools in Sports City, Motor City and the Jumeirah Village communities. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, so the spread is wide. We name schools to describe that landscape and nothing more; no affiliation or endorsement with any school or group is implied.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor start once we ask for one?
faqs.answer: Two to three working days for common IGCSE subjects, which covers mathematics, the separate sciences, English and the main humanities. Longer for Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a First Language 0508, minority languages and some ICT practical components, where the pool of genuine specialists is small. We give a date rather than a reassurance, and if the right person is in a different time zone we say which evening slots that makes possible before a family plans around one that does not exist.

dubai/best-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Send the marked mock and name the component
dubai/best-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to a useful first session is a photograph of your child's most recent marked paper, with the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the year group. We will reduce it to the four losses that repeat, tell you whether each is a habit, a misconception or a gap, and propose the tutor who marks that component most often. A thirty-minute trial lesson follows with no card details taken. If the tier question is still open, say so, because that conversation needs to happen a term before the board's entry deadline rather than after it.

Some teach almost entirely on a shared whiteboard; others work from the student's photographed script. Both work; knowing which you are getting helps you judge the trial.

intro.heading: The craft question nobody asks in the trial
paragraphs: Parents interviewing an online tutor almost always ask about qualifications and almost never ask about method. That is the wrong way round. Subject knowledge at IGCSE level is widely available in Dubai, and a graduate who scored well in chemistry eight years ago can explain chemistry. What is scarce is the ability to hold a fifteen-year-old's attention through a screen, see what they are actually writing, and intervene at the moment the misunderstanding happens rather than at the end of the hour.

That ability shows up in small mechanics. Does the tutor ask the student to work and then watch them work, or do they talk and then ask if it made sense? Does the student's handwriting appear on screen, or does the tutor narrate over a slide? Is there a moment in the first ten minutes where the student has to produce something, so the tutor learns what they can do rather than what they say they can do? These are observable in thirty minutes and they predict the next six months.

Online delivery also changes what the evidence looks like, usually for the better. A paper script marked in a living room stays in the house and gets lost. A script photographed, annotated on screen and saved can be re-read by a parent, compared with the one from three weeks earlier, and shown to a classroom teacher. The record is a by-product of the medium rather than something a tutor has to be chased for.

There are honest limits and this page states them. A Year 7 student who needs somebody physically beside them to stay on task is a harder case online than in a room. A subject assessed through making physical objects does not transfer cleanly. A household without a quiet corner and a stable connection will have a worse experience than one with both. None of those is fatal and all of them are worth knowing in advance rather than discovering in week three.

The upside is reach, and in a market the size of Dubai's that matters more than it would in a small town. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of that enrolment, which means a very wide spread of syllabus combinations and option blocks. A family whose child sits an unusual pairing, or a subject their school teaches in a combined group, is far more likely to find the right specialist in a pool defined by the hour of the day than in one defined by driving distance at six in the evening.

What a Dubai family gets from this model is reach. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video, so the person teaching Cambridge 0625 Physics to a student in Dubai Creek Harbour is chosen for having marked that paper repeatedly, not for living nearby. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, because tutors travelling to an address is a service we run only in India. Everything below is about making the online version as good as it can be rather than apologising for it.

dubai/best-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Online delivery works differently at each stage of an IGCSE journey, because what the student needs from the medium changes. Younger students need structure and shorter blocks; exam-year students need whole papers and live marking; private candidates need administrative help as much as teaching.

programmes.name: Year 9 into IGCSE, online
programmes.description: The year before the syllabus starts suits shorter online blocks: two thirty-minute sessions rather than one hour, with work set between them. Attention is the constraint at this age, not content, and a tutor who runs a thirty-minute session with three distinct activities will get more out of a Year 9 student than one who talks for sixty.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use Year 9 outcomes to allocate sets and tiers for Year 10, so the practical aim of online work in this year is to make sure the allocation reflects the student rather than a quiet term. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October, which gives a natural checkpoint to work towards.

programmes.name: IGCSE Years 10 and 11, online
programmes.description: The core use case. One sixty-minute session a week per subject, the student's work photographed and marked on screen, and a fortnightly saved script. Live marking is the thing online delivery does better than a living room, because the tutor can annotate, the student can see each annotation appear, and the file is kept.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai school weeks are busy with fixtures, assessment weeks and shortened Ramadan days, and a video slot can move without anyone re-planning a drive across the city. That flexibility is worth more over an academic year than most families expect when they first compare the two models.

programmes.name: Private candidates and retakes
programmes.description: Students sitting a subject outside their school's entry, retaking after a series, or studying a subject their school does not offer. Teaching is the straightforward part; the administration is not. Entry must go through a centre that accepts external candidates, and the centre's internal deadline sits before the board's.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai examination centres accept private candidates, each with its own closing date ahead of the board's final entry deadline. Where a subject carries a coursework or supervised practical component, a centre may not offer it, which usually points a family towards a syllabus route assessed entirely by written paper. We check this before teaching is booked.

programmes.name: The bridge into A Level and the Diploma
programmes.description: Online sessions in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 are the cheapest academic insurance available, because nothing competes for the time. The work is about independent study habits and the specific content step between an IGCSE grade and the first term of a post-16 course, which is steeper in mathematics and the sciences than elsewhere.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify current requirements through the Ministry; IB Gram does not perform equivalency.

dubai/best-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subjects do not all behave the same way over video. What follows is each popular IGCSE syllabus with the specific thing a tutor has to do differently on screen, and where the medium is actually an advantage.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Works well, provided the student writes and the tutor watches rather than the reverse. A shared whiteboard with the student holding the pen for most of the hour is the arrangement that produces progress; a tutor demonstrating elegant solutions while the student watches produces the illusion of it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Diagram-heavy, which suits a screen: ray diagrams and circuits can be drawn, corrected and redrawn in seconds. The practical-skills paper is taught by marking the student's own tables and graphs, which is exactly what the component assesses, so nothing is lost by the medium.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Equation work and mole calculations transfer directly. The honest gap is the feel of a titration, which the school laboratory provides and we do not; what we teach is reading the burette scale, tabulating with units and explaining anomalies, because those are the marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and command-word precision are the work, and both are better on screen because the student's own sentence can be rewritten in front of them. Genetics crosses benefit particularly: a tutor can see immediately whether the student set out the key before the cross.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: The strongest case for online delivery of all. The student's writing is shared as a document, annotated live, and the two versions sit side by side. Teaching analysis of a writer's choices requires text on a screen that both people can mark, which is awkward on paper and natural here.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475)
subjects.description: Extract-based questions are ideal for a shared screen: the passage is annotated jointly before any writing happens. The risk online is a discussion that feels productive and produces no marked writing, so sessions are structured to end with a timed paragraph.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: Includes listening and speaking components, both of which work over video given a decent microphone. The speaking practice is arguably better online, because the student can be recorded with permission, listen back and hear their own hesitations rather than being told about them.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application, which means reading a stem together and highlighting the data that must appear in the answer. A shared document makes that visible; a tutor describing good practice does not. Evaluation paragraphs are drafted in the session and marked immediately.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are the discriminator and a shared whiteboard handles them well. Students draw the curve, shift the wrong one, and see it corrected in the same minute, which is a faster loop than a weekly paper exchange allows.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are typed and shared, which removes the handwriting problem entirely. The tutor can run a student's logic line by line in view of both, and the syllabus pseudocode conventions get enforced as the student writes rather than afterwards.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, cross-sections and population pyramids are easier to teach on a shared screen than on paper, because the figure can be zoomed and annotated. Case-study work needs discipline, as the temptation online is discussion rather than marked answers.

subjects.name: Art and Design (Cambridge 0400)
subjects.description: The honest limit case. Critique of photographed work, sketchbook planning and written components can be supported online, but the making is physical and happens in the studio with the school's own supervision. We say so rather than pretending the medium is neutral here.
