dubai/bluewaters-island.programmesIntro: Three programmes run across the schools this community uses. The notes below describe what each one demands of the hours a student has left after the crossing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, examined by terminal papers. Cambridge uses four-digit codes with a Core and Extended split that fixes the grade ceiling at entry; Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 with modular entry on some subjects. The work that moves marks in the final two terms is timed past-paper practice, which has no timetabled slot anywhere.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge runs June and November series with a March series in some regions. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and states that candidates who use the wrong zone timetable are not its responsibility.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The programme assumes a large quantity of independent work, and for a student losing ninety minutes a day to travel that assumption is the problem rather than the content.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every IB session, upload and results date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. This page publishes no IB dates, because none could be verified from the IB directly for this project, and the school's own internal deadlines bind a student weeks earlier in any case.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, totalling thirty-two and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. Tasks assess some criteria and not others, so a student who revises content before a task weighted towards process or communication sees no improvement at all.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from the island sits mainly in Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh. Because assessment is continuous, a slip shows up earlier than it would in an IGCSE course, which is useful for a household that has limited hours and needs to spend them on the right subject.

dubai/bluewaters-island.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects requested most often from this community, described by the specific marks at stake rather than by syllabus content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with reasoning marks dominating: a correct answer without justification scores a fraction of the credit available. Higher Level adds a long problem-solving paper that needs stamina, which is hard to build in a session that starts after a long journey.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology. Marks are lost presenting a test without its hypothesis, assumptions or a conclusion in context, and the exploration often repeats a textbook procedure rather than interpreting a result.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: The move from recall to derivation catches strong IGCSE students in the first Diploma term. Uncertainty handling in practical work is examinable and almost never deliberately practised, and at IGCSE the recurring loss is circuit reasoning under changed conditions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and mole calculations account for most lost marks. Higher Level depth in energetics and kinetics cannot be absorbed in a final term, which is why the subject rewards a steady weekly slot more than most.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The volume of content pushes students into rereading instead of answering. Marks follow command terms precisely, and the fastest gain available in this subject is the habit of answering the verb that was printed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision decides grades, and an unlabelled axis costs marks the prose cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative questions, and the commentaries need published articles chosen to support the required analysis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is an unseen guided analysis, so rereading set texts does not prepare for it. The individual oral needs a global issue and two extracts prepared months in advance, which suits a long steady arrangement rather than a late rescue.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and comprehension under time pressure. The common loss is register rather than language: a strong piece in the wrong form for the stated audience loses marks before the English is assessed at all.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus rather than recall of frameworks earns the marks. The internal assessment depends on an organisation that will supply usable figures, a choice best made early in the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Taught in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Students who join Dubai schooling later need script and vocabulary work the timetable cannot pace individually.

dubai/bluewaters-island.regionsIntro: What distinguishes the areas around Bluewaters is the direction of the journey and what it costs at four in the afternoon.

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Directly across the footbridge and the island's nearest neighbour. Children at schools reached through JBR gain ten minutes over those heading inland, which is enough to make a 16:45 slot rather than a 17:15 one.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: A few minutes south across the bridge, and the shortest route to the Marina and Al Sufouh school corridor. The internal Marina roads are the bottleneck rather than the bridge itself in the mid-afternoon.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where several of the long-established schools used by island families sit. The morning run is straightforward; the return between 15:00 and 16:00 is the slowest regular journey this community makes.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with established primary and secondary provision. A short distance that behaves badly at peak because of the interchange rather than the distance.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The widest choice of schools reachable from the island, including IB continuum provision. Also the longest afternoon, which is why Diploma students on this route often take later evening slots.

regions.name: Emirates Living, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: Villa communities inland with their own schools. Island families sometimes choose schools here for the upper year groups, accepting a longer journey in exchange for option choice.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Further along the same inland corridor. The journey is tolerable outside peak and poor within it, so households on this route tend to anchor their main session at a weekend.

schoolClusters.city: The Marina and Al Sufouh corridor
schoolClusters.note: The closest established schools to the island, reached across the bridge and down the coast. Mostly British curriculum with IGCSE at sixteen, plus IB provision, and the shortest afternoon journeys available to island households.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with the broadest curriculum choice reachable from Bluewaters including American and IB continuum routes. Larger upper year groups, at the cost of the longest regular return journey.

dubai/bluewaters-island.modesIntro: Three formats cover what this community needs, and the choice follows from how much usable time the crossing leaves rather than from the subject.

modes.title: One anchored weekly session
modes.description: A single well-designed session each week in the household's best slot, with work set for the days in between. For a household with two usable slots and homework competing for one of them, one properly used hour beats two badly placed ones. The session is designed to leave the student with specific work rather than general reassurance.

modes.title: Weekend-anchored arrangement
modes.description: The main ninety-minute session on a Friday or Saturday morning, when nobody has crossed a bridge and nobody is tired, with a short weekday review if useful. This is the pattern that holds for Diploma students and for families whose afternoons are unpredictable.

modes.description: A concentrated block across a term break with a defined objective and an end point: closing a specific backlog, building a foundation before a new course, or preparing one component. Not a general top-up, and not a substitute for term-time work.

sections.heading: What the crossing actually costs, by destination
paragraphs: Bluewaters is well connected for an island and that is not the same as being well placed for a school run. Everything off the island goes through the bridge, and the bridge feeds into the Marina road network and then onto Sheikh Zayed Road. In the morning this works, because school buses and family cars leave before the corridor fills. In the afternoon the whole city is moving at once and the island is at the end of the queue rather than the start.

The numbers that matter are not distances. A school in Al Sufouh is a short drive and a long journey at 15:30. A school in Al Barsha South is further and sometimes quicker, because the route avoids the worst of the coastal congestion. Families regularly discover after a year that a school they rejected as too far produces an earlier arrival home than the one they chose.

The practical step is to measure rather than estimate. Write down the time your child actually walks through the door, every day, for two weeks, including the days that run late. Not the school finish time, not the bus timetable. Two weeks of that gives an honest distribution, and the slot chosen from it will still be working in March rather than having quietly collapsed in October.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a promise, because traffic varies and your school's finish time is the dominant variable. Use it to see the shape of the problem: by the time a child has crossed back, changed and eaten something, the usable window is between two and three hours, and school homework has the first claim on it.

sections.heading: What one weekly hour can actually cover in a term
paragraphs: Families routinely over-estimate what a single weekly session achieves, and providers rarely correct them. Twelve weeks at one hour is twelve hours of contact. That is enough to do a small number of things properly and nowhere near enough to teach a syllabus, and being honest about which is the difference between a satisfied household and a disappointed one in March.

Twelve hours will close a specific recurring error, build one technique to the point of reliability, teach three or four discrete topics to a secure standard, or supervise one coursework component from question to final check. It will not cover a two-year syllabus, repair a two-year arithmetic gap while also preparing papers, or carry three subjects at once. Attempting the second list produces shallow coverage of everything and secure knowledge of nothing.

The implication for a household with one usable slot is that the subject choice has to be deliberate. The right subject is usually the one where a small intervention changes the most: a foundation subject that other subjects depend on, a subject where the student is closest to a grade boundary, or a component with a fixed deadline. The wrong choice is the subject the student dislikes most, which is the instinctive answer and rarely the highest-return one.

Where more than one subject genuinely needs work, the honest options are to buy more hours, to sequence the subjects across terms rather than running them together, or to accept a lower target in one. We will say which we think applies rather than quietly spreading twelve hours across three subjects and letting the results arrive in August.

sections.heading: Why a late session can still work, if it is built properly
paragraphs: A 19:00 session with a tired fifteen-year-old is not doomed, but it cannot be a lecture. Attention late in the day is poor for absorbing new explanation and acceptable for retrieval, practice and discussion of work the student has already attempted. That distinction is the whole design principle for an island household, and it is why the shape of the session matters more here than its length.

Three things make a late hour productive. The first is that the student arrives having already attempted something: a past-paper question, a draft paragraph, a set of problems. Reviewing attempted work is cognitively easier than receiving new content and produces more learning per minute. The second is retrieval rather than re-explanation, where the tutor asks the student to produce what they know before being told, which feels harder and works better.

The third is spacing. Material met once and never revisited decays, which is why a student can genuinely learn something in October and have nothing left by February. Short, repeated returns to the same material across weeks produce durable knowledge from the same total minutes. In practice that means ten minutes of the session spent on something from three weeks ago, every week, and ten minutes of daily retrieval between sessions.

None of this is exotic and almost nobody does it, because it feels less productive than covering new ground. A session that revisits old material looks like going backwards to a parent watching from the next room. It is the opposite: new content covered once at 19:30 on a Tuesday is the least durable learning available, and revisiting it three times is what converts it into a mark in June.

sections.heading: When a holiday intensive is the right purchase
paragraphs: Island households travel, and term breaks are long. That makes the holiday intensive a tempting purchase and an easy one to get wrong. An intensive works when it has a specific, bounded objective: closing a named backlog, building the foundation for a course starting next term, or taking one coursework component from question to method. It fails when it is sold as a general top-up, because concentrated hours without a target produce coverage nobody retains.

The second condition is spacing. Ten consecutive daily sessions on new content violate everything in the previous section: material met once, never revisited, and then followed by six weeks of holiday during which it decays. A better shape is alternate days across two weeks with short practice in between, or a block followed by a weekly session when term resumes to consolidate what the block covered.

The third condition is honesty about the student. A teenager who has just finished a hard term may need a week of nothing before anything useful can happen, and an intensive beginning the day after term ends often buys resentment rather than progress. We would rather start in the second week of a break with a willing student than the first with an exhausted one.

Used properly, the breaks are genuinely valuable for this community because they remove the constraint the whole page is about. No crossing, no bus, no homework competing for the slot. A ninety-minute morning session with a rested student does several times the work of a 19:00 session in term time, which is the strongest argument for using a break at all.

sections.heading: Choosing a school by traffic direction, which an island address makes possible
paragraphs: One genuine advantage of this location is that it is not committed to a direction. A family in a distant villa community has two or three realistic school clusters. From Bluewaters, the Marina and Al Sufouh corridor, the Greens and the interchange, Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, and the Emirates Living schools are all reachable, which means the choice is unusually wide and can be made on criteria other than proximity.

The criterion most families under-use is the afternoon return rather than the morning run. Mornings are similar in every direction because everyone leaves early. Afternoons differ by twenty or thirty minutes depending on whether the route runs along the coast or inland, and twenty minutes a day is around sixty hours across a school year. That is more hours than a weekly tutoring arrangement provides in a term.

The second under-used criterion is upper year-group size. A school with an established sixth form runs more option columns, more Higher Level groups and more specialist teaching than a newer school with a strong primary phase, and KHDA inspection reports break performance down by phase and subject so that this can be checked rather than guessed. A strong overall band tells you about the whole institution; the phase and subject lines tell you about your child.

Dubai's supply is also changing, which widens the choice further. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven new private schools, four following the UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under an incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion, so a move considered now is not also a fee increase.

sections.heading: The specialist problem, and what this market charges
paragraphs: A visiting tutor coming to Bluewaters for a 17:00 lesson crosses the bridge at the worst hour, parks in a building they do not have access to, teaches for an hour and leaves into the evening traffic. That is three hours of their day for one paid hour, and the consequences are predictable: the rate carries the travel, the tutor takes fewer students, and your choice narrows to people prepared to make that journey at that time.

The second consequence costs marks rather than money. Subject depth is unevenly distributed, and the number of people who can teach Higher Level Physics, the quantitative half of Higher Level Economics, or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to a genuine standard is limited anywhere. Filtering that group by willingness to drive onto an island at five in the afternoon leaves very few. A parent insisting on a tutor in the room is choosing proximity over specialism.

The figures below are Dubai market rates collected in October 2026, each with its publisher named. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list, and the pattern is consistent across every level: in-home delivery sits above online delivery because travel is inside the price whether or not anyone itemises it. Bestimate's Dubai figures place home visits in a higher band than online lessons throughout.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is not a choice we can sell either way. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, which means an hour costs an hour, the slot can move when the afternoon collapses, and the tutor is chosen on subject and level rather than on geography. On an island with one bridge, that last point is the argument that matters.

sections.heading: Which weeks must be protected, and which can move
paragraphs: A household with one or two usable slots cannot afford to lose them randomly, and it also cannot hold them rigidly across a year that contains travel, Ramadan and school events. The answer is to decide in advance which weeks are protected and which are movable, rather than negotiating each one as it arrives.

The protected weeks are narrow and specific: the four before mocks, the six before a public examination series, the fortnight before an internal coursework deadline the school has set, and the first week back after a long break. That last one surprises people and matters most, because material half-learned before a break has decayed over it and a review session in the first week back prevents a term of compounding confusion.

The movable weeks are everything else. During Ramadan the school day shortens and sessions move later, often after Iftar, which suits older students and suits younger ones less. School trips, sports fixtures and family travel can displace a session without harm if the displacement is planned. A session shortened to thirty minutes because of traffic is also far better than one cancelled, because cancellations are how these arrangements quietly end.

Writing this down in September takes ten minutes and is the single strongest predictor of whether an arrangement survives to the following summer. Most do not, and they almost never end in a decision: they end in a missed week in October, a moved week in November, and a pause over a break that nobody restarts.

sections.heading: Getting started from Bluewaters Island
paragraphs: Begin with two weeks of arrival times, because every other decision depends on them. Send those alongside the school, the exact syllabus code and level from the examination entry, the most recent marked piece of work, and the date of the next school assessment. For a Diploma student, add the internal deadlines the school has set, which sit earlier than anything a board publishes.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor reads the marked work with the student and separates four problems that look identical on a report: content not known, technique not trained, timing lost under pressure, confidence gone. You receive a written summary naming which, and a recommendation on format and length based on your own arrival data rather than a standard template.

Where a household has one usable slot and two subjects that need work, we will say which subject should have it and why, and we will say if the honest answer is to buy more hours or to sequence the subjects across terms. Spreading twelve hours across three subjects is the comfortable answer and the one that produces nothing in August.

Three limits before any payment. We do not promise grades. We do not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE, so if you want someone at the door we are the wrong provider. We do not supply board past papers or mark schemes, which belong to the boards and are held officially by your school. And where a scarce specialism is involved we will tell you how long the match takes, and whether the only available specialist works hours that suit an early morning, before you commit.

process.title: Measure the return journey
process.description: Record the time your child actually arrives on the island for two weeks, including the late days. That distribution, rather than the school finish time, determines the slot and the session length that will still be working in March.

process.title: Send the academic detail
process.description: School, exact syllabus code and level from the examination entry, the most recent marked piece of work, the next assessment date, and for a Diploma student the school's internal coursework deadlines.

process.title: Diagnostic session
process.description: One online hour reading marked work with the student to establish whether the problem is content, technique, timing or confidence. The written summary names which, and recommends a weekday slot or a weekend anchor based on your arrival data.

process.title: Choose what the hour is for
process.description: With one or two usable slots, the objective has to be deliberate: one recurring error, one technique, three or four topics, or one coursework component. We will name the highest-return choice and say plainly what twelve hours cannot cover.

process.title: Agree protected and movable weeks
process.description: Mark the four weeks before mocks, the six before an examination series, the fortnight before a coursework deadline, and the first week back after a long break as protected. Everything else can move, including through Ramadan.

whyPoints.title: Designed for a short window
whyPoints.description: With one bridge and no school on the island, most households have one or two usable slots a week. Sessions are built for that reality: attempted work reviewed, retrieval rather than lecture, and spacing built in so a late hour still produces durable learning.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what an hour buys
whyPoints.description: Twelve weekly hours will close one recurring error, build one technique, teach three or four topics, or supervise one component. It will not teach a syllabus or carry three subjects, and we say so before you buy rather than in March.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, because nobody crosses a bridge
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the tutor is chosen for subject, level and board rather than for willingness to drive onto an island at five in the afternoon. For Higher Level sciences and quantitative subjects that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is free.

whyPoints.title: A calendar decided in advance
whyPoints.description: Protected weeks, movable weeks and Ramadan timing are agreed in September. Arrangements here almost never end in a decision; they end in attrition, and anticipating the year is what prevents it.

whyPoints.title: Nothing asserted without a source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure names its publisher and the month collected, every board date names the board that set it, and where a date could not be verified the page says so. No grade promises, no invented statistics, no claimed accreditation from any regulator or board.

faqs.question: How much of the afternoon does the crossing actually take?
faqs.answer: Enough to change what is possible. Everything off the island runs through the bridge into the Marina road network and onto Sheikh Zayed Road, and the afternoon return coincides with every school in Dubai finishing inside the same hour. Depending on the school cluster, children arrive back between roughly 16:15 and 17:40. After changing and eating, the usable window is two to three hours, with school homework having first claim, which is why most households here realistically have one or two tutoring slots a week rather than four.

faqs.question: Why does measuring arrival times matter more than picking a convenient slot?
faqs.answer: Because a slot that does not fit gets missed, then moved, then abandoned, and almost every failed tutoring arrangement in this community died that way rather than from poor teaching. Two weeks of recorded arrival times, including the late days, gives an honest distribution instead of an estimate. A slot chosen from that data survives the year. One chosen because it sounds reasonable collapses in October, usually after two missed sessions nobody intended to miss.

faqs.question: Is a 19:00 session with a tired teenager worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is built for the time of day. Late attention is poor for absorbing new explanation and acceptable for retrieval, practice and discussion of work already attempted. So the session should start from something the student has tried, use questioning rather than re-explanation, and spend ten minutes revisiting material from three weeks earlier. A late hour used that way produces durable learning. A late hour spent on new content at low attention produces very little, however well it is taught.

faqs.question: What can twelve hours of tutoring realistically achieve in a term?
faqs.answer: One of the following, done properly: closing a specific recurring error, building one technique to the point of reliability, teaching three or four discrete topics securely, or supervising one coursework component from question to final check. It cannot teach a two-year syllabus, repair a long-standing arithmetic gap while also preparing papers, or carry three subjects at once. Spreading twelve hours across three subjects is the comfortable option and the one that changes nothing by August.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one subject, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Usually not the one your child dislikes most, which is the instinctive answer. The highest-return choice is the subject where a small intervention changes the most: a foundation subject other subjects depend on, a subject where the student sits closest to a grade boundary, or a component with a fixed school deadline. We will name which applies after reading marked work, and if the honest answer is that two subjects genuinely need hours, we will say that rather than pretending one slot covers both.

faqs.question: What is spacing and why would a tutor spend time on old topics?
faqs.answer: Material met once and never revisited decays, which is why a student can learn something securely in October and have nothing left by February. Short repeated returns to the same material across weeks produce durable knowledge from the same total minutes. In practice that means around ten minutes of each session spent on something three weeks old. It looks like going backwards to a parent watching from the next room, and it is the step that converts a lesson into a mark in June.

faqs.question: Does rereading notes count as revision?
faqs.answer: Barely. Rereading produces familiarity, which feels like knowledge and is not the same thing. The student recognises the material and cannot produce it under examination conditions. Retrieval practice, where the student writes down or says what they know before checking, feels harder and works considerably better. Self-marking a timed paper against a published scheme is better still, because it teaches where marks actually sit in an answer. Rereading is the default because it is comfortable, not because it works.

faqs.question: Is a holiday intensive a good use of a term break?
faqs.answer: With a bounded objective, yes, and it is particularly valuable here because a break removes the crossing, the bus and the homework competing for the slot. A rested student in a morning session does several times the work of a tired one at 19:00. The conditions are a specific target, alternate days rather than ten consecutive sessions, short practice in between, and a start in the second week of a break rather than the day after term ends.

faqs.question: Should we do anything academic over the long summer?
faqs.answer: A small amount, well placed. For a student entering an examination year, four or five sessions spread across the weeks with short practice in between protects content that would otherwise need relearning in September. Twenty sessions in August is not better; it produces diminishing returns and resentment. The target is maintenance rather than progress: keep the hardest topics warm, keep arithmetic or language fluency ticking, and avoid starting the year from behind.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come across to the island?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we operate only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. On an island with a single road link that is the better arrangement twice over. A visiting tutor spends around three hours of their day for one paid hour, which sits inside the rate however it is itemised, and the people willing to make that journey at five in the afternoon are a small subset of the specialists available.

faqs.question: Does an island address limit our choice of school?
faqs.answer: The opposite, in practice. Because the island is not committed to a direction, the Marina and Al Sufouh corridor, the Greens and the interchange, Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, and the Emirates Living schools are all reachable. The criterion most families under-use is the afternoon return rather than the morning run, which varies by twenty or thirty minutes depending on direction. Twenty minutes a day is around sixty hours a year, more than a term of weekly tutoring provides.

faqs.question: Is Dubai adding school places we should know about?
faqs.answer: Yes. For the 2026-27 academic year Dubai adds seven new private schools, four following the UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A move considered now therefore does not also carry a fee increase.

faqs.question: Should a session be shortened or cancelled when traffic is bad?
faqs.answer: Shortened, every time. Thirty minutes of focused work on the planned objective is worth far more than a cancellation, because cancellations are how arrangements end in this community: one missed week, one moved week, then a quiet stop. We agree the rule at the outset so nobody is deciding under pressure, and the written note records what was not reached so it goes first in the following session.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the year should never be moved?
faqs.answer: Four: the four weeks before mocks, the six before a public examination series, the fortnight before an internal coursework deadline the school has set, and the first week back after a long break. That last one is the surprise and often matters most, because material half-learned before a break decays over it, and one review session in the first week back prevents a term of compounding confusion that otherwise looks like a new academic problem.

faqs.question: What will IB Gram not do or claim for an island family?
faqs.answer: We make no promises about grades or points totals and publish no success statistics we cannot support with a sample size, date and method. We send nobody to a UAE address. We will not write, rewrite, translate or complete any part of an assessed component. We do not distribute board past papers or mark schemes. And we hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operate no UAE office.

dubai/bluewaters-island.closingHeading: Decide what the one hour is for
dubai/bluewaters-island.closingBody: On an island with a single road link and no school, the scarce thing is time rather than choice. Record two weeks of actual arrival times, send them with the syllabus code and the last marked piece of work, and one diagnostic hour online will tell you what the real problem is, which slot and session length your afternoon supports, and what twelve hours this term can honestly achieve. If two subjects need work and only one slot exists, we will tell you which should have it and why, and whether the sensible answer is more hours, a weekend anchor, or sequencing the subjects across two terms.

dubai/bur-dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below cover CBSE, both IGCSE boards and the IB continuum at the levels taught in and around Bur Dubai. Start by naming the specification your child sits; in this district that single detail separates a useful match from a tutor who teaches the right subject under the wrong rules.

intro.heading: Who lives in Bur Dubai, and what each household is actually solving
paragraphs: Bur Dubai is older than almost anywhere else in the city and it has the household mix to prove it. Long-settled Indian and Pakistani families whose children have been through the same school for three generations. Arab families in the villa pockets near Al Hamriya and Al Raffa. Newer professional arrivals renting apartments near the Al Fahidi and Al Souk districts because the commute into Downtown and DIFC is short. Filipino, Egyptian, Jordanian and Russian families spread across the mid-rise blocks. These households do not share a curriculum, an exam month or a view of what tutoring is for.

That mix produces a specific problem. The schools within reach of Bur Dubai run at least four different systems, and the systems diverge exactly at the age when tutoring demand peaks. A CBSE student sits board examinations in Grade 10 and Grade 12 with an internal pattern of unit tests. A Cambridge IGCSE student sits terminal papers in a June or November series with Core and Extended tiers that cap the grade. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE student sits a 9-1 scale with its own paper structure. A Diploma student is managing six subjects, internally assessed components and an Extended Essay across two years. The word "tutor" means four different jobs here.

The second thing a Bur Dubai parent is usually solving is a transfer. This is one of the districts where students most often change system mid-school: from a national board into IGCSE at Year 9 or 10, or from IGCSE into the Diploma at sixteen. The gap in those moves is rarely raw knowledge. It is the style of question. A student who has been rewarded for a correct final answer for eight years meets a paper that awards most of its marks for reasoning written down, and the grade drops for reasons nobody in the house can name.

Third, space. Bur Dubai living is largely apartment living, often with siblings sharing a room and a household where somebody is always awake. The practical effect is that the length and the timing of a session matter as much as the content, and a plan built on the assumption of a quiet study for ninety uninterrupted minutes will not survive the term.

This page is organised around those households rather than around a generic pitch. It sets out the four systems and where each one actually hurts, maps the transfer routes subject by subject, publishes what the market charges in dirhams by programme, and states what a tutor may and may not do with assessed work. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, and never has. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video, which is how a household can reach a Pearson Edexcel specialist and a Diploma Higher Level specialist in the same week.

dubai/bur-dubai.programmesIntro: These are the programmes we cover for Bur Dubai families, with the part of each one that causes the most trouble in this district rather than a general description.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate boards with separate syllabus codes. Cambridge subjects frequently split into Core and Extended tiers, and the tier chosen in Year 10 sets a ceiling on the grade available in Year 11. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses a 9-1 scale on most specifications and structures its papers differently. Cambridge examines in June and November; Pearson Edexcel examines in May/June and November.
programmes.countryNote: In Bur Dubai the first task is often simply identifying the board. Several schools within a short drive use different providers for the same subject, and families who have moved school mid-course sometimes carry past papers from the previous specification. We ask for the code on the school's own assessment sheet before matching anyone.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an internally assessed component with published criteria, and the school sets internal deadlines that arrive well before anything the board publishes. The hardest term is usually the second half of DP1, when content, coursework and mock preparation collide.
programmes.countryNote: Bur Dubai Diploma students generally travel to a school outside the district, so the realistic session window starts later than parents expect. For students who came up through IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme, the first obstacle is Theory of Knowledge and the research register the Extended Essay assumes.

programmes.name: National board into IGCSE or the Diploma
programmes.description: A structured bridge rather than a subject. The content overlap between a national board and IGCSE is high in mathematics and the sciences and low in English and the humanities, but the assessment style diverges everywhere. Marks move once a student learns to answer inside the command term, show reasoning as a sequence and manage extended written responses against a mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most requested piece of work in Bur Dubai, because the district has both the national-curriculum schools students leave and the international schools they arrive at. We plan it as six to twelve weeks of targeted work, front-loaded on question technique, not as an indefinite subscription.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, using task-specific descriptors rather than percentages. Criterion D, which asks for reflection and evaluation, is where transferring students lose the most ground, because the register it requires has usually never been taught to them explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Bur Dubai students who join the Middle Years Programme partway through often arrive with strong content knowledge and no exposure to criterion language. The work is translation rather than teaching: taking what the student already knows and rebuilding how it gets written down.

dubai/bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: Demand in Bur Dubai is weighted towards mathematics, the sciences and accounting-adjacent subjects, with steady English language work from households where English is the third language spoken at home.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1
subjects.levels: Cambridge IGCSE Extended and Pearson Edexcel
subjects.description: Two codes, two paper structures, one subject. Transferring students lose marks by producing the right answer with no visible method, because method marks are awarded for written reasoning. The Core and Extended decision in the Cambridge code is the most consequential choice made in Year 10.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic Diploma route, and the natural destination for a student who took Additional Mathematics at sixteen. Higher Level adds proof and complex numbers and assumes algebraic fluency that cannot be rebuilt in DP2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and heavy use of the graphical display calculator. Students from a computation-first background often find the arithmetic easy and the interpretation questions hard, because the paper asks what a number means rather than what it equals.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves hold the marks that go missing. The practical paper rewards students who can describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it, which is a writing skill as much as a science skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reactions, with the quantitative questions separating grades at the top. Students who learned chemistry as a set of facts rather than a set of calculations hit a wall in Year 11 that practice on the correct board's papers resolves.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The highest-volume subject for vocabulary loss. A student can describe a process accurately in their own words and still score nothing because the mark scheme requires specific terms. Correcting that is quick, visible and usually worth a grade.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Popular in Bur Dubai's business-family households and unforgiving about layout. Marks depend on the correct format of the statement as much as the arithmetic inside it, so the fastest gains come from drilling presentation against past papers.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the organisation in front of them. The Diploma research project needs a narrow question and genuine source material, both of which take longer to settle than students expect.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510 and English A
subjects.description: Two very different jobs. The IGCSE second-language paper rewards accuracy and register control; the Diploma English A courses reward structured argument and evidence selection across set texts. A tutor matched to the wrong one wastes a term.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to every student, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab learners. Non-Arab students follow a different route with different expectations, and tutoring has to match the school's stream or it produces work the school cannot use.

dubai/bur-dubai.regionsTitle: Bur Dubai and the districts beside it
dubai/bur-dubai.regionsIntro: Bur Dubai is a cluster of older sub-districts rather than one neighbourhood, and the practical details differ between them. These are the areas we cover from the same school belt.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Mid-rise apartments with the Oud Metha school belt a short drive away. Arrivals are early by Dubai standards, which makes a 3:45pm session workable where most of the city cannot manage before 4:15pm.

regions.name: Al Hamriya and Al Raffa
regions.note: Older villa pockets and townhouses among the apartment blocks. Households here are frequently multi-generational, and the reliable session window sits before the evening meal rather than after it.

regions.name: Al Souk Al Kabeer
regions.note: The historic trading core beside the creek. Many families run businesses within walking distance, so parents are often available for a mid-afternoon handover but not for a fixed evening slot.

regions.name: Al Fahidi
regions.note: Low-rise and densely built, with limited quiet study space in many apartments. Shorter sessions twice a week tend to produce better outcomes here than one long weekday block.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The school belt itself. Families living here have the shortest school run in old Dubai and are the one group who can realistically hold a 3:30pm start during term.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense apartment living a few minutes from the Oud Metha schools. The binding constraint is usually a shared room and a shared device rather than travel time.

regions.name: Al Jafiliya and Za'abeel
regions.note: Closer to the Trade Centre corridor, with families whose working parents commute into Downtown. Sessions here are often placed later to overlap with a parent being home.

regions.name: Deira across the creek

dubai/bur-dubai.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Bur Dubai household. The right one depends less on budget than on how many children are involved and whether the task is teaching, transition or technique.

The format that works best when a specific grade has slipped and the family wants to see whether tutoring moves it before committing further. We review against the school's next assessment rather than against how the sessions felt.

sections.heading: Four Bur Dubai households, four different tutoring problems
paragraphs: Take a single apartment block near Al Mankhool. On the second floor a Grade 10 student is heading for CBSE board examinations with a pattern of unit tests behind her and a syllabus that will be examined in full. Two floors up, a Year 11 student sits Cambridge IGCSE on the Extended tier, with terminal papers in a June series and a Core or Extended decision already made for him last year. On the fifth floor a Year 11 student sits Pearson Edexcel International GCSE on a 9-1 scale with a different paper structure and different grade descriptors. On the top floor, a DP1 student is three months from an internally assessed investigation deadline nobody at home has seen the criteria for.

All four parents will type something close to the same search. The useful answer is different in every case. The CBSE student needs full-syllabus coverage with retrieval practice, because everything is examinable and the test pattern rewards breadth. The Cambridge student needs papers from his own code under timed conditions, because his content is largely secure and his losses are technique. The Pearson student needs the same thing from a different code; swapping them would be a quiet waste of a term. The Diploma student needs criterion coaching and a tutor who will not touch the writing.

This is why we refuse to quote before asking what looks like an administrative question. Which school, which board, which code, which tier. In most parts of Dubai that sequence is a formality because one school dominates a neighbourhood. In Bur Dubai it is the whole diagnosis, and getting it wrong does not produce a bad session. It produces six months of plausible sessions aimed at the wrong paper.

The fourth household is the one most likely to be sold something unsuitable, because coursework anxiety is the easiest thing in this market to monetise. A parent who does not know what criterion C asks for cannot evaluate an offer of help with it. The section below on assessed work exists so that any Bur Dubai parent can read the boundary once and recognise an offer that crosses it.
bullets: A national-board student needs breadth and retrieval
A Cambridge student needs papers from the Cambridge code
A Pearson student needs papers from the Pearson code
A Diploma student needs criteria coaching, never written help

sections.heading: The four systems inside one district, side by side
paragraphs: Parents comparing schools in Bur Dubai are usually shown fee tables and inspection ratings, which tell you about the institution and nothing about what the child will be asked to do at sixteen. The table below is the comparison that matters for planning tuition: what each system examines, when, and where the tutoring demand reliably appears.

The pattern worth noticing is that the systems differ most in how forgiving they are about timing. A national-board student can recover a weak term because the final examination covers everything and revision has leverage. A Cambridge student on the Core tier cannot recover a grade ceiling set a year earlier, whatever the revision. A Diploma student carries internally assessed marks into the final grade from more than a year before the papers, so a weak investigation cannot be revised away in April.

That has a direct consequence for when a family should spend money. For the national-board route, the highest-value window is the final two terms. For Cambridge and Pearson, it is Year 10, because that is when the tier and the habits are set. For the Diploma, it is the coursework months in DP1, which is the window families most often skip because no examination is visible yet.

Across all four, the mandatory UAE subjects run in parallel. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA calculates the instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. A Bur Dubai timetable is therefore fuller than the international curriculum alone suggests, and a tutoring plan that ignores those lessons is planning around a week that does not exist.

sections.heading: Moving from a national board into IGCSE or the Diploma, subject by subject
paragraphs: Transfers are the characteristic Bur Dubai tutoring job, and they are badly served by generic advice. The usual framing is that international curricula are "broader" and national boards are "deeper", which tells a parent nothing actionable. The useful framing is: what will the examiner now reward that nobody rewarded before, and how many weeks does it take to retrain that?

In mathematics the content overlap is high and the marking is the difference. A student arriving from a board that awards the answer meets a scheme that awards the method, and the first three weeks are spent learning to write down steps that previously stayed in the head. In the sciences the content overlap is also high but the practical and description marks are new, and the recurring failure is describing a method imprecisely. In English the gap is widest: extended written response against a mark scheme, with structure and evidence selection carrying the marks.

The humanities are the quiet problem. A student who has learned history as a narrative meets source evaluation and provenance questions, which are a different skill entirely and are worth a large share of the paper. The same student may be fluent and still score poorly for two terms before anyone identifies that the issue is a question type rather than knowledge.

We plan these transitions as finite blocks, usually six to twelve weeks, with a defined end point: the student can answer unaided under time. Open-ended transfer tutoring is the format most likely to drift into dependency, and a Bur Dubai family paying for a second year of it should ask what changed.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing, and why the answer differs by board
paragraphs: Marks leave a script in a small number of predictable places, and a tutor who knows the board can name them from a single marked paper. On Cambridge science papers the common losses are in the extended-response questions where a six-mark answer needs six distinct points and the student supplies three well-written ones. On Pearson papers the structure differs and the losses cluster differently, which is the whole argument for practising on the right code.

In mathematics across both boards, the single biggest avoidable loss is the unshown step. An examiner cannot award a method mark for reasoning that is not on the page, and a student who has spent years being told to be efficient will have been trained into exactly the wrong habit. The fix is quick and it is behavioural rather than intellectual, which is why it so often produces a visible grade change in one term.

In the Diploma, marks move at the criterion level and the student usually cannot see where. An internally assessed investigation can be scientifically sound and still score poorly on evaluation, because the student described limitations rather than assessing their effect. A tutor who reads the criteria aloud with the student and asks them to self-mark before submission will find that gap; a tutor who offers to improve the writing will hide it.

For a Bur Dubai family the practical step is to send one recent marked script rather than describing the problem. The script says which of these applies. A description does not, and the first paid session then gets spent discovering something a document already contained.
bullets: Six-mark answers need six points, not three good ones
Unshown steps lose method marks in every mathematics code
Diploma marks move at criterion level, usually invisibly to the student
One marked script is worth more than a phone conversation

sections.heading: What tutoring costs by programme in Bur Dubai, in dirhams
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are dirham market rates, sourced to the providers who published them, and organised by programme rather than by tier, because that is the comparison a parent choosing between IGCSE and Diploma support actually needs. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list.

The shape of the market is consistent across sources. Budget online tutoring from university students or generalists starts around AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, with one platform advertising from roughly AED 33. Qualified subject tutors online sit between about AED 150 and AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run higher because travel sits inside the rate: roughly AED 180 to AED 350 from one cost index, and AED 200 to AED 500 among independent home tutors. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one agency publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650.

Monthly figures seen in the market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. One published cost index puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

Set that against school fees, which KHDA confirmed in May 2026 will not increase for the 2026-27 academic year in Dubai. For most Bur Dubai households, one weekly subject is a modest addition to an existing education budget and four weekly subjects is a significant one. The useful discipline is to start with the subject where a grade is closest to a boundary, rather than the subject the child dislikes most.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in a Bur Dubai flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts by conceding what in-home tutoring does well. An adult in the room can see a student's working on the page without being asked, can write on it, and does not depend on a connection. For a younger child, or a household where screen time is already contested, that is a genuine advantage and some Bur Dubai families will reasonably choose it from another provider.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. The reason is the mathematics of a small specialist pool. A family needing a Pearson Edexcel Chemistry specialist, or a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches tutor who can give criterion feedback, is asking for a narrow skill set. Adding the requirement that the person drives to Al Mankhool at 4pm removes most of the candidates, and the family receives availability dressed as expertise.

In a Bur Dubai apartment there is a second practical argument that rarely appears on tutoring pages. A visiting tutor needs a room, and in a two-bedroom flat with siblings that room is somebody's bedroom for the hour. Online, two children can take consecutive slots at the same desk, and the household gives up one quiet hour instead of two disrupted ones.

The table sets out the trade-offs without pretending there are none. Where in-home wins, it wins; where online wins in this district, it wins on the clock, the catalogue and the number of rooms a household actually has.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, track by track
paragraphs: Equivalency is the part of UAE schooling that competitors in this market almost never mention, and it is the part that decides whether a certificate is usable here. Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign school certificate, and it matters for university applications and for employment. It is a process families complete through the official channel; it is not something a tutoring service performs, arranges or guarantees.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That last detail is worth repeating, because one ranking page in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says.

The American track runs on test scores rather than subject counts. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. For the IB route, no points threshold is published that we have been able to read on an official ministry page, so we will not print one; a Bur Dubai family on the Diploma should verify the current requirement with the ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

The practical tutoring consequence is about subject choice rather than tuition. A student dropping to four IGCSE subjects to reduce pressure may be making a decision with a consequence three years away, and a student counting Arabic towards the five has miscounted. Those are conversations to have in Year 9, not in Year 13.

sections.heading: Siblings, one device, and a week that actually holds
paragraphs: A large share of Bur Dubai enquiries involve more than one child, and the household constraint is almost never money first. It is rooms and devices. A two-bedroom apartment with three children has one place where a lesson can happen without interruption, and whoever books it second does not get a lesson, they get an hour of being half-present.

The arrangement that works is consecutive one-to-one slots on the same device, with the younger child first. The younger child's session is shorter, thirty or forty-five minutes, and finishes while they can still concentrate. The older child follows with a full hour. The household gives up one quiet block rather than negotiating twice, and the parent only has to manage the room once.

What does not work is one tutor teaching two children together to save money. Two students at different stages in one session produces a lesson aimed between them, and the quieter child disappears. If the budget only supports one subject, it is better to pick the child closest to a grade boundary, run a defined block, then move the slot to the other child than to split a session that then helps neither.

There is one legitimate exception. Where two siblings sit the same specification in consecutive years, a tutor can sometimes teach the older child while the younger listens in a genuinely secondary role, usually for a short block before mock examinations. That has to be an explicit decision with an explicit purpose, not a default dressed up as efficiency.
bullets: Consecutive slots on one device beat two parallel arrangements

sections.heading: The line on assessed work, and how to start
paragraphs: Coursework is where this market behaves worst. One provider found in this search sells completed Internal Assessments. A Bur Dubai parent paying for finished coursework is buying an academic-integrity breach that their child signs for, and the consequence under board malpractice rules falls on the student rather than the seller. The sum involved is trivial next to the risk.

The permitted boundary is specific enough to hold a tutor to. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion and what its marks reward, discuss whether a research question is viable, point out that a method will not generate usable data, read a draft and name which criterion is under-served, and ask the questions that make a student find their own gap. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, pick the question on the student's behalf or edit a draft into a finished state. We also do not redistribute board syllabuses, past papers or mark schemes; we reference the official source and work from what the school has issued.

Starting is deliberately low-commitment. Send one recent marked script, name the board and syllabus code, and say which afternoon slot is realistic. The first session is a diagnostic and produces a written note describing what the gap actually is, which is sometimes not what the school report said and occasionally is "this child needs a fortnight of structured independent practice, not a tutor". We would rather write that than sell a term.

Where we cannot help, we say so. Narrow Higher Level subjects with a deadline inside six weeks, or an unusual language pairing, can take longer than a few days to match properly. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is exactly why families keep discovering one after paying for it.
bullets: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and reviews the student's own work
No text supplied, no draft edited to completion, no data generated
Board materials referenced and linked, never redistributed

process.title: Name the system, not just the subject
process.description: CBSE, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel or the IB continuum, plus the syllabus code and the tier where one applies. In Bur Dubai this is the diagnosis rather than paperwork, because four systems are in play within a few minutes of each other.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent marked paper shows whether marks were lost to content, to technique or to vocabulary, and it shows which board the school actually uses. It answers in two minutes what a phone call takes two sessions to establish.

process.title: Run a diagnostic first session
process.description: The first session tests the hypothesis from the script at your chosen slot. You receive a written note naming the gap, the order to work on it and a realistic estimate of how long that takes, including the case where the answer is no tutoring.

process.title: Fix the slot, and the second slot if needed
process.description: We set a weekly hour and, for households with two students, a consecutive slot on the same device. Where a board change is involved we agree a finite transition block with an end point rather than an open arrangement.

process.title: Review against school data at six weeks
process.description: The review uses the school's next assessment, not an impression. It is where we decide to continue, change format, change subject or stop, and where a transition block is judged against whether the student can now answer unaided.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the specification, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Two Bur Dubai schools can teach the same subject under different boards with different papers. We confirm the code and tier before matching, because practice on the wrong specification builds habits that cost marks and take a term to unlearn.

whyPoints.title: Built for mid-course transfers
whyPoints.description: Moving from a national board into IGCSE or the Diploma is the characteristic job in this district. We treat it as a finite block focused on question technique, with a defined end point, rather than an open subscription that quietly becomes permanent.

whyPoints.title: A household plan, not a child plan
whyPoints.description: Most enquiries here involve siblings, one quiet room and one device. We schedule consecutive one-to-one slots rather than combining children into a shared session that helps the quieter one least.

whyPoints.title: Dirham figures, each attributed
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is the market's, published by the provider named, in the currency Dubai families transact in. We do not present somebody else's rate card as ours and we do not quote before seeing the problem.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained, never performed
whyPoints.description: We set out what the Ministry of Education requires for each track and point to the official channel. We do not run attestation, we do not guarantee an outcome, and we do not publish an IB points threshold we cannot source.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own work. No part of an assessed piece is written, rewritten or edited to completion. The boundary is published here so a parent can recognise an offer that crosses it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's Bur Dubai school uses?
faqs.answer: The school's own assessment sheet or report usually carries the syllabus code, and that is the detail to look for. A Cambridge IGCSE code looks like 0580 or 0625; a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE code looks like 4MA1 or 4PH1. If the paperwork is unclear, the subject teacher or head of year will confirm it in a sentence. Ask for the tier as well on Cambridge subjects, because Core and Extended cap different grades. We confirm this before matching a tutor, since practice on the wrong code builds the wrong habits.

faqs.question: My child is moving from CBSE to IGCSE in Year 10. What actually needs fixing?
faqs.answer: Rarely the content, usually the marking. In mathematics the overlap is high and the difference is that method marks are awarded for reasoning written on the page, so a student trained to produce a clean answer has to relearn how to show work. In the sciences the new demand is precise method description. English and the humanities are the widest gaps, because extended written response against a mark scheme and source evaluation are question types rather than knowledge. Plan four to sixteen weeks depending on subject, with an end point.

faqs.question: Do you offer home tuition in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time. The practical reason is the size of the specialist pool: a Pearson Edexcel Chemistry or Higher Level mathematics tutor who can give criterion-level feedback is a narrow skill set, and requiring that person to drive to Al Mankhool at four in the afternoon would mean choosing on proximity instead.

faqs.question: How much should a Bur Dubai family expect to pay for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tutoring from university students is advertised from about AED 45 to AED 65, and one platform quotes from around AED 33. In-home visits run higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, because travel is inside the rate. Monthly packages of around AED 799 for eight online sessions circulate in this market. Those are other providers' published figures.

faqs.question: Why does IB Diploma tutoring cost more than IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and neither is marketing. The subject pool is smaller: a tutor who can teach Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches to Diploma standard and give criterion-level feedback on an internally assessed investigation is scarcer than a tutor who can teach the same subject at sixteen. Second, the work is denser, because Diploma sessions frequently cover content, coursework process and paper technique in parallel. Published market figures put specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, against IGCSE from AED 150.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Bur Dubai apartment share a tutor?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor across the week, but not usually a session. Two students at different stages in one hour produces a lesson aimed between them, and the quieter child gets least. What works is consecutive one-to-one slots at the same desk, with the younger child first on a shorter session. The household gives up one quiet block instead of two, and one tutor can still cover both children where the specifications are close enough to make that sensible.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted towards the five subjects for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Those subjects remain compulsory in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules, but they sit outside the equivalency count. One page ranking in this market tells UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current position with the Ministry of Education before making a subject decision.

faqs.question: What does the UAE require from an American-curriculum student for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published requirements are test-based rather than subject-count based. English proficiency can be shown with a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test, and the guidance states this should be in place before applying. No EmSAT requirement appears in the published guidance we have read. For the IB route no points figure is published that we can source, so confirm it directly with the ministry.

faqs.question: Is a Core or Extended tier decision reversible later?
faqs.answer: Not in practice, and this is the most consequential choice made in Year 10 on Cambridge subjects. The tier determines which papers a student sits and caps the grade available, so a Core entry limits the ceiling regardless of how much revision happens in Year 11. Schools make the decision from Year 10 performance, which means the window where tutoring can influence it is the first year, not the second. Families who want the Extended option kept open should ask about it in Year 10, early.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a transfer student from a national board usually need?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and the honest ranges are wide. Mathematics typically takes four to eight weeks of focused work, because the change is behavioural: writing down method. Physics and chemistry take six to ten, mostly on practical description. Biology is often four to six, since the gap is mark-scheme vocabulary. English language and literature is the longest at ten to sixteen weeks, and history or geography eight to twelve because source evaluation is a new skill. We agree an end point rather than running an open block.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Diploma internally assessed investigation in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Within a specific boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain each criterion and what its marks reward, say whether a research question is viable, warn that a method will not produce usable data, and read a draft to name which criterion is weak. A tutor cannot supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, choose the question or edit a draft into a finished state. The student declares the work as their own. One provider in this market sells completed coursework; the malpractice consequence falls on your child.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Bur Dubai families most often ask for?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, in both IGCSE codes and both Diploma routes, then chemistry and physics, then accounting and business, then English language. The weighting reflects the district's household mix: trading and professional families, and homes where English is the third language spoken. Accounting is more requested here than in most parts of Dubai, and it rewards a specific kind of practice, because marks depend on the correct layout of a statement as much as on the arithmetic inside it.

faqs.question: We live in Bur Dubai but the school is across the creek. Does that change the session time?
faqs.answer: Yes, by fifteen to thirty minutes. The crossing points are limited to Al Shindagha Tunnel and the bridges, and they are busiest exactly when schools close. A family whose child attends school in Oud Metha can often hold a 3:45pm start. A family travelling from Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City is more realistically looking at 4:15pm. We set the slot from the time your child actually arrived home last week, with a buffer, rather than from the school's finishing bell.

faqs.question: What should I send before the first session?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them take long. One recent marked script or school report, so a specialist can see where marks were lost rather than hearing it described. The board and syllabus code, with the tier for Cambridge subjects. And the realistic afternoon arrival time on a weekday. With those three, a first session can be designed as a diagnostic. Without them, the first paid hour becomes an interview, and you have paid a specialist rate for information a document already contained.

dubai/bur-dubai.closingHeading: Start from the specification, then the household
dubai/bur-dubai.closingBody: Bur Dubai is the district where generic tutoring advice fails fastest, because four examination systems sit within a few minutes of each other and two children on the same staircase can need opposite things. The sequence that works is simple: identify the board, the code and the tier; send one marked script; set a session time from the real arrival rather than the school bell; and schedule for the household rather than the child, because one quiet room usually has to serve two students. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, every rate quoted here belongs to the provider that published it, and the boundary on assessed work is written down so you can hold us to it.
