dubai/business-bay.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Business Bay households are chosen for transition work specifically. A tutor who can teach IGCSE Mathematics is not automatically a tutor who can tell a CBSE Class 9 student which four topics their previous syllabus never introduced, and that second skill is the one that matters in the first term.

intro.heading: Who lives in Business Bay, and why their question is a transition question
paragraphs: Business Bay is a canal-side district of high-rise towers immediately south of Downtown, built out rapidly and still filling. Its housing stock is overwhelmingly apartments, much of it one and two bedroom, with a growing number of three bedroom units that families take as a first Dubai home. That combination produces a population that is younger, newer to the city and more internationally varied than almost anywhere else in Dubai.

The practical consequence for schooling is that a large share of children in these towers started their education somewhere else. Dubai licenses seventeen different curricula across its private schools, with Indian-curriculum schools accounting for twenty-six per cent of private enrolment, UK curriculum thirty-seven per cent, US fourteen per cent and International Baccalaureate seven per cent. Business Bay households arrive from all of those directions, and from Russian, CIS, Filipino, Egyptian and Pakistani systems besides.

So the tutoring question here is different from the one a settled villa community asks. It is not that a child is behind. It is that the child learned a different ordering of the same subject, was assessed by different conventions, and is now sitting in a classroom where the teacher reasonably assumes a shared foundation. A CBSE Class 9 student entering IGCSE Year 10 arrives strong in algebraic manipulation and unused to a question that gives context and expects a method to be chosen. That is not a weakness, but it reads as one in October.

The second feature of this district is that the transition is often invisible for a term. Transfer students work hard, want to fit in, and do not always know what they do not know. The first report arrives in November, looks mediocre, and the family concludes the child is struggling with a harder system. Usually the truth is narrower: three or four specific topics were never covered, and a set of assessment conventions was never taught.

Apartment living adds its own constraint. In a two-bedroom tower apartment with two children, there is one usable desk and limited quiet, and the room a parent works from in the evening is often the room a child would study in. This matters for scheduling in a way it does not in a villa, and it shapes what format of support actually works here.

Everything described on this page runs as one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a newly arrived household in a tower, the advantages are practical: no visitor access to arrange, a tutor matched on the syllabus rather than on who covers Business Bay, and a session that happens at the hour the family chooses.

dubai/business-bay.programmesIntro: A transfer student is entering a programme at a point other than the beginning, so what matters is the entry point rather than the programme in general. These are the four entry points Business Bay families most often face.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: The commonest entry point for arrivals from CBSE, ICSE, American and Russian systems, usually at the start of Year 10 or part-way through it. The content load is broad rather than deep, with nine or ten subjects, and the tiering decisions in mathematics and the sciences fix the grade ceiling.
programmes.countryNote: A mid-year arrival into Year 10 or Year 11 must ask the exams officer two things immediately: which awarding body and syllabus code the school enters, and whether the entry deadline for the intended series has passed. Cambridge allocates centres to one of six timetable zones, so the dates are centre-specific rather than generic.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Entered from IGCSE, from MYP 5, from a British Year 11, from an Indian Class 10 or from an American Grade 10. Six subjects at three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with a large share of the grade sitting in work the student manages independently.
programmes.countryNote: Arrivals from exam-focused systems find the examined papers manageable and the self-managed components hard, because nothing in their previous education required them to run a two-year project. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator, since the IB is the only authority on its own calendar.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight. For a student arriving from a content-and-examination system, MYP is the most disorienting destination available, because the marks come from investigation, communication and reflection rather than from knowing the answer.
programmes.countryNote: A transfer into MYP 4 or 5 needs explicit teaching of what each criterion rewards and in what language. Students who were top of a CBSE or Russian class frequently sit mid-band in MYP for a term, not through weakness but because nobody has shown them that the marks are awarded for something they were never asked to do before.

programmes.name: Key Stage 1-2 and the Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Primary transfers are the cheapest to fix and the most often left alone. The gaps are procedural: written methods for multiplication and division, fraction conventions, spelling patterns and handwriting expectations all differ between systems, and a child using a different written method is marked wrong for a correct answer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, a primary transfer also meets the mandatory UAE subjects for the first time. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and a child entering at Year 4 or above starts Arabic from a standing position.

dubai/business-bay.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where transition gaps concentrate. Each note names what a transfer student typically arrives with and what the new syllabus will expect that the old one did not.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: CBSE and Russian arrivals are usually strong on manipulation and weak on contextual problem-solving, where a question describes a situation and expects the student to choose the method. American arrivals are often the reverse. Tier confirmation comes first in both cases.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof is the recurring surprise for arrivals from systems that do not teach it, and the Higher Level Paper 3 investigation has no counterpart in most national curricula. Both are specific, teachable gaps rather than general weakness.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology use and interpretation in context dominate. Students from manipulation-heavy systems can produce a correct statistical result and lose the marks that require them to say what it means for the situation described.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Transfer students typically know more content than the syllabus requires and have never written an explanation question that asks for a mechanism. Practical and data-handling conventions also differ sharply between systems.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations are usually secure for CBSE and ICSE arrivals; organic chemistry conventions, nomenclature emphasis and the expected form of a written answer are not. This is the subject where a transfer student is most often over-prepared and under-scoring.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Command terms are the gap. The difference between describe, explain, outline and evaluate is not taught in most systems and decides marks in this one. A short block on mark-scheme language moves a grade faster than more content.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge First Language English · Pearson English Language A
subjects.description: The subject most likely to look fine and score badly after a transfer. Directed-writing tasks reward register and audience awareness, and literature answers reward argument about how a text works rather than summary of what it says.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Often a new subject entirely for arrivals from systems with a fixed science and mathematics stream. The technique is learnable quickly: diagram accuracy, application to the named case and an explicit judgement sentence.

subjects.name: MYP subjects across all criteria
subjects.description: The destination that needs the most explicit teaching after a transfer, because the assessment model is unfamiliar. Work concentrates on criterion language and on evidencing process, not on content the student usually already has.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs. A student entering Dubai at Year 5 or above begins this subject with no foundation and needs a realistic plan rather than an assumption that it will resolve.

sections.heading: The transition map: where each system lands in Dubai
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes this, which is strange given how many Dubai families need it. One competitor has a single subheading on the gap between IGCSE and the IB. There is no structured, subject-aware map of what happens when a student moves from a national system into a Dubai international curriculum, even though that move is the defining academic event for a large share of the city's children.

The table below is that map at the level of entry points. The right-hand column is the honest part: how long the work usually takes. The figures are what we see across transition blocks rather than a promise, and the range exists because the single biggest variable is how much of the gap is content and how much is convention. Content gaps take longer; convention gaps close fast.

Two patterns hold across almost every row. First, students from examination-heavy systems arrive with more content than the new syllabus requires and fewer of the skills it marks. Second, students from inquiry-led systems arrive with the skills and less secured content. Both look like weakness in a first report, and both are fixed by different work, which is why a generic tutoring arrangement that just does more of the subject rarely helps.

The practical instruction is to get the new school's scheme of work for each subject in the first fortnight, not the syllabus. The syllabus says what will be examined; the scheme of work says in what order it is being taught, which is what tells you precisely which topics the class covered before your child arrived.

sections.heading: What each system trains, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Every education system is good at something and silent about something else, and knowing which is which turns a vague worry into a work list. This is not a ranking. A student arriving from CBSE with four years of algebra drill has an advantage that a student from an inquiry-led primary does not, and the reverse is true for explaining reasoning in writing.

The pattern that recurs most often in Business Bay is the over-prepared, under-scoring transfer. A student who was in the top group at their previous school sits a Dubai assessment, knows the content thoroughly, writes a correct answer in the wrong form and collects half the marks. The family reads the result as a difficulty with a harder system. The actual issue is that nobody has taught them what an answer is supposed to look like here.

The second recurring pattern is the opposite: a student from a system that valued presentation and process, arriving into IGCSE where nine subjects of content have to be retained and recalled under time pressure. That student needs volume and retrieval practice, which is a different intervention and takes longer, because content cannot be taught in four sessions.

The table below sets out the main origin systems with their strengths and their blind spots. Use it as a starting hypothesis rather than a diagnosis: the real diagnosis comes from the student's own marked work in the new school, which usually confirms one of these patterns within two sessions.

sections.heading: CBSE and ICSE into IGCSE, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the single most common transition in Business Bay and it deserves detail rather than a general reassurance. Indian-curriculum schools account for twenty-six per cent of Dubai private enrolment, and a large share of the families in these towers are either moving from one of those schools into a British or IB school, or arriving directly from India mid-year.

The headline is that the content overlap is substantial and the assessment overlap is not. A CBSE Class 9 student entering IGCSE Year 10 has usually met more mathematics than the Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher syllabus requires at that point. What they have not met is a question that describes a situation in four sentences and expects the student to decide which method applies, nor a mark scheme that awards marks for method shown rather than for the final answer.

In the sciences the picture is similar with a twist. Content depth is often greater, but IGCSE asks for practical and data-handling skills in a specific form, and the written explanation questions reward a chain of reasoning rather than a statement. A student who writes the correct physics in three words gets one mark where five were available, and this is correctable in a handful of sessions.

English is where the real gap sits, and where families most often underestimate it. A student with excellent English can score poorly on an IGCSE directed-writing task because register and audience were never the point of their previous assessments. The table sets out the subject-level picture; the final column is the work.

sections.heading: The first six weeks after a move: a checklist
paragraphs: Transition problems are cheap to fix in September and expensive to fix in February, and the difference is almost entirely whether the first six weeks were used. Most families spend them on housing, visas, furniture and a driving licence, which is understandable, and the academic work waits for the first report. By then a term has gone.

The checklist below is deliberately administrative, because the information needed is held by other people and has to be asked for. None of it requires a tutor. What it produces is a picture specific enough to act on: which topics were missed, which conventions are unfamiliar, which components are already under way and which deadlines have already passed.

One item deserves emphasis. Ask each subject teacher, in writing, for the scheme of work rather than the syllabus. The syllabus lists what will be examined over two years; the scheme of work lists the order and the dates, which is what tells you exactly what the class covered in the weeks before your child walked in. Teachers generally provide this readily when asked directly and rarely offer it unprompted.

The second is the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and a student arriving at Year 5 or above starts Arabic with no foundation. Ask which stream your child is placed in and what the expectation is, because this is the subject most likely to produce an unexpected grade in the first report.

sections.heading: Studying in a tower: one desk, two children, and the evening
paragraphs: This is a practical constraint that nobody writing about tutoring acknowledges, and in Business Bay it decides outcomes. A two-bedroom apartment with two school-age children has one reasonable study surface, limited acoustic separation, and an open-plan living space where the television and the family conversation live. The room a parent takes calls from in the evening is often the only quiet room.

The consequences are specific. Two children cannot have sessions at the same time in the same apartment without headphones and separate rooms, so slots have to be sequential rather than simultaneous. A session held at the dining table while a sibling watches television is a session at half efficiency. And independent practice, which is the part that actually produces change, has nowhere to happen if the only desk is in use.

The arrangements that work are unglamorous. Sequential slots, typically 17:30 and 19:00, with the younger child first while concentration lasts. Headphones as standard rather than optional. A second screen or tablet so the student can work on paper while still seeing the tutor, which matters enormously in mathematics and science. And for a mathematical subject at Higher Level, a graphics tablet, which lets tutor and student write on the same page and removes the need for a large writing surface entirely.

There is one further option worth considering in this district specifically. Business Bay and Downtown have abundant quiet public space, and for an older student a scheduled session in a reliably quiet corner with headphones and a laptop can work better than a crowded apartment. It is not ideal, but it beats an unusable room, and online delivery makes it possible at all.

sections.heading: What the Business Bay school run looks like
paragraphs: There is no school campus in Business Bay, so every child travels, and the direction depends on which system the family chose on arrival. Families switching into a British or IB route head inland to Sobha Hartland for Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, across the creek to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf, or west to Safa British School and Citizens School in Al Quoz. Families staying on an Indian curriculum head towards Oud Metha and Al Quoz.

Journey distances are modest and journey times are not, because Business Bay empties onto the same interchanges as Downtown and DIFC at the same moment. The inland routes towards Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf are noticeably more reliable than the westward ones, which join Al Wasl Road or cross the Al Quoz industrial corridor. A child leaving a campus at 15:10 is realistically back in a Business Bay tower around 16:15 to 16:45 depending on direction.

That leaves a usable weekday window from about 17:30, with 19:00 being the dependable one for a secondary student. Primary children can take an earlier slot if an adult is home, which in this district is less common than in the villa communities because a high share of these households have both parents working within a short commute and finishing at the same time.

For a newly arrived family the useful question to put to an admissions office is not the distance but the bus departure and return times for your specific tower, since a route collecting across several buildings behaves very differently from a direct drive. Ask for the actual times rather than the nominal journey length.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor, and what we do instead
paragraphs: Parents here search for home tutors because that is how this market talks and because a newly arrived family naturally wants someone in the room. The honest comparison is worth making. In-home tutoring in Dubai is widely available, with market rates running roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 45 to 150 at the budget online end.

IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. Home visits are part of our India service only, and every country page on this site states the same. For transition work specifically the online model has a clear advantage, because the match is on an unusual requirement: a tutor who can tell a CBSE arrival which four topics the Pearson scheme of work covered in September. That is a narrow specialism, and restricting the pool to people who can drive to Business Bay at 19:00 makes it much narrower.

The practical requirements are the ones named in the previous section: a quiet space, headphones, a second screen and ideally a graphics tablet for mathematical subjects. Families who treat those as optional report a worse experience and usually blame the format. Families who set them up report that sessions are more focused than in-home ones, because screens can be shared, mark schemes sit beside scripts, and a written record exists afterwards.

One further point for a transient district. An online arrangement continues if the family moves again, within Dubai or out of it. The same tutor, the same session notes and the same plan carry across, adjusted for whichever syllabus the new school uses. For a household that may move twice in three years, not repeating the search is worth more than a small difference in hourly rate.

sections.heading: Getting started from Business Bay, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Begin by collecting the four administrative facts: the awarding body and syllabus code for each subject, the scheme of work with dates from each teacher, which Arabic stream your child has been placed in, and whether any coursework component is already under way. Then add the academic evidence: the last marked piece of work from the new school, and the previous school's final report if you have it.

The sequence is a consultation, a diagnostic session against the new scheme of work, and a block of six to twelve weeks with a written list of named gaps and a review date. The block is designed to end. A transition block that has turned into an open-ended weekly arrangement after four months has usually stopped being a transition block and should be re-examined rather than renewed.

Three things we will not claim. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring provider in this market holds a regulator's endorsement of its teaching. We do not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, attestation or school admission, all of which belong to the authority or the school. And we will not offer a grade or a promised number of marks, because nobody can honestly sell one.

One boundary, stated as a boundary. Tutors explain assessment criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not produce content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project, and they do not reproduce or distribute awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are referenced and linked to the official source. The reason is that the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student, not on the provider.

process.title: Collect the schemes of work
process.description: Before any teaching, we ask for the awarding body and syllabus code for each subject and the scheme of work with dates from each teacher. The syllabus says what will be examined; the scheme of work says in what order it is being taught, which is what identifies the topics covered before your child arrived.

process.title: Run a diagnostic against the new system
process.description: One session per subject working through the new school's own material and a past paper from the correct board. The output is a written list of named gaps, split into content the previous syllabus never covered and assessment conventions the student has never been taught.

process.title: Separate content gaps from convention gaps
process.description: These need different work and different timescales. Convention gaps, such as command terms and mark-scheme language, close in four to six sessions. Content gaps take longer because the material has to be taught and then retained. Treating them as one problem is why generic tutoring fails transfers.

process.title: Run a finite block with a review date
process.description: Six to twelve weeks, with the gap list as the agenda and a fixed review at the end. Homework is set between sessions, because corrected independent practice is what converts a closed gap into a retained one. The block is designed to finish rather than roll on.

process.title: Decide deliberately whether anything continues
process.description: At the review, either the gaps are closed and the booking ends, or a subject remains genuinely demanding rather than merely unfamiliar and becomes ordinary weekly support with its own named target. The default is to stop, not to renew.

whyPoints.description: This page sets out where each origin system lands in Dubai, what it trains, what it leaves out and how long the work takes. One competitor in this market has a single subheading on the IGCSE-to-IB gap; nobody publishes a subject-level map, despite it being the defining academic event for a large share of Dubai children.

whyPoints.title: Content and convention diagnosed separately

whyPoints.title: Work from the scheme of work, not the syllabus

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks with a written gap list
whyPoints.description: A transition block starts with a written list of named gaps and ends on a fixed review date. If it has turned into an open-ended weekly arrangement after four months, something has gone wrong and the plan needs re-examining rather than renewing.

whyPoints.title: Built for apartment living
whyPoints.description: One desk, two children and an open-plan living space is the real constraint in these towers. We schedule sequential rather than simultaneous slots, specify headphones and a second screen, and recommend a graphics tablet for mathematical subjects so no large writing surface is needed.

whyPoints.title: An arrangement that survives the next move
whyPoints.description: In a district this transient, a tutor who continues through a relocation is worth more than a marginally cheaper local hire. The same plan and session notes carry across a time-zone change, with the syllabus plan adjusted if the receiving school uses a different awarding body.

faqs.question: My child moved from CBSE Class 9 into IGCSE Year 10. What usually goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Typically not the content. A CBSE Class 9 student has often met more mathematics than the Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher syllabus requires at that stage. What they have not met is a question that describes a situation in several sentences and leaves the choice of method to the student, or a mark scheme that awards marks for working shown rather than for the final answer. The same pattern appears in the sciences, where explanation questions want a chain of reasoning. Six to ten weeks of convention work usually closes it.

faqs.question: How long does it take to catch up after changing curriculum mid-year?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on whether the gaps are content or convention. Convention gaps, such as command terms, mark-scheme language and the expected form of a written answer, close in four to six sessions because they are vocabulary and structure rather than knowledge. Content gaps take longer, because material has to be taught and then retained, and ten to twelve weeks is realistic. The reason generic tutoring often fails a transfer student is that it treats both as one problem and simply does more of the subject.

faqs.question: Why did my child go from top of the class to average after transferring?
faqs.answer: The commonest explanation in this district is the over-prepared, under-scoring pattern. A student who knows the content thoroughly writes a correct answer in the wrong form and collects half the available marks. The family reads the result as difficulty with a harder system; the actual issue is that nobody has taught them what an answer is supposed to look like in the new one. It shows up in marked work within two sessions, and it is among the fastest things in education to fix once identified.

faqs.question: Should we ask the school for the syllabus or something else?
faqs.answer: Ask each subject teacher for the scheme of work, with dates, rather than the syllabus. The syllabus lists what will be examined across two years. The scheme of work lists the order the content is being taught and when, which is the only document that tells you exactly what the class covered in the weeks before your child arrived. Teachers generally provide it readily when asked directly, and almost never offer it unprompted. It is the single most useful piece of paper for a transferring family.

faqs.question: What does an American high school student find hardest moving into IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Depth and timed examination technique. American arrivals usually bring strong discussion skills, presentation confidence and coursework habits, and meet a system where nine or ten subjects of content have to be retained and recalled under time pressure. That is a volume problem, which takes longer to fix than a convention problem, typically ten to twelve weeks of structured content work plus retrieval practice. The upside is that they adapt well to the IB Diploma's self-managed components, where exam-focused arrivals struggle.

faqs.question: Does a student from a Russian or CIS system face specific issues?
faqs.answer: Usually two. Mathematics and physics depth tends to be a genuine advantage, sometimes well ahead of the IGCSE requirement. The gap is answering in English to a published mark scheme rather than to a teacher, which involves both subject vocabulary in English and the convention of writing for an examiner who awards specific points. Command terms, significant figures and units all have to be taught explicitly. It is convention work rather than content work, so it tends to resolve faster than families expect.

faqs.question: My child is entering MYP 4 from an examination system. What should we expect?
faqs.answer: Expect a term of mid-band grades that do not reflect ability, and expect it to be about the assessment model rather than the content. MYP marks four criteria per subject out of eight each, and the later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection rather than knowing the answer. A student who was top of a content-and-examination class has never been asked to evidence a process or evaluate their own method. Explicit teaching of what each criterion rewards, with worked examples, is the intervention.

faqs.question: Does my child have to start Arabic from scratch when arriving in Dubai?
faqs.answer: If they arrive at Year 5 or above with no previous Arabic, effectively yes, and it needs a plan rather than an assumption. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Ask the school which stream your child has been placed in and what is expected, because this is the subject most likely to produce a surprising first report.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For transition work the online match matters, because what you need is narrow: a tutor who can tell a transferring student which specific topics the new scheme of work covered before they arrived. Restricting that pool to people who can drive to a Business Bay tower at a fixed hour would shrink it considerably.

faqs.question: We have two children and one quiet room. How do online sessions work?
faqs.answer: Sequentially rather than simultaneously, with the younger child first at around 17:30 while concentration lasts and the older at 19:00. Headphones are standard rather than optional, and a second screen or tablet lets the student work on paper while still seeing the tutor, which matters a great deal in mathematics and science. For a mathematical subject at Higher Level, a graphics tablet is the single best purchase, because tutor and student write on the same page and no large writing surface is needed at all.

faqs.question: How much does transition tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist, with premium named tutors advertised from AED 500 to 650. Those are published market figures rather than an IB Gram price list; our rate follows a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor. A transition block is finite, which usually makes it cheaper than it sounds.

faqs.question: Is it better to switch systems on arrival or stay on the same curriculum?
faqs.answer: Both are defensible and the decision should turn on how long you expect to stay and where the child will apply to university. Indian-curriculum schools account for twenty-six per cent of Dubai private enrolment, so continuity is genuinely available here in a way it is not in many cities. Switching buys international portability and costs a transition; staying avoids the transition and keeps the child inside one assessment culture. What makes either choice go badly is making it without asking what the first year of the new system will actually demand.

faqs.question: Which exam board will the new school use, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters and it must be asked, department by department. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel award International GCSEs in the same subjects with different syllabus codes, paper structures, tiering and practical arrangements, and schools in Dubai do not always use one board across the whole timetable. Buying past papers for the wrong board wastes a term of practice. Ask the exams officer which syllabus code your child is entered for, in each subject, in which series, and get the answer in writing.

faqs.question: Our previous school's reports are glowing. Why would we need a diagnostic?
faqs.answer: Because a report describes performance inside a system, and your child has left that system. A glowing CBSE report tells you the student handled CBSE assessments well; it says nothing about whether they can read an IGCSE contextual question or write to a published mark scheme. A diagnostic against the new school's scheme of work and a past paper from the correct board takes one session per subject and produces something actionable: a written list of named gaps rather than a general reassurance or a general worry.

faqs.question: What if we relocate again in a year?
faqs.answer: The arrangement continues, which is the main structural reason online delivery suits this district. The same tutor, the same session notes and the same plan carry across a move, adjusted for whichever awarding body the receiving school uses. A family that hires locally in each city pays for a search, a trial period and a ramp-up every time, and in practice loses roughly a month of momentum per move. That cost never appears in an hourly rate comparison and is usually larger than the rate difference.

dubai/business-bay.closingHeading: Name the gaps, then close them
dubai/business-bay.closingBody: If you have recently arrived in Business Bay, the most useful thing you can do is not hire a tutor. It is to collect the awarding body and syllabus code for each subject, the scheme of work with dates from each teacher, and the Arabic stream your child has been placed in. With those, one diagnostic session per subject produces a written list of named gaps, split into content and convention. Then a finite block of six to twelve weeks closes them, delivered online one-to-one over live video, with a review date rather than an open commitment.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-accounting-0452-ho.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452 to Dubai students over live video and keep a dated record of marked practice for each student. Each profile shows the topic areas they focus on and the year groups they currently teach.

intro.heading: How to audit Accounting tutoring when you cannot read a ledger
paragraphs: Accounting is the subject most Dubai parents are least equipped to supervise. English can be read, maths can be checked against an answer, and a history essay can be judged on whether it makes sense. A page of control accounts can do none of those things for a parent who has never studied bookkeeping, and that is why Accounting tutoring runs longer and less accountably than tutoring in almost any other option subject.

The way out is to audit the process instead of the content. An auditor does not re-do a company's bookkeeping; they check that source documents exist, that figures trace from one place to another, and that exceptions are investigated. A parent can do the same thing with a tutor's work, and the three checks involved require no accounting knowledge at all. They are: does the student's own numbered working exist for each session, do the error counts trace from one paper to the next, and is a repeating error being treated as an exception or ignored.

That is the whole method and it works because Accounting produces unusually clean evidence. The subject is procedural and sequential, so every mistake belongs to one of three classes. A transposition error is a wrong digit in the right place. A direction error is a correct figure entered on the wrong side. A format error is correct figures presented in a structure the syllabus does not credit. You can count all three on a marked page without knowing what the page is about, which makes them the ideal measure for a parent to hold.

The second part of the audit is grade movement, and here the honest answer is that it is the least reliable thing available in the short term. A mock mark depends on which paper the Dubai school chose, how it was marked internally and where the school estimated the boundary. Cambridge sets real boundaries after a series against cohort performance, so a February mock boundary is a staff judgement, not a published figure. Error counts move earlier and lie less.

On the search term itself: IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We target the phrase because it is what Dubai parents type, and then answer it properly. The market's in-home rates are published further down with their sources, alongside a format comparison that is specific to this subject rather than generic. Everything we deliver is one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

Nothing here is a promise about a result. No tutor can promise a grade in 0452 and any provider offering one is making a representation it cannot support. What this page commits to is narrower and testable: dated workings in your possession, three numbers you can count yourself, and a review point at which stopping is a real option rather than a difficult conversation.
bullets: Ask for the student's numbered workings, not the tutor's worked examples
Count three error classes per paper: transposition, direction, format
Check that a repeating error is named as an exception and attacked
Treat Dubai mock grades as a rough position, not a measurement
Twelve weeks and four comparable papers is the smallest reliable trail

dubai/cambridge-igcse-accounting-0452-ho.programmesIntro: What counts as evidence of progress changes with the stage a student is at. The notes below say what to look for at each point in the Cambridge commerce pathway in Dubai.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Accounting 0452 covers seven topic areas and is assessed entirely by written examination, with no coursework. Because nothing is internally assessed, the only evidence that predicts the outcome is marked written practice under timing. Everything else, including school effort grades and teacher comments, is a proxy for that.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the subject sits in a commerce option block, often alongside Business Studies, and the critical evidence landmark is the Year 10 end-of-year assessment. Accounting is sequential, so a weak result there is not a snapshot: it is a gap that will still be present in Year 11 unless somebody goes back for it, and it is far cheaper to audit then than in February.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: No Accounting yet, but the evidence that predicts it is already in the house. A maths book with two arithmetic slips per page predicts two transposition errors per ledger. That is the single most useful pre-Year-10 indicator, and it is available for free in any exercise book from the last term.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai families arriving from an Indian-curriculum school, the predictable gap is vocabulary and layout convention rather than numeracy, and it shows up as format errors in the first Year 10 assessment. Two sessions usually close it. Keeping the last assessment from the previous school makes that diagnosis a ten-minute job rather than a term of guessing.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Accounting 9706 raises the demand on interpretation rather than on procedure. The evidence to look at before the transition is not the IGCSE grade but the proportion of it that came from written comment rather than from arithmetic, because that is the half that carries forward and the half AS examines harder.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai sixth form offers 9706 it usually sets a 0452 grade condition. A student whose marked scripts show clean ledgers and thin interpretation comments has exactly the profile that struggles in the first AS term, and the useful spend in Year 11 is on the comments rather than on more ledger drill.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: No direct Accounting equivalent exists in the Diploma. Financial statements appear inside Business Management, which also carries an internally assessed research project, so the evidence a Diploma student produces is drafts and supervisor feedback rather than timed scripts, under strict rules about authorship.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are roughly 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment and three new IB schools join the 2026-27 intake. For an Accounting student the relevant point is that the Diploma route sets no requirement in the subject, so a 0452 grade matters for learning rather than for admission there.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-accounting-0452-ho.subjectsIntro: Evidence takes a different form in each subject a Dubai commerce block pairs with Accounting. The notes below describe what a parent can actually verify in each, which is also how to tell a thorough tutor from a pleasant one.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: The cleanest evidence of any option subject: errors fall into three countable classes and the counts can be compared across papers. Ask for the student's numbered workings and the count, and the subject stops being opaque to a parent without accounting training.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: The usual partner subject. Evidence here is behavioural rather than numerical: does the answer refer to the business in the printed case, and does it reach a judgement. Countable, but you are counting sentences rather than arithmetic slips.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: The evidence is diagram accuracy and the number of steps in a causal chain. A marked script annotated 'reasoning stops after one step' is useful feedback; one annotated 'needs more depth' is not, and the difference is how to judge a tutor's marking.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: If the Accounting workings show correct method with wrong arithmetic, the evidence is pointing at maths. That is worth noticing because it is a cheaper problem: a few 0580 sessions beat several Accounting sessions treating a symptom at Accounting rates.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Relevant to the interpretation half of 0452. Students whose English work shows thin development write thin comments on financial performance, and the two weaknesses appear in both sets of marked scripts at the same time.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Many Dubai candidates sit ESL, and the Accounting evidence shows it as terminology slips: provision for reserve, drawings for expenses. These are visible on a marked page and are not a sign of weak understanding, which is worth knowing before buying content hours.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Carried by stronger Dubai cohorts alongside the commerce options. The evidence to watch is seasonal: Accounting accuracy often dips in the term 0606 becomes demanding, and that is a time-budget problem rather than a comprehension problem.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Common in Dubai commerce-leaning blocks. Progress evidence is completed practical task files with error counts, so it is countable in the same spirit as Accounting, and a student who manages one well often manages the other.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Frequently the competing option at Year 9. Its evidence trail includes a skills paper, which produces early measurable signals in map and graph work, so the two subjects give feedback on different timescales across Years 10 and 11.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the option block by many non-Arab students in Dubai, where Arabic is a mandatory subject in private schools regardless of curriculum. Worth tracking separately in the evidence file because the school timetable treats it as compulsory rather than optional.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-accounting-0452-ho.regionsIntro: These notes are about the practical business of generating evidence in a Dubai household: when a student can realistically sit an uninterrupted paper, and what each community's rhythm does to that.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Apartments with shared study space, so the weekly structured paper usually lands at the weekend. Keeping the dated workings in one folder matters more here than in a villa, because paper migrates in a flat and an undated script is worth very little.

regions.name: Al Barsha and The Greens
regions.note: Short school runs make a weekday evening slot realistic, which allows the useful split: paper written midweek, marking reviewed at the weekend. The gap between writing and seeing the marking is what stops a student recalling their answer instead of rereading it.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Late returns from co-curricular commitments push weekday sessions past 7pm, and accuracy work after a long day produces error counts that overstate the problem. Weekend papers give a cleaner baseline for the file.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Local supply of commerce specialists is thinner than in the Jumeirah corridor, which historically meant the choice of tutor was made on proximity. The evidence standard should not vary with distance, and over video it does not have to.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Dense in schools with well-subscribed commerce options, so group tuition is common. Worth knowing for the audit: group sessions rarely produce individually marked workings, so the evidence file stays empty even when attendance is perfect.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Weekend mornings are the most productive window, and a full structured paper plus live marking needs about two uninterrupted hours. Families here tend to produce the most consistent evidence trails for exactly that reason.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Heavy congestion between 4pm and 6pm makes travel-based arrangements unreliable in term time, and an inconsistent slot produces an inconsistent file. A fixed online slot that never slips is what makes week-on-week comparison possible at all.

sections.heading: Three checks a Dubai parent can run without knowing any accounting
paragraphs: The first check is for source documents. Ask to see what your child wrote, not what the tutor demonstrated. A folder of beautiful worked examples in a tutor's handwriting is evidence that the tutor can do Accounting, which was never in question. A folder of the student's own numbered workings, dated, with somebody else's marks on them, is evidence about your child. If the first folder exists and the second does not, the sessions have been lectures.

The second check is tracing. Take two papers from different weeks and ask for the error counts. The numbers should be comparable, which means both papers were marked the same way and the counts cover the same three classes. If the tutor cannot produce them in a minute, they are not being kept, and a count reconstructed on request from memory is not a count. This is the single most informative question available to a parent in this subject.

The third check is exceptions. In any set of marked papers one or two errors will keep reappearing. The audit question is whether the tutor has named them and done something specific, or whether general practice is being used in the hope they wash out. Ask what the current target is. A good answer is a sentence: 'depreciation on disposals, down from four instances a paper to one'. A poor answer is 'we are working through past papers'.

The table lays these out with what good looks like in each case. None of it requires you to know what a control account is. It requires only that you ask for documents, numbers and a named target, which is exactly what you would ask for about any other service you were paying several thousand dirhams for across a year.

sections.heading: Why the student's own workings are the only usable evidence
paragraphs: Accounting is unusual in how completely it hides a student's understanding from a final answer. A statement can balance for the wrong reasons, and a wrong figure can carry forward so that every subsequent line is consistent and incorrect. This means the answer alone is close to uninformative. The workings are where the thinking is, and a marker who only looks at totals is marking the wrong thing.

It also means practice has to be numbered and legible, which sounds like a trivial administrative point and is not. A student who writes workings in a scatter across the page cannot be told where the error entered, so they learn that the answer was wrong and nothing about why. Insisting on numbered, ordered workings is the cheapest single intervention available in this subject, and it is one a parent can enforce without understanding a line of it.

This is also why practice has to be independent. A script produced with a tutor sitting alongside measures the pair. The characteristic 0452 failures are failures of unsupported execution: reversing a direction under time pressure, losing track of which side an adjustment belongs to, forgetting a closing entry. All of those disappear when somebody is watching, and reappear in the exam hall.

So the arrangement that generates evidence is simple and slightly inconvenient. The student writes alone, timed, and sends it in. The tutor marks it with the error located and classified, and returns it before the session. The session is spent on the classified errors and on a second attempt at the same question type. Everything in the file is then about the candidate rather than about the arrangement.
bullets: Require numbered, ordered workings; unreadable workings cannot be diagnosed
Practice written alone and timed, then sent in for marking
Marking that locates the error, not marking that scores the answer
A second attempt at the same question type in the following session

sections.heading: The three error classes, and how to count them yourself
paragraphs: Every mistake in a 0452 script belongs to one of three classes, and the classes are distinguishable by sight rather than by understanding. A transposition error is a digit problem: the right figure in the wrong form, 4,570 written as 4,750, or a total added incorrectly. A direction error is a side problem: the correct amount entered as a debit when it should have been a credit, or deducted when it should have been added. A format error is a presentation problem: the figures are right and the structure is not what the syllabus credits.

Each class has a different cause and a different fix, which is why counting them separately matters. Transposition errors are an accuracy and checking habit, and they respond to a mechanical routine rather than to teaching. Direction errors are conceptual: the student has not internalised what the entry represents, and more drill alone will not help. Format errors are pure syllabus knowledge, and they close in one or two sessions with somebody who knows the required presentation.

A parent can count all three on a marked page. Transposition errors appear as a corrected figure with the same digits. Direction errors appear as an amount moved from one column to another. Format errors appear as a comment about structure, or as a whole section rewritten in a different order. You do not need to know why the structure is wrong to notice that the marker has rewritten it.

The reason this is worth the ten minutes is that it converts an opaque subject into three numbers that move. A student at six transposition, three direction and two format errors in week one, sitting at two, zero and zero by week six, has improved in a way no mock grade would have shown that early. A student whose direction count has not moved after six weeks has a conceptual gap that more practice is not going to close, and that is a finding worth acting on.

sections.heading: The errors that carry forward, and why one mistake can look like ten
paragraphs: This is the single most misread thing in Accounting marking, and it causes Dubai families to buy hours they do not need. A statement is a chain, so a mistake in an early step propagates: the gross profit is wrong, therefore the profit for the year is wrong, therefore the capital figure is wrong, therefore the statement does not balance. A marker sees four wrong figures. The student made one mistake.

Cambridge markers generally handle this through own-figure credit, awarding marks for correct method applied to a figure the student brought forward, which is why a script can look catastrophic and score respectably. The practical consequence for a parent reading marked work is to resist counting wrong numbers. Count located errors instead, which is what a properly marked script shows and why the marking has to locate rather than score.

The diagnostic consequence is more important. If a tutor responds to a propagated error by re-teaching the whole topic, several hours are being spent on material the student knows. The correct response is to find the upstream step and fix only that, which is usually a single conceptual point and often a direction error. This is the difference between a tutor who marks and a tutor who marks diagnostically, and it is visible in the plan for the next session.

The audit question that catches this is short: of the errors in this paper, how many were separate mistakes? A tutor who has marked the script properly will answer with a small number and name the upstream step. A tutor who has not will describe the topic. Ask it once per block and you will learn more about the tutoring than a term of progress conversations would tell you.

sections.heading: A twelve-week 0452 trail for a Dubai Year 11
paragraphs: The block below is written out because 'we will track progress' is a phrase every tutoring provider uses and almost nobody specifies. It assumes a student with direction errors in the verification and procedures areas and weak interpretation comments, which is the commonest Year 11 profile in this subject. It is an illustration rather than a prescription, and the point of publishing it is so you can ask any provider for something comparable.

Note the structure of the measurement. The same component is sat in week one and week eleven so that the comparison is like for like. The error counts are reported every week, in the same three classes, so the trend does not depend on a grade estimate. And weeks four and eight are explicitly decision points rather than milestones, meaning stopping or changing the target is on the table at both.

Note also how little content teaching appears. Three of the twelve weeks involve re-teaching, and they are the weeks where the diagnosis said direction errors indicated a conceptual gap. The remaining weeks are practice, marking and conversation about the marking, because in a procedural subject that is what moves marks. A plan weighted towards demonstration should prompt a question about why.

Twelve weeks also happens to fit the gap between a Dubai school's February mock and a June series with room to spare, which is when most families in this subject actually start. Starting at the Year 10 end-of-year assessment instead gives the same twelve weeks at lower pressure and usually at lower total cost, because the gaps are smaller and fewer of them have compounded.

sections.heading: What a Dubai mock mark and a school report can tell you
paragraphs: A mock grade is the evidence Dubai parents have most of and it carries less information than it appears to. Each centre selects or writes its own mock, marks it internally, and estimates where the boundary sits. Cambridge sets real boundaries after each series against how the cohort performed, so a February boundary is a professional judgement by the school rather than a published figure. Two Dubai students with the same understanding can receive a 5 and a 7.

The reporting scale compounds it. Some Dubai centres report IGCSE on the 9 to 1 scale and others on A* to G, depending on the syllabus version entered, while sixth-form conditions are quoted on one or the other. A parent reading 'grade 6 required' against a mock reported as a B is comparing two different systems, and this is one of the most common misreadings we see in first messages from families.

What a mock is genuinely good for is the script underneath it. Ask the school for the marked paper and the mark breakdown by question rather than the grade. That document is free, it is the most useful thing a tutor can see before a first session, and for Accounting it is particularly informative because the error classes are visible on it immediately.

School reports are a weaker signal still, because effort grades and attainment grades get conflated and because a comment written for thirty students is necessarily general. The exception is a specific remark naming a topic area. 'Struggles with control accounts' is a diagnosis and worth acting on; 'needs to apply himself more consistently' is a classroom-management note and should not be bought hours against.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Dubai for Accounting: the market, and what we actually do
paragraphs: IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The market's rates belong on the page anyway, because a family searching for a home tutor is pricing a real option. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour with travel absorbed, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are common.

Online one-to-one is quoted lower: roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 for an exam-board specialist, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and TutorChase quoting AED 270. Those are the providers' own published figures from 2026 and not an IB Gram price list; our route starts with a free trial lesson and a plan agreed with the family.

For the audit this page is about, the format difference that matters is not the rate. It is whether the arrangement produces a file. In-home sessions default to one long weekly visit, because travel makes short visits uneconomic, and long visits tend to be spent working through problems together. Together is the enemy of evidence: the script measures the pair. The format that generates a usable trail is the one where the student writes alone and somebody marks it, and that is easier to sustain over video.

The honest counter-argument stands. A Year 10 student who will not sit down without an adult present is better served by an adult in the room, and the in-home market rate may be buying supervision rather than subject depth. Supervision is a legitimate purchase. It is simply a different one, and a family should know which of the two they are paying for.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the option block
paragraphs: Any honest account of a Dubai student's week has to include the mandatory subjects, because they occupy timetable space that families planning tutoring often forget. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational detail is specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. For a family planning Accounting tutoring the relevant arithmetic is simple: these subjects are already in the week, so the free evening hours are fewer than a timetable of eight IGCSE options suggests.

One constraint worth knowing for anyone considering tutoring in these subjects too. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and schools are required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. That is a real limit on how support in those subjects can be described, and it is a reason to treat them separately from an option subject like 0452 rather than bundling everything into one plan.

sections.heading: How sessions run, the limits, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A family sends a marked 0452 paper or the topic areas the school has flagged. The trial lesson is free, collects no card details, and is spent classifying the errors on that paper. It ends with a written note: the three baseline counts, the named upstream steps, a target, and an estimate of how many sessions it should take. If the estimate is four sessions, the note says four.

Sessions then run one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with workings on a shared screen. Practice is set, written alone and timed, marked with every error located and classified, and returned before the next session. The counts go to the parent in plain language, and the scripts belong to the family in date order. That is the file, and it is the thing that makes the tutoring auditable by somebody who has never studied the subject.

On availability, the honest version. Accounting has a smaller cohort in Dubai than maths or the sciences, and the specialists who can mark financial statements and incomplete records properly are not always free at the hours families want. When nobody suitable is available we say so, name the limitation on the nearest alternative, and give the likely wait. We would rather lose a booking than put a generalist in front of a Year 11 eight weeks out.

Two boundaries do not move. A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced, and nobody here will produce assessed material for a student under any board. And we reference Cambridge material rather than distributing it, working from the copies the school has issued. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE premises, and makes no promise about a grade.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A photograph of a marked 0452 attempt with the school's annotations visible is the fastest start available, and it is free. If there is no marked paper, the list of topic areas the school has raised will do. Naming the areas rather than the subject is what turns a first reply into a plan instead of a questionnaire.

process.title: Free trial lesson, spent classifying errors
process.description: One session at no cost and with no card details collected, worked through your child's own attempt. It produces the three baseline counts, the upstream steps behind any propagated errors, a named target and a session estimate. The note is yours whether or not you book anything after it.

process.title: Set the target and the metric together
process.description: The target names an error class and an area, such as direction errors in the verification topic. The metric is instances per paper. Both go in writing before the block starts, because a target agreed afterwards is always the one that happens to have been met.

process.title: Student writes alone, tutor marks and locates
process.description: Practice is written independently and timed, then sent in. Marking locates each error and classifies it rather than scoring the answer, and separates genuine mistakes from figures that were carried forward. The session works the located errors and repeats one question of the same type.

process.title: Decide at four sessions and again at eight
process.description: Two fixed decision points with stopping as a real option at both. If the target count is not falling, the diagnosis or the match is wrong and more hours will not fix either. The counts, the scripts and the written note stay with the family in all cases, including when the decision is to stop.

whyPoints.title: The subject stops being opaque
whyPoints.description: Three error classes a parent can count on a marked page without knowing what a ledger is. That is the whole proposition of this page, and it is checkable against any tutor, including ours. Accounting is the one option subject where this kind of audit is genuinely easy.

whyPoints.title: Marking locates, it does not score
whyPoints.description: A marked script shows where each error entered and whether later wrong figures were separate mistakes or one mistake carried forward. That distinction decides whether the next three hours re-teach a topic the student knows or fix the single step that actually failed.

whyPoints.description: Work written alone and timed, because the characteristic failures in this subject are failures of unsupported execution. They vanish when an adult is sitting alongside and reappear in the exam hall, which is the main reason a long weekly supervised session can feel productive and change very little.

whyPoints.title: Two fixed decision points
whyPoints.description: Four sessions and eight sessions, with stopping on the table at both. The most expensive thing in Dubai tutoring is not an hourly rate; it is a block that renews quietly for three terms because nobody set a point at which the evidence had to justify continuing.

faqs.question: I know nothing about accounting. How can I tell whether 0452 tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Run three checks that need no accounting knowledge. Ask to see your child's own dated, numbered workings rather than the tutor's worked examples. Ask for error counts on two papers from different weeks and check they are comparable. And ask what the current named target is, expecting an answer like 'direction errors in control accounts, four a paper down to one'. If the workings do not exist, the counts are not kept and the target is 'working through past papers', there is nothing yet to evaluate.

faqs.question: What are the three error classes in Accounting that I should be counting?
faqs.answer: Transposition, direction and format. A transposition error is a digit problem, such as 4,570 written as 4,750 or a total added wrongly. A direction error is a side problem, where the correct amount is entered as a debit instead of a credit. A format error is correct figures presented in a structure the syllabus does not credit. You can see all three on a marked page: corrected digits, amounts moved between columns, and sections the marker has rewritten in a different order.

faqs.question: Why does one mistake in my child's statement make ten figures wrong?
faqs.answer: Because a statement is a chain. An early error carries forward, so the gross profit, the profit for the year and the capital figure are all wrong from one mistake, and the statement will not balance. Cambridge markers generally award own-figure credit for correct method applied to a figure brought forward, which is why a script can look dreadful and score respectably. The practical point is to count located errors rather than wrong numbers, and to ask a tutor how many separate mistakes a paper actually contained.

faqs.question: Should my child do 0452 practice with the tutor or on their own?
faqs.answer: Alone, timed, then sent in for marking. The characteristic failures in Accounting are failures of unsupported execution: reversing a direction under pressure, losing track of which side an adjustment belongs to, omitting a closing entry. Those disappear when somebody is sitting alongside and reappear in the exam hall. A script produced together measures the pair rather than the candidate, which is why a long supervised session can feel productive and leave the evidence file empty.

faqs.question: How long before marked Accounting work shows a real trend?
faqs.answer: About four papers, which in practice means four to six weeks for a weekly block and twelve weeks for a full before-and-after comparison. One improved paper proves nothing: it may reflect an easier question set or a better night's sleep. Four independently written papers of the same component, marked the same way, with three error counts each, is the smallest set that supports a conclusion. That is also why the first and last papers in a block should be the same component rather than two different ones.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send an Accounting tutor to our villa or apartment in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with workings on a shared screen. For the evidence this page is about, the format matters: online arrangements make it easier to sustain the pattern of writing alone and having the script marked, which is where the usable record comes from.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai tutor's written feedback on an Accounting paper contain?
faqs.answer: Four things. Where each error entered, which class it belongs to, whether later wrong figures were separate mistakes or one error carried forward, and what the next session will do about the most frequent one. A tick-and-total marking job gives none of that. The difference is not thoroughness for its own sake: a tutor who cannot separate one propagated error from ten separate ones will spend hours re-teaching a topic your child already knows.

faqs.question: Does a direction error mean my child needs more practice?
faqs.answer: Usually the opposite. A direction error means the entry has been memorised rather than understood, so the student does not know which way it should go when the question is phrased unfamiliarly. More drill reinforces the memorisation. The fix is conceptual: a short re-teach of what the entry actually represents, after which the error class tends to collapse quickly. If a direction count has not moved after six weeks of practice, that is the finding, and it should change the plan.

faqs.question: Can I ask a tutor to review work my child's existing tutor has marked?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Accounting it is a reasonable single purchase. One session reading the existing marked papers, counting the three error classes across them and writing a note on what the trail shows is usually enough to tell you whether the current arrangement is doing its job. It frequently concludes that no change is needed, which is a useful outcome for a family who simply had no way of judging an opaque subject.

faqs.question: How reliable is a mock grade from a Dubai school in Accounting?
faqs.answer: As a rough position only. Each centre selects or writes its own mock, marks it internally and estimates its own boundary, while Cambridge sets real boundaries after a series against cohort performance. Two Dubai students with the same understanding can receive different grades. Ask instead for the marked script and the breakdown by question, which is free and is the single most useful document a tutor can see, because the error classes are visible on it at a glance.

faqs.question: My child's report says he must apply himself more. Is that worth buying tutoring against?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. A comment written for a class of thirty is necessarily general, and effort remarks get conflated with attainment. The exception is a report that names a topic area: 'struggles with control accounts' is a diagnosis you can act on and cost. 'Needs to apply himself consistently' is a classroom-management note. Before committing to hours, ask the subject teacher which topic areas are weak, because that question converts a report into something a tutor can work from.

faqs.question: Do the UAE mandatory subjects affect how much tutoring time we actually have?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families regularly underestimate it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on forty-minute lesson units. Those lessons are already in the week, so the number of free evening hours available for an option subject like Accounting is smaller than an eight-subject timetable implies.

faqs.question: What does an in-home Accounting tutor cost in Dubai compared with online?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one is quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour with travel absorbed, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are common. Online, a qualified subject tutor is quoted at AED 150 to 300 and a specialist at AED 200 to 450. These are the providers' published 2026 figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check my child's school assignment in Accounting?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the topic it rests on, discuss how to approach it and give feedback on what your child has written. A tutor will not produce the piece or rework it into something your child did not write, and that limit applies under every board. Cambridge IGCSE Accounting has no coursework component, so school-set tasks here are internal practice rather than assessed material, but we apply the same boundary to them and say so to the student at the outset.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai family start auditing the tutoring rather than trusting it?
faqs.answer: At the fourth session. By then there should be two or three independently written papers, three error counts each, and a named target. That is the earliest point at which the three checks produce a real answer, and it is early enough that stopping costs very little. Leaving the first audit until the February mock means a term has already been bought on faith, and in a sequential subject like Accounting a term of unaddressed gaps compounds rather than waits.
