intro.heading: What a 0606 entry actually means for your child
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate syllabus sat alongside Mathematics 0580 or 0607, almost always in Year 11. It is not an extension of the ordinary maths course and it is not tiered: there is one route, reported on an A* to E scale, and the papers assume the candidate has already met every Extended topic in 0580. Most Dubai schools enter only a small group of candidates, which is why a parent who goes looking for an Additional Maths tutor in Dubai finds the subject missing from the list on most tutoring sites and present only as a line in a long subject menu.

The first shock for families is the content. Additional Mathematics 0606 introduces differentiation and integration, the factor and remainder theorems, logarithmic and exponential functions, permutations and combinations, the binomial expansion, circular measure in radians and vectors in two dimensions. A student who scored comfortably on 0580 can open a 0606 Paper 2 and recognise almost nothing on the first page. That is normal rather than alarming, and it is the gap a specialist session is for.

The second shock is pace. The course is usually taught in a single academic year, often in fewer timetabled periods than the main maths course, and in several Dubai schools it runs as a twilight or extension class outside the ordinary timetable. There is no coursework and no practical, so every mark is decided in two written papers in the exam room. Nothing is banked in advance, which makes the quality of written practice across the year the only variable a family can actually influence.

This is where the search for a home tutor starts. A parent wants someone sitting beside their child, working a question through on paper. That instinct is sound, because 0606 is learned by writing rather than by watching. What has changed is that the person doing the writing no longer has to be in the room, and in a subject this thin on local teachers, insisting on proximity narrows the choice to whoever happens to be free within a twenty-minute drive of your community.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. In the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and the trade is deliberate. Instead of the nearest available maths teacher, your child works with someone who teaches 0606 every week and can mark a question in front of them and explain the marks lost while the working is still fresh. The rest of this page sets out what that looks like week by week, what the Dubai market charges for both formats, and what evidence you should expect to see inside the first month of online 0606 tuition.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.programmesIntro: An Additional Mathematics entry sits at one point on a longer route, and the programmes below are the ones a Dubai family is choosing between either side of the Year 11 decision. Each reads a 0606 grade differently when it looks at an application, and that difference is worth understanding before you buy a single hour of tuition.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The main maths course almost every British-curriculum school in Dubai enters, tiered into Core and Extended. Extended candidates meet algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics across two written papers. It contains no calculus, which is exactly why a strong 0580 grade is a poor predictor of comfort in 0606. The two syllabuses are usually taught by different teachers in different periods.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Extended tier is the default in the selective British schools and the near-default everywhere else, because sixth forms that offer A Level Maths or the IB Diploma generally want to see Extended content rather than Core. Families who later ask why 0606 feels impossible usually find their child was fine on Extended algebra and was never taught to differentiate anything.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A single-tier syllabus graded A* to E, assessed by two written papers of equal weight and no coursework. It is taken alongside 0580 or 0607 rather than instead of either. The content is deliberately a bridge to AS Level: functions and inverse functions, polynomials, surds and indices, logarithms, trigonometric identities, radians, series, permutations and combinations, vectors, and both differentiation and integration.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use 0606 in two quite different ways. Some enter a small top set as preparation for A Level Mathematics in their own sixth form. Others enter it as an enrichment option with limited timetable support and leave the harder half of the syllabus to be covered at speed in the spring term. Which of those your child is in changes the tutoring plan completely, and the honest way to find out is to ask the head of maths how many periods a week the class gets.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The two-year route most Dubai British-curriculum sixth forms offer after IGCSE, built from Pure Mathematics, Mechanics and Probability and Statistics components. A candidate who has sat 0606 arrives already able to differentiate a polynomial, integrate to find an area, work in radians and expand a binomial, which removes a substantial amount of the first-term workload in Pure Mathematics 1.
programmes.countryNote: This is the real argument for 0606 in Dubai. Sixth forms here run on tight timetables and large AS cohorts, and the first weeks of Pure Mathematics 1 move quickly through material 0606 has already introduced. Students who skipped Additional Mathematics can still do well, but they spend the autumn term learning calculus for the first time while their classmates are consolidating it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Split into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard or Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is calculus-heavy and proof-heavy from the first term, and it is the route Dubai's IB schools steer strong mathematicians towards. Both courses carry an internal exploration written by the student over several months.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run both IGCSE at 16 and the IB Diploma at 18, so a Year 11 taking 0606 may be heading for Analysis and Approaches rather than A Level. The overlap is real but partial: 0606 covers differentiation and integration of standard functions, while Analysis and Approaches Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and far heavier algebraic manipulation. A 0606 grade is evidence of readiness, not a head start on the whole course.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.subjectsIntro: The grid below is not a subject menu, because 0606 is one subject. It is the ten strands of the Cambridge 0606 syllabus, with what each one actually asks and where candidates in Dubai lose marks on it. Use it to tell your child's tutor where to start, rather than beginning at the front of the textbook in week one.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: Products, quotients, chains, trigonometric and exponential functions, then stationary points, increasing and decreasing functions, connected rates of change and small increments. Marks go on sign errors in the chain rule and on failing to justify whether a stationary point is a maximum or minimum. The second derivative test has to be shown, not implied.

subjects.name: Integration
subjects.description: Integration of powers, exponentials and trigonometric functions, definite integrals, areas between curves and kinematics problems linking displacement, velocity and acceleration. The commonest loss is a missing constant of integration in an indefinite integral, followed by area questions where the limits are taken in the wrong order or a region below the axis is counted as positive.

subjects.name: Functions and inverse functions
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite functions, inverse functions and the condition for one to exist, modulus functions and their graphs. Candidates lose marks by stating a range as an interval of the domain, by forgetting that an inverse requires a one-to-one function, and by sketching a modulus graph without marking where the reflection happens.

subjects.name: Logarithmic and exponential functions
subjects.description: Laws of logarithms, change of base, solving equations that reduce to logarithmic or exponential form, and linearising a relationship to find constants from a straight-line graph. The straight-line-form question is the one Dubai students most often leave blank: taking logs of both sides of a power law and reading the gradient and intercept is a procedure, and it is teachable in one session.

subjects.name: Factors of polynomials
subjects.description: The factor theorem, the remainder theorem, factorising cubics and solving the resulting equations. Marks are lost in the division step rather than the idea: a dropped sign in synthetic division wrecks the quadratic factor and every mark that depends on it. Checking a root by substitution before continuing costs twenty seconds and saves four marks.

subjects.name: Trigonometric identities and equations
subjects.description: The reciprocal functions, the Pythagorean identities, proving identities and solving equations over a stated interval. The single largest source of lost marks in this strand is giving one solution where the interval contains three, or working in degrees when the question is set in radians. Reading the interval aloud before starting is a habit worth drilling.

subjects.name: Circular measure
subjects.description: Radians, arc length, sector area and the composite shapes built from them, usually combined with triangle trigonometry in a multi-step question. Candidates who have only ever worked in degrees convert back and forth repeatedly and accumulate rounding error. Learning the small exact values in radians removes most of that, and it is a rote task that can be set as homework.

subjects.name: Permutations and combinations
subjects.description: Arrangements, selections, restrictions such as items that must stay together or apart, and the distinction between order mattering and not. This strand rewards clear structure over cleverness: the examiner wants to see the case split written down. Students who try to do it in their heads lose method marks even when the final number is right.

subjects.name: Series
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to n terms, the sum to infinity and its condition, and the binomial expansion of a bracket raised to a positive integer power. Binomial questions asking for a specific term rather than the whole expansion are the ones most often attempted the long way, which runs the candidate out of time on a paper where time is tight.

subjects.name: Vectors in two dimensions
subjects.description: Position vectors, magnitude, unit vectors, addition and scalar multiplication, and problems involving relative velocity or a point dividing a line in a given ratio. Marks are lost on notation as much as on method: a vector answer written without the column or unit-vector form, or a magnitude given as a vector, does not earn the accuracy mark.

The constraint here is the number of competing activities on a Jumeirah weekday evening, which argues for a fixed weekly 0606 slot booked for the whole term rather than week-by-week rescheduling.

regions.note: A long bus run from most sixth-form-feeder schools, with arrivals after 4.30pm common in the Ranches. Families here feel the travel-cost problem most sharply: a tutor driving out from Deira for one hour is charging for at least ninety minutes of road time, in both directions.

The cross-city drive from the Marina side is the reason local in-home rates sit at the top of the Dubai band, and the reason a specialist on video costs less here than a generalist in a car.

regions.note: Closest to the largest cluster of British-curriculum schools in the emirate, so the walk-in tuition centre is a real option in Barsha. What a centre cannot usually do is staff a 0606 class, because the cohort in any one year is too small to fill a group.

regions.note: Apartment-heavy communities with a lot of newly arrived families whose children joined a Dubai school mid-course. Catch-up on the first half of the 0606 syllabus is the usual request here, and it is the case where a twice-weekly block for six weeks does more than a weekly session for a term.

schoolClusters.city: Selective British schools, western Dubai
schoolClusters.note: The cluster where an Additional Mathematics entry is most likely to be a timetabled top-set course with its own teacher. Students here usually arrive at tuition with the algebra secure and the calculus half-finished, so sessions start at differentiation rather than at functions.

schoolClusters.city: Large British-curriculum schools, central and eastern Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Bigger year groups, broader ability ranges, and Additional Mathematics more often offered as an extension option with limited periods. The common pattern is a student who has met every topic once and practised none of them under timed conditions, which makes marked past papers the whole of the plan.

sections.heading: Why a 0606 search in Dubai returns so little
paragraphs: A search for a Cambridge IGCSE Additional Maths 0606 home tutor in Dubai turns up pages about IGCSE maths, A Level maths and IB maths, and almost nothing about 0606 itself. The reason is cohort size. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with 37% of them on a UK curriculum, and yet Additional Mathematics is entered by a small top set in the schools that offer it at all. A tuition centre cannot fill a group class from that, and a freelance tutor cannot specialise in a subject that generates a handful of enquiries a year in any one community.

The effect on parents is a market that quotes for the subject and then staffs it with whoever teaches maths. That is not necessarily a bad tutor, but it is a specific risk: 0606 is the first syllabus in the Cambridge sequence where the teacher needs to be fluent in calculus and in the way Cambridge marks calculus. Someone who teaches 0580 well can explain differentiation correctly and still miss that the mark scheme wants the second-derivative justification written down.

This page is built around the opposite assumption. The subject is narrow, so the tutor should be narrow too, and the only way to find a genuinely narrow 0606 teacher for a Dubai family is to stop filtering by driving distance. That is the trade this page is asking you to make, and the sections below put numbers on both sides of it rather than asserting it.

sections.heading: The two 0606 papers, and what each one costs you
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics is assessed entirely by two written papers of equal weight. There is no coursework, no practical and no tiering, so the grade is decided by two sittings and the candidate's ability to produce complete written solutions under time pressure. Both papers draw on the whole syllabus, which means there is no safe topic to drop and no paper on which a weak strand can be avoided.

The practical consequence is that the mark scheme matters as much as the mathematics. Cambridge awards method marks for a correct approach and accuracy marks for the right value, and a candidate who writes only a final answer forfeits the method marks when the arithmetic slips. In a subject where multi-step questions are the norm, that distinction routinely separates two grades between students who understand the same amount.

A second consequence is that pacing has to be taught as a separate skill. Both papers are long enough that a candidate who is secure on every strand can still lose a grade by spending twenty minutes on a question worth five marks. Timed question sets, rather than whole papers, are the usual way to fix that in the autumn term, because a full paper takes an evening to sit and an evening to mark and produces one data point where six short sets produce six.

The table below maps each component and each strand group to where marks are actually lost, drawn from what comes back on marked 0606 past papers rather than from the syllabus summary. Treat the durations and mark totals as indicative and confirm them against the syllabus document for your child's exam year, because Cambridge revises assessment structures between syllabus cycles and the version that counts is the one printed for that series. The school's own exams officer holds that document and will share it on request.

sections.heading: The calculus cliff, and the four causes behind most lost marks
paragraphs: Students who struggle with 0606 rarely struggle with all of it. Marked scripts tend to cluster around four causes, and separating them changes what a session is for. The first is notation: writing a derivative without saying what it is a derivative of, or giving a vector magnitude as a vector. These cost accuracy marks on questions the student has solved correctly, which makes them the cheapest marks available anywhere on the paper.

The second is the missing justification. Cambridge wants the nature of a stationary point established, not asserted, and wants the condition for an inverse or for a sum to infinity stated. The third is interval handling in trigonometry: a student who gives one solution where the stated range contains three has understood the identity and lost most of the question. The fourth is arithmetic under time pressure in the final long question, which is a pacing problem rather than a mathematical one.

Sorting a student's errors into those four buckets takes one marked paper and about twenty minutes. It is also the point at which tutoring stops being generic. A child whose problem is notation needs ten minutes of correction a week and nothing else; a child whose problem is pacing needs timed question sets and should not be taught any new content for a fortnight. Teaching both children the same syllabus order wastes most of the hour.

The fifth cause, which is not an error at all, deserves naming because it drives a good deal of unnecessary tutoring in Dubai. A student can be failing 0606 assessments because the underlying Extended 0580 algebra is not secure, in which case no amount of calculus teaching will help. Rearranging an equation, handling surds and manipulating algebraic fractions are assumed throughout 0606, and a diagnostic that tests only the new content will miss it entirely. Where that is the cause, the honest recommendation is to repair the foundation first, even though it is not what the family enquired about.
bullets: Notation: derivatives, vectors and ranges written in a form that cannot score
Missing justification: second-derivative test, conditions, domains
Interval handling: one solution given where three are required
Pacing: the last long question attempted with eight minutes left

sections.heading: What a home tutor costs in Dubai, and what the alternative costs
paragraphs: Market rates for private tuition in Dubai are published patchily, and most tutoring sites in this market publish no figure at all. The bands below are collected from providers who do publish and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list: our own pricing is discussed on a consultation after the free trial lesson, because the right number depends on session length, frequency and how many weeks are left.

What the bands show is that an in-home visit sits above an online session of the same quality, and that the gap is travel rather than teaching. A tutor crossing Dubai at six in the evening is selling you an hour and absorbing ninety minutes of road time, which has to be priced somewhere. It usually arrives either as a higher hourly rate or as a minimum booking of two hours, and for a subject like Additional Mathematics a second unbroken hour is often less productive than a second session later in the week.

The scarcity premium works the same way. Because few people teach 0606, a parent asking for it locally is competing for a very short list, and quotes rise accordingly. Removing the travel constraint widens the list to anyone who teaches the syllabus and can work Gulf Standard Time, which is the mechanism by which online 0606 tuition is usually both cheaper and more specialised rather than one or the other.

sections.heading: Travel, traffic and a 0606 session that starts at seven
paragraphs: The argument for in-home tuition is that nobody has to travel. In Dubai that is only true for the family. Somebody still crosses the city, and the hour they lose shapes what they can offer: a tutor who commits to a 5pm slot in Arabian Ranches cannot also take a 6.30pm in Mirdif, so the number of weekly slots they can sell is low and the price of each has to carry the gap. That is the arithmetic behind the in-home band in the table above.

It also shapes the schedule your child gets. School buses in the outer communities often arrive after 4.30pm, which leaves a window that collides with Al Khail Road and Sheikh Zayed Road at their worst. Families who insist on a visit usually end up with either a late start, a tired child, or a weekend slot that eats the one morning the household has free. A video session at seven in the evening, after dinner and after the bus, uses the hour when a Year 11 is actually able to concentrate.

None of this makes in-home tuition a bad product. For a primary-age child who needs an adult physically present, it is often the right answer, and there are capable independent tutors in Dubai doing it well. For a sixteen-year-old working through 0606 past papers, the physical presence buys very little and the travel costs a lot, and that is the specific case this page is about. IB Gram does not run in-person tutoring in Dubai at all, so the comparison above is a comparison with the rest of the market rather than between two things we sell.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what the first twelve weeks should produce
paragraphs: The most useful question a parent can ask a tutor is not what they charge but what they will send you. Tutoring that produces nothing you can read is impossible to judge until the results arrive, and by then the year is over. The schedule below is what a weekly 0606 arrangement should generate, and it is deliberately written as a set of documents rather than as a promise about grades, because the documents are the part anyone can verify.

Week one is diagnostic. A timed paper or a set of questions across every strand, marked to the published scheme, produces a map of which strands are secure and which are not, and an error log sorted by cause rather than by topic. That log is the plan. If a tutor begins teaching before producing one, they are teaching the syllabus rather than your child, and in a single-year course there is no time for that.

From there the pattern is teach, set, mark, re-test. What you should see on your side is a marked script every week or two with the mark scheme alongside it, and a short written note every fortnight naming what moved and what did not. Grade movement is not promised here and no tutor can honestly promise it, but the direction of travel on repeated question types is visible within about six weeks, and it is visible to you rather than described to you.

The reason to insist on documents rather than updates is that a flat trend is useful information and a verbal reassurance is not. If the re-test at week six shows the same errors as the diagnostic, the arrangement needs to change: a different explanation, a different homework pattern, or a different tutor. Families who only receive cheerful messages find this out in June. Families who receive marked scripts find it out in October, while there is still a term in which to act.

sections.heading: Does your child actually need 0606?
paragraphs: Sometimes the honest answer to a tutoring enquiry is that the subject should be dropped. Additional Mathematics is an optional extra sat alongside a full IGCSE timetable, and it is not required for entry to A Level Mathematics or to either IB Diploma maths course. A student carrying nine or ten subjects, a weak 0580 position and a 0606 entry they did not ask for is usually better served by securing the grades that count than by spreading the same hours across one more paper.

The case for keeping it is strongest in three situations. The first is a student heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics in a Dubai sixth form, where the calculus introduction removes real pressure from the autumn term. The second is a student applying to competitive engineering or mathematics courses who wants evidence of depth beyond the standard IGCSE set. The third is simply a student who enjoys it and finds 0580 unchallenging, which is a better reason than it sounds.

The case for dropping it is equally clear: a predicted grade below the school's own threshold, a timetable with no periods allocated to the subject, or a child whose 0580 Extended grade is not yet secure. Schools in Dubai are generally willing to have this conversation in the autumn term, and the entry can usually be withdrawn before the final entry deadline. That deadline is the part families miss, and it is covered in the next section.

sections.heading: Cambridge deadlines, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Cambridge runs its International GCSE exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. UAE centres sit the main series, and the deadlines that govern them fall months before the papers. The published key dates for the March 2027 series show the shape: an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Read that sequence backwards and the planning becomes obvious. The decision about whether a child sits 0606 at all is made roughly ten weeks before the first paper, by a school administrator working to an entry deadline. Mock results that arrive in late January are therefore evidence for a conversation that has already happened. A family that wants a say in the entry has to be looking at marked work in the autumn term, not in the spring.

One further Cambridge detail catches UAE families out. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's exact paper dates come from the school's own timetable for its zone, not from a date circulated in a parents' group. Check it against the school office and against cambridgeinternational.org.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a subject with no coursework
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics has no coursework and no practical, which removes the commonest academic-honesty problem in international education before it starts. There is no portfolio for anyone to interfere with and no draft to be improved by an adult. That is worth saying plainly, because this market contains providers selling finished assessed work for other subjects, and families reasonably want to know where the line sits.

The line in a maths subject falls around past papers and mock scripts. A tutor may teach a topic, set questions, mark them against the published mark scheme and explain why a mark was awarded or withheld. A tutor may not supply material a school has not released, sit anything on a student's behalf, or hand over answers to a piece of work the school intends to use as evidence of attainment. Published past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge; the right way to use them is to work from the official source and link to it, not to redistribute copies.

It is also worth being clear about regulation, because it is a fair question to ask any tutor in Dubai. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted by a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. IB Gram is a matching platform rather than a licensed school or training institute in the UAE, and we do not claim any regulator's approval.

faqs.question: Can I get a 0606 home tutor in Dubai who comes to the house?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and some agencies in Dubai do travel to homes, and market rates for that sit roughly in the AED 180-500 band according to Bestimate's 2026 survey, usually with a two-hour minimum to make the drive worth it. IB Gram does not sell that service anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we run only in India. For your child the practical question is whether a visit is worth the travel premium and the narrower choice of tutor it forces. For Additional Mathematics, where the teaching happens on paper and the scarce resource is someone who knows the syllabus, our answer is no.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 taught in most Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: No. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 and the UK curriculum accounted for 37% of enrolment, but Additional Mathematics is usually offered to a top set rather than a whole year group, and a good number of schools do not enter it at all. Some run it as a timetabled course with its own teacher; others offer it as an extension option with very few periods. The difference matters enormously for tutoring, because the second group arrives having met the calculus once and practised it almost never. Ask the head of maths how many periods a week the class gets.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Dubai Year 11 need for 0606?
faqs.answer: One well-structured hour a week from September, with homework marked between sessions, is enough for a student whose school teaches the course properly and whose 0580 Extended work is secure. Two sessions a week for six to eight weeks is the usual shape for a student who joined mid-course or whose school covered the first half at speed. In the eight weeks before the papers, the useful unit stops being teaching hours and becomes timed papers marked to the scheme. More hours on top of untouched homework changes nothing.

faqs.question: What does 0606 cover that Cambridge 0580 does not?
faqs.answer: The headline additions are differentiation and integration, which 0580 does not contain in any form. Beyond calculus, 0606 adds the factor and remainder theorems, logarithmic and exponential functions and their laws, radians and circular measure, trigonometric identities and equations over a stated interval, permutations and combinations, the binomial expansion, series including sums to infinity, inverse and composite functions with domain and range, and vectors in two dimensions. That is why a strong 0580 grade predicts very little about 0606 comfort, and why a 0606 tutor needs to be fluent in calculus rather than merely good at maths.

faqs.question: My daughter scored well in 0580 but is failing 0606 mocks. Why?
faqs.answer: This is the most common enquiry on this subject and it usually has a diagnosable cause rather than a general one. The four patterns that show up on marked scripts are notation that cannot score, missing justification where Cambridge wants a condition or a second-derivative test written down, incomplete solution sets in trigonometry where the interval contains more answers than were given, and arithmetic collapsing on the last long question because of pacing. All four are fixable and none of them mean she cannot do the mathematics. One marked paper sorted by cause will tell you which it is.

faqs.question: Does 0606 have coursework or a practical component?
faqs.answer: No. Additional Mathematics is assessed entirely by two written papers of equal weight, with no coursework, no practical and no tiering into Core and Extended. Everything is decided in the exam room, which has two consequences. There is nothing banked in advance to cushion a difficult paper, so written practice across the year is the only lever a family has. It also removes the academic-honesty problem that attaches to portfolio subjects, because there is no draft for an adult to improve and no assessed work for anyone to interfere with.

faqs.question: What is the market rate for an Additional Maths tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures cluster into bands rather than a single rate. Budget online tutors advertise from around AED 45-150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online from AED 150-300, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and IGCSE or IB specialists AED 200-450, with premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650. Those come from providers' own published pages and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey, not from us. Additional Mathematics tends to sit at the upper end of whichever band applies, because the number of people who teach it locally is small.

faqs.question: Can a 0606 session run after the Dubai school bus gets home?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it should. Buses serving the outer communities often arrive after 4.30pm, and the hour that follows is the worst of the Al Khail Road and Sheikh Zayed Road traffic as well as the hour a sixteen-year-old is least able to concentrate. A session between 6.30pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time, after dinner, is the slot that reliably works, and because the lesson is over live video there is no travel to add to either side of it. The slot is then fixed for the term.

faqs.question: Which 0606 topics should we fix first with eight weeks left?
faqs.answer: With eight weeks remaining the order should come from a marked paper rather than from the syllabus. In practice the highest-yield sequence for most candidates is the cheap-mark strands first, because they pay back fastest: notation corrections, series and binomial recall, circular measure in exact radians, and vector notation. Calculus comes next and takes the most time, so it needs the middle weeks. The final fortnight should be timed papers only, spent on the recurring causes in the error log rather than on new content, and no new topic should be introduced in the last ten days.

faqs.question: Do you mark my child's own 0606 past-paper scripts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the part of the arrangement worth paying for. Work is marked against the published Cambridge mark scheme with method marks and accuracy marks shown separately, so you can see whether a mark was lost to the mathematics or to the way it was written down. You receive the marked script, not just a score, along with an error log grouped by cause. Past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and we work from the official source and link to it rather than redistributing copies.

faqs.question: Is 0606 graded on the same nine-point scale as 0580?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge reports Additional Mathematics 0606 on an A* to E scale, which is narrower than the grading used on tiered syllabuses and has no Core and Extended split underneath it. There is one route through the subject and one set of papers. For a Dubai family this matters in two ways: a sixth-form application reads a 0606 grade as evidence of depth rather than as part of the headline count of IGCSE passes, and the UAE equivalency rules for the British track count accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects rather than optional extras, so 0606 is a bonus rather than a requirement.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai tutor need a MoHRE permit to teach 0606 privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor directly, and apply through the MoHRE smart app or the service page for private tutor licensing.

faqs.question: How does 0606 help with A Level Maths in a Dubai sixth form?
faqs.answer: It front-loads the first term. A candidate who has sat Additional Mathematics arrives in Pure Mathematics 1 already able to differentiate and integrate standard functions, work in radians, expand a binomial and use the factor theorem. Dubai sixth forms run large AS cohorts on tight timetables and move through that material quickly, so a student meeting calculus for the first time in September is learning while classmates consolidate. It is a head start rather than a requirement: A Level Mathematics assumes only Extended 0580 content as a formal entry point.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0606 specialist is free on our preferred evening?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than sending a generalist and calling it a 0606 tutor. The usual options are a different evening with a specialist, a slightly later slot on your preferred day, or a short wait while a slot opens, and in the meantime we will tell you honestly whether the work can start with a strong 0580 Extended teacher. Demand for this subject concentrates between January and May, so the week to ask is in the autumn term. Availability is a real constraint and concealing it would only waste your first month.

faqs.question: Can we start online 0606 tuition in the middle of the school year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families do, because the problem usually becomes visible after the first set of 0606 assessments. A mid-year start changes the shape rather than the content: the first session is a wider diagnostic because more of the syllabus has been taught, and the early weeks run twice weekly to close the gap before settling to one session. What a mid-year start cannot do is replace a term of missed practice in a few weeks, so the plan will name the topics that will not be covered and let you decide the priority.

intro.heading: How a live 0606 lesson is actually run
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject parents are most sceptical about teaching remotely, and the scepticism is reasonable if what you picture is a video call with two talking heads. That format does not work for Additional Mathematics, because the entire subject is a conversation about written working. What does work is a shared writing surface: the tutor on a tablet with a stylus, the student on a tablet or writing on paper and holding it to the camera, and both people looking at the same evolving page of algebra.

A typical hour has four parts, and the proportions matter more than the technology. Roughly ten minutes go on the homework marked since the last session, starting with a question that lost marks rather than with a summary. Twenty-five to thirty minutes go on new content or a repaired topic, taught by working examples with the student writing at the same time rather than watching. Fifteen minutes go on an unaided question the student attempts while the tutor stays quiet. The last five minutes set the homework and name what will be re-tested.

The unaided fifteen minutes is the part that gets cut when a session drifts, and it is the part that decides whether the lesson did anything. A student who has watched someone differentiate a quotient has not learned to differentiate a quotient, and the only way to find out is to make them do one with the help switched off. Online this is easier to enforce than it is in a room, because the tutor can mute, let the student write, and then see the whole attempt rather than an interrupted one.

Three things are kept from each session. The whiteboard file, which becomes a growing set of worked examples in your child's own notation. The homework, marked against the published Cambridge mark scheme before the next lesson. And the error log, which groups mistakes by cause rather than by topic. Those three artefacts are what make online 0606 lessons auditable, and they are the reason a parent who never sits in on a session can still tell whether it is working.

None of that requires expensive equipment, which is the other thing worth saying early. The scientific calculator your child will take into the exam, a stable connection and some way of showing written working are the whole of the requirement, and a phone propped against a stack of books pointed at an A4 pad meets the third. Families routinely spend money on a tablet before discovering the room is the problem rather than the hardware.

What this page does not do is claim online teaching is better in every situation. A twelve-year-old who needs an adult in the room to stay on task is a different case. A sixteen-year-old working through Cambridge 0606 Paper 1 questions is not: the work is written, the feedback is written, and the scarce resource is a teacher who knows how this syllabus is marked. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, so what follows describes the only format we sell here and the reasons it suits this particular subject.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.programmesIntro: Additional Mathematics is one of several ways a school stretches a strong mathematician before sixth form, and families in Dubai are often choosing between them without being told they are choices. The four qualifications below overlap heavily in content and differ in how they are assessed, which changes both the tutoring and what a sixth form reads into the grade.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, no coursework, single tier, reported A* to E. Content runs from functions, surds, polynomials and logarithms through trigonometric identities, radians, series, permutations and vectors to differentiation and integration. It is taken alongside a main maths IGCSE rather than instead of one, and the syllabus is openly designed as a bridge into AS Level work.
programmes.countryNote: The Cambridge route is the common one in Dubai simply because most British-curriculum schools here are Cambridge centres for maths. Where a school offers Additional Mathematics at all, it usually enters the same set that is already on Extended, and the teaching often sits outside the main timetable. That timetable position, rather than the syllabus itself, is what decides how much private support a Dubai student needs.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Edexcel's equivalent stretch qualification, assessed by two written papers and covering calculus, series, trigonometry, coordinate geometry, matrices and vectors. The topic list is close to 0606 without being identical: matrices appear here and not in the Cambridge syllabus, and the question style is noticeably more structured in places. A tutor needs to know which of the two a student is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of Dubai schools run Edexcel for maths and Cambridge for sciences, or switch boards between year groups, so mixed entries are more common here than parents expect. Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the exam dates for a 4PM1 candidate and a 0606 candidate in the same house can differ by weeks.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The first year of the A Level, built around Pure Mathematics 1 and a second component. It assumes Extended IGCSE content and then moves quickly into differentiation, integration, radians, trigonometric equations and series, which is the overlap that makes 0606 useful. The step up is in algebraic fluency and in the length of the questions rather than in the ideas themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms generally start Pure Mathematics 1 in the first week of September with large groups and no diagnostic period. Students who sat Additional Mathematics spend that term consolidating; students who did not spend it meeting calculus for the first time in a class moving at the pace of those who already have. Neither group is disadvantaged at the end of two years, but the autumn term feels very different.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The proof-and-calculus route through IB maths, available at Standard and Higher Level, with an internal exploration written by the student over several months. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and substantially harder algebra on top of calculus that 0606 has already introduced in outline. Standard Level overlaps with 0606 closely enough that the first term feels like revision.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large IB sector alongside its British one, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places in total. A Year 11 sitting 0606 in a school with its own IB Diploma is often heading for Analysis and Approaches rather than A Level, so the tutoring conversation should include which route is intended before the strand order is set.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.subjectsIntro: Families rarely need one subject in isolation. The syllabuses below are the ones most often requested alongside Additional Mathematics by Dubai Year 11 students, with the code that matters on the statement of entry and a note on what the assessment actually rewards.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The main maths entry in most Dubai British-curriculum schools, tiered so that Core caps the available grades and Extended does not. Marks are lost on multi-step problem-solving questions and on accuracy with algebraic fractions. Extended fluency is assumed throughout 0606, so weakness here shows up as an apparent calculus problem.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: The alternative Cambridge maths syllabus, written for international schools and requiring a graphics display calculator. It includes an investigation and modelling component that 0580 does not, which rewards a different skill: choosing an approach and justifying it rather than executing a known method.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Multiple-choice, theory and a practical or alternative-to-practical component. Marks go on equation recall, on describing experimental method precisely, and on the difference between describe, explain and calculate. The maths load is light but constant, which makes it a common pairing with Additional Mathematics.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical or written alternative. The reliable losses are in mole calculations, in ionic equations and in the precision of definitions, where a nearly-right wording scores nothing. Students who are strong at maths often underestimate how exactly the chemistry answer has to be phrased.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy with a practical component, assessed largely through command terms. Marks are lost by describing a graph when the question says explain, and by omitting the control in an experimental design. It is the subject where learning the examiner's vocabulary pays back fastest.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: Edexcel's stretch maths paper, with matrices and a heavier coordinate-geometry strand alongside the calculus. Students sitting it alongside Edexcel Mathematics A face two boards' question styles in one term, and the main tutoring task is often teaching the difference rather than the mathematics.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory and problem-solving papers covering data representation, networks, algorithms and programming concepts. Pseudocode questions are where marks concentrate, and where a mathematically able student can lose heavily by writing code that works instead of pseudocode that matches the syllabus conventions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Two papers, one multiple choice and one structured, with diagram accuracy carrying a large share of the available marks. Labelled axes, correctly shifted curves and a stated new equilibrium are mechanical marks that students who revise only the prose consistently leave on the table.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading and writing papers assessed against published criteria rather than a content list. Marks are lost in the directed-writing task by answering the topic instead of the brief: audience, form and purpose are all assessed, and a well-written response in the wrong register is capped.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study-led, with application marks that require the answer to refer to the specific business in the insert. Generic textbook answers score the knowledge mark and nothing above it, which is the single most common reason a confident student stalls at a middling grade.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.regionsIntro: For online lessons the geography that matters is domestic rather than municipal: where in the apartment the student can work undisturbed, and what the connection does at eight in the evening. The notes below cover the practical constraints families in each of these Dubai communities raise most often.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Small apartments with the study space usually a corner of a shared living room. The recommendation here is a headset and a fixed slot the household knows about, because the interruption rate matters more than the bandwidth, which in these towers is rarely the constraint.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: A dense student population and strong connectivity, with several large British and Indian-curriculum schools inside the same ring road. Sessions here often run earlier than the Dubai average because the commute home is short, which makes a 5pm slot genuinely available.

regions.name: The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Mid-rise apartments with families who moved from villa communities for the school commute. The common issue is a younger sibling in the same room, which is solved by scheduling the 0606 session after the younger child's bedtime rather than by buying better equipment.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: A long bus run from the central school cluster and arrivals often after 4.30pm. Families here tend to use the 7pm to 8.30pm window, and a 90-minute double at the weekend as well during the eight weeks before the written papers.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large villas where the student usually has a dedicated desk, which removes the hardest variable. The constraint is the number of competing commitments on weekday evenings, so the fixed-slot discipline is the thing worth insisting on from September.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: A high proportion of families who arrived mid-academic-year, which is why catch-up blocks rather than year-long arrangements are the normal request here. Two sessions a week for six weeks closes a half-syllabus gap in a way one session a term cannot.

regions.name: Deira, Al Mamzar and Garhoud
regions.note: Older established communities on the Creek side with a long drive to the newer school clusters. This is where removing travel from the arrangement makes the clearest difference, because a visiting tutor would spend more time on Al Ittihad Road than in the lesson.

schoolClusters.city: International and IB-continuum schools
schoolClusters.note: Schools in this group often run 0607 rather than 0580 for mainstream maths, and enter Additional Mathematics only for students heading towards Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Sessions for these students usually need to bridge two question styles at once.

schoolClusters.city: Indian-curriculum schools running Cambridge streams
schoolClusters.note: Several long-established Dubai schools run a CBSE or ICSE mainstream alongside a Cambridge IGCSE stream. Students moving between those streams arrive with strong procedural algebra and limited experience of Cambridge command terms, which is a specific and quickly fixable gap.

sections.heading: What the student needs on the desk, and what is optional
paragraphs: The single piece of equipment that changes the quality of an online maths lesson is a way for the student to write and be seen writing. Everything else is convenience. A tablet with a stylus is the comfortable answer, but a mobile phone on a stand pointed at an A4 pad achieves most of the same thing, and in some ways better, because the student practises on paper exactly as they will in the exam room.

A scientific calculator is not optional. The 0606 syllabus assumes one, and the model the student uses in the exam is the model they should use every session, because keystroke familiarity with statistics menus, radian mode and fraction entry is itself a source of marks. The commonest avoidable error in Additional Mathematics is a calculator left in degrees for a question set in radians, and that is a habit problem solved by using the same device for a year.

A headset matters more than most families expect. Mathematics teaching contains a lot of short, precise verbal correction, and a laptop microphone in a tiled Dubai apartment picks up enough reverberation to make that tiring across a 90-minute session. Wired earphones with an inline microphone solve it for under a hundred dirhams, which is a better first purchase than a tablet.

One thing that is not equipment at all deserves a line. The room matters more than the hardware: a door that closes, a desk rather than a bed, and a household that knows the slot is booked will do more for the session than any device on the list. The table below separates what is genuinely needed from what is merely convenient, with an indicative Dubai retail cost and a workaround where one exists.

sections.heading: Which 0606 strands suit a screen, and which need paper prepared first
paragraphs: Not every part of the syllabus behaves the same way over video, and pretending otherwise is how online lessons get a bad reputation. Strands built on manipulation and procedure work extremely well: logarithms, polynomials, series, permutations and combinations, and most of differentiation and integration are taught by working an example line by line, which is exactly what a shared writing surface is good at. The student writes along, the tutor sees the line where it went wrong, and the correction lands on that line.

Strands with heavy diagram work need a little preparation. Circular measure questions involving composite sectors, vector geometry with a ratio dividing a line, and modulus graph sketching all benefit from the diagram existing on paper before the session starts, because drawing it live on a tablet is slower than drawing it with a pencil. The practical fix is simple: the tutor sends two or three questions ahead, the student prints or copies the diagrams, and the session spends its time on the mathematics rather than on the drawing.

The strand that needs the most deliberate handling is pacing. A timed paper cannot be sat usefully inside a lesson, because an hour of supervised writing is an expensive way to produce a script. The arrangement that works is sitting the paper at home under timed conditions, photographing it, and using the session to go through the marked version. That split is the main structural difference between online and in-room tutoring for this subject, and once it is understood it tends to produce more timed practice rather than less.

sections.heading: Scheduling a Dubai school week on Gulf Standard Time
paragraphs: The Dubai school week runs Monday to Friday in most private schools, with a weekend on Saturday and Sunday, and that shapes which slots are worth booking. Thursday evening is the worst weekday slot in practice, because the weekend has effectively begun and attention is thin. Sunday evening is the best, because it sits before the week's homework has accumulated and after the student has rested, and because anything set in it has five days to be done.

Timing within the day matters as much as the day. Buses reach the outer communities after 4.30pm, so a 5pm start only works for families close to school. The window that works almost everywhere is 6.30pm to 8.30pm, which clears the bus, dinner and the worst of the traffic that a visiting tutor would otherwise be sitting in. Weekend mornings are the other reliable slot, and they are the only ones long enough for a 90-minute double.

The Dubai calendar then moves things twice a year. Mock examinations cluster in January and are worth planning around rather than through: the sensible pattern is an intensive block ending before the mocks and a lighter fortnight during them. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts family routine substantially, and sessions can move to post-Iftar timing for the month.

Two smaller things are worth building in from the start. The first is the half-term and winter break, when families here travel heavily and a slot left unbooked for three weeks is hard to recover; a short holiday block, or an agreed pause with a restart date, beats letting the arrangement lapse. The second is the fixed slot itself, held for the whole term rather than agreed week by week, because a schedule renegotiated every Sunday is the reason fourteen planned sessions quietly become nine. sections.heading: The four numbers tracked every fortnight
paragraphs: Progress in a maths subject is usually reported as a feeling, and a feeling cannot be checked. The four measures below are deliberately crude, cheap to produce from work that is being marked anyway, and sent to you with the marked scripts attached. None of them is a predicted grade, because a predicted grade from a tutor is a guess dressed as data and your child's school is the only party positioned to issue one.

What the four together show is direction. Method-mark capture rising while accuracy stays flat means the understanding is arriving and the arithmetic is not, which is a different intervention from the reverse. A re-test score that does not move after two attempts at the same strand is the signal to change approach, and it is the one number that occasionally ends an arrangement, which is the point of measuring it.

The reason this sits on an online page rather than being a universal claim is that remote delivery makes it easier. Everything is already digital: the whiteboard file, the photographed script, the marked PDF. Producing a fortnightly note is a few minutes of work when the artefacts exist, and it is a chore when they are sheets of paper in a student's bag.

A word on what these are not. They are not benchmarked against other students, because a sample of one tells you nothing about a cohort and we hold no dataset worth quoting. They are not a substitute for the school's own assessments, which test the whole syllabus on a calendar the school controls. They are a record of whether the specific thing worked on two weeks ago has stuck, which is the only question a weekly tutoring arrangement is in a position to answer honestly. sections.heading: What a 0606 session cannot do, and the three jobs that stay with the school
paragraphs: An online tutor is a narrow instrument and it is worth saying what sits outside the arrangement. The entry itself stays with the school: which syllabus codes a child is entered for, whether Additional Mathematics is on the list, and whether an entry can still be withdrawn are all decisions made by the exams officer against a Cambridge deadline. A tutor can tell you what to ask and when, and has no standing to do more than that.

Predicted grades stay with the school as well. Sixth-form and university applications use the school's prediction, informed by its own assessments, and no external tutor should be offering a number for that purpose. The same applies to access arrangements for extra time or other support, which are applied for by the school under Cambridge regulations and require its own evidence. A tutor who claims to arrange any of that is describing something they cannot do.

The third job that stays with the school is the one parents find hardest to accept: coverage. If a school has not taught half the syllabus by March, tutoring can mitigate and cannot replace it, and the honest conversation is with the head of maths rather than with us. Where we can help is in making that conversation specific, because a parent arriving with a marked script and a list of untaught strands is in a much stronger position than a parent arriving worried.

There is a fourth limit that is about us rather than the school. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, so if what your family needs is an adult physically present in the room, this is not the right service and we would rather say that at the start than discover it in week three. In-home tuition is something we run only in India. Within the UAE the format is one-to-one over live video, and the whole argument of this page is that for a sixteen-year-old working through written mathematics, that format costs less and reaches a narrower specialist.

sections.heading: Checking that the tutor is permitted to teach, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a parent is entitled to ask about it directly. The relevant instrument is the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE through its smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated completion time of two working days and no fee. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

Two further rules are worth knowing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also reflects. Marketing a child's own teacher privately is therefore not a service any honest provider offers.

IB Gram's own position is stated plainly because several pages in this market are vague about it. We are a matching platform. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or IB endorsement, we are not a licensed school or training institute in the UAE, and we have no office in the country. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, since in-home tuition is a service we run only in India.
