sections.heading: Why online 0606 tuition is usually cheaper as well as narrower
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates group into bands rather than points. Budget online tutors, often university students, advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to 300. In-home visits run about AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, and specialist IGCSE or A Level tutors AED 200 to 450, with premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650. Those figures come from the providers' own pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost survey, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

The gap between the online and in-home bands is not a quality discount. It is the travel that is no longer being bought, plus the fact that a tutor who does not drive can sell more slots in an evening and does not need each one to carry a dead hour. For a scarce syllabus the second effect matters more: the pool of people who teach Additional Mathematics and can work Gulf Standard Time is many times larger than the pool who teach it and live twenty minutes from your community.

There is one genuine cost that moves the other way, and it belongs on the page. Online marking takes real time, and a tutor who marks properly to the published mark scheme between sessions is doing work that a cheaper hourly rate does not include. When comparing quotes, the question to ask is not the rate but what happens between the lessons, because an arrangement with no marking is a conversation rather than a course, whatever it costs per hour.

sections.heading: Honesty boundaries in a subject assessed entirely by exam
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics carries no coursework and no practical, so there is no portfolio an adult could interfere with. That removes the largest integrity risk in international education before it arises, and it is worth stating because this market contains providers selling finished assessed work for other subjects at published prices. Nothing of that kind is on offer here, in any subject, and it would put a student at risk of malpractice proceedings rather than help them.

The boundary in an exam-only subject sits around materials and marking. A tutor may teach, set questions, mark them against the published mark scheme, and explain why a mark was awarded or withheld. A tutor may not supply material a board has not released, may not redistribute syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, and may not sit or submit anything on a student's behalf. The right practice is to work from the official source at cambridgeinternational.org and link to it.

The other boundary is about claims. We publish no grade promises, no star ratings, no student numbers and no success percentages, because any figure of that kind would need its sample size, date and method on the same page to mean anything, and most that circulate in this market have none of the three. What this page offers instead is a description of the work specific enough that you can tell within six weeks whether it is being done.

The last boundary concerns your child's data. A tutoring arrangement collects a name, a school, a set of marks and sometimes photographs of written work, and under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection that collection needs a stated purpose and a route to deletion. Ours is narrow by design: what is needed to match a tutor and to mark the work, kept while the arrangement runs, deleted on request. A form that asks for a child's school, grades and photograph without saying why is a reasonable thing to refuse, wherever you see it.

process.title: Send the codes and the series
process.description: The statement of entry or the school's option sheet tells us whether the maths entry is 0580 or 0607, whether Additional Mathematics is on it, and which series applies. A 0606 candidate and a 4PM1 candidate need different tutors, and the only way to know which you have is the paperwork rather than the subject name.

process.title: Check the setup in the trial
process.description: The free 45-minute trial lesson doubles as an equipment check: whether the writing surface works, whether the audio is usable in that room, and whether the slot is realistic once the bus has arrived. It costs nothing, needs no card, and if the setup needs changing you find out before you have paid for a term.

process.title: Agree the four measures
process.description: Before the first paid session we confirm what will be sent to you every fortnight: the method-mark capture rate, the error log by cause, the re-test delta and the timed-section completion, with marked scripts attached. Agreeing this in writing is what stops the arrangement becoming unverifiable three months in.

process.title: Protect one slot and run it
process.description: The weekly slot is booked for the term rather than week by week, because a moving slot is the main reason fourteen planned sessions become nine. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, typically between 6.30pm and 8.30pm or on a weekend morning.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and change if it is flat
process.description: At about six weeks there is enough evidence for a real decision. If the re-test delta and the error log show nothing moving, the response is a changed approach or a changed tutor, not more hours. We will say so rather than wait for you to notice, and no part of this involves a prediction about a grade.

whyPoints.title: The hour is structured, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Review marked work, teach, unaided practice, set homework. The unaided block is protected because it is the only part that reveals whether the teaching landed. Sessions that drift into a tutor working examples for fifty minutes feel productive and leave the student unable to start a question alone.

whyPoints.title: Everything is written down and kept
whyPoints.description: The whiteboard file, the marked script and the error log accumulate across the year into a revision set in your child's own notation. Nothing depends on remembering what was said in a lesson in October, which is the usual failure mode of tuition that produces no artefacts.

whyPoints.title: Marked to the published scheme, with method marks split out
whyPoints.description: Seeing method and accuracy marks separately tells you which marks were lost to understanding and which to carelessness. Those need opposite responses, and a single percentage conceals the difference entirely. The mark scheme is the one at cambridgeinternational.org, used as the reference rather than redistributed.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Dubai week, including Ramadan
whyPoints.description: Slots clear the school bus, mock season is planned around rather than through, and sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan by arrangement. A schedule that ignores the local calendar quietly loses a third of its sessions to clashes nobody wrote down.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated in writing
whyPoints.description: No regulator endorsement, no office in the UAE, no grade promises, no statistics without their method. Entries, predicted grades and access arrangements belong to the school and we will tell you so. Market rates quoted here are attributed to whoever published them and are not our price list.

faqs.question: Can calculus really be taught properly over a video call?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided both people can write on the same surface and the student does the writing. A shared digital whiteboard with a tutor on a stylus and the student either on a tablet or writing on paper to camera reproduces the thing that matters, which is the line-by-line conversation about working. What does not work is a video call where the student watches. That is why the session structure protects fifteen minutes of unaided attempt with the tutor silent, and why every session ends with homework that has to be produced on paper.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child need for online 0606 lessons?
faqs.answer: Three things are genuinely required: the exam-approved scientific calculator they will use in the exam, a way to show written working live, and a connection stable enough not to drop mid-question. A headset is strongly advised because mathematics teaching involves constant short corrections and a laptop microphone in a tiled room makes those tiring. A tablet with a stylus is comfortable but optional; a phone on a stand pointed at an A4 pad works, and has the advantage that your child practises on paper exactly as they will in the exam room.

faqs.question: Which evening slot works best for a Dubai Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sunday between 6.30pm and 8.30pm is the most useful weekday slot, because homework set in it has five days before the next session and the student has rested over the weekend. Thursday evening is the weakest, since the weekend has effectively started. Buses reach the outer communities after 4.30pm, so a 5pm start only suits families living close to school. Weekend mornings are the other reliable window and the only ones long enough for a 90-minute double, which matters in the eight weeks before the papers.

faqs.question: How do you measure whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Four crude measures, produced from work that is being marked anyway and sent to you every fortnight with the scripts attached. Method-mark capture rate shows whether the approach is arriving. The error log, grouped by cause rather than topic, shows which specific habit is still costing marks. A re-test on the same question type two to three weeks after teaching shows retention. Timed-section completion shows pacing. None of them is a predicted grade, which is the school's job and not a tutor's.

faqs.question: Do you record the sessions so my child can revise from them?
faqs.answer: The written working is kept as the primary record: the whiteboard file from each session accumulates into a set of worked examples in your child's own notation, which is more useful for revision than a video nobody rewatches. Session recordings can be kept where a family wants them, with the usual caveat that recordings of a minor need a stated purpose and a way to have them deleted, consistent with UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection. The error log and marked scripts are the documents that actually drive the next session.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a weekly 0606 schedule in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan and household routine shifts substantially, so insisting on a 6.30pm slot through the month tends to produce missed sessions rather than progress. The usual arrangement is shorter sessions after Iftar, focused on recall and notation rather than on new calculus content, with the normal pattern resuming afterwards. Because the lessons are over live video, the change costs nothing to make and does not depend on a tutor's travel plans.

faqs.question: How much does an online Additional Maths tutor in Dubai cost?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands are the honest answer. Budget online tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, in-home visits AED 180 to 500 with travel included, specialists AED 200 to 450, and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. Those come from providers' own pages and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey rather than from us. Additional Mathematics sits at the upper end of whichever band applies because few people teach it, and our own figure comes on a consultation after the free trial.

faqs.question: Is a group class a reasonable alternative for 0606?
faqs.answer: Rarely in Dubai, for an unglamorous reason: the cohort is too small. A tuition centre needs three or four students at the same stage of the same syllabus at the same time, and Additional Mathematics candidates in any one community are usually too few and too differently taught for that. Where a group does form, it tends to teach the syllabus from the front, which suits nobody who has already met half of it. Group pricing is lower per student, so the trade is real, but the matching problem is the reason it seldom appears.

faqs.question: My son is entered for 4PM1 rather than 0606. Does the tutor change?
faqs.answer: It should. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 covers much of the same ground as Cambridge 0606 but includes matrices, weights coordinate geometry more heavily and sets questions in a noticeably different style. A tutor fluent in one board's mark scheme is not automatically fluent in the other's, and the differences cost marks precisely where a student is otherwise competent. Send the statement of entry rather than the subject name, because mixed-board entries are more common in Dubai than families expect.

faqs.question: What happens in the first paid session after the trial?
faqs.answer: The first session works from the strand map and error log produced in the free trial, so it starts at a named weakness rather than at the front of the syllabus. Typically that means one strand taught with the student writing along, fifteen minutes of unaided practice on the same material, and homework set to be marked before the next lesson. You receive the written plan before that session, naming the strand order, the homework pattern and what will be sent to you every fortnight.

faqs.question: Can the tutor talk to my child's maths teacher at school?
faqs.answer: Only if the school wants that, and it is the school's call rather than ours. Many Dubai heads of maths are willing to share the scheme of work and the assessment calendar with a parent, which is almost as useful and much easier to arrange. What we would rather not do is create a channel in which an external tutor appears to speak for the school on entries, predicted grades or access arrangements, because those decisions belong to the school and a tutor has no standing in them.

faqs.question: Does my child need to sit timed papers at home rather than in the lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that split is the main structural difference between online and in-room tutoring for this subject. Using a paid hour to supervise silent writing is an expensive way to produce a script. The arrangement that works is sitting the paper at home under timed conditions, photographing it, and spending the session on the marked version question by question. In practice this produces more timed practice than in-room tutoring does, because the limit stops being how many hours you have bought.

faqs.question: How quickly can an online 0606 tutor start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For most evening slots, days rather than weeks, with the free trial usually available within the first week of asking. The constraint is not geography but the size of the specialist pool for this syllabus, which tightens sharply between January and May as mock results arrive. Autumn is the easy season and the spring is not. If no specialist is free at your preferred time we will say so and set out the alternatives rather than matching a general maths tutor to a 0606 request.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable if my child is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: It depends on the age and the room more than on the format. A sixteen-year-old working on a specific syllabus with a protected unaided-practice block and homework that gets marked is generally fine, because the structure does the work that physical presence would otherwise do. A younger child who needs an adult present to stay on task is a different case, and we would say so rather than sell a format that will not suit. The practical fixes are a headset, a door that closes and a slot the whole household knows about.

faqs.question: What should I ask any Dubai tutor before paying the first invoice?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Does their permit exist and is it in their own name, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. What happens between sessions, and specifically whether homework is marked to the published mark scheme. What you will receive in writing, and how often. Whether the quoted rate is per hour or per session, and whether it includes marking. And what happens if the match does not work. Any provider promising a grade, claiming a regulator's approval, or quoting a fine amount for unlicensed tutoring is telling you something useful about themselves.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.closingHeading: Book the trial as a setup test, not a sales call

Book the free 45-minute trial lesson and treat it as a test of three things at once: whether the writing surface and audio work in the room your child will actually use, whether the slot survives contact with the school bus, and whether the tutor can mark a 0606 question and tell you what the mark scheme wanted. You keep the strand map and the error log afterwards whether or not you continue, no card is required and there is nothing to cancel. intro.heading: Why 0606 is hard, and why the reason is almost never calculus
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics, syllabus code 0606, is the only qualification at this level that teaches calculus. A student sitting it meets differentiation, integration, kinematics by calculus, logarithms, radians, the binomial expansion and permutations in the same year as nine other IGCSE subjects. It is examined by two written papers, each carrying half the grade, with no coursework, and the available grades run from A* to E. The syllabus assumes the Extended content of Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is already in place, and that assumption is where almost all of the trouble lives.

Here is what actually happens in a Dubai 0606 classroom in October. A capable student who got a strong mark in Extended mathematics in Year 10 is shown how to differentiate a polynomial and does it correctly. Two weeks later they are asked to differentiate something written as a fraction with a root in the denominator, and they stop. Not because differentiation is hard, but because they cannot rewrite that expression as a power. The maths they are failing is a 0580 index law, met two years earlier, never made automatic because 0580 never punished it hard enough.

That pattern repeats across the syllabus and it is the single most useful thing a parent can know. A stationary point question fails at factorising. An inverse function question fails at rearranging when the subject appears twice. A circular measure question fails because the calculator is in degrees. A trigonometric equation question fails because no unit circle was ever drawn. In each case a tutor who diagnoses calculus and teaches more calculus will spend six sessions on the wrong thing while the student becomes convinced they cannot do it.

So the first thing this page offers is a readiness audit: six prerequisite skills, each with a test question you can set at the kitchen table tonight, and what to do if one fails. It takes twenty minutes and it is more diagnostic than any conversation. If three or more fail, the honest plan is three weeks of Extended algebra before touching 0606 content, which feels like going backwards and is the fastest route forwards available.

The second thing this page offers is a straight answer on whether to take the subject at all. 0606 is genuinely optional, it is demanding, and it is the right choice for a specific student: one already secure at Extended level who intends to do mathematics-heavy study at sixteen to eighteen. It is the wrong choice for a student being stretched into it by ambition, because a thin pass in 0606 costs more in confidence and in time away from nine other subjects than it ever returns. Nobody in this market will tell you that, which is one reason to write it down.

The rest of the page sets out what 0606 adds beyond Extended 0580, the four calculus misconceptions that survive a whole year, the measurables that tell you by week six whether it is working, what the subject actually buys at A Level and in the Diploma, and the awkward topic of scarcity: there are far fewer people who can teach 0606 well than who can teach 0580, in Dubai as everywhere, and a family who starts looking in March may not find anybody at any price. Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, as that service exists only in India.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.programmesIntro: 0606 exists to bridge somewhere, so the destination determines whether it is worth taking. These are the four routes a Dubai student takes out of Year 11 and what 0606 is worth on each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: Two written papers, each worth half the grade, no coursework, grades A* to E. The content covers functions, quadratics, polynomials, indices and surds, logarithms and exponentials, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, two-dimensional vectors, differentiation, integration and kinematics. A scientific calculator is expected, and exact-form answers are frequently required anyway, which catches students who reach for a decimal.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school offers 0606, and where it is offered it is usually restricted to a set within the top mathematics group, often with an internal threshold from Year 10. That means a 0606 cohort in a Dubai school can be fifteen students rather than ninety, so a student who falls behind has far fewer classmates to compare notes with and the isolation becomes part of the problem.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The destination 0606 was designed for. A student arriving in Year 12 having already met differentiation, integration, radians, logarithms and the binomial expansion is not learning those ideas for the first time under pressure; they are deepening them. The first term of AS Mathematics is where the benefit actually shows, and it shows as spare capacity rather than as a higher ceiling.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the first-term collapse in sixth-form mathematics is common and predictable, and it almost always traces to Extended algebra that never became automatic rather than to new content. A 0606 student has usually had that algebra stress-tested a year earlier, which is the most durable benefit the subject offers.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebra-and-proof route of the Diploma, at Standard or Higher Level, and the Diploma course that most rewards prior calculus. A 0606 student meets differentiation rules, stationary points and definite integrals before Year 12 begins, which matters most at Higher Level where the content volume is the real difficulty. The internally assessed exploration is a separate skill and 0606 does nothing for it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, so more Year 11 students in the emirate will be weighing a British-curriculum sixth form against the Diploma. For a student seriously considering Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, 0606 is the most useful optional subject available in Year 11.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling and statistics route, where technology use is assumed throughout and the emphasis sits on interpreting and justifying rather than on algebraic manipulation. 0606 is pleasant preparation and not necessary. A student who intends to take this route and is choosing between 0606 and a better grade in an extra subject should usually choose the extra subject, and few advisers will say so.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route where the honest Dubai answer is most often no. Families frequently take 0606 as insurance against a future they have not yet chosen, and where that future turns out to be Applications and Interpretation, a social science or a creative course, the insurance was paid for in Year 11 time that nine other subjects needed.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-0.subjectsIntro: The 0606 subject content divides into topic areas, several of which do not appear anywhere in Extended 0580. These are them, with what each one newly demands.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Domain, range, composite functions, inverse functions and the modulus function, with graphs. The new demand is notation rather than idea: students who can evaluate a function fluently often cannot say what its range is, and inverse questions fail at rearranging when the variable appears twice rather than at the concept of an inverse.

subjects.name: Quadratic Functions and the Discriminant
subjects.description: Completing the square, the maximum or minimum point, and using the discriminant to decide how many roots exist and to find conditions on a constant. Extended 0580 solves quadratics; 0606 reasons about them. The recurring error is treating the discriminant as a formula to compute rather than a condition to impose.

subjects.name: Indices, Surds and Exact Form
subjects.description: Negative and fractional indices, rationalising denominators and leaving answers exactly. Technically revision, practically the gate to the whole syllabus, because differentiation and integration are applied to terms written as powers. A student who cannot turn a root in a denominator into a negative fractional index cannot start calculus, whatever they understand about it.

subjects.name: Factors of Polynomials
subjects.description: The factor and remainder theorems, dividing a cubic and solving it fully. New to most students and quickly learned. Marks go missing in the bookkeeping rather than the method: a sign error in synthetic division invalidates everything after it, and students rarely check by substituting their root back.

subjects.name: Simultaneous Equations and Intersections
subjects.description: Line-and-curve and curve-and-curve intersections, including conditions for tangency. Extended 0580 touches the non-linear case; 0606 uses it constantly, particularly in tangent and normal questions in calculus. Tangency as a discriminant condition is the step students most often never meet properly.

subjects.name: Logarithmic and Exponential Functions
subjects.description: Laws of logarithms, solving equations with the unknown in the exponent, natural logarithms and exponential growth and decay. Entirely new territory. The commonest error is distributing a logarithm across a sum, which is a misread of the laws rather than a slip, and it needs correcting in the first week it appears or it sets.

subjects.name: Circular Measure
subjects.description: Radians, arc length and sector area in radians. Conceptually small, operationally brutal, because the calculator has to be in the right mode and students forget. A whole trigonometry question can evaluate to nonsense from one mode setting, and the habit of checking the display before starting has to be built deliberately.

subjects.name: Trigonometry Beyond the Right Angle
subjects.description: Identities, solving trigonometric equations over a given interval, and graphs of the three functions with transformations. The dominant loss is missing solutions: a student finds one angle from the calculator and stops, where the interval contains two or three. The fix is a drawn unit circle or sketched graph every single time, without exception.

subjects.name: Permutations and Combinations
subjects.description: Arrangements and selections, with and without restrictions. Short, self-contained and unusually well rewarded, because many students skip it in revision as the odd topic out. Errors come almost entirely from deciding whether order matters, which is a reading problem rather than a counting one.

subjects.name: Series and the Binomial Expansion
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to infinity, and the binomial expansion including particular-term questions. The binomial is where sign and index bookkeeping punishes carelessness, and the particular-term question is the one students attempt by expanding everything rather than using the general term.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: Rules including product, quotient and chain, stationary points and their nature, tangents and normals, connected rates of change and small increments. The genuine conceptual content of the course. Most difficulty is upstream of it: the differentiation itself is mechanical once the expression has been written as powers.

subjects.name: Integration and Area
subjects.description: Integration as the reverse of differentiation, definite integrals, areas under and between curves, and integration of standard forms including exponentials and trigonometric functions. The recurring error is the omitted constant of integration in indefinite work, and in area questions, failing to notice a region below the axis.

subjects.name: Kinematics by Calculus
subjects.description: Displacement, velocity and acceleration related by differentiation and integration, with motion in a straight line. This is where calculus stops being abstract and where weaker students often improve fastest, because the physical meaning anchors the operations. The classic loss is treating distance travelled as displacement when the direction reverses.

subjects.name: Vectors in Two Dimensions
subjects.description: Position vectors, magnitude, unit vectors and velocity as a vector, including meeting and collision problems. Extended 0580 does vector arithmetic; 0606 uses vectors to describe motion over time. The step that catches students is parameterising by time and then solving two equations that must agree.

sections.heading: Who 0606 is for, and who should be talked out of it
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Additional Maths 0606 tutor in Dubai gets two kinds of enquiry, and they need opposite answers. The first is a student already secure at Extended level who has hit a specific topic wall, usually logarithms, tangency or trigonometric equations. That is straightforward work with a short, finishable shape. The second is a student who was placed into 0606 on the strength of a Year 10 grade, is now three weeks behind, and whose real problem is 0580 algebra that was never automatic. Teaching that student more calculus is the commonest waste of money in this corner of the market.

0606 is optional, and the honest selection test is about destination rather than ability. It is worth taking for a student who intends mathematics-heavy study at sixteen to eighteen: Cambridge AS and A Level Mathematics, or Diploma Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level. For those routes the benefit is real and shows up as spare capacity in the first term of Year 12 rather than as a higher ceiling. For a student heading towards Applications and Interpretation, a social science, a creative course or a route where mathematics stops at sixteen, 0606 is an expensive luxury paid for in Year 11 hours that nine other subjects needed.

The second test is readiness, and it is specific rather than general. By the start of Year 11 a 0606 candidate should be able to rewrite an algebraic fraction as a sum of powers, rearrange a formula where the variable appears on both sides, factorise a quadratic without being told which method to use, solve a non-linear pair of simultaneous equations, rationalise a denominator and solve a basic trigonometric equation over an interval. Those six are tested in the next section. Three or more failures is not a reason to abandon 0606; it is a reason to spend three weeks on Extended algebra before touching the new content, and to do that in September rather than in February.

The third consideration is workload, which Dubai families consistently underestimate. 0606 is an additional qualification with two full papers, added to a timetable that already contains nine or ten subjects and, in a Dubai private school, the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision as well. Schools must deliver those regardless of the licensed curriculum, so the fixed part of a Dubai Year 11 week is fuller than in many comparable systems. A student taking 0606 is accepting real extra homework in the examination year, and that trade needs to be made deliberately rather than by default.

sections.heading: The readiness audit: six questions to set tonight
paragraphs: This is the most useful twenty minutes available to a 0606 family and it costs nothing. Set the six questions in the table below, with a calculator permitted and no help, and watch rather than mark. What matters is not whether the answer is right but whether the student starts confidently and finishes without hesitation. A correct answer produced slowly and painfully is a fail for this purpose, because 0606 will require the same step as a sub-step inside something harder.

Each row names the prerequisite, says why 0606 needs it from the first weeks, gives the test question and says what to do if it fails. The fourth column is the honest part. Three weeks of Extended algebra in September is a smaller cost than six months of 0606 lessons that cannot land, and the student who does that groundwork typically overtakes the one who did not by February. Families resist it because it feels like paying for work already covered, which is exactly what it is and exactly why it works.

Pay particular attention to the second row. Index-form rewriting is the single most predictive skill on the list. Differentiation and integration in 0606 are applied to terms written as powers, so a student who cannot turn a root in a denominator into a negative fractional index is blocked from the core of the course regardless of how well they understand it conceptually. It is also one of the fastest things on the list to repair, often a week of short daily drills, which makes the return on that week unusually high.

One caution on how to use the audit. Do not present it to your child as a test of whether they are good enough for the subject, because that framing produces anxiety and a worse result than their actual ability. Present it as finding out what to do first, which is true. The audit is a planning instrument, not a selection one, and its main output is a sequence rather than a verdict.

sections.heading: What 0606 adds beyond Extended 0580, topic by topic
paragraphs: Parents often assume 0606 is Extended mathematics made harder. It is not. Several topics are genuinely new and do not appear in 0580 at any tier: logarithms and exponentials, radians and circular measure, the factor and remainder theorems, the binomial expansion, permutations and combinations, and the whole of calculus including kinematics by differentiation and integration. Other topics appear in both but are used differently, which is a subtler and more dangerous category because a student assumes familiarity.

The table maps each area to what is newly demanded and where it is first needed, which matters for sequencing. A school that teaches circular measure in November and trigonometric identities in February leaves a student holding radians for three months without the context that makes them useful, and that gap is a frequent source of apparent regression. A tutor working alongside the school should know the school's order and compensate for its consequences rather than impose a different order.

The fourth column is the one worth reading closely, because 0606 errors are highly stereotyped. Distributing a logarithm across a sum. Leaving the calculator in degrees for a radian question. Omitting the constant of integration. Finding one trigonometric solution and stopping when the interval holds two. Treating distance travelled as displacement when the direction reverses. Expanding a whole binomial to find one term. Every one of those is a specific, nameable habit rather than a conceptual failure, and naming it is most of the fix.

A practical note on calculator mode, because it costs more marks in this subject than it reasonably should. The habit that works is checking the display before the first line of every question rather than before the paper, because a student who switches to radians for a circular measure question and then meets a degrees question four pages later will not remember to switch back. Making the check part of reading the question, rather than a separate act of memory, is the only version that survives an examination.

sections.heading: The four calculus misconceptions that survive a whole year
paragraphs: Calculus at sixteen produces a specific set of wrong ideas, and they are durable because each one works often enough to go unnoticed. A student holding any of these can pass a mid-year test and then collapse on a paper that probes slightly differently. They are worth naming because they are invisible in ordinary classwork.

The first is that differentiation is a procedure applied to expressions that look a certain way. A student fluent at differentiating a polynomial freezes when the same function is written as a fraction or with a root, because they learned a pattern rather than an operation. The diagnostic is simple: give the same function in three different written forms and see whether all three are attempted. The repair is index-form rewriting, which is why it appears twice on this page.

The second is that a stationary point is wherever the derivative is zero, full stop, with the nature of the point a separate decorative question. Students compute the derivative, set it to zero, find the coordinate and stop, then lose the marks for determining whether it is a maximum or a minimum and for giving a reason. The repair is making classification part of the same answer rather than an optional extra, with the second derivative or the sign change written down every time.

The third is that integration is differentiation backwards and therefore requires no care. The constant of integration vanishes, definite integrals get evaluated without subtracting, and an area below the axis is reported as negative or silently made positive without comment. The fourth is that kinematics is a word-problem topic separate from calculus, so students who can differentiate cleanly fail to see that velocity is the derivative of displacement. That last one usually resolves fast once it is named, and students often improve most quickly here, because the physical meaning gives the operations something to hold onto.

Kinematics treated as a separate topic rather than as calculus with physical meaning

sections.heading: What progress in 0606 actually looks like by week six
paragraphs: 0606 is easy to feel good about and hard to measure casually, because a session in which a tutor works through two beautiful examples feels productive to everybody and proves nothing. The measurables below are chosen because each one is a thing the student does unaided, in writing, that you can look at without being a mathematician yourself.

The crucial word is unaided. The gap between what a sixteen-year-old can do with a tutor's prompts beside them and what they can do alone is wider in calculus than in almost any other school mathematics, because the operations are short and the selection of which operation to use is the real difficulty. A prompt as small as asking which rule applies collapses that difficulty invisibly. So the evidence that counts is questions attempted with nobody present, marked afterwards.

By week six a reasonable expectation is modest and specific rather than impressive: index-form rewriting fast and automatic, a derivative produced unaided on an unseen function in an awkward written form, stationary points classified with a reason without being reminded, a definite integral evaluated with the limits subtracted the right way round, exact-form answers left exact, and at least one past-paper section sat at correct duration. Six narrow things. A student holding all six is in good shape for the rest of the course; a student holding two needs the plan changed rather than extended.

What should also exist by then is a written record: a three-line note after each session saying what was taught, what the student could do unaided by the end and what was still wrong, plus the marked work itself. Those documents are what make the week-twelve conversation a comparison rather than an opinion. In a subject where the content moves fast and the cohort is small, a student with no written record is being assessed entirely on how the last session felt.

sections.heading: What 0606 actually buys at sixteen to eighteen
paragraphs: The case for 0606 is usually made vaguely, in terms of a head start. The honest version is more specific and more persuasive. What the subject buys is spare capacity in the first term of sixth-form mathematics, which is precisely when students who have not met calculus are using all of theirs on content while simultaneously adjusting to a new timetable and a new set of teachers.

The table sets out what 0606 has and has not covered for each destination. Read the third column as carefully as the second, because the gaps matter. 0606 does nothing for the Diploma's internally assessed exploration, which is a research and writing task rather than a content one. It does nothing for statistics, which is a significant component of Applications and Interpretation. And it does not cover the proof and rigour that Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level expects, so a student arriving with 0606 calculus still has substantial new ground.

There is a quieter benefit that is arguably the largest. A 0606 student has had their Extended algebra stress-tested a year before everybody else, under conditions where failure is visible immediately. Index form, rearranging, exact answers and factorising cannot be faked in a calculus question. That is the real reason 0606 students tend to cope with the first sixth-form term, and it means the benefit is largely delivered even by a student who ends up with a modest 0606 grade, which is a point in favour of attempting it where readiness is genuine.

One thing 0606 does not buy, and should not be sold as buying: an advantage in university admission in its own right. It is an IGCSE-level qualification, admissions decisions at this level rest on sixth-form grades, and no tutoring page should imply that an additional subject at sixteen is required for a route or a place. Do not let anybody frame it as insurance against a regulatory or admissions process, and verify any requirement with the institution or the Ministry rather than with a provider.

sections.heading: Scarcity: what happens when nobody local teaches 0606
paragraphs: This is the part of the market nobody discloses, so it is worth stating plainly. The pool of people who can teach 0606 well is far smaller than the pool who can teach 0580. The subject requires comfort with calculus and with teaching sixteen-year-olds meeting it for the first time, which is a different skill from teaching A Level calculus to students who have already seen it. Across the UAE, and not only in Dubai, a family looking for this in February is looking in a thin market.

The practical consequence is about timing rather than price. A September or October enquiry for 0606 can usually be matched to somebody who has taught the syllabus. A February enquiry may be matched to a strong mathematician who has not, which is a different product and should be described as such rather than quietly substituted. The question to ask any provider is narrow: how many 0606 cohorts has this specific person taught, and when. An answer about calculus experience in general is not an answer to that question.

Where a specialist genuinely is not available, there are three honest options and it is better to choose between them deliberately. The first is a strong general mathematician working strictly from the syllabus document and the school's sequence, which works for the algebra and the mechanical calculus and is weaker on the stereotyped 0606 errors. The second is a narrower engagement: use the scarce hours only on the genuinely new topics, logarithms, circular measure, the binomial and calculus, and handle the Extended-level prerequisites with a cheaper and more plentiful 0580 tutor. The third is to accept that the subject will be carried by the school and spend the money on the nine other subjects instead.

We would rather tell a family that the right specialist is not free this term than place somebody who will be learning the syllabus alongside their student. Availability transparency is a low bar and almost nobody in this market clears it: no competitor page examined discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-local delivery entirely. If a provider tells you a scarce subject is always immediately available, they are describing their sales process rather than their supply.

sections.heading: Sitting 0580 and 0606 in the same series
paragraphs: Almost every 0606 candidate is also sitting 0580, which means four written papers rather than two and two syllabuses with substantial overlap but no shared timetable. Treating them as two separate projects is the commonest planning error, because it double-counts the algebra and under-counts the timed-paper load.

The overlap is real and should be used. Index form, rearranging, factorising, surds, simultaneous equations and basic trigonometry serve both qualifications, so work on them is paid for once and banked twice. In practice that means a Year 11 plan should front-load algebra regardless of which subject prompted the enquiry, because it is the highest-leverage work available for either paper set. What does not overlap is calculus, logarithms, radians, series and permutations, which are 0606 only and have to be found extra hours from somewhere.

The timed-paper arithmetic is where families get caught. Four papers, each needing to be sat at least once under correct duration, with a marking session attached to each, is eight weekend slots that have to exist somewhere in the spring term. In Dubai, where the uninterrupted two-hour window generally only exists on a Saturday morning, that calendar needs writing in January rather than being decided week by week. Entry deadlines sit months before the exams, as Cambridge's published key dates make clear, and the preparation calendar should be built with the same lead time.

Finally, decide in advance where to stop. If the term goes badly and something has to give, it is better to have agreed beforehand whether the answer is to protect the 0580 grade, since that is the qualification sixth forms actually require, or to protect 0606 because a specific Higher Level route depends on it. Families who have not had that conversation make the decision in April under pressure, and usually make it by accident rather than by choice.

sections.heading: What the two 0606 papers reward, and how to practise for them
paragraphs: 0606 is assessed by two written papers with no coursework, each carrying half the grade, and a scientific calculator is expected. Confirm the duration, mark totals and calculator requirements in the syllabus for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, because syllabuses are revised and an older sibling's memory is not a source.

What both papers reward is completion of multi-step questions, which has a specific practice implication. A 0606 question commonly asks for a derivative, then a stationary point, then its nature, then something about a tangent, with each part depending on the one before. A student who makes an arithmetic error in the first part and abandons the question loses everything; a student who carries the wrong value forward correctly keeps the later marks under follow-through credit. So the single most valuable practice habit is never abandoning a question after a mistake, and that is trained by marking rather than by teaching.

The second habit is writing the method out. Calculus working is short, which tempts students to do it mentally and write only a result, and that is where method marks evaporate. A derivative worked in the head and written as a single expression earns nothing if the expression is wrong. The same derivative with the rule applied visibly, term by term, keeps most of the credit. Three sessions of enforced line-by-line working fixes this, and it is worth more marks in 0606 than in 0580 because the question chains are longer.

The third is exact form. 0606 regularly requires answers exactly, in surds, in terms of a logarithm or in terms of pi, and a student who computes a decimal because the calculator offered one scores nothing on an otherwise perfect question. This is pure convention and it is corrected by a standing instruction: read what form the answer must take before starting, every time. Reference Cambridge's syllabus and specimen material for the official wording and link it rather than reproducing it, which is both the correct copyright position and the only way a parent can check what is true.

whyPoints.description: Differentiation and integration are applied to terms written as powers. A student who cannot turn a root in a denominator into a negative fractional index is blocked from the core of the course, whatever they understand. It is also the fastest thing on the list to repair.

faqs.question: My daughter's school has offered her 0606. How do we decide whether to take it?
faqs.answer: Two tests, in order. First, destination: 0606 pays for itself if she intends Cambridge AS and A Level Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level, and much less so for Applications and Interpretation, a social science or a route where mathematics stops at sixteen. Second, readiness: run the six-question audit on this page tonight, with a calculator and no help, and watch for hesitation as well as errors. Three or more weak answers is not a no, but it means three weeks of Extended algebra first, starting in September rather than February.

faqs.question: What does 0606 actually contain that Extended 0580 does not?
faqs.answer: Several topics that appear nowhere in 0580 at any tier. Logarithms and exponential functions. Radians and circular measure. The factor and remainder theorems. The binomial expansion and progressions. Permutations and combinations. And all of calculus: differentiation with the product, quotient and chain rules, stationary points, tangents and normals, integration, areas under and between curves, and kinematics done by calculus. Other areas such as functions, quadratics and trigonometry appear in both but are used differently, which is the more dangerous category because familiarity is assumed where it should not be.

faqs.question: Which 0580 skills have to be automatic before 0606 starts?
faqs.answer: Six. Rewriting expressions in index form, including negative and fractional powers. Rearranging a formula where the variable appears on both sides. Factorising a quadratic without being told which method to use. Solving a pair of simultaneous equations where one is non-linear. Handling surds and leaving an answer exactly. And solving a basic trigonometric equation over a given interval, finding all the solutions. Automatic means fast and confident, not merely possible: 0606 uses each of these as a sub-step inside something harder, so a slow step becomes a stalled question.

faqs.question: Is a calculator allowed in both 0606 papers?
faqs.answer: A scientific calculator is expected for the written papers, which is different from 0580 where one paper per tier does not permit one. That does not make 0606 the easier arithmetic experience, for two reasons. Exact-form answers are frequently required, so a decimal from the calculator scores nothing on a question asking for a surd, a logarithm or a result in terms of pi. And calculator mode causes real losses once radians arrive. Confirm the current calculator requirements in the syllabus for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: How much of 0606 is calculus, and how much is everything else?
faqs.answer: Calculus is the conceptual core but not the majority of the content. Differentiation, integration, areas and kinematics together form the largest single block, and the rest of the syllabus spans functions, quadratics, polynomials, indices and surds, logarithms and exponentials, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series and two-dimensional vectors. For planning purposes the useful split is different: perhaps a third of the course is genuinely new ideas, and much of the remaining difficulty is Extended algebra being used harder than 0580 ever used it.

faqs.question: My son can differentiate but cannot rewrite a fraction as a power. Is that the real problem?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly yes, and it is the commonest diagnosis in this subject. Differentiation in 0606 is applied to terms written as powers, so a student who cannot turn a root in a denominator into a negative fractional index is blocked before the calculus begins, however well they understand it. The symptom looks like a calculus failure, which is why six sessions of extra calculus teaching so often change nothing. The repair is a week of short daily index-rewriting drills, which is the highest-return week available in the whole course.

faqs.question: How do we tell in week six whether 0606 is going to work out?
faqs.answer: Six specific things, all of them written and unaided. Index-form rewriting done in seconds. A derivative produced alone on an unseen function in an awkward written form. Stationary points classified with a reason, without being reminded. A definite integral with the limits subtracted the right way round and the working visible. Exact-form answers left exact. And at least one past-paper section sat at correct duration and marked. A student holding all six is in good shape. A student holding two needs the plan changed rather than extended by more of the same.

faqs.question: What does exact form mean, and why does my daughter keep losing those marks?
faqs.answer: It means leaving the answer as a surd, as a logarithm, or in terms of pi, rather than as a decimal from the calculator. 0606 asks for it regularly and a decimal scores nothing on a question that required exact form, however correct the mathematics. The loss is pure convention rather than understanding, which is why it feels so unfair and is so quick to fix. The habit that works is reading what form the answer must take before starting a question, every time, rather than deciding at the end what to write down.

faqs.question: Does taking 0606 make Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level easier?
faqs.answer: It helps more there than anywhere else, because at Higher Level the real difficulty is content volume rather than individual topic difficulty, and a student who has already met differentiation rules, stationary points, definite integrals, logarithms and radians is deepening rather than meeting them. What 0606 does not cover is proof, complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions and the internally assessed exploration, which is a research and writing task rather than a content one. So it reduces the first-term load materially and does not remove the course's main demands.

faqs.question: Will 0606 help my son start Cambridge A Level Mathematics in Year 12?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the benefit arrives as spare capacity rather than as a higher ceiling. The first term of AS Mathematics is where students without prior calculus spend everything they have on new content while also adjusting to a new timetable and new teachers. A 0606 student is revisiting rather than meeting differentiation, integration, radians, logarithms and the binomial expansion. There is a quieter benefit too: their Extended algebra was stress-tested a year earlier under conditions where it could not be faked, and that is what usually decides the first term.

faqs.question: My son's school does not offer 0606. Can he take it anyway?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it has to be arranged with an examination centre rather than assumed. Some centres in the emirate accept private candidates for some subjects and series and some do not, and the entry still has to be submitted within Cambridge's published deadline for that series, which falls months before the papers. Contact centres directly and ask specifically about the syllabus code and the series you need. Then be honest about the teaching: a subject carried entirely outside school needs considerably more support than one with timetabled lessons behind it.

faqs.question: How much extra homework does 0606 add on top of nine other subjects?
faqs.answer: Enough that it should be a deliberate decision rather than a default. It is a full additional qualification with two written papers, added to an examination-year timetable that already carries nine or ten subjects, and in a Dubai private school also the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision that every school must deliver whatever its licensed curriculum. That makes the fixed part of a Dubai Year 11 week fuller than in many comparable systems. The trade is real: 0606 hours come out of other subjects, so the destination has to justify them.

faqs.question: What happens if we start 0606 and it turns out to be too much?
faqs.answer: Have the conversation before you need it, because in April it gets made by accident. Decide in advance whether the priority is protecting the 0580 grade, which is the qualification sixth forms actually require, or protecting 0606 because a specific Higher Level route depends on it. Entries carry deadlines set by Cambridge well before the papers, so withdrawing or amending is an administrative matter for the school's exams officer with its own cut-off. Knowing which way you would choose turns a crisis into a decision.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to start 0606 support in January for a June series?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is already secure. If the Extended prerequisites are automatic and the problem is two or three specific topics, January is comfortably enough: logarithm laws, tangency conditions and missing trigonometric solutions are each a two or three session repair. If the prerequisites are not secure, January is late, because the algebra block has to happen first and the calculus cannot land until it has. Run the readiness audit before deciding, and be prepared for the honest answer to be that the realistic target is the 0580 grade.

faqs.question: Why is a 0606 tutor harder to find in Dubai than a 0580 tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is genuinely smaller. Teaching 0606 requires comfort with calculus and with sixteen-year-olds meeting it for the first time, which is a different skill from teaching A Level calculus to students who have already seen it, and many strong mathematicians have never taught this specific syllabus. The practical consequence is about timing rather than price: an autumn enquiry can usually be matched to somebody who has taught the course, and a February one may not be. Ask how many 0606 cohorts the specific person has taught, and when.

intro.heading: What in-home tuition buys, and what evidence buys instead
paragraphs: The search for an Arabic home tutor in Dubai is rarely about convenience. It is about visibility. A parent who cannot read a British-curriculum school's Arabic feedback, or who reads Arabic fluently and finds the report says nothing, wants to see a person working with their child and conclude that effort is being made. That instinct is sound and the conclusion is unreliable. Presence in a room tells you a lesson happened. It does not tell you whether the summary question is still being answered from memory of the passage, or whether register drifts in the second paragraph of every composition.

The market for in-home Arabic tuition in Dubai is real and priced. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500 once travel is absorbed, and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are market figures, not ours. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every country page on this site says so.

What replaces the reassurance of presence is documentation, and on a language subject it is unusually checkable. A marked 0508 composition shows the band, the register slips, the accuracy errors and the structural move that was missing. A marked reading answer shows whether the student quoted from the text or paraphrased from memory. An error log shows the same four mistakes recurring in weeks one, three and five, and then not recurring in week seven. A parent who reads Arabic can audit all of it directly, which is more than most subjects allow.

The second thing online delivery buys for a 0508 family is the tutor itself. Dubai has no shortage of Arabic teachers. It has a genuine shortage of tutors who mark first-language Arabic writing against the Cambridge criteria and can say which band a piece sits in and why. Inside a twenty-minute drive of any given community, the overlap between those two groups may be nobody. On video it is whoever is free in that slot, anywhere, which is the practical argument rather than the convenience one.

A fair objection: a tutor in the room sees a disengaged fifteen-year-old faster. Our answer is the same documentation. A student who has stopped working shows up in the marked script inside a fortnight, and a six-week review exists to catch a plan that is not moving. If the evidence after six weeks shows nothing, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes. That is a more useful commitment than a promise about attendance, and it is the one thing a family can hold a provider to from outside the room.

sections.heading: In-home Arabic tuition in Dubai, honestly priced, and what online returns instead
paragraphs: In-home Arabic tuition in Dubai is a real market with real numbers. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour; independent home tutors quote AED 200-500 once travel is absorbed; and monthly in-home packages advertised in this market run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. Against that, qualified online subject tutors sit at roughly AED 150-300 and examination-year specialists at AED 200-450 or more. The gap is not the whole story, because the in-home hour usually carries a minimum booking length the online hour does not.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the same sentence appears on every country page on this site. We would rather state the market rate for the thing we do not sell than pretend it does not exist. If a family wants somebody physically present, Dubai agencies arrange it and the figures above are what to expect.

The case for online on this particular subject is the tutor pool, and it is stronger here than almost anywhere. Arabic teachers in Dubai are plentiful. Tutors who mark first-language Arabic writing against Cambridge's published criteria and can name the band a composition sits in are not. In a given community at a given hour, that overlap can be empty. The comparison table below sets the two formats against each other on the terms that matter for a language subject: who is available, what documentation comes back, and what happens when the usual tutor cannot make a session.

One cost nobody itemises deserves naming. A travelling tutor's marking happens between houses or late at night, if it happens at all, and in this market a meaningful number of in-home arrangements deliver verbal feedback and no marked script. Marking a 0508 composition properly against the criteria takes 30 to 45 minutes. Ask any provider, in-home or online, whether that time is inside the rate and what document arrives afterwards.

sections.heading: The baseline: what a first marked 0508 paper tells you in ten minutes
paragraphs: Everything starts with a timed past-paper task sat in week one, marked properly. Parents sometimes resist this, because it feels like paying for a test rather than for teaching. It is the cheapest hour in the whole plan. A marked baseline separates four different problems that look identical on a school report, and treating the wrong one for six weeks is how families spend AED 2,000 and see nothing move.

The four problems are these. A comprehension problem, where the student has genuinely not understood the passage, which on a first-language paper is rare and usually means the syllabus placement should be examined. A retrieval problem, where understanding is complete and answers come from memory of the passage rather than from the text, which is the single commonest pattern in Dubai scripts. A selection problem, where the summary answer rewrites the passage elegantly instead of choosing from it. And a timing problem, where the early answers are over-written and the high-mark question at the end is unfinished.

Each has a different signature on the page, and a tutor who cannot point at the signature has not diagnosed anything. Retrieval failures show as answers that are true, relevant and unquotable. Selection failures show as a summary longer than the limit with the focus words absent. Timing failures show as handwriting degrading and the final answer stopping mid-argument. None of those are visible in a grade, which is why a grade alone is not a baseline.

The written output of the baseline is three lines: the band the script sits in, the named problem, and the session count the repair is likely to take. A parent should receive those three lines before buying anything beyond the diagnostic hour. Ours arrives after the free trial lesson, and it is the document to compare against any other quote in the Dubai market, because it is the part that tells you whether a provider has looked at your child's work or at your budget.

sections.heading: A marked composition, read band by band
paragraphs: A marked 0508 composition should be readable by a parent who reads Arabic, and most are not, because they carry a number and a tick. What a useful marked script carries is four things: the band the piece sits in and the sentence from the criteria that puts it there; the register slips circled with the Standard Arabic alternative beside them; the recurring accuracy errors counted rather than individually corrected; and one structural instruction for the next piece.

The band justification is the part families should insist on. Criteria-based marking means a piece sits in a band because of specific features, not because it felt like a five. A tutor who writes that content is relevant but register is inconsistent across the second and third paragraphs, and quotes the criterion wording for the band above, has told the student what to do. A tutor who writes a number has told them nothing they can act on.

Counting rather than correcting is the move that produces movement. If a composition contains eleven accuracy errors across four categories, correcting all eleven teaches nothing; naming the four categories and asking the student to find the rest teaches the categories. Six weeks later the error log shows whether those categories have gone. That is what grade movement looks like at the level of evidence, well before it looks like a changed letter on a report.

The structural instruction should be singular. A composition that lacks a clear opening move, drifts in register and misreads the audience has three problems, and a student given three instructions follows none. Pick the one that costs the most marks, make it the whole brief for the next piece, and let the other two wait. Families who ask tutors for comprehensive feedback usually get comprehensive feedback and no change.

sections.heading: Two documents that show movement: the error log and the register sheet
paragraphs: Progress on a first-language subject is slow at the level of grades and fast at the level of categories, which is why two running documents do more for a worried parent than any report. The error log lists the categories of accuracy error a student makes, with a count per piece. The register sheet lists the spoken construction the student reaches for, the Standard Arabic equivalent, and the context each belongs in. Both are built from the student's own work rather than from a textbook, and both are the student's property.

The error log works because it makes recurrence visible. Week one: four categories, eleven instances. Week three: four categories, seven instances. Week five: three categories, four instances. Nobody needs to interpret that, and it is immune to the optimism that creeps into verbal feedback. It also catches the opposite case honestly: a log that reads four categories, eleven instances in week one and four categories, ten in week five is a plan that is not working, and the review exists to say so.

The register sheet is the document that moves 0508 writing marks more than any other single intervention we use in Dubai. Students here code-switch all day between English, dialect and a messaging register, and sustained formal Arabic is a register almost nothing in their week demands. Listing the substitutions as they appear, in the student's own words, converts an invisible habit into a checkable list. By the end of a term a 0508 student has twenty to thirty entries and reads their own drafts differently.

Both documents should be visible to the family, and on this subject many parents can read them better than they can read an English-language progress report. That is a genuine advantage of Arabic as the subject in question: the evidence is in a language the household often uses, so the audit does not depend on trusting the tutor's summary.

sections.heading: What actually moves in a first-language subject, and what does not
paragraphs: Honesty about timescales saves families money. Three things on 0508 move quickly with marked practice: summary procedure, timing discipline, and the language-commentary move of quoting briefly and naming an effect. Four to six focused sessions each, with work marked in between, is a fair expectation, and the evidence shows up in the scripts rather than in a mood.

Two things move slowly. Reading speed in Modern Standard Arabic is built over months of regular unseen passages, because it is a habit of the eye rather than a technique. Register control improves across a term as the register sheet fills, with relapse under time pressure for weeks after the student can do it calmly. A family arriving twelve weeks before the papers should be told plainly that reading speed is not the project; summary, commentary and timing are, because those are what can still change.

One thing does not move through tutoring at all, and saying so is part of being useful: a syllabus placement that is wrong. A student who genuinely cannot comprehend first-language passages has been entered for the wrong Cambridge code, and no amount of technique work fixes that. The correct action is a conversation with the school, in writing, before the entry deadline closes. Tutoring on top of a wrong placement is the most expensive thing a parent in this market can buy.

No tutor can promise a grade and this page does not. What the plan commits to is a diagnosis in writing after the baseline, criteria-based marking on every piece, two running documents the family can read, and a six-week review that either continues or changes course. If after six weeks the marked work shows the same four error categories at the same frequency, the right response is to change the diagnosis rather than to sell more hours.

sections.heading: Why the school report says good and the mock says D
paragraphs: This contradiction arrives in our inbox every January and it usually has a structural explanation rather than a dishonest one. Dubai private schools report on the school's own curriculum and on effort, behaviour and attainment in class. Cambridge reports on performance in two written components under timed conditions. A student can participate confidently in Arabic lessons, hand in homework, be a pleasure to teach, and still answer summary questions from memory of the passage. Both statements are true at once.

The second explanation is group size. Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibiting combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. In a British-curriculum school the Arab first-language group may be one class per year, taught by a department carrying several streams. Detailed written feedback on extended Arabic writing in that setting is limited by arithmetic.

The third is that KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes per lesson, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met. Those are real hours and they are not examination-technique hours. A school meeting its Arabic obligations fully can still not have spent a lesson on how the Cambridge summary question awards marks, because that is not what the obligation is about.

What a parent should do with the contradiction is narrow it. Ask the school for the mock script, not the mock grade. Ask which components the student lost marks on. Then have one piece of written Arabic marked against the published criteria by someone who marks to them. At that point the conversation stops being about whether the report or the mock is right and becomes a list of two or three specific repairs, which is a conversation that can actually produce a different result.

sections.heading: Marking a draft without crossing the line
paragraphs: On a language subject the boundary between teaching and producing is narrow, and it needs stating precisely because the temptation is real. A tutor may mark a student's composition against the published criteria, name the band and justify it, circle a register slip and write the Standard Arabic alternative beside it, count error categories, model a construction, and set a rewrite that the student carries out themselves. A tutor may not supply sentences for a student to transcribe, rewrite a piece into something the student could not have produced, or hand over finished work.

The safe pattern is also the effective one. Correction by category rather than by sentence means the student learns the rule and does the labour, which is the only version that improves the next unseen task. A tutor who rewrites a paragraph has produced a better paragraph and a student who has learned nothing, and on a school-submitted piece has also crossed into territory that puts the student at risk rather than the tutor.

Material is the other boundary. Cambridge owns its syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to cambridgeinternational.org rather than reproducing them as downloads. For the mandatory UAE subjects there is a further constraint: the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support in Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies works with the prescribed material.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge International or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Private tutors working with UAE students need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years; tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted here.
