faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Arabic tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page on this site. Cambridge 0508 is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical argument is the tutor pool rather than convenience: Arabic teachers in Dubai are plentiful, while tutors who mark first-language Arabic writing against Cambridge's published bands are scarce, and within driving distance of a given community that overlap can be empty. If you want someone present, Dubai agencies arrange it at AED 180-500 an hour.

faqs.question: What should a first marked 0508 paper actually tell us?
faqs.answer: Three lines: the band the script sits in, the specific problem, and roughly how many sessions the repair takes. A marked baseline separates four problems that look identical on a school report. A comprehension problem, which on a first-language paper is rare and suggests the placement should be examined. A retrieval problem, where answers come from memory of the passage rather than from the text. A selection problem, where the summary rewrites rather than chooses. A timing problem, where early answers are over-written and the last one is unfinished. Each has a visible signature on the page.

faqs.question: How do we know our child's written Arabic is genuinely improving?
faqs.answer: Watch categories, not grades. An error log lists the categories of accuracy error with a count per piece, so week one at four categories and eleven instances against week five at three categories and four instances is movement nobody has to interpret. A register sheet does the same for formality: the spoken constructions the student reaches for, the Standard Arabic equivalents, and whether the same slips recur. Grades on a first-language subject move slowly and lag the underlying change by weeks, which is why families who track only the grade conclude nothing is happening when something is.

faqs.question: What do the band descriptors on a marked 0508 composition mean in practice?
faqs.answer: They mean a piece sits where it sits because of named features rather than an overall impression. Criteria-based marking should produce a band plus the criterion wording that places the script there: content relevant and developed, structure controlled, register consistent, accuracy secure. Useful marking also quotes the wording for the band above, so the student can see the specific distance. A mark out of a total with no justification is not criteria-based marking, and on this subject it is the commonest thing families are handed. Ask for the band and the sentence that justifies it.

faqs.question: How often should marked work come back to us?
faqs.answer: Every written task, before the next session, with the band named. In practice that means weekly on a standard 0508 plan: one composition or one unseen reading set, marked, then taken apart in the lesson. Marking a composition properly against the criteria takes a tutor 30 to 45 minutes, so ask any provider in Dubai whether that time is inside the rate and what document arrives afterwards. A plan where feedback is verbal and nothing is written down is a plan a family outside the room cannot audit at all.

faqs.question: Can we see the error log and register sheet ourselves?
faqs.answer: They belong to the student, so yes. Both are built from your child's own work rather than from a textbook: the log counts accuracy errors by category across pieces, and the register sheet lists the spoken construction, the Standard Arabic alternative and where each belongs. On Arabic specifically this matters more than on most subjects, because many Dubai households read the evidence more comfortably than they read an English-language report. By the end of a term a 0508 student typically has twenty to thirty register entries and reads their own drafts differently because of it.

faqs.question: Our school report says Arabic is good but the 0508 mock came back a D. Which is right?
faqs.answer: Usually both. School reports cover the school's own curriculum plus effort, behaviour and classroom attainment; Cambridge reports performance in written components under timed conditions. A student can participate confidently, hand in homework and still answer summary questions from general understanding rather than from the text. Group size contributes: in a British-curriculum school the Arabic first-language stream may be one class per year, so detailed written feedback on extended writing is limited by arithmetic. Ask the school for the mock script rather than the grade, then have one piece marked against the published criteria.

faqs.question: How long before a 0508 reading mark actually moves?
faqs.answer: It depends which repair is needed. Summary procedure, timing discipline and the language-commentary move each respond within four to six focused sessions with marked work in between. Reading speed in Modern Standard Arabic is different: it is a habit of the eye built over months of regular unseen passages, and it cannot be compressed into a term. A family arriving twelve weeks before the papers should be told plainly that reading speed is not the project and that summary, commentary and timing are, because those are the things that can still change in the time available.

faqs.question: Can a parent who reads Arabic check the tutor's marking themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would encourage it. Look for four things on a marked script: the band with the criterion wording that places it there, register slips circled with the Standard Arabic alternative written beside them, accuracy errors counted by category rather than individually corrected, and one single instruction for the next piece. If all four are present, the marking is criteria-based. If the script carries a number and a tick, it is not, regardless of how fluent the marker is. This is the one subject where a Dubai family can verify the quality of the work directly.

faqs.question: What evidence should we ask any Dubai tutor for before paying?
faqs.answer: Four things, all before money changes hands. One marked paragraph of your child's writing, so you can see what the marking looks like. A written diagnosis naming the band and the problem. A statement of whether marking time sits inside the hourly rate. And confirmation that the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge and valid for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. A provider who cannot supply the first two before payment is asking you to buy a process you cannot inspect.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough to produce visible movement on 0508?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided a marked piece of written work sits between each session. The session is where a script is taken apart; the movement happens in the writing the student does alone afterwards. What does not work is a weekly session with nothing written in between, which becomes a conversation about Arabic rather than practice in it. Where we recommend twice weekly is the final eight weeks before a series, when timed practice has to happen frequently enough that writing to the clock stops being a novelty.

faqs.question: What should a six-week 0508 review actually cover?
faqs.answer: The week-one baseline script and the week-six script side by side, with the band named on each, the error categories counted on both, and the same question type re-sat so the comparison is like for like. The review states what moved, what did not, and whether the original diagnosis holds. It should be capable of two outcomes: continue, or change the diagnosis. A review that can only recommend more sessions is not a review. Families should ask for it in writing before starting, not request it at week six.

faqs.question: Should we keep our child's mock script or return it to the school?
faqs.answer: Ask the school whether you may photograph it before returning it. The mock script is the single most useful diagnostic document a 0508 family can hold, because it shows the actual signature of the loss rather than a grade standing in for it. Schools differ on release policy, and a photograph is usually acceptable where keeping the paper is not. Where no script is available, a full past-paper task sat under timed conditions in week one does the same job, which is exactly why the baseline exists in the plan.

faqs.question: What happens if the marked work shows no movement after six weeks?
faqs.answer: The diagnosis changes. If the same error categories recur at the same frequency across six weeks of marked pieces, continuing the same plan is selling hours rather than teaching. The usual outcomes are a different repair, a different tutor, or a conversation about whether the syllabus placement is right, because a student who genuinely cannot comprehend first-language passages has been entered for the wrong Cambridge code and no technique work fixes that. That conversation belongs with the school, in writing, and well before the entry deadline closes.

faqs.question: How do we check a tutor's marking matches Cambridge's criteria?
faqs.answer: Read the published assessment criteria for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, then read the tutor's band justification against them. The wording should correspond: a tutor placing a composition in a band should be using the language the criteria use about content, structure, register and accuracy. We link the official syllabus rather than reproducing it, because Cambridge owns those documents and a tutor distributing mark schemes as downloads is distributing somebody else's copyright. If a marker cannot point to the criterion behind a band, the band is an opinion.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.closingHeading: Ask for the marked paragraph first
dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.closingBody: Before paying any Dubai tutor for Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language, ask for one paragraph of your child's writing marked against the published criteria, and read what comes back. A band with the criterion wording behind it, register slips circled with the Standard Arabic alternative, and error categories counted rather than individually corrected tells you more than an hour of conversation about experience. Our free trial lesson produces exactly that, plus three written lines naming the band, the problem and the likely session count. dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language to examination and mark reading and writing work against the published criteria. In the trial lesson they will share an unseen passage on screen and work it with your child so you can see how the annotation actually functions.

intro.heading: Why a shared screen suits a close-reading subject
paragraphs: There is a version of the online-tutoring argument that is purely about convenience, and it is the weaker one. The stronger argument for Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language is that 0508 is built on documents. The reading components give the student a passage they have never seen. The writing components produce a handwritten script. The marking happens against published criteria. Every one of those is a document, and a document that two people can annotate simultaneously on a screen is more useful in a lesson than one passed back and forth across a table.

In a reading session the passage goes up, the student highlights what they think answers the question, the tutor highlights in a second colour what the mark scheme would credit, and the gap between the two colours is the lesson. That gap is visible, immediate and impossible to talk around. A tutor sitting beside a student with a printed sheet does something similar with a pencil, slower, and with nothing to look back at the following week. The annotated passage is saved, and the week-three passage can be compared with the week-one passage.

The second thing online delivery changes is measurement. Families usually discover how a 0508 student is doing when a mock comes back, which is two or three times a year and far too coarse to steer by. Working on a screen makes small checks cheap: a five-minute retrieval drill at the start of a session, scored; a summary attempted to length and counted; a timed paragraph written and photographed. Each is a single data point, and six of them in a row tell you more than one mock result.

What online does not change is the handwriting. The Cambridge paper is written by hand, in a script where letter forms and diacritical precision matter and where speed under pressure is a real variable. A student who practises only on a phone or a laptop keyboard writes more slowly and less accurately on the day than their knowledge deserves. Practice answers in our plans are written on paper, photographed and submitted for marking. The screen is for reading, teaching and reviewing; the pen is for producing.

The third change is the tutor pool, and for Arabic in Dubai it is decisive. Fluent Arabic teachers are everywhere in this city. Tutors who mark first-language Arabic writing against Cambridge's published bands and can say which band a composition sits in, and why, are not. Within a twenty-minute drive of a given community that overlap may be nobody at all. On video it is whoever is free in the slot, which is the real reason this page exists rather than a page about saving travel time.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.programmesIntro: Arabic runs through a Dubai student's whole school career, and what an online session should be doing changes at each stage. These are the five points where families ask for help.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Arabic
programmes.description: School-assessed years where the useful online work is a weekly unseen passage read against the clock. No examination technique is needed yet; reading speed in Modern Standard Arabic is the asset being built, and it is built by reading rather than by being taught.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students in English-medium schools read far more English than Arabic by weekly hours, so the two reading speeds diverge quietly through Years 7 to 9. A fortnightly timed passage at this stage costs little and prevents the single problem a Year 11 tutor cannot compress.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language (0508)
programmes.description: The examined course. Online sessions split between annotated reading work on screen and handwritten composition marked against the criteria between lessons. Confirm the current components, durations and weightings for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai candidates reach 0508 through the school's Arabic first-language stream, which KHDA requires to be taught separately from the non-Arab group. What is usually missing is explicit teaching of how the Cambridge components award marks, and that is a technique gap rather than a language one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
programmes.description: The parallel learner route, assessed across listening, reading, writing and speaking at learner level. Mentioned here because online delivery handles the listening and speaking elements of 0544 as naturally as it handles 0508's reading, through audio on a shared call.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students occasionally sit the wrong one of these two codes, usually an Arab child schooled entirely in English who speaks dialect at home. A marked piece of writing and one unseen passage settle it. Raise any change with the school in writing before the entry deadline closes.

programmes.name: A Level Arabic and IB Diploma Arabic A
programmes.description: The two continuations. Both demand sustained analytical writing; IB Arabic A adds oral assessment that 0508 does not examine at all. Online delivery suits the oral preparation particularly well, because a recorded practice oral can be played back and annotated.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Dubai centres run A Level Arabic than run 0508, and a number of students move between a British-curriculum school and an IB Diploma sixth form at 16. Check both availability and assessment shape in Year 11 rather than in the summer afterwards.

programmes.ageRange: Any age · entered through a centre
programmes.description: Students whose school does not enter them for 0508, or who are retaking, sit through an examination centre that accepts private candidates. The centre handles entry, invigilation and the zone timetable and charges its own fee directly.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.subjectsIntro: 0508 competes for evening hours with these subjects in a Dubai timetable, and each one tells you something about where the Arabic sits.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: The subject here: close reading of unseen text and formal composition in Modern Standard Arabic. The screen carries the reading; the pen carries the writing. Most of the available gain in a Dubai cohort is in technique rather than in vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: The learner syllabus, examined across four skills including speaking. Relevant on this page because online delivery handles audio-based skills as easily as reading, which surprises families who assume a screen is a limitation for languages.

subjects.name: Islamiyat (0493)
subjects.description: Where a school offers it, the demand for accurate quotation and formal written expression runs parallel to 0508. A student who quotes loosely in one subject almost always quotes loosely in the other, and the habit is fixable once named.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: A useful control subject. Strong English summary answers alongside weak Arabic ones point to a technique transfer problem, which is a short repair, rather than a comprehension problem, which is not.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: Close reading of text with commentary on effect. The transferable habit is brief quotation followed by analysis, which is precisely what 0508's language questions reward and what most candidates substitute with retelling.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Carried by a large share of Dubai 0508 candidates. The practical consequence is two language subjects with heavy written homework competing for the same evenings, which is a scheduling fact a plan has to accommodate.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-based questions that reward selection and inference, both of which transfer into 0508 reading work. Students who handle a historical source well often handle an Arabic passage badly, which is almost always a reading-speed issue.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Data response and structured extended answers. Mentioned because the minutes-per-mark discipline we teach on 0508 applies identically here, and a student who adopts it in one subject tends to carry it into the rest.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Usually named in a sixth-form conditional offer, which makes it the first claim on tutoring hours. A 0508 plan should be sized against what an offer actually requires, not against which subject feels most worrying.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Included because it is often the subject a student is doing when their Arabic homework slides. Three written-heavy subjects in one block produces fatigue, and it shows up in whichever has least marked work attached.

sections.heading: Annotating an unseen Arabic passage on a shared screen
paragraphs: The core activity of a 0508 reading lesson is simple to describe and hard to do well. A passage the student has not seen goes on the screen. The student reads the question, then marks in one colour the parts of the text they believe answer it. The tutor then marks in a second colour what the published criteria would actually credit. The space between the two colours is the entire diagnosis, and it does not require either party to be articulate about what went wrong.

This works better on a screen than on paper for three reasons that have nothing to do with convenience. The annotation is in two distinguishable layers rather than overlapping pencil. The marked-up passage is saved, so the week-five passage can be set beside the week-one passage and the change in the student's selection shown rather than asserted. And the mark scheme can be opened next to the text at the moment the student's attention is on the exact sentence in question, which is when it is useful rather than afterwards.

The habit the activity builds is the one Dubai 0508 candidates most often lack: answering from the text rather than from memory of the text. A fluent Arabic speaker reads the passage, understands it fully, closes the mental book and answers from general understanding. The answer is true, relevant and unquotable, and it scores poorly on retrieval, inference and summary questions alike. Two colours on a screen make the omission visible in a way that a conversation about reading carefully never does.

The technique column in the table below is deliberately small. Each row is a single, teachable move rather than a skill, and each has an observable output a parent can be shown. On a subject where the household often reads the language better than it reads an English progress report, that visibility is worth more than it would be elsewhere.

sections.heading: Handwriting Arabic: what online changes and what it must not
paragraphs: A reasonable worry about online language tutoring is that everything becomes typed, and in Arabic that worry is well founded. The Cambridge paper is handwritten. Letter forms, joins, diacritical precision where needed and sheer speed are all variables on the day, and none of them are practised by typing on a phone keyboard with predictive text helping. A plan that produces fluent typed Arabic and a slow, inaccurate handwritten script has optimised the wrong output.

Our rule is that the screen is for reading, teaching and reviewing, and paper is for producing. Practice compositions and timed answers are written by hand, photographed on a phone and submitted for marking before the next session. That one constraint keeps handwriting speed under development and gives the tutor something to mark that resembles what an examiner will see, including the degradation that sets in when a student is rushing the last question.

There is a diagnostic bonus in photographed handwriting that typed work hides completely. Handwriting that deteriorates sharply in the final third of a script is a timing problem, not an accuracy problem, and it is solved with minutes-per-mark arithmetic rather than with more vocabulary. Crossings-out clustered in one paragraph usually mark the point where formal register ran out and the student started again. Neither of those signals survives transcription into a document.

The practical setup is modest: a device with a working microphone and camera, a quiet room with a door, a table, pen and lined paper, and a phone to photograph the work. Bandwidth matters less than stability; dropped audio in the middle of an explanation wastes more of the hour than low video resolution ever does. For apartment communities the single most useful thing a family can arrange is the table, because posture and attention are connected more tightly than most parents expect.

sections.heading: Measuring 0508 progress weekly instead of waiting for a mock
paragraphs: Most Dubai families find out how a 0508 student is doing two or three times a year, when a mock or a report arrives. That is far too coarse an instrument to steer a plan by. If a repair is not working, nine weeks is a long time to discover it, and if it is working, the student deserves to know before the summer. Working on a screen makes small measurements cheap enough to take every week, and six small measurements in sequence carry more information than a single mock grade.

The measurements that matter are narrow on purpose. How many of six retrieval answers quoted from the text rather than paraphrasing from memory. Whether a summary came in under the length limit with the focus words present. How many register substitutions appeared in a composition, counted by category. Whether a timed paragraph was finished. Each is a number, each takes minutes to collect, and each maps onto one teachable move rather than onto a vague sense of progress.

What makes this honest rather than decorative is that the numbers can go the wrong way and be reported anyway. A plan where the retrieval score sits at two out of six in week one and two out of six in week five is a plan that is not working, and the correct response is to change the diagnosis rather than to sell more sessions. The measurement exists so that conversation can happen on evidence instead of on impressions.

Mock results still matter, and they matter more when there is a weekly series behind them. A mock grade in isolation produces panic or complacency. A mock grade read against six weeks of narrow measurements produces a decision: the technique moved and the timing did not, so the final eight weeks go on timed practice. That is the difference between a plan and a subscription.

sections.heading: Reading aloud: the layer Cambridge does not examine and the school does
paragraphs: 0508 is assessed in writing, which means reading aloud earns no Cambridge marks. It still belongs in a tutoring plan, for two reasons that matter in a Dubai school. The first is that school Arabic assessment frequently includes oral work, and a student's school grade affects streaming, sets and the forecast grade a centre submits. The second is diagnostic: reading a passage aloud exposes where comprehension is breaking in a way silent reading conceals completely.

On a video call this works well. The student reads; the tutor listens for the hesitations, the misread endings, the places where a long sentence loses its structure. Those hesitation points are almost always the same points where comprehension answers go wrong. A tutor who has heard a student read two paragraphs can predict which questions they will struggle with, which makes the next twenty minutes targeted rather than general.

Vocalising also helps the register problem, oddly. Students who cannot hear the difference between a formal written construction and the spoken form they would use at home begin to hear it when they read formal text aloud regularly. The ear is doing work the eye was skipping. Ten minutes of reading aloud in a session is not a Cambridge skill and it buys Cambridge marks indirectly, which is worth saying plainly rather than dressing up.

Where this interacts with the school is the forecast grade. Centres submit forecast grades to Cambridge ahead of the series, and those forecasts are built from the evidence the school has, including oral participation and classwork. A student whose written technique is improving fast and whose classroom presence has not changed can be forecast below their trajectory. Keeping the school informed, politely, with the dates of marked work, is a sensible part of an exam-year plan.

sections.heading: Scheduling 0508 around the Dubai week, Gulf Standard Time and Ramadan
paragraphs: Scheduling is where online delivery is genuinely easier and where families still get it wrong. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the whole category of problems created by a tutor in another time zone being quoted as available at eight in the evening. What it does not remove is the Dubai school week: long bus rides, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside a full IGCSE block, and an evening window between 7pm and 9pm that every family in the emirate wants.

The honest advice is to book a fixed weekly slot early in the term and defend it, rather than negotiating a lower rate for a slot that moves every week. A moving slot produces missed sessions, lost homework rhythm and a plan that never accumulates. Where a student is tired, the answer is a shorter session rather than a later one: forty-five focused minutes at 5pm beats ninety minutes at 8:30pm with a student who has already done three hours of homework.

Ramadan needs planning rather than improvisation. School days shorten, household rhythms change, and the month often falls in the stretch when timed practice should be intensifying. What works is shorter sessions moved earlier in the afternoon or to after Iftar, agreed before the month begins, with one short unseen passage kept going each week even when the writing load is reduced. Abandoning reading practice for a month costs more than the writing pause does.

The examination calendar is the other scheduling master. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version; Cambridge states that using the correct version is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Entry deadlines sit months ahead: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Ask your centre for its zone and its internal deadline before building a revision plan.

sections.heading: From 0508 to IB Arabic A or A Level, and what transfers
paragraphs: A fair number of Dubai students sit 0508 in a British-curriculum school and then move at sixteen into an IB Diploma sixth form, or stay and take AS and A Level Arabic. Families ask what carries over, and the answer is more than they expect in reading and less than they expect in assessment shape. Secure reading of formal Arabic and controlled written register are the foundations both continuations assume, and 0508 builds both. What 0508 does not touch is oral assessment, which is a substantial component of IB Arabic A and absent from the IGCSE entirely.

The practical consequence is that the preparation for Arabic A in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 should not be more reading comprehension. It should be the oral: structuring a spoken response, speaking about a text for several minutes without notes, and handling follow-up questions. Online delivery suits this unusually well, because a practice oral can be recorded, played back and annotated with the student listening to their own hesitations rather than being told about them.

For AS and A Level Arabic the demand that increases is analytical writing at length, and the useful bridge is the language-commentary work 0508 already requires. A student who can quote briefly, name a writer's choice and state its effect has the move that A Level will ask for in longer form. A student who writes that a passage is beautiful has to learn the move from scratch, which is a term's work rather than a summer's.

One planning note for Year 11 families. Fewer Dubai centres offer A Level Arabic than offer 0508, and IB Diploma schools differ in whether they run Arabic A Literature, Arabic A Language and Literature, or only Arabic B. Ask the sixth form in writing which courses it is actually running for the year your child enters, not which it lists. Availability changes with cohort numbers, and an assumption made in February can collapse in September.

sections.heading: What online delivery cannot do, and the limits of this page
paragraphs: Three honest limitations. A tutor on a screen reads the room more slowly than a tutor in the room, so a student determined not to engage is harder to catch early; our answer is the weekly measurement series, which exposes disengagement within a fortnight but not within a session. Handwriting practice depends on the family enforcing paper, because a student left to choose will type. And a household without a quiet room with a door has a real problem that no amount of teaching quality solves.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. If a family wants someone physically present, Dubai agencies arrange it and the published market band is AED 180-350 an hour per Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent tutors quoting up to AED 500 once travel is absorbed. Online qualified subject tutors sit at roughly AED 150-300 and examination-year specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Those are market figures, not ours; our model is a free trial lesson followed by a written plan with the total stated in AED.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge International or Pearson, and we operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Private tutors working with UAE students need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years; tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

On assessed work the boundary is fixed. A tutor marks against the published criteria, names the band, circles a register slip, models a construction and sets a rewrite the student carries out themselves. A tutor does not supply sentences to transcribe or hand over finished pieces; what is submitted to Cambridge or to the school is the student's own throughout. We reference Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes at cambridgeinternational.org rather than reproducing them, and for the mandatory UAE subjects we work with the prescribed material, since different or additional content requires prior Ministry permission. No tutor can promise a grade, and this page does not.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the centre and one written piece
process.description: Code 0508, the school or examination centre, which series your child is entered for, and one recent piece of handwritten Arabic. A photograph is fine. The handwriting itself carries diagnostic information that a typed version destroys.

process.title: Trial lesson on a shared passage
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, before any payment. An unseen passage goes on screen, your child marks what they think answers the question, the tutor marks what the criteria credit, and the gap between the two colours is the diagnosis. Nothing is owed if the match is wrong.

process.title: Agree the measurements, not just the hours
process.description: The written plan names which weekly measurements will be taken: retrieval score out of six, summary length and focus words, register substitutions by category, timed completion. A plan that specifies only frequency and price cannot be evaluated by anybody.

process.title: Weekly cycle: screen for reading, paper for writing
process.description: Reading worked and annotated live, with the passage saved for comparison. Writing produced by hand, photographed and marked against the criteria before the next session. A short session note to the parent naming what was scored and what moved.

process.title: Steer on the numbers, including when they stall
process.description: If a measurement sits flat for four or five weeks, the diagnosis changes rather than the session count rising. The measurements exist so that decision can be made on evidence, and so a family can see the same evidence we are looking at.

whyPoints.title: The text is shared, not described
whyPoints.description: Two colours on one passage show exactly what the student selected and what the criteria credit. That gap is the lesson, and it needs neither party to be articulate about what went wrong, which is why it works with a tired fifteen-year-old.

whyPoints.title: Measured weekly, not twice a year
whyPoints.description: Narrow measurements taken every session, logged and reported, including when they go the wrong way. Six data points in a row carry more usable information than a single mock grade arriving in January.

whyPoints.title: Paper for producing, screen for reading
whyPoints.description: The Cambridge paper is handwritten, so practice answers are handwritten, photographed and marked. Handwriting that degrades in the last third of a script is a timing diagnosis that typed work hides entirely.

whyPoints.title: A Cambridge-criteria marker, wherever they are
whyPoints.description: Fluent Arabic teachers are plentiful in Dubai; tutors who place a composition in a band and justify it from the criteria are not. Online delivery means the match is to the second group rather than to the nearest member of the first.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time, and a slot that holds
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on local time, booked as a fixed weekly slot early in the term. The 7pm to 9pm window is the most contested in the emirate, and a moving slot is the commonest reason a plan never accumulates.

whyPoints.title: The limitations written down
whyPoints.description: A screen reads the room more slowly than a person. Handwriting needs enforcing at home. A quiet room is required. Those are stated here rather than discovered in week three, alongside the market rate for the in-home option we do not sell.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring effective for a reading-heavy subject like 0508?
faqs.answer: On this syllabus it has a structural advantage. 0508 is built on documents: unseen passages, published criteria and handwritten scripts. A passage shared on screen can be annotated by both people at once in two distinguishable colours, so what the student selected and what the criteria credit sit side by side. The marked-up passage is also saved, which means week five can be compared with week one rather than progress being asserted. A tutor beside a student with a printed sheet does something similar in pencil, more slowly, with nothing to look back at.

faqs.question: How does a tutor annotate an Arabic passage on screen with my child?
faqs.answer: The passage is shared live. The student reads the question, underlines the words that constrain the answer, then marks in one colour the parts of the text they think answer it. The tutor marks in a second colour what the published criteria would credit. The published criteria are opened beside the passage at the moment the student's attention is on the relevant sentence. The space between the two colours is the diagnosis, and it works without either party having to articulate what went wrong, which matters with a tired fifteen-year-old.

faqs.question: Should my child type or handwrite 0508 practice answers?
faqs.answer: Handwrite, always, then photograph and submit for marking. The Cambridge paper is handwritten, and letter forms, joins and speed under pressure are real variables on the day that typing with predictive text does nothing for. Handwritten work also carries diagnostic information typing destroys: script that degrades in the final third signals a timing problem rather than an accuracy problem, and crossings-out clustered in one paragraph usually mark where formal register ran out. A plan producing fluent typed Arabic and a slow handwritten script has optimised the wrong output.

faqs.question: How can we measure reading progress without sitting a full paper every time?
faqs.answer: With narrow weekly measurements that take minutes. How many of six retrieval answers quoted from the text rather than paraphrasing from memory. Whether a summary came in under the length limit with the focus words present. Whether a timed paragraph was finished. How many register substitutions appeared, counted by category. Each maps onto one teachable move, and six in sequence tell you more than a single mock grade. They can also go the wrong way, which is the point: a flat retrieval score across five weeks means the diagnosis needs changing.

faqs.question: What device and room setup does a 0508 online lesson need in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a working microphone and camera, a quiet room with a door that closes, a table, pen and lined paper, and a phone to photograph handwritten work. Connection stability matters more than speed, because dropped audio mid-explanation wastes more of the hour than low video resolution. In apartment communities the table is the piece families most often skip and the one that matters most: a timed Arabic composition written on a sofa with a television on is practice in the wrong conditions.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring help with reading Arabic aloud?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth doing even though Cambridge assesses 0508 in writing. Reading aloud on a call exposes where comprehension is breaking: the hesitations, the misread endings and the long sentences that lose their structure are almost always the same places where written answers go wrong. It also helps register, because students who cannot see the difference between formal written Arabic and the spoken form they use at home begin to hear it. School Arabic assessment often includes oral work too, and that feeds the forecast grade a centre submits.

faqs.question: How are sessions scheduled around Dubai school hours and Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, so no family is offered a slot that only works in another time zone. The real constraints are local: long bus routes make a 4pm start optimistic in outer communities, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies add weekday homework, and the 7pm to 9pm window is the most contested in the emirate. The advice is to book a fixed weekly slot early in the term and defend it. Where a student is tired, shorten the session rather than moving it later.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one online 0508 session?
faqs.answer: Only when both are genuinely at the same point, which is less common than families hope. A paired session costs roughly a third to a half of the one-to-one rate per student in this market, and it works when two students need the same repair on the same component. It fails when one needs summary procedure and the other needs register control, because then each is watching the other's lesson. Our rule is that both students write and both are marked; if the measurements diverge for two cycles, we recommend splitting them back.

faqs.question: What happens if the internet connection drops mid-session?
faqs.answer: The session is rejoined, and if the interruption takes a meaningful part of the hour, the time is made up rather than written off. Ask any provider for that policy in writing before paying, along with the cancellation terms and the minimum notice for moving a slot. Practically, stability beats speed: a wired connection or a position close to the router prevents more lost minutes than a faster package does. Work already submitted is unaffected, since written tasks are photographed and sent rather than produced live on the call.

faqs.question: How do we send handwritten Arabic work for marking?
faqs.answer: Photograph each page with a phone in reasonable light and send it before the session, so marking happens in advance rather than during the lesson. Marking a composition properly against the criteria takes a tutor 30 to 45 minutes, which is why work arriving at the start of a session cannot be marked and taught in the same hour. Lay pages flat, keep the whole page in frame including margins, and number them. The marked script comes back with the band named, register slips circled and error categories counted.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the Arabic tasks my child's school sets?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a boundary. A tutor may read a task, explain what it is asking, teach the technique it needs, mark a practice attempt against criteria and set a rewrite the student carries out. A tutor may not supply sentences to transcribe or hand over finished work, because anything submitted to the school or to Cambridge must be the student's own throughout. For the mandatory UAE subjects there is an additional constraint: using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so support works with the prescribed material.

faqs.question: Is an online 0508 tutor cheaper than an in-home one in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the gap is wider than the headline figures suggest. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent tutors quoting up to AED 500 once travel is absorbed, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200-450 or more for an examination-year specialist. The in-home hour also commonly carries a two-hour minimum booking the online hour does not. Those are market figures rather than ours; IB Gram offers a free trial lesson and then a written plan with the total stated.

faqs.question: How do we know an online Arabic tutor is actually qualified for 0508?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions and look at one document. Which Cambridge series have you taught 0508 to. Have you marked first-language Arabic writing against the published bands. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge and valid for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Then ask for one paragraph of your child's writing marked before you pay, and check whether the band comes with the criterion wording that justifies it. A marker who cannot point to the criterion behind a band is offering an opinion.

faqs.question: What record do we get after each online session?
faqs.answer: A short note naming what was taught, what was set, and what the week's measurements were: the retrieval score, the summary length, the register count, whichever applied. Plus the annotated passage, saved, and the marked script where a written task was due. The point of writing it down is that a family outside the room can audit the plan rather than trust a summary, and on Arabic specifically many Dubai households read the evidence more comfortably than they read an English-language progress report.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor carry on into IB Arabic A after 0508?
faqs.answer: Often, and the thing to prepare for is different from what families expect. Secure formal reading and controlled written register transfer directly, and 0508 builds both. What 0508 never examines is oral assessment, which is substantial in IB Arabic A. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is better spent on structuring a spoken response and speaking about a text without notes than on more comprehension. Online delivery suits that well, since a practice oral can be recorded, played back and annotated with the student hearing their own hesitations.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.closingBody: The quickest way to judge whether an online 0508 tutor is worth paying is to watch a single unseen passage being worked on a shared screen. Your child marks what they believe answers the question; the tutor marks what the published criteria would credit; the gap between the two colours is the whole diagnosis, and it takes about fifteen minutes to become obvious. Book the free trial lesson, send one piece of handwritten Arabic beforehand, and you will leave with a named problem and the weekly measurements that will track it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, around your child's centre and series.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language to examination and mark composition and comprehension work against the published assessment criteria. In the trial lesson they will read one of your child's written answers aloud with them and show where the marks were available.

intro.heading: Why fluent Arabic speakers lose marks in 0508
paragraphs: The commonest conversation we have with Dubai parents about Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language starts with bewilderment. The child speaks Arabic at home, with grandparents, in the car, on the phone. The 0508 mark comes back at a C. Something must be wrong with the marking. Almost always nothing is wrong with the marking. 0508 is not a fluency test. It assesses close reading of a text a student has not seen before, and the production of formal written Modern Standard Arabic shaped to a specific task. Neither of those is what speaking Arabic at home teaches.

The reading side asks a student to find information, infer what is implied rather than stated, select material for a summary, and comment on how a writer has used language to create an effect. A fluent speaker reads the passage, understands it completely, and then answers the question from general understanding instead of from the text. That costs marks on almost every question type. The repair is technique: underline, select, quote precisely, answer the question asked rather than the topic raised.

The writing side asks for composition and directed writing in Modern Standard Arabic, with register controlled to the task. A student whose written Arabic has been shaped by messaging apps and spoken dialect writes informally without noticing, mixes registers inside a paragraph, and reaches for vocabulary that is correct in speech and wrong in a formal letter or article. Dubai's linguistic environment makes this more common here than in a monolingual country: many students code-switch between English and Arabic all day and have never been required to sustain formal Arabic across two pages.

There is a third factor specific to this city. Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. In a British-curriculum school, the Arabic first-language group can be small, taught by a department carrying several streams, and timetabled against subjects the school treats as higher priority. Students in that position often arrive at 0508 having never been taught the assessment explicitly.

Confirm the current component structure, durations and weightings for Cambridge 0508 on the syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org for your child's examination year. This page describes what the components assess and where Dubai students lose marks; it does not restate figures that Cambridge revises, because a tutor working from an out-of-date printout is a real risk on a subject with a small teaching community. What this page can tell you is what each component is testing, which is the part most Dubai students have never had explained, and what a marked script reveals within the first ten minutes of reading it.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.programmesIntro: Arabic as a first language runs as a continuous track in Dubai schools, and the stage your child is at changes what a session should be doing. These are the four stages around 0508.

programmes.name: Lower secondary Arabic first language
programmes.description: The years where reading stamina in Modern Standard Arabic is either built or quietly skipped. Students read set texts, write short compositions and are assessed by the school rather than by Cambridge. Work at this stage is about reading unfamiliar formal prose without losing the thread, and writing a paragraph that holds one register.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is where the gap opens. A student in an English-medium school may spend five hours a week in English literature and a fraction of that reading formal Arabic. By Year 10 the reading speed difference between the two languages is wide enough to cost 0508 marks under timed conditions.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language (0508)
programmes.description: The examined course: close reading of unseen passages, selecting and summarising material, commenting on a writer's use of language, and producing extended writing in Modern Standard Arabic shaped to a stated purpose and audience. Assessment is entirely by written examination.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai students entered for 0508 are placed there because the school has identified them as Arab or first-language speakers, which is also how KHDA's mandatory-subject streaming works. The placement is usually right. What is often missing is any explicit teaching of how the Cambridge components award marks.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Arabic
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation for students who want to keep formal Arabic to an advanced level, with literary texts and sustained analytical writing. Fewer Dubai centres offer it than offer 0508, so availability is worth checking before Year 11 planning is finalised.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students who carry Arabic through to A Level usually do so for a specific reason: a degree in law, media, Arabic literature or regional studies, or university applications inside the Gulf. It is a deliberate choice rather than a default, and worth making on purpose in Year 11.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Arabic A
programmes.description: The IB equivalent route for first-language speakers, assessed through literary and language study with oral and written components rather than two written papers. Students moving from 0508 into Arabic A find the reading load heavier and the assessment shape entirely different.
programmes.countryNote: A fair number of Dubai students sit 0508 in a British-curriculum school and then move to an IB Diploma school for sixth form. The transition is manageable, and the piece to prepare for is the oral assessment, which 0508 does not examine at all.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-langu.subjectsIntro: 0508 shares a timetable, and sometimes a department, with these subjects in Dubai schools. The reason each one appears in the same conversation is given.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: The core syllabus on this page. Marks are lost to imprecise selection from the text and to register drift in extended writing, not to weak vocabulary. A first marked paper usually shows both within ten minutes of reading it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: The second-language syllabus, aimed at students learning Arabic rather than speaking it at home. Some students are placed here when 0508 would suit them better, and vice versa; a marked piece of writing settles the question faster than a conversation does.

subjects.name: Islamiyat (0493)
subjects.description: Where offered, this sits alongside Arabic and shares the demand for precise quotation and formal written expression. Students who can quote accurately in one subject usually transfer the habit to the other once it is named.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, so the reading demand overlaps directly with 0508.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum, with Arabic as the primary language of instruction for Arab students. Content may not be varied without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, which is why its material is fixed and worth reading as formal Arabic practice.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: The structural twin. Summary, directed writing and analysis of language are tested in both subjects in recognisably similar ways, so a student who understands what a summary question wants in English can be shown the same logic in Arabic.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: Close reading and commentary on a writer's choices. The transferable skill is quoting briefly and commenting on effect rather than retelling the plot, which is exactly the move 0508 language questions reward.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Many 0508 candidates in Dubai are stronger readers in Arabic than in English and sit ESL for their English qualification. Timetabling both language subjects well is a real constraint on when a 0508 session can run.

subjects.name: French (0520) and Spanish (0530)
subjects.description: A third language in the block for some students. Worth knowing because three languages in one timetable produces a specific kind of fatigue, and the subject that suffers is usually the one with the least homework attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Unrelated in content and highly relevant in practice. Where a conditional sixth-form offer names Mathematics, that is where tutoring hours belong first, and a 0508 plan should be sized around what the offer actually requires.

sections.heading: 0508 or 0544: how Dubai schools place students, and when the placement is wrong
paragraphs: Cambridge offers Arabic as a First Language under code 0508 and Arabic as a Foreign Language under 0544, and they are not two difficulty levels of one course. They assess different things for different students. 0508 assumes the student reads and writes Arabic as a first language and tests close reading and formal composition. 0544 assumes the student is learning Arabic and tests the four skills of a language learner. A student placed in the wrong one will look weak in a way that has nothing to do with their ability.

Dubai schools place students by heritage and by the school's own assessment, and the placement interacts with KHDA's mandatory-subject rules. Arabic is required in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibiting combined classes for both groups because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. That streaming is usually the basis of the Cambridge entry decision too.

The hard cases are the students the categories do not fit. An Arab child schooled entirely in English since nursery, who speaks dialect at home and has never written a formal Arabic essay, is a first-language speaker by heritage and a learner by capability. A non-Arab child raised in Dubai since infancy with Arabic-speaking friends may read better than their classification suggests. The honest way to settle it is a marked piece of writing and an unseen reading passage, not a conversation, because conversation flatters a fluent speaker and hides exactly the gap 0508 examines.

If the placement looks wrong, raise it with the school in writing before the entry deadline rather than after the mock. Entries close months ahead of the papers, and a change of syllabus code after the deadline is not a change the school can make. The table below sets out what each route assumes and who it genuinely suits.

sections.heading: What the reading component actually asks for, question type by question type
paragraphs: The reading side of 0508 is where fluent speakers are most often surprised, because every question type has a specific mechanic and none of them reward general understanding of the passage. There are broadly four things a reading paper asks a student to do: retrieve information that is stated, infer what is implied, select and reorganise material into a summary, and comment on how the writer's language choices produce an effect. A student who treats all four as comprehension answers the first two adequately and loses most of the marks on the last two.

Retrieval and inference questions are repaired with discipline rather than teaching. Read the question before the passage. Underline the words in the question that constrain the answer. Find the place in the text that answers it and quote or paraphrase precisely from there. Students lose marks by answering from memory of the passage rather than from the passage, and by writing three sentences where one is asked for, which wastes time they need later.

The summary question is the one that most repays tutoring, because it is a procedure. Identify the focus the question sets, go through the passage marking only material relevant to that focus, group what is marked, then write it in continuous prose in the student's own words and within the length allowed. Fluent speakers tend to rewrite the passage elegantly instead of selecting from it, which scores on expression and not on content. Marks here are concentrated and recoverable.

Language commentary is the hardest to teach and the most teachable. The move is to quote briefly, name what the writer has done, and say what effect it has on the reader, with the effect stated in terms of meaning rather than in a label. Students who write that a word is powerful have said nothing. Students who say what image it builds and why that matters to the argument have earned the mark. Four or five marked attempts, each with the criteria beside it, changes a student's commentary permanently.

sections.heading: The writing component: register, Modern Standard Arabic and the drift nobody notices
paragraphs: 0508's writing side asks for extended composition and directed writing in Modern Standard Arabic, with form, purpose and audience controlled. The single largest cause of lost marks in Dubai scripts is register drift. A student begins a formal article in confident Standard Arabic, runs out of formal vocabulary somewhere in the second paragraph, and substitutes the spoken construction they would use at home. The meaning survives. The marks do not, because control of register is explicitly what is being assessed.

This is a Dubai-specific pattern rather than a deficiency. Students here code-switch all day: English at school, dialect at home, a mixture with friends, and a messaging register that belongs to neither. Sustained formal written Arabic is a register almost nothing in their week requires. The fix is practice with correction, and the practical version is a running register sheet: the spoken construction the student reaches for, the Standard Arabic equivalent, and the context each belongs to. Built over a term, it is the single most useful document a 0508 student owns.

The second cause of loss is structure. A directed-writing task sets a form and an audience, and marks depend on the student producing that form rather than a general essay on the topic. A letter has conventions. An article has a headline move and a closing one. A speech addresses an audience directly. Students who know the content and ignore the form give away marks that require no knowledge at all to earn.

The third is handwriting and accuracy under time pressure. The paper is handwritten, in a script where diacritical precision and letter forms matter, and a student who practises only by typing on a phone keyboard will be slower and less accurate on the day. Practice answers should be written by hand, photographed and submitted for marking. Accuracy work is best done on the student's own errors rather than from a textbook list: a marked script shows the four mistakes that recur, and those four are the lesson.

sections.heading: Who may teach Arabic in a Dubai school, and what that means for choosing a tutor
paragraphs: Dubai regulates Arabic teaching more tightly than it regulates most subjects, and the detail is useful to a parent choosing a tutor. KHDA requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects. That is a requirement on schools and their staff, not a credential a private tutor holds, and no tutoring service should present it as one. What it tells you is that the bar inside the classroom is a specific and checkable thing, and it is reasonable to ask a tutor what their equivalent qualification and experience is.

Instructional time is also prescribed. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For a parent this explains why Arabic appears in the timetable as it does, and why a school cannot simply trade Arabic time for examination revision in Year 11.

Content is constrained too. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That is a genuine limit on what tutoring material for Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies may be described as, and it is why support in those subjects should be framed as helping a student with the prescribed material rather than as an alternative syllabus. 0508 itself is a Cambridge qualification and sits outside that constraint, which is a distinction worth holding.

Separately, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without that permit exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

sections.heading: Why the 0508 grade does not count in the Ministry of Education's five subjects
paragraphs: This surprises families every year, so it belongs on the page. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That exclusion is not a judgement on the subject. It reflects the fact that Arabic and Islamic Education are mandatory parts of schooling in the UAE rather than elective qualifications a student chose, so the equivalency count looks at the five beyond them. The practical consequence for a Year 11 family is arithmetic: count your five accredited subjects excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and check that five of them are genuinely on track at grade E or 3 or above. One ranking competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced position is five.

A 0508 grade still matters for other reasons. It is on the certificate. It supports a route into AS and A Level Arabic or IB Arabic A. Some Gulf universities and law or media pathways value demonstrated formal Arabic directly. And a student who can read and write Standard Arabic confidently has an advantage in this region that no equivalency table measures. None of that is the same as counting towards the five.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs. It is not something IB Gram performs, influences or guarantees, and no tutoring is required for it. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning a subject count around it, because published rules are revised and a page is a secondary source. On the American track, for reference, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math.

sections.heading: The 0508 year counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable version for each. Cambridge states that using the correct version for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. The first thing a Dubai family should do when planning 0508 revision is ask the school which zone it sits in, then use only that timetable.

Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which reshapes what tutoring can achieve. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series are the clearest worked example of the gap: final entries due 27 November 2026, examination period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May, certificates in late June. Whatever series your child sits, assume the entry decision is made roughly ten weeks before the first paper and confirm actual dates with the centre.

For a language subject the backwards plan has its own shape, because reading speed and register control improve slowly and cannot be crammed. Reading stamina in Modern Standard Arabic needs months of regular unseen passages. Register control needs a term of corrected writing. Summary technique and language commentary can be repaired in four to six focused sessions. Timed practice belongs in the final eight weeks. A family arriving twelve weeks out should spend them on summary technique, commentary and timing rather than attempting to rebuild reading speed.

Ramadan deserves a line in the plan. It usually falls in the stretch when timed practice should be intensifying, and the honest adjustment is shorter, earlier or post-Iftar sessions rather than an abandoned month. Forty-five focused minutes during Ramadan is worth more than ninety minutes nobody is present for, and planning the adjustment in advance beats improvising it in week two.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's Arabic writing
paragraphs: This matters more in a language subject than in most, because the line between teaching and producing is thinner. A tutor may read a student's composition, mark it against the published criteria, explain which band it sits in and why, point to a sentence where register slipped, model an alternative construction, and set a rewrite the student does themselves. A tutor may not supply sentences for a student to transcribe, rewrite a composition into something the student could not have produced, or hand over finished work. Anything submitted to Cambridge or to the school must be the student's own throughout.

In practice the safe pattern is correction by category rather than by sentence. Instead of rewriting a paragraph, a tutor names the pattern: this is a dialect construction in a formal context, there are four more in the piece, find them. The student does the work and learns the category, which also happens to be the only version that improves the next unseen piece. Rewriting the student's paragraph produces a better paragraph and a student who has learned nothing.

Material is the second boundary. Cambridge owns its syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables. We reference them and link to the official source at cambridgeinternational.org. We do not reproduce or distribute them as downloads, and a tutor offering a bundle of mark schemes to keep is distributing somebody else's copyright. For the mandatory UAE subjects there is an additional constraint: using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so support there works with the prescribed material.

On outcomes, nothing on this page promises a grade and no tutor honestly can. What a plan offers is a diagnosis written down after the first marked piece, work marked against the criteria rather than graded by impression, a register sheet and error log the student keeps, and a review timed to the entry deadline. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the practical gain for a Dubai family is that the match is to a 0508 specialist rather than to whoever teaches Arabic nearby.

The written piece does more diagnostic work than any conversation, because it shows register control and accuracy at the same time.

process.title: Weekly work, marked against the criteria
process.description: An unseen passage every fortnight and a written piece in between, handwritten, photographed and marked against the published criteria before the next session. The register sheet and error log grow across the term and belong to the student.

process.title: Review before the entry deadline
process.description: A checkpoint timed to the examination centre's deadline rather than to invoicing. Either the marked work says the plan is working, or the diagnosis was wrong and it changes. On a language subject, three months of the wrong repair is a term nobody gets back.

whyPoints.description: Your child already speaks Arabic. What 0508 marks is close reading of unseen text and controlled formal writing, so that is what sessions work on. The distinction is the whole reason a fluent speaker can sit at a C.

whyPoints.title: A specialist in the Cambridge criteria
whyPoints.description: Dubai has no shortage of Arabic teachers and a real shortage of tutors who mark 0508 writing against the published bands. Online delivery means the match is to the second kind, wherever they happen to live.
