subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: The subject here. Grades are decided by reading speed in an unvowelled script and by whether vocabulary has been learnt by topic area rather than in alphabetical lists. Speaking confidence often masks how slowly a student reads.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: The parallel code for students schooled in Arabic, examined through close reading and formal composition. Relevant because placement between the two decides what the whole two years looks like, and the decision is sometimes wrong in both directions.

subjects.description: The closest structural comparison. Students who have done well in a European-language IGCSE already own the machinery: topic-area vocabulary, listening under pressure, writing to a prompt. What Arabic adds is the script, and nothing in French prepares anyone for that.

subjects.description: Often the alternative a Dubai option block offers against Arabic. Worth naming because families sometimes choose between them, and the honest comparison is that Spanish is faster to read and Arabic is more useful where the family lives.

subjects.description: Taken by a minority of Dubai students, usually in schools with a German-stream history. Mentioned here because carrying two additional languages plus mandatory Arabic produces a specific fatigue, and the subject that slips is the one with least marked homework.

subjects.description: Many 0544 candidates are already learning in their second or third language. That matters: a student decoding both an English question and an Arabic passage is paying a double tax on reading speed, and the plan should acknowledge it.

subjects.description: A useful control. A student who summarises well in English and badly in Arabic has a decoding problem rather than a thinking problem, which is a reassuring and actionable diagnosis.

subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools. For non-Arab students KHDA specifies the school's licensed-curriculum language for Islamic Education and for Moral, Social and Cultural studies, so the reading load there does not overlap 0544 the way it does for the Arab stream.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum, with content that may not be varied without prior Ministry of Education permission. Support here works with the prescribed material rather than offering an alternative course.

subjects.description: Almost always named in a sixth-form conditional offer, which makes it the first claim on tutoring hours. A 0544 plan should be sized against what the offer requires rather than against which subject a family worries about most.

sections.heading: 0544 or 0508: the placement decision and how Dubai schools make it
paragraphs: Cambridge publishes Arabic as a Foreign Language under 0544 and Arabic as a First Language under 0508. The distinction is about the student, not the difficulty. 0544 assumes someone acquiring Arabic as an additional language and assesses them accordingly. 0508 assumes someone schooled in Arabic and asks for close reading of unseen text and formal written composition. A student in the wrong code produces work that looks like weak ability and is in fact a mismatch.

Dubai schools place students by heritage first, because that is how the mandatory Arabic streaming works. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For most students the stream and the Cambridge code line up correctly. The exceptions are predictable and worth checking.

Two exceptions recur in this city. The first is an Arab child schooled entirely in English since nursery, who speaks dialect at home, has never written a formal Arabic essay, and is placed in the first-language stream by heritage. They are a learner in capability and will struggle with 0508's composition demands. The second is a long-resident non-Arab student who reads Arabic genuinely well and sits in a learner group that under-stretches them. Both are resolved by evidence: a timed unseen reading passage and one written task.

If the placement looks wrong, raise it with the school in writing well before the entry deadline, because entries close months ahead of the papers and the code cannot be changed afterwards. The table sets out what each route assumes and who it fits, including the IB equivalents for families whose sixth form will be a Diploma school.

sections.heading: The four skills a learner syllabus can sample, and where each leaks marks
paragraphs: A foreign-language qualification tests some combination of understanding spoken language, reading, writing and speaking. Which of those your child's 0544 series examines, and in what proportion, is a question for the live syllabus page and for the school, because versions differ and Cambridge revises specifications. What does not change is the pattern of loss among Dubai learners, and that pattern is consistent enough to plan around.

Reading is where most marks are lost, and the cause is decoding speed rather than vocabulary. A student who reads letter by letter can understand a passage given twice the time available. The examination does not offer twice the time. Everything else in the plan is downstream of this, which is why our 0544 plans open with a daily ten-minute reading drill rather than with a vocabulary list.

Understanding spoken Arabic is the skill students most overestimate in Dubai, because they hear the language daily and assume familiarity equals comprehension. Recorded examination audio is a different animal from a conversation with a friendly shopkeeper: unfamiliar voices, no gestures, no repetition, and a question to answer while listening. Students who practise only with their tutor's voice are practising one voice. We use varied audio deliberately.

Writing to a prompt rewards structure over flourish. A learner who produces four accurate simple sentences addressing every part of the prompt outscores one who attempts an elaborate construction and loses control of it. Speaking, where a series examines it, is about keeping going: a prepared bank of linking phrases and the discipline of answering more than the question was asked turns a nervous exchange into a sustained one. Both are teachable in a handful of sessions.

sections.heading: Script literacy: the project nobody schedules
paragraphs: Twenty-eight letters, each written differently depending on whether it stands alone, begins, sits inside or ends a word. Several distinguished only by dots above or below. Short vowels marked in teaching material and absent from almost everything else, including examination passages. That is the system a 0544 candidate has to read at speed, and the gap between recognising it and reading it fluently is where this grade is won or lost.

The reason it goes unscheduled is that it looks like primary-school work and a Year 10 student resents it. The answer is to make it short, daily and measurable rather than long and humiliating. Ten minutes of reading aloud, timed, with the number of words per minute recorded. A word-shape drill on the letter pairs the student actually confuses, not all of them. A passage re-read on three consecutive days so the improvement is felt rather than described. Students who resist this on day one usually stop resisting in week three, because the speed change is noticeable to them.

Vowelling is the decision that divides opinion and deserves a plain answer. Reading vowelled text builds confidence and does not build the skill the examination needs, so vowelled material is useful early and becomes a crutch quickly. Our pattern is vowelled for new vocabulary, unvowelled for everything the student has already met, and unvowelled only within a term of the series. Families should ask any tutor what their position on this is, because a tutor who works entirely in vowelled text is teaching a different task.

Handwriting deserves the same treatment. The paper is written by hand, in a script where joins and letter forms carry meaning, so practice answers are written on paper, photographed and submitted rather than typed. Typing with predictive assistance produces a fluent-looking student who writes slowly and inaccurately on the day, and the examination has no predictive text.

sections.heading: Listening practice that resembles the examination
paragraphs: Dubai learners of Arabic have an advantage and a trap in the same place. The advantage is exposure: the language is around them constantly, and their ear is more tuned than a learner's in London. The trap is that everyday exposure is cooperative. A shopkeeper repeats, slows down, gestures and switches to English when the student stalls. Recorded examination audio does none of that, and a student whose confidence comes from cooperative conversation can be badly surprised.

What makes listening practice useful is matching the conditions rather than the content. Unfamiliar voices, played once or at most twice, with the question in front of the student before the audio starts, answered while listening rather than afterwards from memory. The habit of reading the questions first is worth several marks on its own, because it tells the ear what to listen for. Students who listen first and then read the questions are relying on recall rather than on selection.

Sources matter less than variety. Short news bulletins, announcements, dialogues and recorded messages all appear in learner materials, and the point of rotating them is that each has a different pace and register. A tutor's own voice is the one voice a student must not become dependent on, which is a specific risk in one-to-one tuition and worth naming to any provider you are considering.

Online delivery handles all of this without compromise, which surprises families who assume a screen is a limitation for languages. Audio is shared cleanly, replayed precisely, paused at the exact word that broke, and the transcript opened beside it afterwards. That last step is the one most classroom listening practice skips and the one that converts a wrong answer into a learned pattern: see the word written, hear it again, say it, move on.

sections.heading: Writing and speaking: four accurate sentences before any ambition
paragraphs: Learner writing is marked on whether the task has been addressed and on accuracy within the range of language the student controls. A Dubai student who writes four short accurate sentences covering every element of a prompt scores better than one who attempts a complex construction, loses the agreement halfway through and leaves one bullet of the prompt untouched. That is not a counsel of low ambition; it is the order of operations. Accuracy first, range second, and range only on structures that have been practised to the point of reliability.

The mechanical habit we teach is to tick off the prompt. Most learner writing tasks specify several things to include. A student who lists them in the margin and crosses each off as it is covered does not lose the marks that are available simply for addressing the task. It is the cheapest mark recovery in the whole syllabus and it takes one session to install.

Speaking, where a series examines it, rewards keeping going. The common failure among Dubai learners is a three-word answer followed by silence, which gives an examiner nothing to credit. The repair is a small bank of linking phrases and one rule: answer the question, then add a reason or an example without being asked. Practised fifteen times, it becomes automatic, and a nervous student who adds one clause to every answer sounds markedly more capable than one who does not.

What a tutor must not do, here as everywhere, is produce the work. A tutor may teach the structures, model a response, mark a written attempt against criteria, name the pattern of error and set a rewrite the student carries out. A tutor may not supply sentences for a student to memorise and reproduce as their own in an assessed task, or hand over finished pieces. What reaches Cambridge or the school must be the student's own. On speaking that line is especially worth holding: a scripted answer delivered from memory collapses on the first follow-up question an examiner asks.

sections.heading: Mandatory Arabic, the 0544 entry, and what each one is for
paragraphs: Families often merge two separate things: the Arabic their child must study because Dubai requires it, and the Cambridge qualification their child sits at sixteen. Keeping them apart makes several decisions easier. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April.

The language rules differ by group, which is directly relevant to a 0544 family. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. A non-Arab student therefore meets formal Arabic text mainly in Arabic lessons themselves, which is a smaller weekly dose than their Arab classmates receive.

Instructional time is prescribed too. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

What this means in practice is that school Arabic is a compliance requirement delivered to a fixed specification, and it may or may not have taught your child how a Cambridge paper awards marks. That is not a criticism of schools; it is a difference of purpose. A 0544 plan works alongside the school's lessons rather than replacing them, and the honest division of labour is that the school delivers the curriculum while the tutoring delivers reading speed and examination technique.

sections.heading: After 0544: continue, switch, or stop at sixteen
paragraphs: Three honest options follow a 0544 grade, and families are rarely offered all three. The first is continuation into IB Diploma Arabic B, which assumes prior study and adds substantial oral assessment. A solid 0544 grade is the normal evidence for that placement, and schools generally reserve ab initio for genuine beginners, though they interpret eligibility differently and the decision is the school's.

The second is AS and A Level Arabic, available at fewer Dubai centres than 0544 and considerably more demanding in analytical writing. It suits a student with a specific destination in mind: law, media, regional studies, or a Gulf university route where demonstrated Arabic carries real weight. It does not suit a student continuing out of inertia, because the reading load is substantial.

The third is stopping, and it is a legitimate choice that deserves saying out loud. A student who sits 0544 at sixteen has a qualification on the certificate and will continue to hear Arabic daily as long as they live here. Where the sixth-form offer names Mathematics, English and two sciences, spending two years of effort on an Arabic course nobody has asked for is a real cost. The useful conversation is which subjects the offer actually requires, in writing, from the sixth form itself.

One equivalency note, because it surprises families every year. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A 0544 grade is a real qualification and it does not fill one of those five slots. Equivalency is run by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring service, so verify the current rule on its own channel.

sections.heading: What a 0544 plan costs, and the limits of what it can promise
paragraphs: Market rates for one-to-one tuition in Dubai collected in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45-150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200-450 or more for an examination-year specialist. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500 once travel is absorbed. Monthly online packages advertised in this market have been seen at AED 799 for eight sessions. Those are the market's figures, not IB Gram's price list.

0544 has an unusual cost profile among language subjects, and it works in a family's favour. The topic list is finite, the skills are discrete, and script literacy improves with short daily practice the student does alone. That means a disciplined plan of one weekly session plus ten minutes a day achieves more than two expensive sessions a week with nothing in between. A provider selling you four sessions a week on a learner language is selling hours rather than designing a plan.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and for this subject the real gain is access: specialists in teaching Arabic as a foreign language to a Cambridge syllabus are scarce in every Dubai community, so the choice within a twenty-minute drive is usually between a first-language Arabic teacher and nobody. Those are not the same product as a tutor who has taught 0544 to a series.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge International or Pearson, and operate no office or centre in the UAE. Private tutors working with UAE students need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. No tutor can promise a grade, and this page does not.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Arabic 0544 and 0508?
faqs.answer: They assess different students rather than different difficulty levels. 0544 is Arabic as a Foreign Language, for students acquiring Arabic as an additional language, and tests understanding, reading and writing at learner level with speaking in most syllabus versions. 0508 is Arabic as a First Language, for students schooled in Arabic, and asks for close reading of unseen passages and formal composition. A student entered for the wrong code produces work that looks like weak ability but is really a mismatch. Confirm which code your child is entered for and which components the series examines with the school.

faqs.question: Why has my non-Arab child been entered for 0544 rather than another language?
faqs.answer: Because Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and your child's school teaches the non-Arab group separately from the Arab group as KHDA requires. Once a student has studied Arabic as an additional language for years, entering them for the learner qualification at sixteen converts that time into something on the certificate. Some schools offer a European language as an alternative in the option block instead. If that choice is live for your family, the honest comparison is that Spanish or French is faster to read and Arabic is more useful where you live.

faqs.question: Can my child start 0544 in Year 10 with almost no Arabic?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it is demanding, and the deciding factor is script literacy rather than vocabulary. Eighteen months is enough to reach a solid learner standard if reading is practised daily from the first week: ten minutes of timed reading aloud, built on the specific letter pairs the student confuses. Vocabulary follows the finite topic list and is the easier half. What does not work is a plan that starts with word lists and discovers at the mock that the student decodes letter by letter, because reading speed is the one thing that cannot be compressed late.

faqs.question: How much of a 0544 grade actually depends on reading the Arabic script?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, and indirectly as well as directly. Reading passages obviously require decoding at speed, but written tasks also depend on reading the prompt accurately, and even listening questions have to be read before the audio starts. A student who reads letter by letter pays a time penalty in every component. That is why our plans open with a daily drill and record words per minute weekly: it is the single measurement that predicts a 0544 outcome better than any other, and it responds to frequency rather than to session length.

faqs.question: How do we practise Arabic listening at home in a way that resembles the paper?
faqs.answer: Match the conditions, not the content. Use recordings with unfamiliar voices, play them once or at most twice, have the questions read before the audio starts, and answer while listening rather than afterwards from memory. Rotate the type: bulletins, announcements, dialogues and recorded messages all move at different speeds. The trap in Dubai is that everyday exposure is cooperative, because people repeat, slow down and switch to English, while examination audio does none of that. Avoid practising only with the tutor's voice, which is a real risk in one-to-one tuition.

faqs.question: Does 0544 include a speaking test?
faqs.answer: Most Cambridge foreign-language syllabuses examine speaking, and the arrangement differs by syllabus version and by what the centre enters, so this is a question for your child's school and for the live syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org rather than for a tutoring page. We do not restate component structures that Cambridge revises. What we can say is how to prepare if it applies: a small bank of linking phrases, the habit of answering and then adding a reason unprompted, and practice handling a follow-up question, because a memorised script collapses the moment an examiner deviates from it.

faqs.question: Does a 0544 grade count towards the Ministry of Education's five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. For equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Count your five excluding Arabic. The grade is still a real qualification and supports continuation into Arabic B or A Level. Equivalency is run by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring service, so verify the current rule through its own channel.

faqs.question: Does sitting 0544 satisfy the school's mandatory Arabic requirement?
faqs.answer: They are two separate things worth keeping apart. Mandatory Arabic is a regulatory requirement on the school: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies must be taught in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for, with KHDA's instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The Cambridge entry is a qualification decision taken at sixteen. A student continues in school Arabic lessons whether or not they are entered for 0544, and a tutoring plan works alongside those lessons rather than replacing them.

faqs.question: Which variety of Arabic should my child learn for 0544?
faqs.answer: Modern Standard Arabic is the written and formal variety the examination works in, and it is what reading passages and written tasks require. Dialect is what your child hears in Dubai daily, and it helps with listening comprehension and confidence without earning marks on its own. The useful framing for a learner is that dialect is the language of the street and Standard Arabic is the language of the page, and 0544 assesses the page. A good tutor will use the student's existing dialect exposure as a bridge rather than pretending it does not exist.

faqs.question: How much work outside lessons does a 0544 student need each week?
faqs.answer: Ten minutes a day of timed reading aloud, plus one written task or vocabulary set per topic cycle. That is a smaller load than most subjects and it is non-negotiable, because reading speed responds to frequency rather than to volume. A student doing the daily drill with one weekly session will outpace a student doing two sessions a week and nothing in between. Any provider recommending four sessions a week on a learner language without a daily practice structure is selling hours rather than designing a plan.

faqs.question: Is 0544 easier or harder than French or Spanish IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The machinery is the same and the script changes the arithmetic. Topic-area vocabulary, listening under pressure and writing to a prompt work identically across Cambridge's language syllabuses, so a student who did well in French already owns the method. What French does not prepare anyone for is reading an unvowelled script with twenty-eight letters in four positional forms. For a learner starting from scratch, Arabic costs more reading hours. For a student living in Dubai, it is also the language they will go on hearing every day.

faqs.question: Can a 0544 grade lead to IB Arabic B in sixth form?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the placement decision belongs to the school. Arabic B assumes prior study and workable reading fluency, which a solid 0544 grade evidences, while ab initio is intended for genuine beginners and schools interpret eligibility differently. The new demand in either course is oral assessment, which 0544 prepares a student for only partly. The useful preparation in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is structuring a spoken response and speaking about a topic for several minutes, rather than more reading comprehension. Ask the IB coordinator in writing which course your child would enter.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge 0544 tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates collected in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and examination-year specialists at AED 200-450 or more, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table and independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is absorbed. Monthly online packages advertised in this market have been seen at AED 799 for eight sessions. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram's prices. 0544 is also a subject where one disciplined weekly session plus a daily drill beats a heavier and more expensive schedule.

faqs.question: My child speaks some Arabic but cannot read it at all. Which route fits?
faqs.answer: 0544 almost certainly, and the plan has to treat script literacy as the first project rather than assuming it. Spoken familiarity is genuinely useful: it carries listening comprehension and makes vocabulary stick faster than it would for a learner outside the region. What it does not do is transfer to reading, because recognising a spoken word and decoding it in unvowelled text are separate skills. Expect the first six to eight weeks to look like reading practice, with words per minute recorded, before the topic-area work takes its normal shape.

faqs.question: What if our school does not enter students for 0544 at all?
faqs.answer: Then the route is a private candidate entry through a Dubai examination centre that accepts them. The centre handles entry, invigilation and the zone timetable and charges its own fee directly to the family, and the teaching is arranged separately. Ask the centre three things before planning around it: whether it enters 0544, what its internal deadline is, and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in. The centre's own deadline sits earlier than Cambridge's, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss a paper after the wrong zone timetable was used.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-arabic-foreign-lan.closingBody: The quickest honest assessment of a Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language candidate takes about six minutes: have them read a short unvowelled passage aloud while somebody times it, and note which letter pairs they stumble over. That single measurement tells you more about a likely 0544 outcome than a conversation about how many years of Arabic they have had. Book the free trial lesson and that is what the tutor will do, before naming a reading speed, a confusion set and a realistic session count. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, around your child's school, centre and series.

intro.heading: What a Cambridge 0400 home tutor in Dubai actually costs, and what the number is made of
paragraphs: Market rates for one-to-one IGCSE support in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online for a qualified subject tutor, and roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour for a tutor who travels to the family. Those bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. What this page adds is the part the market does not explain: why Art and Design sits at the upper end of whichever band you are looking at, and which of the six Cambridge 0400 areas of study quietly costs a Dubai household the most to resource.

Art is priced differently because the billable hour is not where the work happens. A maths tutor can diagnose a weakness in twelve minutes of a past paper. A 0400 tutor has to read thirty or forty sketchbook spreads, decide which assessment objective each one is evidencing, and then write a page plan the candidate can actually make in the week available. A tutor who charges AED 200 and does that reading unpaid is subsidising the quote. A tutor who charges AED 320 and includes it is often the cheaper purchase across a term. The first question to ask any Dubai art tutor is therefore not the rate. It is what the rate covers between sessions.

The second cost driver is distance. Dubai is a long city. A tutor living in Al Barsha and teaching a candidate in Arabian Ranches absorbs forty to eighty minutes of driving into every visit, and that time is paid for whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice. It also narrows the choice of tutor to whoever happens to live within a sensible radius, which on a specialism as thin as Cambridge 0400 can mean a general art teacher rather than somebody who has read the syllabus against real candidate work. That trade is the reason IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai at all.

Lessons for Dubai families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. On a practical subject that surprises people, so the mechanics are worth stating: the candidate props the sketchbook under a phone or a document camera, the tutor sees the page at the size an examiner sees it, and annotation is drafted live in a shared document while the candidate talks through their own reasoning. Nothing is drawn for them. The portfolio stays entirely the candidate's own work, which is both an IB and a Cambridge requirement and a line this page will not blur.

What follows is built in the order a Dubai parent actually decides: the market rate by provider model, why art prices move, the drive costed as the line item it is, which area of study eats a materials budget, where marks go missing in a Dubai cohort, the entry calendar counted backwards from a Cambridge key-dates sheet, the academic-honesty boundary, and how to check that whoever teaches your child is permitted to charge for it under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.programmesIntro: Cambridge 0400 sits in the middle of a longer art route, and the cost of support changes depending on where a candidate joins it. These are the four stages Dubai families most often ask about, with what each one means for a tutoring budget in this emirate.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Art and Design
programmes.description: The years where observational drawing is either built or avoided. Candidates who arrive at 0400 without the habit of drawing from a real object in front of them spend Year 10 learning it under deadline pressure, which is the single most expensive catch-up in the subject. Support at this stage is cheap because it is short: a handful of hours on sighting, proportion and measured mark-making rather than a two-year programme.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run Cambridge Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and art is not among them, so there is no external marker on a candidate's drawing ability before the IGCSE option is chosen. Families here usually discover the gap at the Year 9 options evening. Asking the art department which of its Year 10 entrants it expects to need extra drawing time is a more useful question than asking for a predicted grade.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design (0400)
programmes.description: Two years of practical work assessed on gathering and research, development of ideas, organisation of visual form and control of media, ending in an externally set component worked under supervised conditions. Which combination of components a candidate sits is decided by the school at entry, not by the family, so the art department is the only reliable source for what your child is actually registered against. Check it in writing before buying tutoring hours.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres normally enter the June or November Cambridge series. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones, and Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a supervised practical component with a fixed window, that is not a clerical detail. Ask your Dubai school which zone it sits in and get the dates from the department rather than a general web search.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Art and Design (9479)
programmes.description: The continuation route for candidates who want a portfolio strong enough for a foundation course or a design degree. Expectations on independent research and on the volume of personal investigation rise sharply. A 0400 candidate who learned to annotate honestly at 15 arrives here able to work alone, which is the difference between a manageable A Level and an unmanageable one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum sixth forms vary widely in whether they offer 9479 at all, and some candidates move school at 16 to get it. Families weighing that move should ask the receiving school how many candidates it entered for the subject in the last series and what the department's studio access looks like outside timetabled lessons, since independent studio time is the resource art A Levels run short of.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Visual Arts
programmes.description: The alternative at 16 for candidates in Dubai's International Baccalaureate schools. The assessment model is different in kind: a comparative study, a process portfolio and a curated exhibition, with written analysis carrying real weight. A 0400 candidate who can write about why a decision was made, rather than what was made, transfers into this comfortably.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students account for about seven per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, and the 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools overall. That means more Dubai families will face the 0400-to-Visual-Arts decision at 16 than did two years ago, and the honest answer is that the written strand, not the practical one, decides whether the move works.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.subjectsIntro: Cambridge 0400 is taught through areas of study, and the one a candidate picks changes both the marks available and the household spend. These are the six Cambridge areas plus the four cross-cutting skills that decide the grade regardless of which area is chosen.

subjects.name: Painting and related media
subjects.description: The default choice in most Dubai departments, and the one where an unexamined palette costs the most. Sessions work on mixing a small number of pigments the candidate can actually control, on recording those mixing tests inside the sketchbook rather than on loose sheets, and on resisting the urge to over-finish a surface that was already working.

subjects.name: Printmaking
subjects.description: Generous on marks for development because every state and proof is evidence of a decision. The constraint in Dubai is press access: a candidate without school press time has to design for reduction lino or monoprint, which is still fully creditable. Planning the edition around available equipment is a tutoring conversation, not a compromise.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional studies
subjects.description: Strong for candidates who think in objects and punishing for candidates who photograph badly. Marks are lost when a resolved maquette is documented in a single flat shot. Sessions cover turntable documentation, scale indication and recording construction stages as they happen rather than reconstructing them afterwards.

subjects.name: Photography, digital and lens-based media
subjects.description: The area where Dubai candidates most often confuse quantity with investigation. A contact sheet of two hundred frames with no selection rationale evidences nothing. Work here centres on editing down, on stating in writing why one frame survived, and on showing the technical variable that was being tested in each run.

subjects.name: Graphic communication
subjects.description: Attractive to candidates who already use design software and risky for the same reason. Examiners want to see the hand-drawn thinking behind a digital outcome. Sessions insist on thumbnails, typographic sketching and a visible route from a rough to a resolved layout before any file is opened.

subjects.name: Textiles and fashion
subjects.description: The area with the heaviest consumables load and the richest sampling evidence. Dyeing and stitch tests photograph well and read clearly as development. The tutoring focus is keeping sample sizes small, labelling every test with what was changed, and designing a final piece that can be finished in the time the candidate actually has.

subjects.name: Observational drawing
subjects.description: The skill the assessment objectives keep returning to even when the final outcome is digital or constructed. Candidates who can draw what is in front of them score better on gathering and recording because their primary sources are genuinely theirs. Short, timed, repeated drawing is the cheapest intervention available in this subject.

subjects.name: Annotation and written support
subjects.description: Annotation that describes the image wastes space. Annotation that names the decision, the alternative rejected and the reason earns marks. Dubai candidates working in a second or third language often know exactly why they made a choice and cannot get it onto the page, which is a coachable problem rather than a language verdict.

subjects.name: Critical and contextual studies
subjects.description: Referencing an artist is not the same as using one. The credit sits in showing what was borrowed, tested and changed. Sessions work on reading one work closely instead of listing five, and on recording the specific technique a candidate tried because of it.

subjects.name: Portfolio sequencing and presentation
subjects.description: A portfolio marked out of order loses marks the candidate already earned. Pages need to show a route: source, test, decision, development, outcome. The last six weeks of a 0400 course are usually better spent sequencing and annotating existing work than starting anything new.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.regionsTitle: Where Dubai 0400 candidates find first-hand source material
dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.regionsIntro: The gathering and recording objective rewards primary sources the candidate collected themselves. Dubai is unusually well supplied with them, and which part of the city a family lives in changes what is reachable on a school night without an hour in traffic.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Alserkal Avenue sits here: a working cluster of independent galleries and studios in converted warehouses, open most afternoons and free to walk. It is the strongest primary-source destination in Dubai for a candidate who needs drawings made from real work rather than screenshots.

regions.name: Dubai Design District
regions.note: Purpose-built around design studios and seasonal exhibitions, with enough signage, typography and industrial detail at street level to fill a graphic communication sketchbook in a single visit. Useful for candidates whose outcome is digital and whose evidence of hand-drawn thinking is thin.

regions.name: Jaddaf Waterfront
regions.note: Home to the Jameel Arts Centre, which runs changing exhibitions and a sculpture garden. The garden matters for three-dimensional candidates, who can draw and photograph form in daylight from multiple angles rather than working from a catalogue image.

regions.name: Al Fahidi and Bur Dubai
regions.note: The historic district gives wind towers, coral-stone walls, carved doors and the abra crossing. Candidates working on texture, pattern or architectural form get primary material here that no stock library can supply, and the walk is short enough for a weekday afternoon.

regions.name: Jumeirah
regions.note: The Etihad Museum and the surrounding low-rise streets suit candidates working on documentary photography or on social and historical themes. Families here are typically close to several British-curriculum schools, so afternoon sessions can start by half past four.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: The densest school cluster in Dubai for IGCSE cohorts, which means heavy after-school traffic between four and six. Online sessions here usually settle at a later slot, and the fishing harbour at Umm Suqeim gives boats, nets and rope as drawing subjects.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Villa communities where studio space at home is usually not the constraint but distance is. A tutor driving in from Al Barsha or Jumeirah loses most of an hour each way, which is precisely the cost that online delivery removes from the quote.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Older established communities with a different school set and a long drive to the Al Quoz and d3 gallery clusters. Candidates here benefit from planning one substantial gathering trip per half term instead of several short ones, and from building the sketchbook around it.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend long-established British and American schools in this corridor, where art departments tend to be well staffed and option cohorts are large. A candidate here competes inside a strong internal group, so the useful question is which assessment objective the department under-weights rather than whether the teaching is sound.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Jumeirah Park and the Meadows
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where families often moved school once already, so candidates arrive at 0400 with portfolios begun under a different scheme of work. The first hour of support usually goes on auditing what exists against the Cambridge objectives before any new page is made.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Academic City and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Schools here draw from villa communities across the eastern side of the city, and candidates often have usable space at home for messier media. Studio access outside lesson time varies sharply between these centres, which changes what a realistic final outcome looks like.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.modesIntro: Art support is bought in different shapes depending on when a family starts and what the portfolio already contains. These are the three patterns Dubai 0400 households use most, each priced by the hour rather than by a package with hidden terms.

modes.title: Fortnightly portfolio audit
modes.description: A standing hour every second week through Years 10 and 11. The candidate uploads the fortnight's spreads beforehand, the tutor reads them against one assessment objective, and the session ends with a named list of pages to make next. This is the pattern that prevents a frantic final term, because evidence accumulates steadily instead of in one exhausted burst.

modes.title: Supervised-component rehearsal block
modes.description: A short, dense block of timed sessions in the weeks before the externally set component. The candidate works to the clock Cambridge allocates, with the tutor observing and then debriefing, so that the real supervised session is the second or third time the candidate has worked under that constraint rather than the first.

modes.title: Annotation and sequencing clinic
modes.description: Aimed at candidates whose practical work is stronger than their paperwork, which in Dubai is most of them. sections.heading: What a Cambridge 0400 home tutor costs in Dubai, by the kind of hour you are buying
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working one-to-one online with a Dubai family charges roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at market rates read in October 2026. A tutor who travels to the home charges roughly AED 180 to AED 500, and the top of that range is driven almost entirely by distance rather than by expertise. Specialist IGCSE, International Baccalaureate and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. These are published figures from providers and from a rate aggregator, not an IB Gram price list, and they are set out below with the source attached to each band so a parent can check them.

The spread inside a single band is wider than the gap between bands, and that is the part worth understanding before paying anybody. Two tutors can both quote AED 250 for Cambridge 0400 and sell completely different products. One arrives having read the week's sketchbook and leaves a written page plan. The other opens the call, asks what the candidate has been doing, and spends twenty minutes finding out. Across a ten-week term the first costs the same and produces roughly two extra sessions of actual teaching, because none of the hour goes on orientation.

The second thing the table cannot show is availability. Cambridge 0400 is a thin specialism everywhere, and in Dubai the pool of tutors who have read candidate portfolios against the assessment objectives is small. Restricting that pool further to people who live within a thirty-minute drive of your villa is how families end up with a capable general art teacher who has never seen a 0400 mark scheme applied. Removing the travel constraint is the single biggest expansion of choice available, which is the practical argument for video delivery on this subject.

IB Gram's own position on price is deliberately simple on a page full of other people's numbers: the first lesson is free, with no card details taken, and a rate is quoted only after a tutor has seen the portfolio and said how many hours the work actually needs. Quoting a figure for Cambridge 0400 before looking at the sketchbook is guesswork, and the guess is always in the seller's favour.

sections.heading: Why an art hour is priced differently from a maths hour
paragraphs: In a maths subject the evidence a tutor needs is already written down and already marked. A past paper arrives with a script, a mark scheme and a score, and a competent tutor can locate the weakness in the time it takes to read four questions. The diagnosis is nearly free, so the hourly rate pays almost entirely for teaching. Cambridge 0400 inverts that. The evidence is forty pages of practical work with no marks on it, no mark scheme applied, and no indication of which assessment objective each page was supposed to serve.

Somebody has to do that reading. A tutor who does it inside the billed hour spends a third of the session orienting and two-thirds teaching, which is why cheap art hours feel thin. A tutor who does it beforehand hands the whole hour back to the candidate but has to recover the preparation time somewhere, and the honest way to recover it is in the rate. This is the mechanism behind the apparent premium on art tutoring in Dubai, and it is also why the cheapest quoted figure is frequently the most expensive per useful minute.

There is a second, less obvious driver. Practical work is made before it is judged, so feedback has a shelf life. A page plan issued on a Tuesday is worth something if the candidate makes those pages that week and almost nothing a month later, by which time the work has gone somewhere else. Art support therefore has to be scheduled against the candidate's own making rhythm rather than dropped in before an exam, and sustained fortnightly contact over two years is usually a lower total spend than a panicked block of sessions in the final term.

The practical consequence for a Dubai budget is that the useful comparison is not AED per hour. It is AED per portfolio page that actually improved. A family paying AED 320 fortnightly for twenty months, with reading and a written plan included, typically spends less in total than one paying AED 180 weekly for the last two terms and then adding emergency sessions in the fortnight before the supervised component.

sections.heading: The drive, the studio and the hours nobody bills
paragraphs: A Dubai in-home tutoring rate contains a journey. Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches at five in the afternoon is not a short trip, and a tutor making that round trip for a single hour is committing closer to three hours of their working day. No tutor absorbs that indefinitely; it surfaces either as a higher hourly figure, a two-hour minimum booking, or a quietly declining willingness to keep the slot when something closer comes along. Families who are told the drive is free are being told something that cannot be true over a two-year course.

Art adds a second logistical cost that other subjects do not have. The work is physical, so either the tutor brings materials or the candidate's own setup has to be adequate. Wet media, printmaking and textiles all need surfaces, ventilation and somewhere a half-finished piece can be left undisturbed. In a Dubai apartment that is often the dining table, and a visiting tutor cannot change that. Online delivery does not solve the space problem either, but it does stop the family paying a travel premium for an hour that still happens at the dining table.

Set against those costs, video has two real drawbacks that are worth naming rather than glossed over. A tutor cannot physically turn a maquette in their hands, and a camera flattens surface quality, so decisions about texture and impasto need the candidate to describe what the tutor is looking at. Both are manageable with a second camera angle and with the habit of photographing work properly, which is a skill the candidate needs anyway because the examiner will also only ever see photographs of some of it.

Two of the rows favour a visit, and a family for whom studio supervision is the binding constraint should hire somebody local for that and use video for the marking and planning work, which is where most of the marks actually move.

sections.heading: Which 0400 area of study costs the most to resource in Dubai
paragraphs: Families budgeting for Cambridge 0400 usually budget for tutoring and forget the consumables, then discover in Year 11 that the area of study chosen in Year 10 carries a running cost. The spend is not evenly distributed. Textiles and printmaking consume physical material every time a test is run, three-dimensional studies consumes material and storage, and photography front-loads the cost into equipment the candidate may already own. Graphic communication is the cheapest to resource and the most likely to lose marks for thin hand-drawn development.

Dubai adds two local wrinkles. Specialist art supply is concentrated rather than ubiquitous, so a candidate who needs a particular paper weight or a specific dye is usually ordering it, and lead times matter when a deadline is three weeks away. The second is school equipment access. Press time, kilns and sewing equipment sit inside the department, and how much out-of-hours access a candidate gets varies enormously between Dubai centres. Two candidates following the same area of study at different schools can face completely different practical constraints.

None of this needs to change the area of study, and switching late is usually worse than working within a constraint. What it should change is the plan. A candidate with no press access designs a reduction lino or monoprint sequence and evidences the states, which is fully creditable. A candidate without kiln access builds in a material that air-dries and documents construction properly. A tutor's job on this is to make the constraint visible early and design around it, rather than letting a candidate discover in February that the final piece cannot be made.

sections.heading: Where 0400 marks go missing in a Dubai cohort, and what each fix costs in hours
paragraphs: The most common loss is on gathering and recording, and it is almost always the same failure: sources collected from a screen with no first-hand recording attached. A candidate pastes four images of an artist's work, writes a sentence underneath, and has evidenced nothing about their own investigation. The fix is cheap in hours and expensive in effort. One gathering trip to Alserkal Avenue or the Jameel Arts Centre, with dated photographs the candidate took and drawings made in front of the work, converts a weak objective into a strong one in a single weekend.

The second loss is development that is not development. Pages that repeat an idea at slightly different sizes read as output, not as exploration. Examiners are looking for a visible route: a source, a test, a decision, a change made because of the test. Dubai candidates working across three languages often make those decisions perfectly well and record none of them, which is why the annotation clinic is usually the highest-value short intervention available. Two or three hours on existing pages moves more marks than six hours of new making.

The third loss is the supervised component itself, where candidates run out of time because they have never worked to that clock. A candidate who has rehearsed the allocation twice paces differently from one meeting it cold. The fix is a short block of timed runs, with the tutor observing and then debriefing on what was abandoned too early, and it has to happen weeks before the window rather than in the final days when nothing can be changed.

The fourth, quietest loss is sequencing. A portfolio that contains the evidence but presents it out of order makes an examiner reconstruct the route, and reconstruction is where credit leaks. The last stretch of a 0400 course is usually better spent ordering and annotating what exists than beginning anything new. Parents who ask a tutor for extra making sessions in the final month are frequently buying the least productive hours in the whole programme.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines sit months before the paper: the 0400 year counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Dubai centres almost always enter June or November. The detail families miss is how early the administrative chain starts: final entries are submitted by the centre months before anybody sits anything, and once that entry is made the component combination and the tier are fixed.

Cambridge publishes a full key-dates sheet for its March series, and it is used here as the worked example precisely because it is the one Cambridge sets out end to end. For the March 2027 series the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results are released on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The shape of that timeline, not the specific dates, is what a Dubai parent should take from it: the entry decision precedes the examination by about ten weeks, and the certificate arrives nearly four months after it.

Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong timetable was used. For a supervised practical component with a fixed window this is the single most consequential administrative fact on this page. The only reliable source for your child's dates is the Dubai school's examinations officer, and the question to ask is which zone the centre sits in.

Working the calendar backwards is what turns a tutoring budget into a plan. If the supervised window is roughly ten weeks after final entries, then timed rehearsals belong about four to six weeks before the window, the portfolio audit belongs a term earlier, and the gathering trips belong in the first year. Families who buy support in that order spend less than families who buy it in reverse.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessment is a portfolio
paragraphs: Cambridge 0400 is assessed on work the candidate made, which makes the honesty boundary sharper here than in a written subject. A tutor may teach technique, demonstrate on their own separate sheet, ask questions about a decision, point at an assessment objective and say the evidence for it is missing, and mark a page the way an examiner would. A tutor may not draw, paint, cut, stitch or retouch anything that will be submitted, and may not dictate annotation for the candidate to copy down.

The grey area families ask about most is annotation, because a candidate writing in a second language often cannot express a decision they made perfectly well. The workable line is that the thinking must be the candidate's and spoken first. A tutor can ask what the candidate was testing, listen to the answer, and then help tighten the sentence that captures it. A tutor who supplies the sentence has supplied the thinking, and an examiner reading a portfolio where every annotation sounds like an adult can tell.

The second grey area is the supervised component, and there is no grey in it. Work produced under supervised conditions has no tutor involvement at all, before or during. Preparation happens on the preparatory material in the weeks beforehand, and then the tutor steps away. Any provider offering to help with the supervised piece itself is offering something that would put the candidate's entry at risk, and a parent should treat that offer as disqualifying.

This is also the line that separates honest tutoring from the essay-and-portfolio mills that advertise in this market. Some of them sell finished coursework outright. IB Gram does not supply assessed work in any subject, does not sell portfolio pages, and does not reproduce or distribute Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those sit on cambridgeinternational.org and should be read there, through the school, which is where the authoritative version lives.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and checking who is teaching your child
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source. What a parent can do is ask directly whether the person teaching their child holds the permit, and treat an evasive answer as information. The permit is free and takes two working days, so there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one.

Two further points matter in Dubai specifically. An operation with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different instrument issued to a physical centre; no individual tutor and no online platform should describe themselves as holding it. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carrying a similar restriction. Hiring your child's own class teacher privately is not the shortcut it appears to be.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it operates no office or centre in the UAE. Any provider claiming regulator endorsement for tutoring should be asked to produce the permit number, because the permits that exist are issued for specific things and none of them means what that phrase implies.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor and the lesson happens over live video
paragraphs: The phrase in this page's address is the phrase Dubai parents type, and it is worth targeting honestly rather than pretending it means something else. What a family usually means by a home tutor is one-to-one attention on their own child's work, at a time that fits around school and traffic, without a group class. Every part of that is deliverable over video. The part that is not deliverable is somebody physically arriving, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service run only in India.

Saying so plainly is more useful than the alternative, which is a page that implies a visit and a phone call that quietly explains otherwise. It also allows an honest account of what each format is good for. A visiting tutor can hold a maquette, supervise a wet process and sit with a reluctant fifteen-year-old in a way a screen cannot. An online specialist can be the right person for Cambridge 0400 rather than the nearest person, can read the sketchbook before the hour starts, and can hold the slot when Sheikh Zayed Road does not cooperate.

In practice the sessions look like this. The candidate sets a phone or a document camera over the open sketchbook, so the tutor sees the spread at roughly the size and angle an examiner sees it. Pages are uploaded in advance where possible, so the hour starts with a judgement rather than a search. Annotation is drafted live in a shared document while the candidate talks, and the tutor types what the candidate says rather than what the tutor thinks. A written page plan follows within a day, naming what to make before the next session.

Scheduling is built around the Dubai week. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, start late enough to clear the school run in Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, and move to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan, when studio work at home realistically happens after nine in the evening. Families who travel over the long summer keep the same tutor and the same slot from wherever they are, which on a two-year portfolio course is worth more than it sounds.

process.title: Tell us what the school has entered
process.description: The first useful fact is not the grade target but the registration: which area of study, which component combination, which Cambridge series, and which administrative zone the centre sits in. Ask the art department in writing. Everything in a sensible plan follows from those four answers, and guessing at them wastes paid hours.

process.title: Send the portfolio as it stands
process.description: Photographs or scans of the sketchbook as it is now, including the pages the candidate is embarrassed by, because those are usually the diagnostic ones. A tutor reads the spreads against the assessment objectives before the trial lesson, which is what makes the free hour a diagnosis rather than an introduction.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One hour, no card details, with the sketchbook open on camera. The candidate talks through two or three spreads and the tutor marks them aloud the way an examiner would. By the end both of you know which objective is weakest and whether this particular tutor is somebody your child will actually talk to.

process.title: Get the hours quoted after the diagnosis, not before
process.description: A rate and an honest number of hours are proposed once the portfolio has been seen. A candidate needing annotation and sequencing work needs a handful of hours. A candidate in Year 10 with no first-hand sources needs a fortnightly slot for a year. The two plans should not cost the same.

process.title: Work the calendar backwards
process.description: Gathering trips in the first year, portfolio audits through the course, annotation and sequencing a term out, timed rehearsals four to six weeks before the supervised window. Buying support in that order costs less than buying it in reverse, and the final month is spent ordering evidence rather than making new pages.

process.title: Say so if the match is wrong
process.description: Tell us after one session rather than after six. Art tutoring depends on a candidate being willing to show unfinished work to somebody, and that either happens in the first hour or it does not. A different tutor is arranged without an argument, and no family is asked to justify the request.

whyPoints.description: Cambridge Art and Design is a thin specialism, and choosing a tutor by driving distance across Dubai narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby. Delivering over video means the match is made on whether somebody has read 0400 portfolios against the assessment objectives, which is the thing that actually moves a grade.

whyPoints.description: Pages are uploaded in advance and marked against one assessment objective, so the session opens with a judgement instead of a scroll. On a subject where the evidence is forty unmarked spreads, this is the difference between an hour of teaching and twenty minutes of orientation followed by forty of catching up.

whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, demonstrates separately, questions and marks. No page that will be submitted is drawn, finished or retouched by a tutor, no annotation is dictated for copying, and there is no involvement in the supervised component at all. Providers in this market sell finished coursework; that route puts a candidate's entry at risk.

Sessions follow a family that travels over the summer, which on a two-year portfolio course prevents the long gap that usually costs a candidate their gathering evidence.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400 home tutor charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor working online with a Dubai family at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and a tutor who travels to the home at roughly AED 180 to AED 500. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors sit between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with examiner-tier providers publishing higher. Those are published market figures from providers and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, not an IB Gram price list. Our own first lesson is free, and a rate is proposed only after a tutor has read the portfolio and said how many hours the work needs.

faqs.question: Why does an art tutor in Dubai quote more per hour than a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the diagnosis is not free. A maths tutor can find a weakness in four questions of a marked past paper. A 0400 tutor has to read thirty or forty unmarked sketchbook spreads, decide which assessment objective each one evidences, and write a page plan the candidate can make that week. A tutor who does that reading inside the billed hour gives you a thinner lesson. A tutor who does it beforehand has to recover the time in the rate. The apparent premium is usually the preparation being paid for honestly rather than hidden.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate normally cover a tutor reading the sketchbook between sessions?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is the question worth asking before agreeing any figure in Dubai. Ask directly whether pages can be uploaded in advance, whether they will be read before the session, and whether a written plan follows afterwards. A rate of AED 320 including all three is frequently cheaper per useful minute than AED 180 where the hour starts with the tutor seeing the work for the first time. Get the answer in writing, because the difference across a ten-week term is roughly two extra sessions of actual teaching.

faqs.question: What does a tutor's drive across Dubai add to an in-home art rate?
faqs.answer: Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches at five in the afternoon commits a tutor to close to three hours for one billed hour. That surfaces as a higher rate, a two-hour minimum, or a slot that quietly becomes unreliable when something closer appears. The market in-home band of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 contains that journey whether or not it is itemised. It also shrinks your choice of tutor to whoever lives within a sensible radius, which on a specialism as narrow as Cambridge 0400 is the more expensive consequence of the two.

faqs.question: Is a group art class in Dubai cheaper than one-to-one 0400 support?
faqs.answer: Per hour, almost always. Per useful minute on your child's portfolio, usually not. Cambridge 0400 is assessed on an individual body of work with its own sources, its own development route and its own final outcome, so there is very little a group session can address at once beyond general technique. Group teaching works well for a demonstrated process such as a printing method or a dyeing technique. It works poorly for the marking, annotation and sequencing work where most of the recoverable marks sit, because that is page-by-page and candidate-specific.

faqs.question: How many hours of 0400 support does a Year 11 candidate in Dubai usually buy?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the portfolio already contains, which is why a figure quoted before anybody has seen it is guesswork. A candidate whose practical work is strong and whose paperwork is thin may need a handful of hours on annotation and sequencing. A candidate entering Year 11 with no first-hand sources and no development route needs a fortnightly slot for most of the year, plus timed rehearsals before the supervised window. The honest answer after a free diagnostic hour is a range with a reason attached, not a package.

faqs.question: What do the materials for 0400 cost a Dubai family over the two years?
faqs.answer: No reliable sourced figure exists for Dubai, so none is published here. What can be said is where the spend concentrates: textiles and printmaking consume material with every test, three-dimensional work consumes material and storage, photography front-loads into equipment, and graphic communication is the cheapest to resource. Specialist supply in Dubai is concentrated rather than ubiquitous, so a particular paper weight or dye often has to be ordered with a lead time. Plan material purchases against the deadline, not against the week the idea arrives.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us which Cambridge 0400 area of study is cheapest to resource?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more usefully which one fits the access your child actually has. Press time, kilns and sewing equipment sit inside the school department, and out-of-hours access varies sharply between Dubai centres. A candidate without press access can design a reduction lino or monoprint sequence by hand and evidence every state, which is fully creditable. A candidate without kiln access builds in an air-drying material and documents construction stage by stage. The job is to make the constraint visible in Year 10 rather than in February of Year 11.

faqs.question: Did Dubai private school fees change for 2026-27, and does that affect a tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting tutoring, that matters as context rather than as a saving: the school line is flat, so a tutoring decision is not competing with a fee rise this year. Dubai's private sector also adds seven new schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 places, which over time affects the availability of art specialists more than it affects price.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in a Dubai art tutor's quoted hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for the answer in writing. The UAE tax treatment of tuition is not something this page states as fact, because no Federal Tax Authority citation has been read for it. What a parent can insist on is clarity about the figure they will actually pay: whether the quote is inclusive or exclusive, whether an invoice will be issued, and whether a tax registration number appears on it. A provider unwilling to be specific about the final number is telling you something about the rest of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Does a 0400 tutor working with a Dubai family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE app, website and e-services with a stated two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts have been published.

faqs.question: How does Cambridge 0400 sit against the five-subject rule for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Art and Design is a subject like any other for that count. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before relying on it; IB Gram does not perform equivalency and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor photograph or digitise the portfolio for us instead?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach your child how to do it properly and should, because the examiner will only ever see photographs of some of the work. Flat lighting, a square-on angle, scale indication for three-dimensional pieces and turntable sequences for constructed work are all coachable in a single session. What a tutor will not do is handle, retouch or edit anything that will be submitted. Documenting the portfolio is part of the candidate's own practice, and in a subject assessed on their work that distinction is not negotiable.

faqs.question: Our search was for a home tutor in Dubai, so where does the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: Over live video, one-to-one, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. The candidate sets a phone or document camera over the open sketchbook so the tutor sees each spread at roughly examiner scale, pages are uploaded in advance where possible, annotation is drafted live in a shared document in the candidate's own words, and a written page plan follows within a day. The trade is a 0400 specialist instead of the nearest available art teacher.

faqs.question: Can 0400 sessions move later in the evening during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a practical subject that flexibility matters more than usual. Studio work at home during Ramadan realistically happens after Iftar, so sessions shift to post-Iftar slots and the page plans issued in those weeks are shorter and more specific. The same applies to the long Dubai summer: families who travel keep the same tutor and the same slot from wherever they are, which prevents the two-month gap that otherwise costs a candidate the gathering evidence they were meant to collect.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then the number
dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.closingBody: The useful sequence for a Dubai family looking at Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400 support is narrow: find out in writing what the school has entered, send the sketchbook as it stands, take the free trial hour with the pages open on camera, and get a quote and an honest number of hours only after somebody has read the work against the assessment objectives. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no tutor sent to a UAE address. The AED figures on this page belong to the market and are attributed; ours are quoted after the diagnosis, because a price set before the portfolio has been seen is a guess made in the seller's favour.
