intro.heading: How a Cambridge 0400 portfolio is actually taught through a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online art tutoring is that art is physical. It is, and a camera cannot hold a maquette or feel the tooth of a paper. What a camera does unusually well is the other half of the subject: looking carefully at a finished page and deciding what it evidences. That is also the half where Cambridge 0400 grades are won and lost, because the examiner who marks your child's portfolio will never touch most of it either. They will look at it, read the annotation, and decide which assessment objective each spread serves.

So the session is built around looking. The candidate props a phone or a document camera over the open sketchbook, angled square to the page rather than over a shoulder, and the tutor sees the spread at roughly the scale and flatness an examiner sees it. Where pages are uploaded the night before, the tutor has already read them and the hour opens with a verdict rather than a search. On a subject where the evidence is thirty or forty unmarked spreads, that single logistical habit is worth more than any amount of enthusiasm.

The second thing a screen changes for the better is who teaches your child. Cambridge Art and Design is a narrow specialism. Restricting the search to tutors willing to drive to a Dubai villa on a weekday evening leaves a pool of general art teachers, some of whom have never applied a 0400 mark scheme to real candidate work. Removing the drive widens the pool to people who have. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and this page would rather explain the trade than disguise it.

Price is the other question families arrive with. The Dubai market for one-to-one online subject tutoring runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, read from published provider pages and a rate aggregator in October 2026. Those are market figures, attributed in the tables below, not an IB Gram price list. What the tables add is the part the market never explains: what a given hour is actually spent on, and which 0400 objective returns the most marks per hour of work.

The rest of this page covers the four assessment objectives and what each one punishes, where the recoverable marks sit, the equipment a Dubai household genuinely needs, how a practical option survives a timetable that already includes KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, the November and private candidate routes, annotation in a second language, and the choice between 0400 and IB Visual Arts at sixteen. It ends by stating plainly why the honest label for this service is online tutor.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.programmesIntro: Art sits inside a longer route, and the question a Dubai family is really asking at each stage is whether the practical strand is still worth the timetable it occupies. These are the four stages, with what each demands of a candidate.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Arts
programmes.description: Assessed on four criteria rather than four objectives, with a heavier emphasis on reflection and process than most British-curriculum art teaching at the same age. Candidates arriving in Cambridge 0400 from an MYP arts cohort usually write about their work more fluently than their peers and have less experience of sustained observational drawing. The transition work is therefore drawing, not thinking.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students make up about seven per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, and a number of Dubai families move between an MYP school and a British-curriculum one at fourteen. A candidate joining 0400 mid-route should have their existing arts folder audited against the Cambridge objectives before new pages are made, because the strongest MYP evidence is often filed in a way Cambridge marking does not read.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design (0400)
programmes.description: A practical qualification assessed across four objectives: gathering and investigation, exploration and development, organisation of visual form, and selection and control of media. Candidates build preparatory work and then produce an outcome under supervised conditions. The component combination is chosen by the centre at entry, so a parent cannot look it up and must ask the art department in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres normally enter the June or November Cambridge series. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. With a supervised practical window that is a live risk rather than paperwork, so the examinations officer at your Dubai school is the only source worth trusting for dates.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Art and Design (9479)
programmes.description: Independent personal investigation at a scale 0400 only hints at, with a written element that carries real weight. Candidates who learned at fifteen to record why a decision was made, rather than what was produced, find the step manageable. Candidates who learned to make attractive pages without reasoning find it brutal, and the gap usually shows in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai sixth form offers 9479, and some candidates change school at sixteen to continue the subject. Families weighing that should ask the receiving department how many candidates it entered in the last series and what studio access looks like outside lessons, since independent studio time is the resource art A Levels most often run short of in this city.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Visual Arts
programmes.description: Three assessed strands: a comparative study, a process portfolio and a curated exhibition. The written and curatorial demands are substantially higher than at 0400, and the exhibition asks a candidate to make selection and installation decisions nobody asked them to make before. Strong practical ability alone does not carry a Visual Arts grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, so more families here will face the choice at sixteen than two years ago. The deciding factor is rarely the practical work. It is whether the candidate can write analytically about somebody else's art without summarising a biography.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.subjectsIntro: What a 0400 session actually works on is a skill, not a topic. These are the ten that come up most in Dubai portfolios, each with what the camera can and cannot do for it.

subjects.name: Measured observational drawing
subjects.description: Sighting, proportion and relative measurement, practised in short repeated runs rather than one long sitting. A camera shows the drawing and the object together, so a tutor can see exactly where the proportion went wrong instead of guessing. This is the cheapest and most transferable intervention in the subject.

subjects.name: Controlled colour mixing
subjects.description: Working from a deliberately small palette the candidate can predict, and recording the mixing tests as evidence rather than hiding them. Screens shift colour, so the tutor describes the target in terms of a relationship between two mixes on the candidate's own sheet, which is more rigorous than matching a swatch anyway.

subjects.name: Reduction lino and monoprint
subjects.description: A route for candidates with no school press access, and generous on marks because every state and proof is a visible decision. The tutor reviews the cut between states and the candidate photographs each pull. The constraint produces better development evidence than a single clean edition ever does.

subjects.name: Screen and stencil processes
subjects.levels: Planned remotely, executed in the department
subjects.description: Separation planning, registration and edition sequencing are all paper exercises that work perfectly over video. The physical pulling happens in the school studio. Candidates who plan the separations properly waste far less department time, which matters where press and screen access is rationed.

subjects.name: Maquette construction and documentation
subjects.levels: The hardest thing to teach through a screen
subjects.description: A tutor cannot turn the object, so the candidate learns to document it: turntable sequences, consistent lighting, a scale reference in shot, and construction stages photographed as they happen. That skill is required regardless of tutoring format, because the examiner also works from photographs of some of it.

subjects.name: Dye and stitch sampling
subjects.description: Textiles evidence reads beautifully when samples are small, labelled and each test changes only one thing. The usual failure is a large sample that changes three variables and proves nothing. Reviewing samples on camera is straightforward; the tutoring work is keeping the sampling disciplined and the material consumption sane.

subjects.name: Lens-based editing judgement
subjects.description: A contact sheet of two hundred frames with no selection rationale evidences nothing. Sessions work on stating the technical variable being tested in each run and then on cutting hard, writing down why one frame survived. Screen sharing makes this one of the strongest online formats in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Typographic and thumbnail sketching
subjects.levels: Hand work behind a digital outcome
subjects.description: Graphic communication candidates lose marks because the visible development is a sequence of saved files. Thumbnails, letterform sketching and rough layout sheets put the thinking back on paper. The tutor marks the sheets; the software work the candidate does alone.

subjects.name: Annotation that names the decision
subjects.description: Annotation describing the image wastes the space. Annotation naming the decision, the rejected alternative and the reason earns credit. The method is to ask, listen, and then help tighten the candidate's own sentence, which is a conversation that works better typed in a shared document than spoken across a table.

subjects.name: Portfolio sequencing
subjects.description: Evidence out of order forces an examiner to reconstruct the route, and credit leaks during reconstruction. Mapping the order — source, test, decision, development, outcome — is a single session with a clear output, and it is usually the highest-value hour in the final term.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the slot that actually works there
dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.regionsIntro: Online delivery removes the drive but not the school run, the prayer times or the three-hour homework block. These are the communities Dubai 0400 families most often book from, with the scheduling reality in each.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment living, so wet and messy media usually happen in the school studio and the home session is critique, annotation and planning. Evening slots after seven work best here; the five-to-six window disappears into building lifts and parking.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: A similar tower profile to the Marina with a slightly younger cohort and a heavy tutoring market already operating from the same buildings. Families here frequently compare an online specialist against a centre two floors down, which is a genuine choice rather than a false one.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Short school commutes but long parental working days, so sessions are often booked for after eight in the evening. Candidates here are close to Dubai Design District and to the Opera district, which makes a weekday gathering trip realistic without a long drive.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Villa and low-rise communities with reasonable space for drying work, and a school set spread across Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park. The commute home is long enough that a half past five start is usually optimistic.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: A dense mixed community with one of the fastest-growing school-age populations in the city and a shortage of specialist option teaching nearby. The practical consequence is that families here benefit most from a format that does not depend on who lives close by.

sections.heading: The four Cambridge 0400 assessment objectives and what each one punishes
paragraphs: Cambridge 0400 is marked across four objectives: gathering, recording, research and investigation; exploration and development of ideas; organisation and relationships of visual and other forms; and selection and control of materials, media and processes. Candidates and parents usually know the list exists and have never seen it applied to a real page. Confirm the current weightings on cambridgeinternational.org or through the art department, because they are set by the syllabus version a centre is teaching and are not something this page should restate.

Each objective has a characteristic failure, and they are easy to spot once you know what to look for. Gathering fails when sources came off a screen with no first-hand recording attached. Exploration fails when pages repeat an idea at different sizes instead of changing it in response to a test. Organisation fails when a composition was never considered as a composition. Control of media fails when a candidate attempts a technique they have not practised, usually on the final piece, usually in the last fortnight.

What makes this diagnosable rather than vague is that each failure has a specific remedy with a known cost in hours. A dated gathering trip with drawings made in front of the work fixes the first. Annotating existing pages to name the decision behind each fixes the second. A single session on thumbnail composition fixes the third. Short repeated media tests, recorded, fix the fourth. None of those remedies involves making a new final piece, which is what most families instinctively buy.

A tutor who names the objective at the start of the hour is doing something the department often cannot, because a class teacher with twenty-five candidates marks holistically out of necessity. One-to-one time is the only realistic place to go objective by objective through a specific portfolio, and it is the whole reason this format is worth paying for on a practical subject.

sections.heading: What each Dubai price band actually buys in a 0400 hour
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai span an order of magnitude. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 to AED 65 on EdFlik's own listing and AED 33 to AED 52 on Tutopiya's, a qualified subject tutor runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300 with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and examiner-tier providers such as BartyED publish AED 650. All of those were read in October 2026, and all of them belong to the provider named, not to IB Gram.

What the bands do not tell you is what happens to the hour. At the bottom, the hour is live help with whatever the candidate is doing at that moment, which can be perfectly useful for a technique demonstration and is close to worthless for objective-by-objective portfolio marking, because nobody has read the portfolio. In the middle, the hour usually includes some reading and a short note. At the top, preparation, written feedback and criteria-referenced marking are assumed, and the scarcity is in availability rather than in competence.

For Cambridge 0400 the decision is not which band to buy but which band to buy for which job. A technique the candidate has never tried can be demonstrated by a competent generalist. A sketchbook audit against four objectives cannot, because it requires somebody who has applied the criteria to real candidate work. Families who split their spend this way — a cheap demonstration hour where a demonstration is what is needed, a specialist hour where judgement is what is needed — consistently get more out of the same total budget.

IB Gram's own approach is to quote after the diagnosis rather than before it. The first lesson is free, with no card details, and the sketchbook is open on camera for it. A rate and a realistic number of hours follow once somebody has seen the work. Any figure offered before the portfolio has been seen is a guess, and the guess is always in the seller's favour.

sections.heading: Equipment a Dubai household genuinely needs, and what it does not
paragraphs: The equipment question is usually answered by somebody selling equipment, so here is the short version: a phone made in the last five years, something to hold it steady above the page, a lamp, and a reliable connection. That is the whole list. A document camera is a convenience rather than a requirement, and a graphics tablet contributes nothing to a 0400 portfolio that is going to be submitted as physical work. Money spent on gear is money not spent on hours, and hours are what move objectives.

What does matter is how the phone is used. The camera must look square down at the page, not across it at an angle, because an angled view distorts proportion and a tutor then corrects a drawing error the candidate never made. A lamp to one side rather than overhead keeps the page readable without a hot spot. For constructed work the candidate turns the object while the camera stays still, which is also exactly how the documentation for the portfolio should be made.

A second camera angle is the one genuine upgrade, and a second phone on a stand does the job. It lets a tutor see the page and the candidate's hand at the same time, which matters when the thing being corrected is how a tool is being held rather than what is on the paper. Families already own two phones; nothing needs to be bought. Bandwidth is rarely the limitation in Dubai, but a candidate working from a tower apartment on a shared connection should test the setup once before a paid session rather than during it.

The things that do not help are worth naming too, because they get recommended constantly. Tracing aids, projectors and photo-to-drawing apps all produce pages that read as mechanical to an examiner and undermine the gathering objective they were bought to serve. Expensive paper on which a candidate is afraid to make a mark is worse than cheap paper covered in tests. The table below separates the two lists.

sections.heading: Fitting a practical option around Dubai's mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires those subjects regardless of which curriculum the school runs. The requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Year 10 candidate carrying a practical option, this is the timetable arithmetic that decides whether the portfolio gets made.

The detail matters. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. The practical effect is a timetable with limited slack.

Art loses in that arithmetic more often than other subjects, because its homework is not a task that can be finished in an hour at a desk. A candidate with four hours a week of mandatory subjects, a full option block and a commute from Al Furjan to Jebel Ali does not have an easy evening in which to build a maquette. Pretending otherwise produces a portfolio made entirely in two desperate bursts, which is exactly what the development objective is designed to detect.

The planning answer is to make the portfolio in small, scheduled pieces and to protect one longer weekend block per half term for anything wet, constructed or gathered. A fortnightly tutoring slot suits that rhythm better than a weekly one, because the week between sessions is when the pages are actually made. Families who book weekly and then cancel half the sessions would have done better booking fortnightly and keeping all of them.

sections.heading: November entries, resits and sitting Cambridge as a private candidate in Dubai
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, so a Dubai candidate who needs another attempt does not wait a full year. What families underestimate is the lead time. The entry decision precedes the examination by a long way, and once the centre has submitted it the component combination is fixed. Cambridge's published key dates for its March series show the shape clearly: final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

For a practical subject a resit is a bigger undertaking than in a written one, because the portfolio evidence has to be rebuilt rather than revised. A candidate resitting Art and Design is not re-reading notes; they are producing fresh preparatory work and sitting a new supervised component. That is a term of making, not a fortnight of revision, and it is the reason a resit decision in this subject should be taken as early as the results allow rather than left to drift.

Private candidate entry is a separate question and a Dubai-specific one, because not every school accepts external candidates and the ones that do set their own conditions. A practical subject is harder still, since the supervised component requires space, invigilation and in some cases equipment. A family considering this route should contact centres directly about whether they accept private candidates for 0400 specifically, well before the entry deadline, and should expect the answer to be more restrictive than for written subjects.

Whatever route is taken, the zone timetable matters. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination as a result of using the wrong one. Get the dates from the examinations officer. Not from a forum, and not from a general search.

sections.heading: Annotation in a second or third language, without writing it for them
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai 0400 candidates are working in their second or third language, and the most common consequence is annotation that understates the thinking behind the page. The candidate knows precisely why they abandoned one colour relationship for another and writes a sentence that says the colours are nice. An examiner cannot award credit for reasoning that is not on the page, so the marks go missing even though the decision was made properly.

The method that works and stays honest is to make the candidate say it first. A tutor asks what was being tested, what the alternative was and why it lost, and listens to the answer in whatever form it arrives. Then the two of them tighten the candidate's own sentence together, typed in a shared document while the candidate watches the words change. The thinking stays theirs. The expression improves. An examiner reading a portfolio where every annotation sounds like an adult wrote it can tell, and that suspicion costs more than clumsy English ever does.

What a tutor will not do is supply the sentence. Dictating annotation for a candidate to copy is supplying the thinking, which crosses the line that Cambridge and the IB both draw around assessed work. IB Gram does not produce assessed work in any subject, does not sell portfolio pages or coursework, and does not reproduce or distribute Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those live on cambridgeinternational.org and are properly accessed through the school.

There is a practical by-product worth mentioning. Candidates who practise articulating decisions out loud through Year 10 write much faster in Year 11, and they also perform better in the supervised component, because they have rehearsed making a decision and defending it under time pressure. The annotation work is not a presentational tidy-up. It is the thinking strand of the subject, which is why it belongs in the sessions rather than at the end of them.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0400 or IB Visual Arts at sixteen: how Dubai families should decide
paragraphs: Dubai is one of the few cities where this is a real choice rather than a theoretical one, because the city holds both a dominant British-curriculum sector and a growing International Baccalaureate one. KHDA's figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with UK schools taking the largest share of enrolment and International Baccalaureate schools about seven per cent. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate.

The practical difference at sixteen is not the amount of making. It is the amount of writing and curating. Cambridge AS and A Level Art and Design asks for a sustained personal investigation with a written element. IB Visual Arts asks for three distinct things: a comparative study of other artists' work, a process portfolio showing experimentation, and a curated exhibition the candidate selects and explains. A candidate who can make but cannot analyse somebody else's work will struggle more with Visual Arts than with the Cambridge route.

The second difference is breadth of commitment. Visual Arts sits inside a full Diploma with five other subjects, an extended essay and theory of knowledge, so the time available for studio work is bounded by a structure the candidate cannot adjust. A Cambridge sixth former taking three or four subjects can, in practice, give art more hours. Families whose child wants a portfolio for a foundation course or a design degree should weigh that honestly against the breadth the Diploma offers.

A 0400 tutor is well placed to advise on this because they have seen the candidate's actual evidence rather than a predicted grade. The signal to look for is the annotation. A candidate whose annotation names decisions and engages with other artists' work is ready for the Visual Arts comparative study. A candidate whose strength is entirely in the making is better served by the route that rewards making, and there is nothing second-rate about choosing it.

sections.heading: Why online tutor is the honest label for this service
paragraphs: This page is titled the way it is because that is what it is. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send anybody to a UAE address, and home visits are a service it runs only in India. Many pages in this market imply a visit in the title and explain otherwise on a phone call, and a family that has already paid a deposit by then has been handled rather than informed.

Being direct about it also allows an honest account of the limits. A screen cannot hold a maquette, supervise a wet process, or sit next to a reluctant fifteen-year-old and simply be present until they start working. Those are real advantages of a person in the room, and a family for whom the binding problem is motivation rather than marks should weigh them seriously. What this format offers instead is the right specialist rather than the nearest one, portfolio reading done before the hour starts, and a slot that survives traffic.

There is also a regulatory reason to be precise about what is being sold. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, with the MoHRE private tuition work permit granted free of charge for two years and applied for through the MoHRE app, website and e-services. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre.

What is left after all that honesty is a specific, checkable offer. A free first hour with the sketchbook on camera. Marking against one named objective at a time. Annotation typed from the candidate's own words. A written page plan after every session. No assessed work produced by anybody but the candidate, and no grade promised by anybody at all.

process.title: Confirm the entry in writing
process.description: Ask the art department which area of study, which component combination, which Cambridge series and which administrative zone the centre sits in. A parent cannot look any of that up, and every sensible plan depends on all four. Buying hours before these answers arrive wastes the first two of them.

process.title: Upload the sketchbook as it is
process.description: Photographs or scans of every spread, including the ones the candidate would rather hide, because those are the diagnostic pages. Square-on shots with a side lamp are enough. The tutor reads the whole thing before the trial lesson, which is what makes the free hour a diagnosis rather than an introduction.

process.title: Test the camera setup once, unpaid
process.description: Five minutes with a phone on a stack of books, a lamp to one side and the sketchbook open. Fixing an angled view or a hot spot before a paid session is the difference between an hour of marking and an hour of adjusting furniture. Most families get it right on the first attempt.

process.title: Take the free first lesson
process.description: One hour, no card details, pages open on camera. The tutor marks two or three spreads aloud against a named objective while the candidate listens and argues back. By the end you know which objective is weakest and whether your child will actually show unfinished work to this particular person.

process.title: Split the budget by job
process.description: A technique the candidate has never tried needs a demonstration hour. A portfolio audit against four objectives needs a specialist. Spending the same total across those two jobs deliberately produces more than spending it all at one band, and a tutor should tell you which hour you are buying.

process.title: Book fortnightly and keep it
process.description: The week between sessions is when pages get made, so a fortnightly slot that is never cancelled beats a weekly one that is cancelled half the time. Timed preparation for the supervised component is added four to six weeks ahead of the window, not in the final days.

whyPoints.title: Objective-by-objective marking, not general encouragement
whyPoints.description: Each session names one of the four Cambridge 0400 objectives and works through the portfolio against it. A class teacher with twenty-five candidates marks holistically because there is no alternative. One-to-one time is the only realistic place to do this properly, and it is the reason the format earns its rate.

whyPoints.title: The portfolio is read before the hour begins
whyPoints.description: Spreads uploaded the night before are marked in advance, so the session opens with a verdict instead of a scroll. On a subject whose evidence is forty unmarked pages, that habit converts roughly a third of every session from orientation into teaching.

whyPoints.title: Specialist rather than nearest
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Art and Design is a narrow specialism and a drive-time radius across Dubai is a poor filter for it. Delivering over video means the match is made on whether somebody has applied a 0400 mark scheme to real candidate portfolios, which is what actually changes an objective score.

whyPoints.title: Prices attributed, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider or aggregator that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A hard boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Nothing that will be submitted is drawn, finished, retouched or dictated by a tutor, and there is no involvement in the supervised component. Annotation is typed from the candidate's own spoken reasoning. Providers in this market sell completed coursework; that route risks the candidate's entry.

whyPoints.title: Stated clearly: what IB Gram is not
whyPoints.description: An independent matching platform with no UAE office or centre, no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Schools named on this page are market context. No grade is promised.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor review a Cambridge 0400 sketchbook they cannot hold?
faqs.answer: By looking at it the way the examiner will. The candidate sets a phone square above the open spread with a lamp to one side, so the tutor sees the page flat and at roughly examiner scale. Where pages are uploaded the night before, the tutor has already marked them and the hour opens with a verdict. A second phone on a stand adds a view of the candidate's hand when the correction is about how a tool is held. What a screen genuinely cannot do is turn a three-dimensional piece, which is why documentation technique is taught early.

faqs.question: What are the four assessment objectives in Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400?
faqs.answer: Gathering, recording, research and investigation; exploration and development of ideas; organisation and relationships of visual and other forms; and selection and control of materials, media and processes. Confirm the current weightings on cambridgeinternational.org or through the art department, because they depend on the syllabus version the centre teaches. Each objective has a characteristic failure that is easy to spot: sources taken from a screen, ideas repeated rather than developed, compositions never actually composed, and techniques attempted for the first time on the final piece.

faqs.question: Which 0400 objective gives back the most marks per hour of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usually exploration and development, because the fix works on pages that already exist. Two or three hours of annotation on existing spreads, naming the decision behind each image and the alternative that was rejected, converts output into evidence of a route. Gathering is the next best but needs the candidate to go somewhere and record first-hand, so it costs a weekend as well as an hour of planning. Making a new final piece, which is what most families instinctively buy, is almost always the least productive purchase available.

faqs.question: What equipment do we need at home for online 0400 lessons in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A phone from the last five years, something to hold it steady above the page, a lamp placed to one side rather than overhead, and a connection you have tested once. That is the whole list. A document camera is a convenience, not an upgrade. A graphics tablet contributes nothing to a portfolio submitted as physical work. Avoid tracing aids and projection apps entirely: they produce pages that read as mechanical to an examiner and weaken the gathering objective they were bought to help.

faqs.question: What does a specialist 0400 hour cost compared with a budget online hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor runs about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those figures belong to the providers named. Our own first lesson is free and a rate follows the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can we use a cheap tutor for technique and a specialist for marking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families who do this deliberately get more from the same budget. A technique the candidate has never attempted, such as a dyeing process or a lino cut, can be demonstrated competently by a generalist at the lower band. An audit of a portfolio against four assessment objectives cannot, because it needs somebody who has applied the criteria to real candidate work. The mistake is paying a specialist rate for a demonstration, or a budget rate for a judgement. Ask any tutor which of the two jobs the hour is being spent on.

faqs.question: How do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies affect time for a practical option?
faqs.answer: Significantly, and it is the arithmetic families forget. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed curriculum under KHDA requirements, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit and separate classes mandated for Arab and non-Arab groups. A Year 10 candidate carrying those lessons, a full option block and a long commute has very little free evening. The planning answer is small scheduled portfolio pieces during the week and one protected weekend block per half term for anything wet or constructed.

faqs.question: Can my child resit Cambridge 0400 in the November series?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, so another attempt does not mean waiting a year. The complication is that Art and Design is not a revision resit. The portfolio evidence has to be rebuilt and a new supervised component sat, which is a term of making rather than a fortnight of revision. Entry deadlines also sit months ahead of the papers, so the decision should be taken as soon as results allow. The centre submits the entry and the examinations officer confirms the dates.

faqs.question: Can a private candidate sit Cambridge Art and Design in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is harder than for written subjects and depends entirely on the centre. Not every Dubai school accepts external candidates, and a practical component needs space, invigilation and sometimes equipment, so the schools that do accept private candidates often exclude Art and Design specifically. Contact centres directly and well before the entry deadline, ask about this syllabus by code rather than about IGCSE generally, and expect a more restrictive answer than you would get for a written paper. Do not assume availability from a general search result.

faqs.question: How can a tutor help with annotation if English is my child's second language?
faqs.answer: By making the candidate say it first. The tutor asks what was being tested, what the alternative was and why it lost, then the two of them tighten the candidate's own sentence together in a shared document while the candidate watches the words change. The thinking stays theirs and the expression improves. What a tutor will not do is supply the sentence for copying, which hands over the thinking as well as the words. An examiner reading annotation that sounds like an adult wrote it notices, and that costs more than imperfect English.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge A Level Art and IB Visual Arts at sixteen?
faqs.answer: Mostly writing and curating rather than making. Cambridge AS and A Level Art and Design asks for a sustained personal investigation with a written element. IB Visual Arts asks for three separate things: a comparative study of other artists' work, a process portfolio of experimentation, and a curated exhibition the candidate selects and justifies. Visual Arts also sits inside a full Diploma with five other subjects, an extended essay and theory of knowledge, so studio hours are bounded. The signal to look at is annotation quality, not practical ability.

faqs.question: Does my child need a document camera, or will a phone do?
faqs.answer: A phone does, provided it looks square down at the page rather than across it at an angle. An angled view distorts proportion, and the tutor then corrects a drawing error the candidate never made, which is worse than no correction. A stack of books holds a phone perfectly well. A lamp to one side stops the overhead hot spot that washes out a spread. Spend the money you would have spent on a document camera on one more hour of marking instead; it will do considerably more for the portfolio.

faqs.question: How many 0400 sessions should a Dubai family book, and how often?
faqs.answer: Fortnightly beats weekly for most candidates, because the week between sessions is when pages actually get made and a weekly slot tends to arrive with nothing new to mark. A realistic pattern is fortnightly critique through Years 10 and 11, a short documentation and sequencing block before submission, and two or three timed runs four to six weeks ahead of the supervised window. A number quoted before anybody has read the portfolio is guesswork, which is why the first diagnostic hour is free.

faqs.question: Does a tutor charging a Dubai family for 0400 sessions need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two working day completion time. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. Since it is free and quick, an evasive answer to this question is itself informative.

faqs.question: Where do these lessons actually take place, given the title says online tutor?
faqs.answer: Over live video, one-to-one, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time and shifted to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address; home visits are a service it runs only in India. The candidate works at their own table with the sketchbook under a camera, the tutor marks what is on the page, and a written page plan follows within a day. The trade a family makes is a Cambridge 0400 specialist in place of whoever happens to live within a short drive.

intro.heading: The grade is in the sketchbook, not in the final piece
paragraphs: Parents judge art by the finished image, and Cambridge does not. A student can hand in a confident, well-made final outcome and sit in the middle bands, because the marks are distributed across four assessment objectives of which the finished piece addresses only part. Research and investigation, the exploration and development of ideas, the handling of visual relationships and the control of materials are each assessed, and three of the four live in the pages nobody frames.

That is why 0400 is an evidence subject, and why a tutor's job here is unlike a tutor's job in Mathematics. There is no past paper to drill. There is a body of the student's own work which either documents a process or does not, and the honest service is to look at it page by page, say which assessment objective each page serves, and name what is missing. Nothing in that description involves a tutor making anything.

The boundary matters so much in this subject that it belongs in the opening rather than in a compliance note at the end. Everything submitted for 0400 has to be the student's own work. A tutor may teach a technique, ask questions about an intention, point at a weak transition between two pages, and suggest what kind of investigation is missing. A tutor may not draw on the work, retouch a photograph of it, select which pieces go in, or supply an idea the student then executes as their own.

Dubai students face a particular version of the problem. Creative subjects here are often chosen by students who are genuinely able and then timetabled against a heavy academic load — in a market of 387,441 students across 227 private schools in the 2024-25 figures, with British-curriculum provision at 37 per cent of enrolment, the typical 0400 candidate is also carrying three sciences or an additional maths. Portfolio work expands to fill available time, and available time collapses in Year 11.

The other local factor is physical. Flats are small, studio space is scarce, light in this city is harsh and directional for most of the year, and dust is a genuine enemy of unfixed charcoal and pastel. A portfolio that exists mainly as photographs on a phone, badly lit and inconsistently scaled, is harder to review and harder to moderate, and it is also what most Dubai students actually have when a tutor first looks.

This page therefore works through the subject in the order the evidence accumulates: where the line sits between teaching and interference, what the portfolio should contain as a trail, how to photograph work properly for review, the four objectives in the order marks are lost, a term-by-term calendar for a Dubai Year 10 and 11, the specific failures we see in portfolios from this emirate, what Dubai offers in the way of materials and studio access, and what to ask the school about a coursework grade.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.programmesIntro: Art is taught as a continuous practice rather than a syllabus, so the stage a student is at changes what a review should focus on. These are the four stages Dubai schools run around 0400.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary Art and Design, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Where sketchbook habits form. Students who are praised for finished outcomes in these years learn to hide the process, which is precisely the habit that costs marks at IGCSE. The useful intervention at this stage is not technique teaching but the discipline of keeping, dating and annotating work that did not turn out well.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how much sketchbook culture they build before Year 10, partly because art department staffing and studio space differ so much between campuses. A student arriving in Year 10 from a school with no sketchbook tradition starts the course at a real disadvantage that has nothing to do with their drawing ability.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design (0400)
programmes.description: Assessed through two components: a coursework portfolio built over the course, and an externally set assignment that includes a supervised making session. Four assessment objectives cover research and investigation, development of ideas, organisation of visual relationships, and selection and control of materials. Confirm the current structure and weightings for your child's series at cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter mainly for the June series. Because the coursework portfolio is built across two years and marked internally before moderation, the deadlines that actually govern a candidate's year are set by the school's art department, and they arrive earlier than families expect — frequently before the written-subject mocks.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Art and Design
programmes.description: A substantial step up in scale and independence, with personal investigation work and extended written support for the practical. Students who reached a strong 0400 grade on the strength of making rather than thinking tend to find the research and critical component the hardest adjustment in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Dubai schools run Art to A Level than to IGCSE, and the decision affects portfolio planning at 16 because art-school and foundation applications draw on work made during these years. Families considering that route should ask in Year 11 what the school's post-16 art provision is, since changing school for one subject is a harder move than it sounds.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Visual Arts
programmes.description: The other post-16 destination in this city, assessed through a comparative study, a process portfolio and an exhibition. It rewards exactly the habits 0400 should have built: documented investigation, evidenced development, and the ability to explain a decision. A student whose 0400 portfolio was thin on process will feel that gap immediately.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a significant IB cohort — about seven per cent of private-school enrolment in 2024-25 — and seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding to the post-16 options. Ask any receiving school how its Visual Arts course handles students arriving from a Cambridge background.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.subjectsIntro: Art competes for evening hours with every other subject, and in coursework terms it competes with the other deadline-driven ones. These are the Cambridge entries most often sitting alongside 0400 in Dubai, described by the demand each makes on a portfolio year.

subjects.name: Art and Design (0400)
subjects.description: A coursework portfolio plus an externally set assignment, assessed against four objectives. The time demand is unlike any written subject: it expands indefinitely, peaks before internal deadlines, and cannot be caught up in a fortnight of revision because the evidence has to have been accumulated.

subjects.name: Design and Technology (0445)
subjects.description: Also coursework-heavy, with a design folder and a made outcome. Students taking both this and Art are carrying two portfolio deadlines in the same terms, which is the single most common reason a Dubai Year 11 art portfolio ends up thin on development pages.

subjects.name: Drama (0411)
subjects.description: Practical performance work with written coursework attached, and rehearsal commitments that cluster around production dates. Those dates rarely coordinate with art deadlines, so a student doing both needs the term calendar mapped in September rather than negotiated in February.

subjects.name: Music (0410)
subjects.description: Composition and performance components with their own submission deadlines. Shares with Art the quality of being assessed on evidenced process as well as outcome, and students who understand that in one subject usually transfer the insight to the other.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: A scarce specialism in Dubai with a problem-solving paper and practical programming. Pairs reasonably with Art in timetable terms because its workload is steadier, without the deadline peaks that creative coursework produces.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers that reward following a specification precisely. That discipline is directly useful in responding to an externally set assignment, where a candidate who drifts from the stated starting point loses marks regardless of how good the work is.

subjects.name: English Literature (0486)
subjects.description: Close reading and essay writing under time pressure. Useful alongside Art because both reward the ability to justify an interpretation with specific evidence, which is the skill an art annotation is supposed to demonstrate and usually does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Tiered, and the subject that most reliably crowds out portfolio time in the weeks before a test. Families with an art candidate should expect this collision and plan the portfolio work for the quieter months rather than assuming it can be done late.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Resource-based questions plus fieldwork-style work. Moderate and predictable in its demands, which makes it one of the better companions to a coursework subject in a crowded Dubai timetable.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research and team components with internal deadlines that arrive in clusters. Taken together with Art it produces two sets of internal deadlines in the same terms, and the art portfolio is almost always the one that gives way.

regions.note: Villa district with reasonable room for a working corner and access to art suppliers along the Jumeirah corridor. Students here more often have a dedicated space, which shows directly in the quality of the development pages rather than in the finished work.

regions.name: Dubai Design District
regions.note: Creative-industry district with galleries and events that are usable primary research for a portfolio. A visit that produces annotated photographs and observational drawing is worth more to an 0400 candidate than an afternoon of copying images from a screen.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Dubai's warehouse arts district, with Alserkal Avenue and a cluster of independent galleries and studios. The most accessible source of genuine primary research in the emirate, and the thing most Dubai portfolios are missing when we first review them.

regions.name: The Springs and The Lakes
regions.note: Townhouse communities with limited space for wet or messy work, so portfolios here tend towards drawing and digital media. That is not a weakness provided materials exploration is evidenced deliberately rather than avoided quietly.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Knowledge Village
regions.note: Mixed campus and residential district close to several schools with established art departments. Students here often have studio access after hours, which is worth asking the school about explicitly since it is rarely advertised.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.modesIntro: Support for a coursework subject divides by what is being looked at rather than by what is being taught. These three shapes cover almost every 0400 request we take from Dubai families.

modes.title: Fortnightly portfolio review
modes.description: A 60-minute shared-screen walk through everything added since the last review, with each page named against the assessment objective it serves. The output is a short written list of what is missing, which the student then addresses in their own sketchbook. This is the default shape and the one that produces the clearest record over two years.

modes.title: Technique session on a named medium
modes.description: A single session on one material or process the student has decided to explore — lino, watercolour layering, monoprint, charcoal control, digital compositing. Teaching a technique is legitimate and useful; it becomes the student's own work the moment they apply it to their own intention rather than copying a demonstration.

Notes on what the medium is good for, in the student's own words

modes.description: A short block in the weeks before the externally set assignment and its supervised session, focused on working from a given starting point rather than a self-chosen one. Students who have only ever developed their own themes find an imposed starting point disorienting, and that is a rehearsable skill.

sections.heading: Where the line sits between teaching Art and interfering with it
paragraphs: In a coursework subject this is the first question, not the last one. Everything submitted for 0400 must be the student's own work, and the consequence of breaching that falls on the candidate rather than on whoever helped. A family buying support for a portfolio subject therefore needs to know exactly what they are buying, and a provider who is vague about it is a risk to the child rather than a shortcut.

The legitimate side is broader than nervous parents assume. A tutor can teach a technique from first principles. A tutor can ask what a student was trying to achieve on a page and why the next page abandoned it. A tutor can say that an objective has almost no evidence behind it, that a development sequence jumps without explanation, or that three pages are doing the same thing and one of them is enough. All of that is teaching, and none of it puts a mark at risk.

The other side is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not draw, paint or make on the student's work, does not retouch or recompose a photograph of it, does not choose which pieces are submitted, and does not hand over an idea for the student to execute. Nor does a tutor prepare material that could be reproduced in a supervised session, which is a specific trap in the externally set assignment and the reason the preparation block above stops before the school's own preparation period.

This market contains providers who cross that line as a selling point, including one that sells finished Internal Assessments for other qualifications at a published price. For an art portfolio the equivalent offer is help that leaves the sketchbook better than the student can account for, and a moderator reading a portfolio looks for exactly that mismatch. The table below is the working version of the rule, written so a parent can hold a tutor to it.

sections.heading: The portfolio as an evidence trail, not a collection
paragraphs: A collection is a set of good pieces. A portfolio is a record of how a student got from a starting point to an outcome, including the parts that failed. The difference is worth stating because almost every Dubai portfolio we see for the first time is a collection with a few process pages added retrospectively, and retrospective process pages are visible as such.

The trail has a shape. A starting point, recorded. Primary research the student gathered themselves — photographs they took, objects they handled, drawings made in front of the thing. Secondary research with a reason for its inclusion. Then exploration: several directions attempted, at least one of them abandoned with a note saying why. Then materials trials, then refinement, then the outcome, with the decisions between each stage legible.

Dating everything is the single cheapest improvement available in this subject, and hardly anyone does it. A dated sequence lets a reader see development happening in real time; an undated set of pages makes the same work look assembled. For a tutor reviewing over video it also makes a genuine difference, because the order the work was made in is the thing a photograph cannot convey.

The table below is a working checklist. Use it as a diagnostic on your child's existing sketchbook rather than as a specification to build to, since the specification is the school's and the syllabus's. What it is good for is locating the gap: in our experience the missing row is almost always primary research, followed closely by an abandoned direction with a written reason.

table.caption: THE 0400 EVIDENCE TRAIL — WHAT SHOULD EXIST AND WHAT ITS ABSENCE MEANS
rows: A recorded brief or theme in the student's own words
That later work connects back to it
Work drifting with no stated intention
The student's own photographs, objects, observational drawing
First-hand looking rather than screen-sourced images

Artist or context references with a stated reason
Relevance to the student's own direction
References included decoratively, adding no marks
Several attempts, at least one abandoned with a reason
A single idea taken straight to outcome
Small tests in more than one medium, annotated
Deliberate selection rather than default habit
The materials objective resting on one technique
The final piece plus the decisions that led to it
A legible path from research to resolution
A strong image with nothing behind it

sections.heading: Photographing work for a video review: the part nobody teaches
paragraphs: If a portfolio is going to be reviewed over video, and increasingly if it is going to be recorded for the school at all, the photographs matter. Badly shot pages waste review time and misrepresent the work, and in Dubai the default conditions are genuinely unhelpful: hard directional sunlight for most of the year, strong colour casts from warm interior lighting, and glare from glazed surfaces.

The method is simple and takes one afternoon to establish. Shoot in open shade or in diffused daylight near a window, with the light coming from the side rather than from behind the camera. Keep the page flat and the camera parallel to it, so the rectangle stays a rectangle. Include a consistent scale reference for three-dimensional work. Shoot everything at the same time of day where possible, so colour is comparable across the portfolio. Photograph each page as it is completed rather than in one session at the end of term.

Three-dimensional and textured work needs more thought. A flat frontal photograph of a ceramic piece or a relief loses the thing that makes it work, so two or three angles plus one raking-light shot that reveals surface is worth more than a single careful frontal. Unfixed charcoal and pastel should be photographed immediately, because in this city dust and air-conditioning will degrade them within weeks.

None of this is a substitute for the physical work, which the school holds and moderates. It is how a parent and an external reviewer can see it honestly, and it has a secondary benefit: a student who photographs each page on completion has, without extra effort, produced the dated sequence the previous section asked for.
bullets: Diffused daylight or open shade, light from the side, never direct sun
Camera parallel to flat work so the page keeps its shape
Two or three angles plus one raking-light shot for three-dimensional work
A consistent scale reference, so size is readable across the portfolio
Photograph each page when it is finished, not all of them in June

sections.heading: The four assessment objectives, in the order marks are lost
paragraphs: Cambridge assesses 0400 against four objectives covering the gathering and recording of research and investigation, the exploration and development of ideas, the organisation of visual and other relationships, and the selection and control of materials, media and processes. Confirm the current wording and weightings for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org; what follows is where, in practice, Dubai portfolios lose the marks.

The research objective is where the largest losses sit, and the cause is almost always the same: secondary images gathered from a screen in place of first-hand investigation. A student who photographs a building they stood in front of, draws an object they are holding, or records a place they visited is evidencing something a downloaded image cannot. In this emirate the raw material is available — Alserkal Avenue and the Al Quoz galleries, the Design District, the old quarter around the creek — and it goes largely unused.

Development is second. The characteristic failure is the jump: a first idea, then a finished piece, with nothing legible in between. Development marks reward attempts that went nowhere, provided the student says why they stopped. Students resist keeping failures because years of praise for finished work taught them to hide the mess, and reversing that habit is one of the few things a reviewer can change in a single session.

The visual-relationships objective tends to be the strongest in portfolios from students who can draw, and the materials objective the weakest in students who found one medium they like in Year 9 and never left it. Two small, annotated trials in unfamiliar media, with a sentence on what each is good for, will usually do more for that objective than another month of refining the medium they already control.
bullets: Research: primary investigation the student gathered first-hand
Development: attempts that failed, kept, with a reason written beside them
Visual relationships: usually the strongest objective in drawing-led portfolios
Materials: two annotated trials in unfamiliar media beat another refinement

sections.heading: A term-by-term portfolio calendar for a Dubai Year 10 and 11
paragraphs: Coursework fails on timing more often than on ability. The portfolio is built over two years, the school's internal deadlines govern the year, and those deadlines usually sit earlier than families expect because the work has to be marked internally before moderation. Meanwhile the written subjects run their own mock cycle, and art is the first thing to be set aside when a science test appears.

The calendar below is a planning aid rather than a schedule to follow, since the real dates belong to your child's art department. What it is useful for is spotting the structural risks: the Year 10 summer term when nothing feels urgent, the Year 11 autumn when three subjects demand coursework at once, and the final stretch when the externally set assignment and its supervised session arrive on top of everything.

One Dubai-specific factor belongs in the plan. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises evenings, and for a practical subject that can mean several weeks with very little made. Families who plan for that — bringing material-heavy work forward, keeping the Ramadan weeks for research, reading and annotation — lose far less than those who discover it in the third week.

The other factor is the Cambridge administrative calendar, which governs the written side of the school's year even for a practical subject. Cambridge runs June and November series, allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Entry deadlines sit months ahead: for the March 2027 series, for instance, Cambridge's published key dates put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027.
