sections.heading: What goes wrong in Dubai portfolios specifically
paragraphs: Patterns repeat by city, and in this one they are recognisable. The first is screen-sourced research, which is partly an artefact of how much of daily life here happens indoors and in air conditioning. A portfolio full of beautifully rendered copies of photographs the student found online is technically impressive and evidentially thin, and the research objective is where it is penalised.

The second is the single-medium portfolio. Where a school's art provision is one class across a year group with limited studio facilities, students work in what is available — usually pencil, fineliner and digital — and the materials objective is left resting on one technique for two years. This is not the student's fault and it is entirely fixable with small trials done at home, provided somebody names it before Year 11.

The third is the retrofitted process. A student makes good final pieces, is told in Year 11 that development evidence is needed, and produces a set of development pages after the fact. Moderators read portfolios as sequences, and work made backwards reads as work made backwards. The remedy is dating pages from the start, which costs nothing and cannot be applied retrospectively.

The fourth is the collision with the academic load. The 0400 candidate in a Dubai school is frequently also carrying three sciences or additional mathematics, and in the exam term the portfolio is what gives way. A family that accepts this in September and front-loads the practical work has a far better Year 11 than one that intends to catch up at Easter, because unlike revision, evidence cannot be compressed.
bullets: Screen-sourced research instead of first-hand investigation
One medium for two years, leaving the materials objective unevidenced
Development pages made after the outcome, which reads as what it is
The academic load absorbing the portfolio term in Year 11

sections.heading: Materials, studios and what this city actually offers
paragraphs: A reasonable 0400 portfolio does not need expensive materials, and anyone implying otherwise is selling something. The objectives reward deliberate selection and control, not cost: a well-used set of graphite grades, one ink, one water-based paint, cartridge and one textured paper, plus a phone camera, covers a great deal. What marks reward is a student who can say why they chose a medium for a particular purpose.

Dubai does have genuine primary-research assets, and they are underused by students here. Al Quoz holds the emirate's warehouse arts district, including Alserkal Avenue and a cluster of independent galleries; Dubai Design District runs exhibitions and events; the older quarters around the creek offer architecture, texture and working life that cannot be found on a screen. One properly documented visit — photographs the student took, drawings made on site, written observations — can support weeks of development work and directly evidences the research objective.

Studio space at home is the practical constraint for most families, particularly in apartments. The workable answer is usually a defined corner with a board that can be carried, rather than a dedicated room: a portable surface, a box for materials, and somewhere to dry work out of the dust. Several Dubai schools also allow after-hours studio access and do not advertise it, so it is worth asking the art department directly.

One thing a tutor cannot do is supply materials, past papers, syllabus documents, mark schemes or exemplar portfolios. Cambridge's materials are its own, and reproducing them is not something we will do; we will cite and link them instead. The right source for the syllabus and any assessment detail is cambridgeinternational.org, and the right source for what your child's school requires is the art department.
bullets: A modest, well-used material set evidences control better than an expensive one
Al Quoz, Alserkal Avenue and the Design District are real primary research
A portable board and a materials box beats waiting for a studio
Ask the art department about after-hours studio access; it is rarely advertised

sections.heading: What to ask the school about a coursework grade
paragraphs: Because 0400 is marked internally before moderation, the school holds far more of the information than it does in a written subject, and most families never ask for it. Four questions at a parents' evening will tell you more about your child's likely grade than any amount of looking at the finished pieces.

First, what are the internal deadlines for the portfolio, with dates. Second, which assessment objectives is my child currently weakest on, in the department's view. Third, on what evidence is the predicted grade based — a predicted grade in a coursework subject rests on work that physically exists, so the answer should be specific. Fourth, what is still missing that could reasonably be added before the deadline.

Those questions also establish the boundary properly from the school's side, which protects everyone. A school that knows a student has an external tutor reviewing their portfolio and knows that the tutor does not touch the work has no reason for concern. A school that discovers unexplained improvement has every reason, and the consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

Two closing points about what we are and are not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge, and will not imply one; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. And individuals providing private tuition in the UAE require the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.
bullets: Ask for the internal deadlines, with dates, in writing
Ask which objectives the department rates weakest
Ask what physical evidence the predicted grade rests on
Tell the school a reviewer is involved and that the work is untouched

process.title: Photograph the sketchbook as it stands
process.description: Every page, in diffused daylight, camera parallel to the page. It takes an hour and it is the only thing needed for a first review. A portfolio photographed properly can be assessed honestly; one shot in hard sun on a glazed surface cannot, and the review time goes on guessing instead of on the work.

process.title: Free 30-minute review, one per family
process.description: A live shared-screen session in which a specialist walks the existing pages and names which assessment objectives are evidenced and which are not. No cost and no card details. For most Dubai families the first useful finding is that research and materials are thin while making is fine.

process.title: Agree the review cadence and the boundary
process.description: Fortnightly is the usual rhythm for a portfolio, since it matches the pace at which work accumulates. The booking also states plainly that the tutor reviews and teaches and never makes, selects or alters anything, and that the school may be told so.

process.title: Work on the gap list, in your own sketchbook
process.description: Each review produces a short written list of what is missing — a primary-research visit, two materials trials, an abandoned direction annotated. The student addresses it in their own pages, alone, between reviews. That work is what the next review looks at.

process.title: Map the deadlines and protect the slots
process.description: Once the art department's internal dates are known, the plan is built backwards from them and two fixed practical slots a week are protected through the exam term. Sessions move; they do not get cancelled. Unlike revision, portfolio evidence cannot be compressed into a final fortnight.

whyPoints.title: The sketchbook is reviewed, not improved
whyPoints.description: Every session is a walk through your child's own pages with the assessment objective named against each one. The tutor's hands never touch the work, no piece is selected for submission by us, and no idea is handed over for execution. That is the only version of this service that does not put a candidate at risk.

whyPoints.title: Objectives tracked separately
whyPoints.description: Research, development, visual relationships and materials are logged individually rather than as a general impression of the portfolio. A parent can therefore see that making is strong and primary research is almost absent, which is a diagnosis with an action attached rather than a comment about talent.

whyPoints.title: Dated sequences, not a collection
whyPoints.description: Photographing each page on completion produces the dated trail that moderators read as genuine development. It costs nothing, it cannot be applied retrospectively, and it is the single most common thing missing from a Dubai portfolio when we first see one.

whyPoints.title: Honest about cost and materials
whyPoints.description: A modest, well-used material set evidences control better than an expensive one, and we will say so rather than recommending purchases. We also do not supply syllabus documents, past assignments, mark schemes or exemplar portfolios; those belong to Cambridge and we cite them instead.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and status stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Reviews are live and online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. We hold no regulator or exam-board approval and claim none, and where no 0400 specialist is free at your hour we will tell you instead of substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor actually review a sketchbook?
faqs.answer: The student photographs the pages and shares the screen, and the tutor walks them in order, naming the assessment objective each page serves and pointing at what is missing. In practice it is closer to looking over a shoulder than parents expect, with one real advantage: the photographs stay, so a page discussed in October can be put beside one from February. The limitation is surface — the physical quality of a heavily worked page is partly lost in a photograph, which is why raking-light shots matter for textured work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor touch my child's artwork at any point?
faqs.answer: No, and that is not a cautious house rule, it is the condition under which this subject can be tutored at all. Everything submitted for 0400 must be the student's own work, and the consequences of a breach fall on the candidate. A tutor may demonstrate a technique on their own paper, ask what the student intended, and say that a page is doing nothing for any objective. A tutor may not draw on, paint on, retouch or recompose the student's work, including on a photograph of it.

faqs.question: What should be in the portfolio by the end of Year 10?
faqs.answer: A sketchbook with dated pages, at least one complete development sequence that runs from a recorded starting point through exploration to an outcome, primary research the student gathered themselves, and small annotated trials in more than one medium. The specific requirement is the school's and the department's, so ask them. What we would look for in a review is whether anything was abandoned with a written reason, since that is the clearest sign that development is being evidenced rather than assembled later.

faqs.question: My child's final piece is genuinely good but the grade is low. How?
faqs.answer: Because the final piece addresses only part of what is assessed. Marks are distributed across four objectives covering research and investigation, exploration and development of ideas, organisation of visual relationships, and selection and control of materials. A strong outcome with thin research pages and no visible development scores on one or two of those and not the others. The diagnosis is almost always visible in minutes when a portfolio is reviewed page by page, and the remedy is evidence rather than more making.

faqs.question: How do we photograph three-dimensional or textured work properly?
faqs.answer: Two or three angles rather than one frontal shot, plus one photograph with the light raking across the surface so texture reads. Use diffused daylight or open shade, never direct Dubai sun, and include a consistent scale reference so size is readable across the portfolio. Photograph unfixed charcoal and pastel work immediately, because dust and air conditioning degrade it within weeks here. Shoot at a similar time of day throughout, so colour stays comparable from one term to the next.

faqs.question: Is 0400 marked by the school or by Cambridge?
faqs.answer: The coursework portfolio is marked internally and then moderated, while the externally set assignment is set outside the school. The practical consequence for a family is that the school holds more information than it does in a written subject, and that internal deadlines govern the year. Ask the art department for those dates in writing, ask which objectives they rate your child weakest on, and ask what physical evidence a predicted grade rests on. Confirm the current assessment arrangements for your series at cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: How many sketchbook pages does a portfolio need?
faqs.answer: Page count is the wrong target and chasing it produces padding, which reads as padding. What a reviewer looks for is whether each objective has evidence behind it: first-hand research, a development sequence with at least one abandoned direction, annotated materials trials, and a legible path to the outcome. Three pages that show thinking are worth more than fifteen that repeat one technique. Ask the school whether it sets an expectation, because departments differ, and then build evidence rather than volume.

faqs.question: What does recording research actually mean in 0400?
faqs.answer: Looking at something first-hand and keeping proof that you did. Photographs the student took themselves, drawings made in front of the object or the place, objects handled and recorded, written observations made at the time. Images collected from a screen are secondary research, and a portfolio built on them evidences the objective thinly however well the copies are rendered. In Dubai this is a solvable problem: Al Quoz and Alserkal Avenue, the Design District and the older quarters around the creek are all within reach of a documented visit.

faqs.question: Can my child use digital work for Cambridge Art and Design?
faqs.answer: Digital media are a legitimate part of the materials and processes available, and for apartment households with no space for wet work they are often the practical choice. The risk is narrower than parents fear and different from what they expect: it is not that digital work scores lower, it is that a digital-only portfolio can leave the materials objective resting on one process. Two small physical trials, annotated with what each medium is good for, usually address that. Confirm any format requirements with the school and the syllabus.

faqs.question: How do we know whether the development work is strong enough to move on?
faqs.answer: Ask whether a reader could reconstruct the decisions without your child in the room. If the pages show a starting point, several directions attempted, one of them abandoned with a written reason, and trials that explain why a medium was chosen, the sequence will stand on its own. If it shows an idea and then a finished piece, it will not, however good both are. That test is also the thing a tutor can usefully apply in a review, because it requires judgement about existing work rather than the supply of new ideas.

faqs.question: Where in Dubai can my child get materials or studio access?
faqs.answer: Materials are widely available and a modest set is enough: graphite grades, one ink, one water-based paint, cartridge and one textured paper will evidence control better than an expensive kit. For space, a portable board, a materials box and somewhere dust-free to dry work beats waiting for a dedicated room, which most apartments will never provide. Several Dubai schools allow after-hours studio access without advertising it, so ask the art department. For primary research, the Al Quoz galleries and the Design District are the obvious starting points.

faqs.question: What should we ask at parents' evening about a coursework subject?
faqs.answer: Four things, and ask for them in writing. The internal deadlines with dates. Which assessment objectives the department currently rates your child weakest on. What physical evidence the predicted grade rests on, since in a coursework subject it should rest on work that exists. And what could reasonably still be added before the deadline. It is also worth telling the school that an external reviewer is looking at the portfolio and that the work is untouched, because unexplained improvement is what creates a problem.

faqs.question: Is taking Art and Design a risk for a student aiming at a science degree?
faqs.answer: It is a timetable question rather than a reputational one. Universities look at the subject profile against their stated requirements, so the real issue is whether the art slot could have carried a subject a target course asks for. The second issue is workload: 0400 is coursework-heavy and its deadlines collide with science practicals and mocks in Year 11. Students who manage both tend to be the ones who front-loaded the portfolio in Year 10. Ask the school what the alternative in that option block would be before deciding.

faqs.question: Our child missed six weeks of Art through illness. Can the portfolio be rebuilt?
faqs.answer: Partly, and honestly, not as if the six weeks had happened. Evidence cannot be compressed the way revision can, and work made after the fact reads as work made after the fact. What can be done is to prioritise: identify which objective has the least behind it, usually research or materials, and address that with a small number of properly dated pieces rather than attempting to reproduce the whole missing sequence. Tell the school early, because departments can sometimes adjust internal deadlines and cannot do so retrospectively.

faqs.question: Will a creative subject grade help with the UAE equivalency subject count?
faqs.answer: On the published British-track requirement, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3 are needed, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. A Cambridge IGCSE such as 0400 is capable of forming part of the five. Equivalency is carried out by the authorities rather than by any tutoring provider, tutoring is not a requirement of it, and the figures should be verified on moe.gov.ae before you plan around them.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.closingHeading: Send photographs of the sketchbook, not of the final piece
dubai/cambridge-igcse-art-and-design-040.closingBody: If you are looking for a Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400 tutor in Dubai, the most useful thing you can send is the part nobody frames: the research pages, the trials, the attempt that did not work. Photograph them in diffused daylight with the camera square to the page, take the free 30-minute review, and you will get an honest read on which of the four assessment objectives has evidence behind it and which does not. The work stays your child's throughout, and we will say so to the school if it helps.

intro.heading: Why a 0610 search usually starts with a disappointing mock
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry for an IGCSE Biology tutor in Dubai arrives in the same week of the year. The Year 11 mock results come back in late January or early February, Biology is three or four grades below the other sciences, and the comment on the report says something general about revision technique. The grade is a number with no diagnosis attached. A parent cannot tell from it whether the problem is unlearnt content, misread command terms, bad timing, or a practical paper nobody has practised. So the search begins, and it begins with the phrase that feels most reassuring: somebody who will sit in the room and sort it out.

That instinct is sound and the diagnosis it is reaching for is real. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is a content-heavy course with twenty-one syllabus topics, and a student can revise diligently for a month while leaving the actual leak untouched. The most common pattern we see in Dubai is a student who knows the biology and still loses a quarter of the available marks, because the answers are written as descriptions when the question asked for an explanation, or because the alternative-to-practical paper has never been attempted outside a classroom. Neither problem is visible in a percentage.

What fixes it is evidence rather than hours. A scored script with the mark scheme next to it shows exactly where marks went: which topic, which question type, which command word. A second script four weeks later, under the same timing and from the same paper format, shows whether the fix held. That is the whole method on this page, and it is the reason the format matters less than the marking. A tutor who marks loosely and encouragingly in your living room is less useful than one who marks strictly over video and sends you the script.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform, not a school and not a licensed training institute. Tutoring for families in Dubai and across the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; that is a service offered only in India. The practical consequence is worth stating plainly, because it is the trade you are being asked to accept: you give up a person in the room, and in exchange the pool of available 0610 specialists stops being limited by who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of your community.

The rest of this page is written to be useful even if you book nothing. It covers the market rates Dubai families are actually quoted, the component structure of 0610 and where the marks sit, the Core and Extended decision that sets the grade ceiling, the Paper 5 and Paper 6 split that most parents discover too late, and the permit rules that govern anybody charging for private lessons in this country.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-home-.programmesIntro: A 0610 student in Dubai sits inside a longer sequence. What came before shapes how much content is missing, and what comes next decides whether the Extended tier is negotiable. These are the four stages that matter when planning support for Cambridge IGCSE Biology.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary science, Year 9
programmes.description: The year before the IGCSE course formally begins in most Dubai British-curriculum schools. Biology is still taught as part of a combined science block, often by a teacher whose specialism is chemistry or physics. Cell structure, transport across membranes and the basics of nutrition are introduced here, and the gaps that open in Year 9 are the gaps that resurface in a Year 11 mock.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely on when the 0610 syllabus actually starts. Some begin the course in Year 9 and run it over three years; others compress it into Years 10 and 11. Ask the head of science which model your child's school uses, because it changes what a tutor should be covering in October of Year 10.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610, year one
programmes.description: Content year. Most schemes of work cover characteristics of living organisms, organisation of the organism, movement into and out of cells, biological molecules, enzymes, plant nutrition and human nutrition in this year. Nothing is examined externally, which is exactly why the gaps accumulate quietly. A student can pass every end-of-topic test by short-term recall and arrive in Year 11 with no retrieval strength at all.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is the cheapest year to buy tutoring in Dubai and the year fewest families do. Market rates sit at the lower end because the work is teaching rather than exam triage, and a weekly session in Year 10 removes the need for an intensive block in the spring of Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610, examination year
programmes.description: The remaining topics are taught while revision of year one runs alongside. Transport in plants and animals, diseases and immunity, gas exchange, respiration, excretion, coordination and response, drugs, reproduction, inheritance, variation and selection, organisms and their environment, human influences on ecosystems and biotechnology all have to land. Mock exams fall in the winter, final entries close months before the papers, and the practical component has to be prepared separately.
programmes.countryNote: This is when most Dubai enquiries arrive, usually in the fortnight after mock results. There is still time: the gap between a January mock and a June series is roughly eighteen teaching weeks, which is enough to rebuild two or three weak topics properly and to fix exam technique across all three papers.

programmes.name: A Level Biology or IB Diploma Biology
programmes.description: The destination that makes the tier decision serious. A Level Biology and IB Diploma Biology at Higher Level both assume Extended-tier fluency with enzymes, transport, respiration and genetics. Students arriving from Core-tier 0610 can succeed, but the first term carries a real content debt, usually in biochemistry and in quantitative handling of data.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms vary in what they require. Several British-curriculum schools in the emirate ask for a grade 6 or 7 at IGCSE before admitting a student to A Level Biology, and IB schools set their own Higher Level entry conditions. Check the published entry criteria for your child's school rather than assuming the national pattern applies.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-home-.subjectsIntro: Biology rarely travels alone. A Year 11 student needing 0610 support usually has one or two other subjects under strain in the same term, and the sequencing matters: fixing the subject with the nearest paper first is often better value than spreading three sessions thinly.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Twenty-one topics, three assessed components, one grade. Marks concentrate in the theory paper at 50%, with multiple choice at 30% and the practical component at 20%. Extended candidates carry supplement content that Core candidates never see, which is why mixed-tier group teaching rarely works.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The most common second subject alongside 0610. Moles, stoichiometry and electrolysis are where Dubai students lose marks, and the mathematical demand catches out students who are comfortable with biology recall but shaky on rearranging a formula under time pressure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Graph work, unit conversion and the long-answer explanation of a mechanism. A student who writes well in biology often scores poorly in physics for the same reason in reverse: physics answers reward compression, and biology habits produce answers that say too much and score nothing extra.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Taken instead of three separate sciences in many Dubai schools. The biology content overlaps heavily with 0610 but is reduced in depth, so a student moving between the two syllabuses needs a map of what is kept and what is cut rather than a full reteach.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade covering biology, chemistry and physics. Students who find 0610 heavy are sometimes moved onto 0653 by the school, which changes the whole revision plan and the post-16 options. Worth understanding before agreeing to a switch.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Not obviously connected to biology until the data-handling questions arrive. Percentage change, rates, magnification calculations and reading values off a graph all appear in 0610 papers, and weak number work quietly costs marks in a science exam.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Relevant because 0610 long-answer marks are awarded for precise wording. A student writing in a second language can hold the biology perfectly and still miss the mark-scheme term, and a tutor who recognises that pattern treats it as a language fix, not a content fix.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The other board in regular use across Dubai. Paper structure and the practical arrangement differ from Cambridge, so a tutor must know which board the school has entered the student for. Using 0610 past papers to prepare a 4BI1 candidate wastes a term.

subjects.name: A Level Biology
subjects.description: The common next step. Transport, gas exchange, respiration and genetics all reappear with far more quantitative demand. Students who arrive with Extended-tier 0610 fluency spend the first term learning new material rather than repairing old material.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Biology
subjects.description: The alternative post-16 route in Dubai's IB schools. The internal assessment is the student's own investigation, and a tutor's role there is teaching method and giving feedback on the student's own drafts rather than supplying content.

Students we support in this corridor sit IGCSE sciences across both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries, so the first question in a trial lesson is always which board and which tier.

schoolClusters.note: A wider mix of curricula and a wider ability range in the same year groups, which is where Core and Extended entries most often sit side by side. Students we support here frequently discover in Year 11 that the tier they are entered for caps the grade they are working towards.

sections.heading: What a 0610 home tutor in Dubai does, and what happens here instead
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 home tutor in Dubai is, in the market's own terms, a person who travels to a villa or apartment and teaches at the kitchen table for an hour or two. That is a real service and plenty of families in the emirate use it. What you are paying for is attention and the absence of logistics on your side: no laptop setup, no screen to supervise, somebody physically present who notices when a fifteen-year-old has stopped following. For a younger child, or for a student who genuinely will not engage with a screen, that presence is worth real money.

It also carries costs that are easy to miss when you are comparing hourly rates. Travel time is priced into the hour or into the fee, and in a city where a cross-town evening run can take forty minutes each way, the tutor who accepts your booking is usually the tutor who lives nearby rather than the one who has taught your child's exact syllabus and tier. The permit position matters too: anyone charging for private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit through MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and plenty of informal arrangements do not have one.

IB Gram delivers this support as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Dubai evenings. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or in any other emirate; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The argument for accepting that is specific to 0610 rather than general. Biology at Extended tier is a precise syllabus with a published mark scheme, and the difference between a tutor who has marked that mark scheme through a full series and one who has not is larger than the difference between a screen and a chair. Removing the drive removes the geography filter from the search.

What you lose in presence, the method tries to replace with documentation. Every session produces something you can read: an annotated script, an updated topic map, a model answer written in your child's own words rather than copied from a guide. You do not have to take the tutor's word for progress, and you do not have to rely on your own reading of a teenager's mood after a lesson.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group: what each format costs a Dubai 0610 family
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. That is unhelpful in a city where every other education cost is quoted in dirhams, so the table below collects the published market rates we could attribute to a source, as of October 2026. None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are what the Dubai market charges, gathered so you can tell whether a quote you have been given is normal.

The pattern across the bands is consistent. Online one-to-one and in-home one-to-one overlap at the bottom, and separate at the top because travel has to be paid for by somebody. Group formats are genuinely cheaper per hour and genuinely less targeted: a class of four students at mixed tiers cannot spend forty minutes on the one topic your child is losing marks on. Tuition centres sit apart again, because a centre with premises in Dubai is a licensed business rather than an individual tutor, and the fee reflects the overhead.

Read the right-hand column before the price column. For a 0610 candidate the binding constraint is usually not money but whether the tutor has taught the tier your child is entered for. A general science tutor at AED 150 an hour who has not worked through Extended supplement content will cost you more in wasted weeks than a specialist at AED 300 who starts from a marked script. Ask any prospective tutor which paper numbers your child will sit and what the practical component is worth. If the answer is vague, the rate is irrelevant.

A note on context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the part of the education budget that does move, so it is worth planning a year of support deliberately rather than buying it in panic blocks in February.

sections.heading: The six-week evidence file for a 0610 student
paragraphs: This is the part of the method that answers the question a parent actually has, which is not what happened in the lesson but whether it worked. The answer is a short stack of documents produced on a fixed schedule, all of it comparable with itself. A score only means something next to another score from the same paper format under the same timing, so the file is built around two comparable papers with the diagnostic work in between.

Week one is the baseline, and it is deliberately uncomfortable. The student sits a released past paper at full length under exam conditions and it is marked strictly to the published mark scheme, question by question, with marks attributed to topics rather than to a general impression. The number is usually lower than the school mock, because school mocks are frequently shortened or marked generously. That is the point: the baseline exists to be beaten by a second measurement, not to reassure anybody in week one.

Weeks two to four are where the work is. The topic map splits the twenty-one syllabus sections into secure, shaky and unseen, which separates the two problems that look identical in a mock result: content the school has not taught yet and content taught but not retained. The command-term work follows, because a substantial share of lost marks in Biology are lost on questions the student could answer. Then the practical paper, which is 20% of the grade and the component almost nobody revises for in a Dubai household.

Week six repeats the measurement. Same paper format, same timing, different series, same mark scheme. The movement between those two numbers is the only honest claim anybody can make about tutoring, and it belongs to your child rather than to us. If it has not moved, that is information too, and the right response is to change the plan rather than to add hours.

sections.heading: Marking a 0610 theory answer the way the mark scheme marks it
paragraphs: The single most transferable thing a tutor can teach a 0610 candidate is how the marks are awarded. Cambridge theory papers award marks against specified points, and an answer that contains the biology but not the point does not score. A student who writes four lines of accurate material about diffusion and never uses the words concentration gradient has written something true and scored nothing. Once a student has seen that happen to their own script three or four times, the habit changes faster than any amount of content revision would move it.

Command terms are where this lives. State, describe and explain are not stylistic preferences; they set the number and type of points required. Describe asks what happens, explain asks why it happens, and a describe-shaped answer to an explain question is the commonest two-mark loss in the paper. Compare requires both sides of the comparison in the same sentence, and suggest invites application of principles to an unfamiliar context rather than recall. These distinctions are published in the syllabus and almost never practised deliberately.

The second pattern is quantity. Dubai students writing in a second language often over-write, producing long answers that repeat one point in three forms. The mark scheme awards the point once. A tutor's job here is not to simplify the biology but to teach compression: identify the number of marks, plan that number of distinct points, write them separately. Students usually find this is the easiest change they make all year, and it shows up in the next marked script rather than in June.

None of this works without the real mark scheme. We reference the published Cambridge documents and link to them on the Cambridge International website rather than reproducing them, because those materials are the board's copyright. A tutor who offers you a folder of mark schemes and subject guides as downloads is selling you something they do not have the right to distribute, which tells you something about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Many Dubai parents discover the tier system late, often during the Year 11 mock season, and some discover it after entries have closed. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is tiered: Core candidates sit one set of papers and Extended candidates sit another, with Extended carrying supplement content on top of the core material. The grades available differ, and that is the part that matters to a family planning for A Level or an IB Diploma science.

The school decides the entry, not the tutor and usually not the parent. It is decided on the evidence the school has, which is classroom performance and mock results, and it is decided before the final entry deadline, which falls months before the paper. The practical consequence is that the window for influencing the decision is Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, not March. If your child needs a grade above a C for a sixth-form place, the conversation with the head of science needs to happen while the entry is still open.

What a tutor can do is make the Extended tier survivable. Extended supplement content is not harder in kind so much as denser, and it tends to concentrate in specific places: more detail in transport and gas exchange, more genetics, more quantitative treatment of data. Roughly a third of session time for an Extended candidate goes to material a Core candidate will never meet, so a tutor who teaches both tiers from the same plan is short-changing one of them.

If the entry is already Core and the ambition is a sixth-form science place, say so in the trial lesson. There is an honest conversation to be had about what a Core-tier grade means for A Level admission in Dubai, and it is better had in October than in August. Sometimes the answer is to work towards a strong Core grade and plan a bridging term; sometimes the answer is to ask the school to review the entry while that is still possible.

sections.heading: The practical component: 20% of the grade, and the least revised part of 0610
paragraphs: Every 0610 candidate sits a practical component worth a fifth of the grade, and the school chooses between a practical test carried out under supervision and a written alternative-to-practical paper. Most Dubai students we work with are entered for the written alternative, and almost none of them have practised it outside a classroom lesson. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in the whole course, because the skills it tests are a short, closed list that can be taught in three or four sessions.

What it actually assesses is experimental method rather than biology recall. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in somebody else's experiment. Reading a measurement from a diagram of a scale. Drawing a results table with units in the headings rather than in the cells. Plotting a graph with sensible axes and a line that answers the question. Spotting the anomalous result and saying what should be done about it. Describing an improvement to a method that would actually reduce error rather than just repeating the experiment.

Biological drawing deserves separate mention because it is the one skill students assume cannot be revised. It can. Marks go for clean continuous lines without shading, correct proportion, labels with straight ruled lines that touch the structure, and a magnification calculation done with consistent units. Every one of those is a rule, and rules can be practised over video with a shared screen as easily as in a laboratory, because the student is drawing from a provided image in the exam too.

The practical strand is timetabled separately in a pre-series block for exactly this reason. Mixing it into theory revision means it gets dropped whenever theory feels more urgent, which is every week. One session in four, protected, is usually enough to move this component substantially before a June or November series.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the dates a Dubai family cannot control
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Most Dubai British-curriculum schools enter Year 11 for the June series. The dates that matter to a tutoring plan are not the exam dates, which the school will tell you, but the administrative deadlines sitting months earlier, which the school often does not.

The March series key dates published by Cambridge make the pattern concrete. For the March 2027 series, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. Whatever series your child is sitting, the tier and subject decisions are locked long before revision reaches its peak.

One further Cambridge rule catches families out and is worth knowing even though the school handles it. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. If you are planning travel around the exam period, confirm the dates from your school's own timetable rather than from a generic one found online.

If your child is entered with Pearson Edexcel rather than Cambridge, the calendar differs. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the two questions worth asking any Dubai tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The second question is about academic honesty, and it separates tutors from the small number of operators in this market selling something else. A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work. For IGCSE Biology that means coaching method on a practical write-up, explaining what a results analysis needs to contain, and marking a draft the student produced. It does not mean supplying text for a student to submit as their own, and any operator offering that is handing your child a malpractice risk in exchange for a fee.

A third thing worth checking, since it is where competitor pages are weakest, is whether the tutor claims credentials nobody holds. IB Gram is an independent matching platform. It is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, it holds no permit for premises in the UAE, and it is not affiliated with any named school. Those bodies are described on this page because understanding them helps you, not because any of them endorses us.

Taken together these three checks - permit, honesty boundary, claimed credentials - filter out most of what is wrong with this market in about four minutes of conversation. They work equally well on an in-home tutor found through a community group and on an online platform found through a search result, including this one.

faqs.question: Can a Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 home tutor in Dubai actually come to our villa?
faqs.answer: Tutors who work in-home do exist across Dubai and the market rate including travel runs roughly AED 180-500 an hour, according to published figures from Bestimate and independent home tutors. IB Gram does not provide that format anywhere in the UAE. Our lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Dubai evenings, and home visits are a service we run only in India. The reason we make that trade on a 0610 page is specific: removing the drive means the tutor can be someone who has taught your child's exact tier and practical paper through a full exam series, rather than whoever is available within a short drive of your community.

faqs.question: What does a 0610 Biology tutor cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, as of October 2026, run roughly AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200-450 or more for an exam specialist. Unitors advertises IGCSE support from AED 150, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and Bestimate's rate table puts specialist tutoring at AED 200-450 and above. Budget online options start much lower, from around AED 45 with EdFlik and from AED 33 with Tutopiya. Those are the market's numbers rather than ours. For IB Gram's own arrangement, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows it.

faqs.question: Which 0610 papers will my child sit at the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: An Extended candidate sits three components: the Extended multiple-choice paper, the Extended theory paper that includes supplement content, and one practical component, which is either the practical test or the written alternative to practical depending on what the school has chosen. The weightings are 30% for multiple choice, 50% for theory and 20% for the practical component. Half the grade therefore sits in a single paper, which is why theory technique is usually the first thing a tutor works on. Confirm the exact paper numbers on your child's entry with the school, because the practical choice is made at centre level.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for the practical test or the written alternative?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of science or the exams officer directly; it is a centre-level decision and they hold the entry details. It matters because the two components are prepared quite differently. The practical test is carried out under supervision with apparatus, while the written alternative asks the candidate to analyse somebody else's experiment on paper: identifying variables, completing results tables, plotting graphs, spotting anomalies and suggesting method improvements. Most Dubai students we support are entered for the written alternative, and it is the component least likely to have been practised at home, which makes it the quickest available improvement.

faqs.question: My son scored 42% in his Year 11 Biology mock - is that recoverable before the June series?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, but only once you know what the 42% is made of. A mark in the low forties can come from two or three unlearnt topics, from command-term errors spread thinly across the whole paper, from running out of time, or from an unprepared practical component, and the remedies for those are completely different. The first thing worth doing is a full past paper marked strictly to the published mark scheme with marks attributed to syllabus topics. From a January mock to a June series is roughly eighteen teaching weeks, which is enough to rebuild two or three topics properly and fix technique across all three papers.

faqs.question: How many of the twenty-one 0610 topics has a Dubai school usually finished by February of Year 11?
faqs.answer: It varies more than parents expect, because Dubai schools run the course over two or three years depending on when they start it. Some schools complete all twenty-one topics by the winter mock and spend the spring on revision; others are still teaching inheritance, variation and selection, or biotechnology and genetic modification in February. This is the single most useful thing to establish before planning support, because unlearnt content and forgotten content look identical in a mock percentage and need opposite responses. The school's scheme of work will tell you, and the topic map we build in week two records it.

faqs.question: Can my daughter move from Core to Extended Biology partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the school and on how close the final entry deadline is. The entry is made by the centre, based on classroom evidence and mock performance, and once the deadline passes it is fixed for that series. Cambridge entry deadlines sit months before the papers: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February. If a grade above a C matters for a sixth-form place, raise it with the head of science while the entry is still open, and bring marked evidence rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Do you send marked 0610 scripts to parents so we can see the mark scheme ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the point of the method rather than an added extra. Each marked paper comes back with the marks attributed question by question and annotations showing which mark-scheme point was awarded or missed. You can read it against the board's own published mark scheme, which is available on the Cambridge International website. We link to those documents rather than redistributing them, because they are Cambridge's copyright. If a provider offers you a download folder of mark schemes and subject guides, they do not have the right to hand those out.

faqs.question: Is a biological drawing question really worth revising for 0610?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the marks go for rules rather than for artistic ability. Examiners credit clean continuous lines with no shading, correct proportion between structures, labels on straight ruled lines that actually touch what they point at, and a magnification calculation carried out with consistent units. Students assume drawing is a talent and therefore skip it, which leaves marks on the table in a component already worth a fifth of the grade. It is also perfectly teachable over a shared screen, because in the exam the candidate is drawing from a provided image rather than from a specimen.

faqs.question: Does a Biology tutor working with my child in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. The official application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, with a stated two working day completion time.

faqs.question: How does IGCSE Biology count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Biology can sit inside that count of five like any other accredited subject. Equivalency is a Ministry process that IB Gram neither performs nor influences, so verify the current requirements through the Ministry's own channel before relying on them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a practical write-up without breaking Cambridge rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach experimental method, explain what a results analysis has to contain, show worked examples from released past questions, and give written feedback on a draft the student produced themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply text for a student to submit as their own. That boundary protects your child: work that is not their own is a malpractice matter with the examination board, and the consequences fall on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. Any operator offering completed work is selling a risk.

faqs.question: What time do your Dubai 0610 sessions run, given school finishes in the afternoon?
faqs.answer: Sessions are scheduled against Gulf Standard Time rather than a tutor's home timezone, and the common slots are between 16:30 and 21:00 on weekdays with weekend mornings also available. The realistic start time depends on your community: a family in Arabian Ranches whose child walks home can begin at 16:30, while a Jumeirah Village Circle family waiting on a school bus is usually better at 17:00 or later. Ramadan timings shift to post-iftar slots where families prefer that, and session times can be moved for the exam period.

faqs.question: What happens if the first 0610 tutor we try is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the match, without an argument about it. The free trial lesson exists partly to catch this before any money changes hands, but fit sometimes fails in week three rather than week one, and a fifteen-year-old who has stopped talking in sessions is not going to improve by persisting. There is no grade guarantee attached to any of this and no refund promise tied to an outcome, because neither would be honest. What is on offer is a documented plan, evidence you can read, and a different tutor if the evidence says the plan is not working.

intro.heading: The real question behind an online Biology search
paragraphs: Parents who type the phrase online tutor are rarely asking about software. They are asking whether a subject with a laboratory attached can be taught through a laptop, and that is a fair question about Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 in particular. A fifth of the grade comes from a practical component. Students are asked to draw specimens, calculate magnifications, build results tables, plot graphs and criticise somebody else's experimental method. On the face of it, none of that sounds like screen work.

The honest answer has two halves. Some of it transfers perfectly, and some of it was never going to be solved by a tutor in any format. What transfers is almost everything that carries marks. Biological drawing is marked against a set of rules rather than artistic skill, and the candidate in the exam is drawing from a printed image rather than from a specimen under a microscope, so practising from an image on a shared screen is practising the actual task. Magnification arithmetic is arithmetic. Variables, anomalies and method improvements are reasoning about a described experiment.

What does not transfer is handling apparatus, and no private tutor in any format fixes that, because the apparatus belongs to the school. A tutor working in a Dubai living room has no pipettes, no visking tubing and no potometer either. If your child is entered for the supervised practical test rather than the written alternative, the laboratory preparation has to come from the school, and the honest role of a tutor is to make the written components strong and to rehearse the reasoning that the practical test also rewards.

The second thing an online search is really asking about is time. Dubai school days finish in the early afternoon but bus routes and traffic mean many secondary students are not home and settled until well after four. A tutor who has to drive across the emirate cannot start at 16:30 and cannot reliably finish on time either. Removing the journey from both ends of the lesson is the most boring advantage of video delivery and probably the one that affects outcomes most, because a session that starts when it is supposed to is a session that happens every week.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform. Lessons for families in Dubai and across the Emirates are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Nothing on this page claims a regulator approval, an examination-board affiliation or a grade outcome, because none of those would be true. What follows is the mechanics of teaching 0610 through a screen, the Dubai calendar it has to fit inside, and the record you should be given.

programmes.description: Cambridge offers 9-1 graded versions of its IGCSE sciences alongside the A* to G versions, with the Biology variant carrying its own syllabus code. The content is closely aligned with the A* to G syllabus; what differs is the reporting scale, which matters when a family is comparing a Dubai result against a UK sibling's.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of Dubai centres use the 9-1 variants. Check the syllabus code printed on your child's statement of entry rather than assuming, because past papers and grade reporting follow the code, and a tutor preparing from the wrong one wastes time on the reporting side even if the biology is the same.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: The route many Dubai IB-continuum students take instead of IGCSE. MYP sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than by terminal papers, which produces students who are strong at investigation design and inquiry but unused to timed recall under exam conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB cohort, and some families move a child from an IB-continuum school into a British-curriculum school mid-secondary. A student arriving into Year 11 from MYP 4 generally needs exam-technique work rather than content work, and the diagnostic has to establish which.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Biology
programmes.description: The post-16 destination in Dubai's IB schools, available at Higher and Standard Level. It assumes fluency with enzymes, transport, respiration and genetics, and it adds a student-designed internal investigation on which a tutor may teach method and give feedback on the student's own drafts, nothing further.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools set their own Higher Level entry conditions, often referencing an IGCSE science grade. If Diploma Biology at Higher Level is the plan, the Extended-tier question at IGCSE stops being optional, and that conversation belongs in Year 10.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-onlin.subjectsIntro: The syllabus code on the statement of entry decides which past papers are useful. These are the science codes we are asked about most across Dubai, and the short version of what changes between them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Tiered, graded A* to G, twenty-one topics. Theory carries half the grade, multiple choice 30% and the practical component 20%. Supplement content for Extended candidates concentrates in transport, gas exchange, genetics and quantitative data handling.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 9-1 (0970)
subjects.description: The 9-1 graded counterpart to 0610 used by some centres. Content is closely aligned; the reporting scale differs. Always check which code appears on the entry before buying past papers or booking preparation.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The other board in regular Dubai use. Paper structure and practical arrangements differ from Cambridge, so 0610 past papers are a poor substitute. A tutor who does not ask which board is on the entry has not started work yet.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Two grades from one course covering all three sciences. The biology content maps onto 0610 but is reduced in depth, which makes it the usual destination for a student the school judges to be over-stretched by three separate sciences.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade across biology, chemistry and physics. Fewer guided learning hours than three separate sciences, and fewer than the double award, so post-16 science options need checking before a family agrees to a move.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside 0610 and frequently the weaker of the two, because the arithmetic load is heavier. Moles, stoichiometry and electrolysis absorb more tutoring time than any biology topic does.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Where graph skills and unit handling are tested hardest. A student who fixes unit conversion for physics usually finds the magnification and rate calculations in Biology stop costing marks as a side effect.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Relevant to Biology through percentage change, ratio, rates and graph reading. Students who lose Biology marks on calculation rather than recall are usually carrying a number problem rather than a science problem.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Long-answer Biology marks depend on precise wording. A student holding the biology in a second language can lose two marks per question to vocabulary rather than understanding, and that is diagnosable from a marked script.

subjects.name: A Level Biology
subjects.description: The common Dubai sixth-form continuation. Biochemistry, transport and genetics all return with far more quantitative demand, which is why Extended-tier fluency at IGCSE shortens the first term considerably.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-onlin.regionsIntro: The limiting factor on a weekday lesson is rarely the tutor's diary. It is when your child is home, fed and able to concentrate. These are the communities we schedule most 0610 sessions for, and what the local pattern usually allows.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment living with children bussed out to schools across the emirate. Return journeys are long and variable, so a 17:30 start holds better than a 16:30 one, and parents here more often use weekend morning slots for the full-length paper practice.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Similar pattern to Downtown with a younger family profile. Noise and shared space in apartments is a real constraint, so headphones and a fixed room matter as much as the timetable for a focused hour.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A single access road shapes everything. Families here consistently report that any lesson requiring a journey ends up starting late, which is why video delivery is the normal arrangement rather than the exception for secondary subjects.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities with established British-curriculum provision nearby and short journeys home. Afternoon slots from 16:00 work here, which suits a full-length practice paper on a weekday rather than at the weekend.

regions.name: Motor City and Sports City
regions.note: Mixed apartments and townhouses with schools inside the communities. Year 11 cohorts are moderate in size, so the specific topic a student is weak in often goes unaddressed by whole-class revision sessions.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A dense cluster of schools across several curricula, including British-curriculum streams running IGCSE sciences alongside large cohorts. Core and Extended tiers often sit in the same year group here, which makes the tier question urgent rather than academic.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Production City
regions.note: Western edge of the city, a long way from the schools in Jumeirah and Garhoud. Historically a thin local tutoring market for specific syllabus codes; online delivery makes the tier specialist the same distance away as everyone else.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Large apartment and townhouse populations with heavy school bus use. Evening sessions from 17:30 are the norm, and families often prefer two shorter sessions a week to one long one during the exam term.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and the coastal schools
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum provision inspected by KHDA, with science departments that generally complete the IGCSE syllabus before the winter mocks. Students we support from this cluster more often need technique work on the theory paper than fresh content teaching.

schoolClusters.city: Southern and new Dubai: Al Furjan, Sports City and Dubailand
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with growing secondary cohorts, where Year 11 groups can be small and revision provision varies year on year. Families we work with here often start earlier in Year 10 because whole-class catch-up sessions are not yet established.

The hour is split: a short recall check on two previously taught topics, then new teaching on the shared whiteboard, then a set of exam questions on what was just taught so the content is immediately tested in the form the paper will use.

sections.heading: What the first fifteen minutes of an online 0610 lesson contain
paragraphs: A screen-taught lesson lives or dies on whether the student is writing. The common failure of online tutoring is a tutor talking over slides while a fifteen-year-old nods, and that produces a pleasant hour and no marks. The arrangement that works is shared-screen work where the student holds the pen: an exam question on screen, the student annotating it, the tutor interrupting at the point the reasoning goes wrong rather than at the end.

So the first few minutes are a recall check rather than an introduction. Two questions on topics taught a fortnight ago, answered cold, on the whiteboard. This does two things at once. It tells the tutor whether the previous content held, which is the only honest basis for deciding what today's lesson should be, and it establishes within ninety seconds that this is an hour of work rather than an hour of listening. Students dislike it for about two weeks and then stop noticing.

The middle of the lesson is new teaching or paper repair, depending on the plan, and it is always followed by questions in exam format. Teaching a topic and then asking an exam question about it in the same hour is the difference between content a student recognises and content a student can use. Recognition is what produces the familiar complaint that revision was done and the mark did not move.

The last five minutes produce the artefacts. The whiteboard file is saved and sent, so the student has their own working rather than a textbook page. Where a family wants it, the session is recorded, which is genuinely useful in the fortnight before a paper: a student can watch the explanation of osmosis again at eleven at night without anybody being awake for it. None of this is possible with an in-home lesson, which leaves nothing behind but a parent's impression of how it went.

sections.heading: Teaching a laboratory subject through a screen: what transfers and what does not
paragraphs: This is the objection worth answering directly, because it is reasonable. The table below separates the skills the practical component actually tests from the things a parent imagines when they picture a biology lesson. The pattern is consistent: the marks sit in reasoning about experiments and in the conventions of recording results, both of which are paper skills. The apparatus handling that a screen cannot provide is also the part no private tutor provides in any format.

It is worth being precise about what the written alternative to practical paper asks for, because many Dubai parents assume it is a watered-down version of a real experiment. It is not. It presents a method somebody else carried out and asks the candidate to interrogate it: name the independent variable, identify what should have been controlled, read a value off a scale drawing, complete the results table with units in the headings, plot the points, identify the anomaly, suggest what a repeat would change. Those are the questions, and they are answered with a pen.

If your child is entered for the supervised practical test instead, the honest position is different. The school supplies the apparatus and the supervised session, and that is where the handling skill is built. What a tutor contributes is the reasoning layer that the practical test also rewards, plus the recording conventions, because candidates lose marks in a supervised test for exactly the same reasons they lose them on paper: untidy tables, missing units, graphs with badly chosen axes.

The final row of the table is the one families underestimate. Students who have watched a recorded explanation of a technique three times before the exam are better prepared than students who saw it live once, and only one of those two formats produces a recording.

sections.heading: Magnification, scale and the arithmetic hiding inside a biology paper
paragraphs: A surprising share of lost marks in 0610 are not biology errors. They are unit errors. Magnification questions give an image size and an actual size, or an image size and a magnification, and ask for the third quantity. The biology involved is nil. What defeats students is that one measurement is in millimetres and the other in micrometres, and the conversion goes the wrong way, which turns a correct method into a wrong number and costs the mark.

The fix is mechanical and it takes about two sessions. Convert everything to one unit before touching the formula. Write the formula down every time rather than rearranging it mentally. Check whether the answer is plausible: a plant cell is not four metres across, and a number that large means the conversion inverted. Students who adopt those three habits stop losing those marks, and the same habits transfer to rate calculations in respiration and to percentage change questions in transport and nutrition.

Scale drawings deserve their own attention. A question may ask a candidate to measure a structure on a printed diagram and use a stated magnification to find the real size. The measurement itself is a ruler skill, and it is the step students skip because it feels like the easy part. Measured to the nearest millimetre, with the ruler aligned to the right points, that step is worth as much as the calculation that follows it.

All of this is better taught over a screen than in a living room, which is counter-intuitive until you see it. The tutor can type the working out in a column, keep the student's attempt beside it, and leave both in the whiteboard file that gets sent afterwards. A student with ten worked magnification questions in their own file is a student who has something to revise from in May.

sections.heading: Command words that separate a B from an A* in 0610
paragraphs: Beyond the content, the difference between a mid grade and a top grade in 0610 is usually technique, and technique in a Cambridge paper means reading the command word correctly. The marks are allocated against specified points, and the command word tells you what kind of point will be credited. A candidate who treats describe and explain as synonyms will lose two or three marks per long-answer question without ever being wrong about the biology.

The table below sets out the ones that cost Dubai candidates most, based on the marked scripts we see rather than on a general list. The pattern across all of them is the same: the command word sets both the type of point and, implicitly, how many. Count the marks, plan that many distinct points, write them as separate statements. Students who learn to do that in October stop having a technique problem by January.

Second-language writers need one extra habit. Over-writing is the standard response to uncertainty: if the student is not sure which point earns the mark, they write the same idea three ways in the hope that one lands. The mark scheme credits the point once, so the long answer scores no better than the short one and costs four minutes that the paper does not have. Compression is a teachable skill and it shows up in the next marked script rather than in June.

The syllabus itself publishes the command-term definitions, and the mark schemes for released papers show them in operation. We reference and link those official documents on the Cambridge International website rather than reproducing them, because the material belongs to the board. A provider handing out mark-scheme folders as downloads is distributing something they have no right to distribute.

sections.heading: Fitting 0610 into the Dubai week
paragraphs: Scheduling is where online delivery earns its place most plainly, and it is worth being concrete about why. Dubai school days end early by international standards, but the gap between the final bell and a child being settled at a desk is long and unpredictable. School buses on routes serving several communities can take an hour. A parent collecting a child from a Jumeirah school to a Dubai Marina apartment at half past three is making a journey nobody can time reliably.

A tutor who has to make a journey too compounds that. The practical result is that in-home evening bookings are either scheduled late enough to be safe, which pushes a Year 11 session towards eight o'clock, or scheduled optimistically and then cut short. A video lesson starts when the student sits down. Over a thirty-week commitment that difference is worth several full sessions, which is more than most families gain by shopping for a lower hourly rate.

The weekly shape that works best for 0610 in Dubai is one content session mid-week and one shorter paper session at the weekend, with the weekend slot used for anything requiring full-length timing. Weekday evenings are a poor time to sit a ninety-minute paper after a full school day, and the score it produces is not a fair baseline. Saturday mornings consistently produce the most useful diagnostic scripts.

Ramadan shifts this, and it should. Families who prefer it move sessions to post-iftar slots, and the pre-dawn hours are not a sensible time for a Year 11 biology lesson regardless of anybody's energy levels. School timetables compress during Ramadan, which in practice means less new content is taught and the month is better used for retrieval and paper technique than for starting a difficult new topic such as inheritance or biotechnology.
