sections.heading: The numbers 0450 expects, and the sentence after each
paragraphs: 0450 is not an accounting qualification and it does expect arithmetic in four of its six units. The calculations are simple enough that a student who panics at numbers can be brought to reliability in two or three sessions, which makes this an unusually good return on tutoring time. The pattern of loss, though, is almost never the arithmetic.

What goes missing is the interpretation. A gross profit margin of 38% is a figure. The mark comes from saying what it means for this business, whether it is rising or falling, and what that implies about pricing or cost control. A current ratio of 1.4 is a figure; the mark comes from the statement about whether the firm can meet its short-term obligations and what the trend suggests. Students compute, underline the answer and stop, because computing feels like the task and the sentence feels like padding. It is the opposite.

The table below lists the calculations that recur with the interpretation each needs. Two deserve a note in prose. Added value is selling price less the cost of bought-in materials, and it is not profit, because profit deducts every other cost too. That confusion begins in Unit 1 and resurfaces in Unit 5 a year later. And break-even output is fixed costs divided by contribution per unit, where contribution is selling price minus variable cost per unit. Students who memorise the formula without the definition of contribution produce confident wrong answers.

The drill we use is a sheet of figures with no surrounding question, each needing one calculation and one interpretation sentence, marked only on whether the sentence is present and defensible. Twenty minutes, and it closes a leak that otherwise runs across both papers for the rest of the year.

sections.heading: Where marks go, unit by unit
paragraphs: Marked scripts in this subject fail in patterns that follow the units, which makes a unit-level diagnosis genuinely useful rather than merely tidy. The table below is the one we fill in from a full marked paper, and it usually shows two or three units carrying most of the loss rather than an even spread.

The pattern across Dubai students we mark is reasonably consistent. Unit 1 losses are definitional and cheap to fix. Unit 2 losses are almost all application: the theory of motivation and leadership is well known and applied without reference to the evidence, so students recommend a democratic style to a firm in crisis. Unit 5 losses are interpretation rather than arithmetic. Unit 6 losses come from students who also take economics and write economics answers.

Unit 3 deserves a separate note because it produces a distinctive error. Asked about one element of the marketing mix, students frequently discuss all four, which spreads the answer too thin for analysis marks on any of them. The fix is a reading habit rather than content: underline which element the question names before writing. It takes five seconds and recovers marks in most papers we have marked.

A unit diagnosis also tells you how long the work should take. Definitional gaps are a fortnight. Application habits are three or four sessions. Interpretation sentences are one session plus repetition. An actual content gap in a single unit is four to six weeks. Nothing in that list is a two-year programme, which is why the usual honest recommendation for a Year 11 student arriving after a mock is a targeted block rather than open-ended weekly support.

sections.heading: Finishing an answer: the justified recommendation
paragraphs: The higher-tariff parts of a 0450 paper very often ask the student to recommend a course of action and justify it. This is where evaluation marks sit, and it is the part of the paper most students write worst, because they treat the recommendation as a conclusion rather than as the thing being assessed.

A weak ending names an option and asserts it: the firm should train its staff. A strong ending does three things in two or three sentences. It makes a choice between the options the answer has discussed, not a new one. It gives the reason in terms of this business, usually referring to a number or a constraint from the insert. And it acknowledges what would have to be true for the recommendation to work, or what the firm risks if it is wrong. That third element is what distinguishes a justified recommendation from a preference.

There is a structural trap worth naming. Students who have carefully balanced two options through the body of an answer often refuse to choose at the end, finishing with a sentence saying both have merits. That is not evaluation; it is a declaration that the question has not been answered. The mark scheme asks for a judgement, and a student who has genuinely weighed both sides has already done the hard part and needs only to commit.

We drill this on endings alone. The student is given a completed answer, body only, and writes three different closing recommendations, each with a different basis: one on cost, one on time, one on risk. Then they decide which is strongest for the business described and say why. It takes fifteen minutes, it is the most mechanical piece of exam training in this subject, and it reliably moves the highest-tariff marks on the paper.

sections.heading: Using Dubai and UAE businesses as examples, honestly
paragraphs: Students in this city have an advantage in business studies and frequently misuse it. Dubai is a working illustration of nearly every topic in the syllabus: free zones and legal forms, logistics and operations, tourism seasonality and demand, retail competition, rapid growth and the financing of it. A student who can draw on that writes more confidently than one working entirely from textbook examples.

The discipline is that in the case-study paper the examples must come from the insert. An answer about a fictional firm in the insert that pivots into a paragraph about a real Dubai retailer has left the question. Outside knowledge belongs in the short-answer paper, where a question asking for an example of a business objective can legitimately be answered with a real one, and in the general-knowledge parts of either paper where no specific business is in play.

Where real examples are used, they have to be accurate. Inventing a figure for a named company, or stating a strategy a firm does not pursue, is a weak answer and a bad habit. In our sessions the rule is that any real-world claim has to be something the student could point to a source for. In practice that means examples stay broad and structural, that this sector behaves in a certain way in this market, rather than specific and unverifiable.

Local context is also useful for understanding rather than for quoting. A student who has watched a mall food court change its pricing across a summer has met price elasticity and demand seasonality directly, and that makes the textbook version easier to hold. We use those observations to teach, then make sure the written answer sources its evidence from the paper in front of the candidate.

sections.heading: Where 0450 sits in the UAE equivalency count
paragraphs: Dubai families planning for UAE university entry eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and it is worth knowing what it actually requires rather than what a tutoring page claims. On the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

0450 is an accredited IGCSE subject, so it can form part of that count. That is the direct answer to the question most parents are really asking. One competitor page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the sourced five-subject rule, so it is worth checking the number against the authority rather than against a tutoring site.

For the American track the requirements are different in kind: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in the source we have read, so no equivalency figure for the Diploma should be quoted without a reading from moe.gov.ae.

Three cautions apply to all of this. Requirements change, and the Ministry administers the process rather than any tutoring provider, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel. Nothing in the process requires tutoring, and anybody implying otherwise is making a false urgency claim about a regulatory procedure. And IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anybody; the table below points to where each requirement should be checked.

process.title: Send a marked case-study paper
process.description: A full attempt with the school's marking on it, not a single answer, because application failures only become visible across a whole paper. Which questions ignored the insert, where the recommendation was asserted, which units carried the loss: none of that shows up in one question or in a report comment.

process.title: A diagnostic answer, then a rewrite
process.description: In the first session the student writes one case-study answer under time, then rewrites it with evidence inserted and nothing else changed. Marking both shows the size of the application gap in a single number, which is more persuasive than any amount of advice.

process.title: Install the insert method in week one
process.description: The six-minute reading method is taught and timed before anything else, because every answer in the case-study paper depends on it. From then on the insert reading is timed separately in every attempt so it cannot quietly compress under pressure.

process.title: Attach interpretation to every calculation
process.description: Ratios, break-even and productivity are taught with the sentence that follows the figure, from the first time they appear. The twenty-minute figures drill is repeated until the sentence is automatic, because this leak otherwise runs across both papers all year.

process.title: Drill endings separately
process.description: Closing recommendations are practised on their own: three different endings to the same answer, each justified on a different basis, then a decision about which suits the business described. Fifteen minutes a session, aimed at the highest-tariff marks on the paper.

process.title: Review against the unit diagnosis every month
process.description: Each month we revisit the unit-level loss table from a fresh marked paper and decide whether to continue, shift the focus or stop. Most students show two or three units carrying the loss, and when those close the honest advice is often to finish.

whyPoints.title: Application is treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: In marked 0450 scripts from Dubai students, application is where most recoverable marks sit, and it is a writing habit rather than a knowledge gap. We drill it on rewrites marked for application alone, so the gain is attributable to one change rather than to general effort.

whyPoints.title: The insert gets its own six minutes
whyPoints.description: Reading the case study properly is the highest-leverage time on the paper and most students give it ninety seconds. The method is taught in session one and timed separately in every attempt afterwards, so it cannot compress away under exam pressure.

whyPoints.title: Every figure comes with its sentence
whyPoints.description: Ratios and break-even are easy to compute and routinely left uninterpreted, which leaves marks on the page in both papers. Calculations are taught with the interpretation attached from the first encounter rather than as a separate numeracy exercise.

whyPoints.title: Recommendations are drilled as endings
whyPoints.description: The highest-tariff parts ask for a justified recommendation, and most students assert one. Practising three different endings to the same answer, each on a different basis, is mechanical, quick and moves the marks that decide grades.

faqs.question: How is Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 assessed?
faqs.answer: By two written papers of equal weight, each eighty marks over an hour and a half, with no coursework. One is a short-answer and data-response paper covering the syllabus broadly. The other is a case-study paper where every question relates to a business described in an insert supplied with the paper. The syllabus sets four assessment objectives: knowledge and understanding, application, analysis and evaluation. Because the split is even, neither paper can be treated as the one that carries the grade. Confirm the current structure for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org, since Cambridge publishes syllabus revisions on a cycle.

faqs.question: What is the 0450 case study paper and how should my child prepare for it?
faqs.answer: An insert describing a business is supplied with the question paper, and every question relates to it. Preparation is a reading method rather than extra content. We teach a six-minute routine: identify what the business does, its sector and its stated problem; label every number in the insert and appendices without calculating anything; underline opinions and constraints; write two-word margin summaries; then name the business's two biggest problems before answering anything. Half the higher-tariff questions turn out to concern one of those problems. In timed practice the insert reading is clocked separately, because under pressure it otherwise compresses to nothing.

faqs.question: What does 'application' mean in 0450 marking, and how do students lose it?
faqs.answer: Application means the answer is about the business in the question, using its sector, size, stated problem, customers and the numbers given about it. Not the firm as a label, but the firm as evidence. Three patterns cost most of the marks: naming the business once at the start and then writing generically; recommending something the insert has already ruled out, usually from reading too little of it; and inventing a plausible detail the insert never supplied. The fix is a rewrite drill where an existing answer has evidence inserted and nothing else changed, marked on application alone, so the gain is attributable to one thing.

faqs.question: Which calculations does Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 expect?
faqs.answer: Added value, break-even output and the margin of safety, labour productivity, gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, the current ratio, the acid test ratio and market share, with cash-flow forecasting arithmetic in the finance unit. None is difficult, and a student who panics at numbers can usually be brought to reliability in two or three sessions. What costs marks is stopping at the figure. A current ratio of 1.4 is not an answer; the mark comes from the statement about whether short-term obligations can be met and which way the trend is going.

faqs.question: How should a 0450 answer that asks for a justified recommendation be finished?
faqs.answer: In two or three sentences doing three things. Choose between the options the answer has already discussed rather than introducing a new one. Give the reason in terms of this business, citing a figure or a constraint from the insert. Then state what would have to be true for the recommendation to work, or what the firm risks if it is wrong. The common trap is refusing to choose and concluding that both options have merits, which reads as a non-answer rather than as balance. A student who has genuinely weighed both sides has done the hard part and needs only to commit.

faqs.question: Which 0450 units do Dubai students find hardest?
faqs.answer: In the papers we mark, losses concentrate rather than spread. Unit 2 on people in business produces the most application failures, because motivation and leadership theory is well known and applied without reference to the evidence, so students recommend a democratic style to a firm in crisis. Unit 5 on financial information produces interpretation failures rather than arithmetic ones. Unit 3 produces a distinctive error where a question names one element of the marketing mix and the student discusses all four, spreading the answer too thin for analysis marks. Unit 1 losses are definitional and the cheapest of all to fix.

faqs.question: Can my child use real Dubai businesses as examples in 0450 answers?
faqs.answer: In the case-study paper, no: the examples must come from the insert, and an answer that pivots into a paragraph about a real local retailer has left the question. In general questions on the other paper, a real example can be entirely appropriate. Where real examples are used they must be accurate, so keep them structural rather than specific: how a sector behaves in this market rather than an invented figure for a named company. Living in Dubai is genuinely useful for understanding seasonality, logistics, free-zone legal forms and retail competition, and that understanding should inform the thinking while the script cites the paper.

faqs.question: Should my child take Business Studies 0450 or Economics 0455 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They reward different kinds of thinking. 0450 applies reasoning to a named business through a case study, with accounting-style arithmetic and an application objective that has no equivalent in economics. 0455 applies reasoning to market models and diagrams, has a multiple-choice component, and uses elasticity and index arithmetic. Students who like concrete situations and evidence usually do better in 0450; those who like models and abstraction usually prefer 0455. Where a school allows both, the external-influences unit overlaps usefully, but the two answer shapes interfere, so each task should begin by naming which paper's rules apply.

faqs.question: Is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business 4BS1 the same as Cambridge 0450?
faqs.answer: The content territory overlaps substantially and the assessment does not. Paper structures, question tariffs and mark-scheme wording differ, which makes past-paper practice board-specific: a student revising Cambridge case studies for a Pearson entry is practising the right business content in the wrong format. Ask your school's exams officer which board and specification code appears on the entry, then work only from that board's published materials. Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so take dates from the live official timetable rather than from any restated version.

faqs.question: Does 0450 count towards the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: 0450 is an accredited IGCSE subject, so it can form part of the count. The British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five. One competitor page ranking for these searches states that six subjects are required, which does not match the sourced rule, so check the number against the authority. Requirements change and the Ministry administers the process, so verify on moe.gov.ae or through your emirate's attestation channel.

faqs.question: How much accounting is in Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450?
faqs.answer: Enough to be a real part of the course and much less than a separate accounting qualification. Students meet income statements, statements of financial position, cash-flow forecasting, the distinction between cash and profit, and profitability and liquidity ratios, alongside break-even analysis in the operations unit. The documents are read and interpreted rather than prepared from scratch. In marked scripts the arithmetic is usually right; what is missing is the conclusion drawn from it. A student who also takes Accounting has an advantage on the numbers and often a disadvantage on the answer shape, because the two subjects reward different endings.

faqs.question: Can a 0450 student see the case study insert before the exam?
faqs.answer: No. The insert is supplied with the question paper in the exam room, which is exactly why the reading method matters so much: six minutes of disciplined annotation is the only preparation available for material nobody has seen. What can be prepared is the routine itself, rehearsed on past inserts until it runs automatically under time. Students who practise on past papers are practising the method rather than the content, and that is the right way to use them. Past papers and inserts are published by Cambridge on cambridgeinternational.org, which is where they should be obtained; we link to the official source rather than redistributing it.

faqs.question: How many weeks of 0450 tutoring does a Dubai Year 11 student need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect, if the diagnosis is done first. A full marked paper usually shows two or three units carrying most of the loss plus an application habit, and that converts into a targeted block of known length. Definitional gaps take a fortnight. The application rewrite drill takes three or four sessions. Interpretation sentences take one session plus repetition. A genuine content gap in one unit takes four to six weeks. None of that is a two-year programme, and a tutor proposing comprehensive weekly support before seeing any of your child's written work is proposing a subscription rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Does 0450 lead naturally into Cambridge A Level Business 9609?
faqs.answer: It prepares the content and under-prepares the standard. 9609 extends into strategy, human resource theory and more demanding financial analysis, and the case material is longer and less pre-digested. The structural change that catches students is evaluation: a recommendation that is justified at IGCSE needs to be weighed against alternatives at AS. Students who learned at 0450 to anchor every point in evidence scale well, because the habit is exactly what the harder paper wants more of. Those who scored well on content alone often find the first AS case study difficult in a way their IGCSE grade did not predict, and a few sessions after the IGCSE papers prevent that.

faqs.question: How do online 0450 sessions handle case-study reading practice?
faqs.answer: The insert goes on a shared screen and the annotation happens live, which is easier to supervise online than across a table because both people see the same marks appearing on the same document. The student annotates while the tutor watches in silence for the six timed minutes, and then the annotation itself is audited before any answer is written: are the numbers labelled, are the constraints underlined, are the two biggest problems named. That audit is the part that changes marks, and it needs the tutor looking at the student's own marked-up insert rather than describing what good annotation would look like.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-business-studies-0.closingHeading: Start with one marked case-study paper
dubai/cambridge-igcse-business-studies-0.closingBody: The fastest way into a useful 0450 plan is a complete marked case-study attempt. It shows which units carry the loss, whether the insert was read or skimmed, how many answers would have been equally true of any business, and whether the recommendations were justified or asserted. Those four readings produce a block of work with a known length rather than an open-ended arrangement. Send the paper, take the diagnostic session, and ask for the application rewrite in the first hour. If the rewrite moves the mark with the content unchanged, you know exactly what you are buying and roughly how long you will need it.

intro.heading: Chemistry tutoring you can audit
paragraphs: There is a particular frustration Dubai parents describe about science tutoring, and it is not about price or availability. It is that nothing is checkable. A tutor arrives, an hour passes behind a closed door, the report is that your son is getting there, and in August a grade arrives that either justifies the year or does not. No marked work, no record of what was attempted, nothing that could be compared with what the school says. By the time the evidence exists, the series is over.

The alternative is not complicated, it is just rarely offered: write everything down in a form that survives the week. In practice that means three documents. An error ledger, which lists every lost mark from every marked script by cause and by topic area, with a running total. A fortnightly pack, which is the ledger plus the marked script plus two lines on what the next fortnight will do. And a termly review, which sets the first ledger against the current one so a term's work can be judged rather than believed. None of that requires new technology. It requires that somebody marks the work and keeps the record.

For chemistry specifically, the record matters more than in most subjects, because 0620 hides its causes well. Twelve topic areas sit in the syllabus and one of them, stoichiometry, is the machinery that at least six of the others run on. A student insecure in moles will lose marks in acids and bases, in electrochemistry, in energetics, in the metals questions and in the analysis questions, and the school's own data will show a general chemistry weakness. The ledger shows something different: the same cause appearing in five different topics. That is a four to six session repair presenting itself as a syllabus-wide problem, and only the record tells the two apart.

The honest position on delivery, stated before you read any further. The URL says home tutor because that is what Dubai families type, and the question behind it is a fair one. IB Gram does not send tutors to houses, villas or apartments anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is something we run only in India. Chemistry lessons for Dubai students are delivered live online, one to one, over video, with a shared screen for equations and mechanisms. One consequence is directly relevant to this page: when the work happens on a shared screen, the evidence trail is automatic. Every annotated equation and every marked script already exists as a file, which is why the documentation is routine rather than an extra service.

What follows is the detail. How the ledger is built in the first fortnight, what the twelve topics usually reveal, what each document is for, why a mark gain often does not move a grade, how the formats compare on what you can actually verify, how to read your centre's own mock history, and where the boundaries sit on what a tutor may touch.

programmes.description: Three years of combined science before the IGCSE option choice, with Checkpoint tests at the end of Year 9 in March, May and October windows. Assessment is largely internal and descriptive, so there is very little marked external-standard work for a parent to look at, and almost no calculation.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is the stage where a numerical weakness becomes invisible rather than absent. A student can finish Year 9 with good science reports and no experience of a quantitative chemistry question. An early diagnostic in Year 9 is the cheapest evidence a family can buy, because it reveals the gap before the 0620 content starts arriving.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Twelve topic areas, no coursework, examined through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component. Core candidates cap at grade C; Extended candidates reach A*. Every mark is examined externally, which means there is an enormous amount of past material against which a student's work can be marked honestly.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where the ledger approach earns its keep in Dubai, because schools vary widely in how much marked work they return. Some send every assessment home annotated; others report a percentage. Where the school returns little, a tutor's marked scripts are the only external-standard evidence a family has.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Criterion-based assessment against four strands rather than paper weightings, with investigation and reflection tasks carrying real weight. Students receive criterion levels rather than marks, which is informative about skills and unhelpful for predicting performance on a timed written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and enter students for external IGCSE papers alongside it, or move them into a Cambridge pathway at Year 10. Those students need marked timed papers specifically, because criterion levels do not tell a family how a ninety-minute written chemistry paper will go.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level Chemistry
programmes.description: Where 0620 leads for Dubai students continuing the subject. AS Chemistry treats mole calculations as reflex background, adds organic mechanisms with electron movement shown, quantitative equilibrium and a formal practical skills assessment. The step is largest for students who reached a strong IGCSE grade through worked-example recall.
programmes.countryNote: Entry commonly requires a grade A or B at Extended 0620 at Dubai schools, and chemistry is a prerequisite for medicine and many engineering routes. Where that threshold is live, the ledger becomes a planning document: it shows whether the gap to the threshold is one cause or several.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-hom.subjectsIntro: The subjects Dubai families most often ask about alongside Chemistry 0620, described by what a marked script in each one actually reveals. The evidence looks different in each case, and that changes what is worth tracking.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: A marked 0620 script separates cleanly into calculation losses, equation-writing losses, description losses and practical-skills losses. That separation is what makes the subject unusually diagnosable: the same script shows whether the problem is arithmetic, chemical language or exam technique.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: A marked biology script shows language precision above all. Lost marks cluster on answers that are nearly right in everyday terms and wrong in the mark scheme's terms, which is why a biology ledger tracks wording rather than topics in its first column.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: A marked physics script reveals unit and prefix handling faster than any other subject, because the errors are visible as answers out by factors of a thousand. Shares the practical component's skills with chemistry closely enough that one repair covers both.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The script that most often explains a chemistry ledger. Where chemistry losses trace to ratio, proportion, rearrangement or standard form, the same errors appear in the maths paper in undisguised form, and the cheaper intervention is usually there.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Combined papers mean a marked script shows recall switching between disciplines as a separate skill. Students lose marks at the seams, where a question moves from a chemical idea to a biological one, and that pattern only shows up on a full paper rather than on topic exercises.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: A marked 0606 script is a useful control. A student secure here whose chemistry calculations still fail is not having an arithmetic problem, which narrows the chemistry diagnosis to chemical reasoning and saves weeks of misdirected work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Relevant because multi-clause chemistry question stems are a reading problem before they are a chemistry one. A marked ESL script showing comprehension losses often predicts chemistry marks lost on questions the student could otherwise answer.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Its data-response questions test the same skills as the chemistry practical paper: describe a trend, quote figures with units, identify an anomaly and suggest a cause. A strong geography data script is evidence that practical-paper losses are conventions rather than reasoning.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside chemistry by Dubai students keeping two routes open. Its marked scripts show command-term discipline clearly, and a student who separates explain from describe in business usually can in chemistry once the convention is named.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Marked scripts here show method-shown-versus-answer-asserted habits more starkly than any other subject, because partially correct algorithms earn partial marks only when written out. The same habit transfers directly to chemistry calculation layout.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-hom.regionsTitle: Where our 0620 students study, and when the evidence arrives
dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-hom.regionsIntro: Sessions reach every Dubai community over video, so these notes are not about distance. They describe when the school clusters in each area generate marked work, because the assessment calendar decides when a ledger can first be built from real evidence rather than from a diagnostic.

regions.note: Long-established British school catchments with autumn assessment cycles that return annotated work. Families here often arrive with a folder of marked papers already, which means the first session can skip the diagnostic and go straight to the ledger.

regions.note: A dense cluster of secondary schools with early mock calendars, often in late November. That makes the autumn half term the natural point to start, so a ledger exists before the mock rather than being built from it.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Lakes
regions.note: Smaller sets at higher-fee schools, with detailed written reporting as standard. The useful work here is comparison: setting the school's own assessment data beside externally marked scripts to see whether the two agree.

regions.name: Green Community and Dubai Investment Park
regions.note: Schools serving a spread-out catchment with assessment weeks that fall later in each term. Diagnostic papers matter more in this area because less marked work comes home before February.

regions.name: Remraam and Dubailand Residences
regions.note: Newer communities with large year groups and percentage-based reporting rather than annotated scripts. Almost every family here starts with a diagnostic paper, since there is no external-standard marked work to read.

regions.name: Al Mizhar and Al Twar
regions.note: Mixed curriculum intakes where some students sit IGCSE alongside another qualification. The ledger separates the two workloads, which is often the first time a family sees which subject is actually absorbing the study time.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Knowledge Village
regions.note: International schools with International Baccalaureate and Cambridge pathways side by side. Students moving between criterion-based and marks-based assessment need timed marked papers early, because criterion levels do not predict paper performance.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with early autumn assessment cycles
schoolClusters.note: These schools generate marked work before December, so a ledger can be built from the school's own evidence rather than from a diagnostic. Students we support from this group typically arrive in October with a mock already behind them.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools running IGCSE alongside criterion-based assessment
schoolClusters.note: Students here receive criterion levels for much of their science work and sit external papers as well. The gap between the two kinds of feedback is the reason families from this group ask for marked timed papers specifically.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-hom.modesIntro: Three ways the documented approach runs, differing in how often evidence is generated rather than in teaching style. All are delivered live online, one to one, over video with a shared annotated screen.

modes.title: Diagnostic and ledger build
modes.description: Two to three sessions that exist to produce evidence rather than to teach. Your child sits paper sections unaided under timing, the work is marked against the published scheme, and the first ledger is built. Families frequently stop here, take the ledger to the school, and decide afterwards.

Every lost mark logged by cause and by topic

No commitment to further sessions attached

modes.title: Weekly sessions with a fortnightly pack
modes.description: The standard arrangement across a term or a year. One session a week on the cause the ledger ranks first, with a marked timed section every second week so the ledger stays current. The pack lands on a fixed day so you know when to expect it.
bullets: Fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time

modes.description: A self-contained run on the practical paper, which carries a fifth of the grade and generates the clearest evidence in the subject because its mark scheme is so consistent. Progress here is visible within two sessions, which makes it a useful place to start when a family is unsure about tutoring at all.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family is really asking for with cambridge IGCSE chemistry 0620 home tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: The search is for somebody competent, nearby and accountable. The market answers the first two and almost never the third. Agencies in Dubai will place a qualified adult in your sitting room for somewhere between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, from a pool limited to whoever can reach your community before the session starts. Marketplaces will list independent tutors by neighbourhood with no verification. In both cases what you get back at the end of an hour is a verbal impression.

The accountability gap is the one worth closing, and it is not a function of where the tutor sits. A tutor in your kitchen can keep no records at all; a tutor on a screen can keep every one. What matters is whether the work gets marked to the standard the examination will use, and whether the result is written down somewhere you can read it. So the honest framing of the choice is not online against in-home, it is documented against undocumented, and the formats differ only in which one makes documentation automatic.

On the in-home question directly, because you asked it by searching: IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai, and tutors are not sent to any UAE address. That service exists only in India. For a student who needs an adult physically present in order to work at all, an in-home arrangement has a real advantage that a screen does not match, and we will say so on a call rather than take a booking we think will fail. For everything else, the case for online is that the specialist pool is not limited by driving distance and the evidence trail already exists as files.
bullets: Dubai in-home market rate: roughly AED 180-500 per hour with travel included
What is usually missing is a record, not a qualification
Online delivery makes the evidence trail automatic rather than extra
No tutor is placed in a UAE home; that is an India-only service

sections.heading: The first fortnight: building the chemistry error ledger
paragraphs: The ledger is a single page with one row per lost mark, collapsed into classes. Your child sits sections of a recent paper at the right tier, unaided, under timing. Each lost mark is then assigned a cause and a topic area, and the causes total up. The output is not a percentage but a sentence of the form: fourteen marks lost to mole-ratio setup across four topics, seven to unbalanced equations, five to describe-versus-explain, three to significant figures.

That sentence is what makes the plan arguable rather than assumed. A family looking at fourteen marks concentrated in one cause can see why four sessions on stoichiometry comes before any revision of organic chemistry, even though organic chemistry is what the school is teaching this month. Without the ledger, that sequencing decision looks like a tutor's preference. With it, the sequencing is arithmetic, and you can disagree with it on the evidence if you want to.

The error classes in chemistry are stable enough to tabulate. Mole-ratio setup, equation balancing, state symbols and formulae, observation versus explanation, particle-level reasoning, significant figures and units, and practical conventions account for the overwhelming majority of lost marks on 0620 scripts we mark from Dubai schools. Each has a recognisable look on the page and a different repair length, which is the information in the table below. The point of naming them is that each repair is far shorter than reteaching a topic, and several transfer across the whole syllabus.

sections.heading: Twelve topics, one tally: where the evidence usually points
paragraphs: The second column of the ledger is topic, and it behaves differently from the cause column. Causes concentrate; topics spread. A single insecure cause will light up five topics, which is exactly why a topic-only reading of a script sends families towards a general chemistry rescue when a specific repair would do. Reading the two columns together is the whole technique.

Across the 0620 scripts we mark from Dubai schools, the first diagnosis lands in recognisable places. Stoichiometry is the most common and the most consequential, because it is upstream of so much else. Acids, bases and salts is the most common presenting complaint, because it is where the mole problem first becomes visible to a student. Electrochemistry produces the most confident wrong answers, because students learn the anode and cathode rules as labels rather than as electron destinations. Organic chemistry generates the most anxiety and often the fewest actual lost marks, since its questions are more predictable than their reputation.

The table sets out what a first diagnosis most often finds in each area. It is not a prediction about your child; it is a description of the pattern, which tells you what kind of finding to expect and what evidence it rests on. Where your child's ledger disagrees with it, the ledger is right and the pattern is irrelevant. That is the point of keeping one rather than working from a general impression of what Year 11 students find hard.

sections.heading: What arrives in your inbox, and what each document decides
paragraphs: Documentation only helps if it is short and if each piece supports a specific decision. Four documents do the work, and none of them takes more than five minutes to read. Sending a parent a twelve-page report every month is not transparency; it is a way of being unreadable while appearing thorough.

The marked script is the raw evidence: your child's own handwriting, annotated with the mark-scheme wording that earned or missed each mark. The ledger is the summary, one page, causes and topics with running totals. The fortnight note is two lines saying what the next two weeks will target and why, which is where you can push back. The termly review puts the first ledger beside the current one, and it is the only document that can honestly answer whether the term worked.

What this is for, beyond reassurance, is leverage. Dubai schools respond to specifics. A parent who writes to a head of science saying my daughter seems to be struggling in chemistry receives a sympathetic reply. A parent who writes saying her last two marked papers show nineteen marks lost to mole-ratio setup across four topics, and we would like to discuss whether the Extended entry is still right, receives a meeting. Families use these documents most often for exactly that conversation, and for tier and set decisions where evidence beats advocacy. The pack is also portable: it belongs to you, it survives a change of tutor or of school, and nothing in it depends on our continued involvement to remain readable.

sections.heading: Why marks move before grades do
paragraphs: The most common disappointment in a documented approach is a term where the ledger improves and the grade does not. It is worth understanding why that happens, because the instinct is to conclude the tutoring failed when the evidence usually says the opposite.

Grades are awarded against boundaries, and boundaries are not fixed percentages. They are set after each series in light of how the cohort performed and how demanding the paper proved to be. So a student who gains nine marks across a paper may cross a boundary or may land just below the same one they were below before. Nine marks is nine marks either way, and in the next series with a slightly different paper those nine marks are what moves the grade. A ledger showing nineteen lost marks reduced to ten is unambiguous progress regardless of the letter it produced on one occasion.

This is also the reason no honest provider promises a grade. Nobody controls the paper, the cohort or the boundary. What can be stated is what the evidence shows: which causes have reduced, by how many marks, and which remain. We will not publish a figure for typical improvement either, because any such number without a stated sample, date and method is unverifiable, and this market is full of them. The claim we will make is narrower and checkable: you will hold the marked work, so the question of whether progress happened is yours to answer rather than ours to assert.
bullets: Grade boundaries are set per series, not fixed at a percentage

sections.heading: In-home or online, judged on what you can actually verify
paragraphs: Most comparisons of these two formats argue about atmosphere. The more useful comparison asks what a parent can check afterwards, because that is the thing that determines whether a term's spend was worthwhile and the thing both formats are usually silent about.

The differences are concrete. In-home work happens on paper that stays in the house or leaves with the tutor; online work happens on a board that is saved as a file. In-home marking depends entirely on whether the tutor chooses to do it and keep it; online marking lands in your inbox because the script was already digital. An in-home session leaves a memory; a recorded session leaves a recording your child can re-watch the week before a mock. None of this makes an in-home tutor worse at chemistry. It makes the in-home arrangement harder to audit, and auditing is what this page is about.

The honest entries in the table are the ones where in-home wins. Physical presence for a student who needs supervision. Reading a teenager's body language, which is harder on a screen. Writing equations by hand side by side, which some students genuinely find easier than a tablet. Those are real, and they are why we tell some Dubai families that the online format is the wrong purchase for their child. The rest of the comparison favours the documented, online arrangement, and the reason is mechanical rather than philosophical: work that is already a file gets marked, stored and sent without anyone having to decide to do it.

sections.heading: Mock to final: reading your centre's own history
paragraphs: One piece of evidence costs nothing and almost no Dubai family asks for it: how mock grades at your child's school have mapped onto final grades in recent series. Schools hold this. Heads of science generally know it. It changes how a mock result should be read, and therefore whether a panic in December is warranted.

Some centres mark mocks deliberately harshly, using boundaries a grade stricter than the real ones, on the view that a shock in December produces work in January. At those schools a grade five mock is routinely a grade six or seven in June, and a family that spends the Christmas holiday in crisis has misread a deliberate signal. Other centres set mocks on generous internal boundaries or on a paper the class has partly seen, and at those schools a comfortable mock is not evidence of anything. Knowing which kind of school you are in is the single most valuable piece of context for interpreting your child's marks.

Alongside that, ask two further questions. Which paper was the mock drawn from, and was it at the right tier? A Core-tier mock tells you nothing about Extended readiness, and a mock built from a paper the class worked through in lessons measures recall of that lesson rather than chemistry. The ledger approach handles this by marking unseen past-paper sections at the correct tier, which is a different measurement from the school's and is meant to be compared with it rather than to replace it. Where the two disagree sharply, that disagreement is itself the finding worth taking to the school.
bullets: Ask how mocks have mapped to final grades at your centre recently
Check which paper the mock came from and at which tier
A mock drawn from material taught in class measures recall of the lesson
Where school data and unseen marked scripts disagree, that is the finding

sections.heading: Ramadan, half terms and planning evidence around a Dubai year
paragraphs: A documented approach depends on regular marked work, and the Dubai academic year does not run evenly. Half terms, National Day, Ramadan with its shortened school days and shifted family routines, Eid, and the long summer all interrupt the fortnightly rhythm. A plan built as though the year were uniform collapses at the first interruption and then quietly stops producing evidence at all.

The practical answer is to plan the interruptions in rather than around. During Ramadan, sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing, and families frequently reduce frequency for the month rather than cancelling, which keeps the ledger alive at a lower intensity. Half terms are the best windows in the year for a practical-component block, because it is self-contained and does not depend on the school's teaching sequence continuing. The weeks either side of a mock are for timed papers rather than new content, since that is when a marked unseen paper is most informative.

The summer is the most misused period. Students who finish Year 10 with an unsecured mole concept arrive in Year 11 in September and have the remaining syllabus taught on top of a gap, and that is the single most common way a 0620 grade ends up below potential. Six to eight sessions across July and August on stoichiometry alone, documented in a ledger, is the highest-leverage block available in this subject, and it is also the easiest to schedule because nothing competes with it. Where families travel over the summer, the online format follows the timezone rather than ending the arrangement.
bullets: Move sessions to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan rather than cancelling
Use half terms for the self-contained practical-component block
Keep the weeks around a mock for timed unseen papers

sections.heading: What a tutor may do to a piece of chemistry work
paragraphs: A documented approach raises an obvious question: if a tutor is marking and annotating your child's work, where is the line? For Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry the answer is clean, because 0620 carries no coursework. Every mark comes from a paper sat under supervision at the centre, so there is no assessed artefact a tutor could improperly influence. Marking practice papers is marking practice, not marking an assessment.

The line matters more at the next stage, and it is worth knowing now because many Dubai students move into an International Baccalaureate Diploma where chemistry carries an internally assessed investigation. There the rule is strict and does not change with the price paid: a tutor may teach the method, discuss the plan, explain the assessment criteria and give feedback on a student's own draft, and may never write, complete or redraft the work. Providers selling finished internal assessments exist in this market and the student carries the consequence, which under academic-honesty rules can be severe.

Two further boundaries apply regardless of stage. Syllabus documents, question papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the board's copyright property, so a tutor cites them and points to the official source rather than distributing a folder of files. And diagnostic work has to be the student's own or it diagnoses nothing, which is why the trial session has your child writing rather than watching. On permits: private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, with the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring in the UAE without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure quoted elsewhere is unsourced.
bullets: 0620 carries no coursework: every mark is examined at the centre

process.title: Send whatever marked chemistry work exists
process.description: Photographs of annotated papers, assessment sheets, even a scribbled teacher comment. If nothing has come home, say so, because that tells us the first sessions need to generate evidence rather than read it. Either way the first conversation starts from paper.

process.title: Sit a short unaided diagnostic
process.description: Sections spread across the twelve topic areas, at the tier your child is entered for, under timing and without help. This runs as the free trial session with no card details requested, and the marked result is yours whether or not anything follows.

process.title: Receive the first ledger
process.description: One page: lost marks by cause, by topic, with totals. It arrives before any teaching plan is proposed, so the plan can be argued about on evidence. Several families take this document to the school and come back later, which is a legitimate use of it.

process.title: Agree the first two causes and the order
process.description: The ledger usually points at two causes rather than twelve topics. Those two, in a stated order, become the block. Everything else is explicitly parked, so later you can check whether the stated plan is the plan that actually ran.

process.title: Fortnightly packs, termly review
process.description: A marked script, an updated ledger and a two-line note every fortnight in term time. Once a term the first ledger goes beside the current one, and that comparison decides whether to continue, change the frequency or stop.

whyPoints.title: Everything is written down
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, a causes ledger with running totals, a two-line plan note and a termly comparison. The question of whether a term of chemistry tutoring worked becomes something you can answer from documents rather than something you have to take on trust.

whyPoints.title: Causes are tracked separately from topics
whyPoints.description: One insecure cause lights up five topic areas and looks like a syllabus-wide problem. Keeping the two columns apart is what turns a term of general chemistry rescue into a four to six session repair, and it only works if somebody keeps the record.

whyPoints.title: The evidence is yours to keep
whyPoints.description: Packs, scripts and ledgers belong to you, including after the arrangement ends. Families most often use them for tier and set conversations with a Dubai head of science, where specific mark counts carry more weight than a parent's impression.

whyPoints.title: No improvement statistics, because none would be verifiable
whyPoints.description: You will not find a percentage of students who improved on this page. A statistic without a sample, a date and a method is unverifiable, and this market is full of them. What is offered instead is your own child's marked work, fortnight by fortnight.

whyPoints.title: Direct about the format and its limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online over video; no tutor is placed in a UAE home. Where a student needs physical supervision more than a chemistry specialist, an in-home arrangement is genuinely better and we will say that on the call instead of taking the booking.

faqs.question: What exactly do I receive after a fortnight of chemistry sessions?
faqs.answer: Three things, none longer than a page. Your child's marked script, annotated with the mark-scheme wording that earned or missed each mark. The error ledger, listing lost marks by cause and by topic area with running totals carried from the previous pack. And a two-line note saying what the next fortnight will target and why. The whole pack takes about five minutes to read. A twelve-page monthly report is not transparency; it is a way of being thorough and unreadable at the same time.

faqs.question: My daughter's marks went up eight but her grade did not change. Is that progress?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the ledger is the reason you can tell. Grade boundaries are set after each series according to how the cohort performed and how demanding the paper was, so eight marks may cross a boundary or land just below the same one. The marks themselves are the durable gain: in the next series, with a different paper, those eight are what moves the letter. A ledger showing nineteen lost marks reduced to eleven is unambiguous whatever grade the single occasion produced.

faqs.question: Can I see the mark scheme wording you used on my son's script?
faqs.answer: It is written on the script. Where a mark was missed, the annotation quotes what the published scheme accepts, next to what your son wrote. That comparison is usually the most useful thing in the pack, because the gap is often small and specific: the current increases rather than the current gets bigger, bond breaking is endothermic rather than energy is needed. We work from and cite the official Cambridge documents rather than distributing them, since they are the board's copyright material.

faqs.question: Do you keep a record I can show my child's school?
faqs.answer: That is one of the main uses families make of it. The ledger is a one-page document with mark counts by cause and topic, and Dubai heads of science respond to that in a way they do not respond to a general concern. Parents most often use it for tier conversations, set placement and questions about whether an Extended entry is still appropriate. The pack belongs to you, including after the arrangement ends, and nothing in it depends on our continued involvement.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a chemistry tutor is diagnosing or just teaching?
faqs.answer: Ask for the first session's output in writing before the second session. A tutor who is diagnosing can tell you which causes the lost marks fell into and roughly how many marks each cause cost. A tutor who is teaching will describe topics covered. Both can be good teachers, but only the first can explain why they are spending four weeks on moles while the school teaches organic chemistry. If the answer to why this order is because it is the next chapter, you are buying coverage rather than repair.

faqs.question: Which 0620 topic does the first diagnosis most often land on?
faqs.answer: Stoichiometry, by a wide margin, and usually presenting as something else. Acids and bases is the most common complaint because that is where a mole weakness first becomes visible to a student, but the cause sits upstream. Electrochemistry produces the most confident wrong answers, since anode and cathode get learned as labels rather than as electron destinations. Organic chemistry generates the most anxiety and often the fewest real losses, because its question styles are more predictable than their reputation suggests.

faqs.question: My son's school does not return marked papers. What can we use instead?
faqs.answer: Unseen past-paper sections at the correct tier, sat under timing in the first sessions. That is less convenient than reading the school's own marking and in one way better, because it is a measurement nobody has coached. Where a school reports percentages only, this is the sole external-standard evidence a family has. We mark it to the published scheme and build the ledger from it, then compare with whatever the school does report. Sharp disagreement between the two is itself worth raising with the head of science.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Dubai for chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not arrange home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Chemistry lessons for Dubai students are delivered live online, one to one, over video, with a shared screen for equations and mechanisms. If your child needs an adult physically in the room to sit down and work, an in-home arrangement is genuinely the better purchase and we will say so on the call. Market rates for that in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan timings change the session plan?
faqs.answer: Sessions commonly move to post-Iftar slots, and most families reduce frequency for the month rather than stopping, which keeps the ledger alive at lower intensity. School days are shortened, routines shift, and a plan that assumes an unbroken fortnightly rhythm simply breaks. Planning the month in advance works better than renegotiating it weekly. The documentation adapts too: a single marked script for the month rather than two, with the note saying explicitly that the pace was reduced by agreement rather than by drift.

faqs.question: What happens if the evidence says the tutoring is not working?
faqs.answer: The termly review is designed to surface exactly that, by setting the first ledger beside the current one. If the targeted causes have not reduced, the sequence changes or the arrangement ends. Continuing unchanged while the record shows no movement is the failure mode a documented approach exists to prevent. Sometimes the finding is that the real problem lies elsewhere, most often in mathematics or in supervision, and in both cases the honest recommendation is to spend the money there instead.

faqs.question: How many marks is a realistic gain over a term in 0620?
faqs.answer: We will not publish a number, and you should be wary of any page that does. A figure without a stated sample, date and method is unverifiable, and this market contains plenty of them. What can be said structurally is that the transferable causes, significant figures, equation balancing and command-term discipline, are each worth marks on every paper once fixed, and that a concentrated cause like mole-ratio setup can account for well over ten marks on a single Extended paper. Your own ledger will give you the real figure.

faqs.question: Does a mock grade at a Dubai school predict the final grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the centre, which is why the question to ask the head of science is how mocks have mapped onto finals in recent series. Some Dubai schools mark mocks deliberately a grade harsh to produce work in January, and at those schools a December shock is a designed signal rather than news. Others set generous internal boundaries or use a paper the class has partly seen, where a comfortable result means little. Also check the tier: a Core mock tells you nothing about Extended readiness.

faqs.question: Can my child's own notes be used as evidence instead of a paper?
faqs.answer: Notes show effort and organisation, not performance, so they are useful context and poor evidence. What a ledger needs is work produced under the conditions the examination will impose: unaided, timed, on unseen questions at the right tier. A beautifully kept notebook sits alongside a weak paper often enough that treating notes as a proxy is actively misleading. Where a student has a strong notebook and weak marks, that combination is itself a finding, and it usually points at exam technique rather than at content.

faqs.question: What does an error ledger look like after eight weeks?
faqs.answer: A single page with the same cause rows as week one and different totals. Typically two or three causes have dropped substantially, one has barely moved, and one or two new ones have appeared because repairing the first problem exposed the next. The topic tally alongside it shows which of the twelve areas have been assessed and which have not been touched. The useful read is the direction of each row rather than the headline total, and that is also what the termly review discusses.

faqs.question: Do you mark the practical paper questions too?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often where the first visible gain appears. The practical component carries a fifth of the grade and has the most consistent mark scheme in the syllabus, so before-and-after marking on the same skills shows movement within two sessions: consistent decimal places in a results table, a scale that fills the grid, a specific source of imprecision rather than a general one, an improvement that changes the method. Ask your head of science which practical route the centre enters, because the timing work differs even though the skills overlap.

intro.heading: Three problems, three different kinds of session
paragraphs: Chemistry at IGCSE level fails in a small number of recognisable ways, and the useful first move is to work out which one applies before buying anything. The first is arithmetic. The mole sits underneath at least half the syllabus, and a student who cannot move confidently between moles, mass, concentration and volume will lose marks in acids and bases, in energetics, in electrochemistry, in the metals questions and in the analysis questions. That student looks generally weak at chemistry and is in fact weak in one place that happens to be load-bearing.

The second is language. Chemistry mark schemes are unusually specific about wording, and a student can hold an accurate mental picture of a reaction and score two out of five for describing it. The scheme wants bond breaking is endothermic, not energy is used up. It wants the precipitate dissolves in excess to form a colourless solution, not it goes clear. It separates observation from explanation and awards them in different places. None of that is unfair and all of it is learnable, but it has to be taught deliberately, because no student infers it from a textbook.

The third is the practical component, which carries a fifth of the grade and is the part most Dubai students have never revised as a topic. Schools teach practical skills inside lessons, which is correct pedagogy and leaves students with no sense that there is a paper with its own conventions: results tables with consistent decimal places, scales that fill the grid, named sources of imprecision, improvements that change the method rather than exhorting care. It has the most consistent mark scheme in the syllabus, which makes it the most efficient component to target.

On delivery, which the URL raises directly: lessons run live online, one to one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared annotated screen carrying the equations, the organic structures and the results tables. IB Gram does not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is an India-only service. For chemistry the screen has a specific advantage worth naming. Organic structures and ionic equations need to be built up, corrected and rebuilt, and on a shared board that happens in seconds and the result is saved. A student in April can reopen the exact ester formation worked through in November.

The rest of this page goes through the components, the mole work, the language the scheme rewards, organic chemistry, electrochemistry, the Core and Extended depth difference, the practical paper, and the structure of a single session. It also says what a session cannot fix, because that is as useful as the rest, and because the three problems that masquerade as chemistry are common enough in Dubai that naming them saves families a wasted term more often than any technique on this page.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-onl.programmesIntro: Four chemistry routes a Dubai student may be sitting on. The content overlaps substantially; the papers, the formula provision and the mark-scheme conventions do not, which is what decides whether a past paper is useful practice or misleading practice.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Twelve topic areas examined through a multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent, a theory paper worth half the grade, and a practical component worth the remaining fifth. No coursework. Core and Extended tiers sit different question papers from the same syllabus, with Extended adding depth and multi-step demand rather than extra topics.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant chemistry route in Dubai's British-curriculum schools. The practical consequence for a parent is that three separate skills are being assessed, and a student can be strong in two of them and lose a grade on the third, which is why a diagnosis that names the component matters more than one that names the subject.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: The alternative specification used by a number of Dubai schools. Content coverage is broadly comparable and the assessment architecture is not: students sit written papers that carry the practical skills within them rather than through a separate component, and formula and data provision follows that board's own conventions.
programmes.countryNote: Mixing boards during revision is the most common avoidable error we see in Dubai chemistry. A student working through the other board's papers is practising the wrong question style and may be revising content presented differently. Confirm the specification code with the school before a single past paper is downloaded.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: Treats the mole as reflex background and builds on it: quantitative equilibrium, reaction kinetics with rate equations, organic mechanisms with electron movement drawn, and a formal practical skills assessment. The written demand rises sharply, with answers expected in precise mechanistic language rather than in description.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools commonly set entry at grade A or B at Extended 0620, and chemistry is a prerequisite for medicine and most engineering routes. That makes the 0620 outcome consequential beyond the certificate, and it is why Extended students with a threshold to meet are the largest group we support in this subject.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Standard or Higher Level, with written papers that weight data analysis heavily and an internally assessed investigation designed, performed and written up by the student. The chemistry is recognisable from IGCSE; the assessment style is not, since extended reasoning and experimental evaluation carry much more weight.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of Dubai's international schools run the Diploma, and the internal assessment raises the academic-honesty question families ask most often. The boundary is fixed: a tutor may teach method, explain criteria and respond to the student's own draft, and may never write, complete or redraft the work itself.

sections.heading: What each 0620 paper asks your child to do
paragraphs: A cambridge IGCSE chemistry 0620 online tutor in Dubai should be able to tell you, in one sentence per paper, what is being tested. The multiple-choice paper tests breadth and speed: forty questions in forty-five minutes, worth thirty per cent of the grade, with no credit for method and no partial marks, which means a careless minute is expensive and a guessed question costs the same as a wrong one. The theory paper tests depth and written precision: eighty marks in seventy-five minutes, worth half the grade, at a working rate of just over a mark a minute. The practical component tests experimental judgement and carries the remaining fifth.

Those three demands are genuinely different, and students are rarely weak in all three. A student who is strong on multiple choice and weak on theory has the content and cannot write it. A student strong on theory and weak on multiple choice is usually slow rather than ignorant, and needs timing work rather than revision. A student strong on both and weak on the practical component has simply never been shown that there are conventions, and that is the fastest of the three to repair.

The tier determines which versions of those papers are sat. Core candidates take the Core multiple-choice and theory papers and can be awarded grades C to G. Extended candidates take the Extended versions and reach A*. Both add the practical component, either the laboratory test or the written alternative, with the centre deciding which route it offers. Confirm the component arrangement and the content for your child's series on the syllabus document at cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabuses are revised on a cycle and the version the school teaches is the one that counts.

sections.heading: The mole is not a topic, it is how the syllabus works
paragraphs: Stoichiometry appears in the syllabus as one of twelve topic areas, which badly understates it. The mole is the conversion layer between what you can measure and what the equation says, and every quantitative question in chemistry passes through it. Titration calculations in acids and bases, electrolysis product quantities, energy changes per mole, percentage yield, purity by titration, formula determination from combustion data: all of it is the same three or four relationships applied to different contexts.

The reason students fail here is almost never the relationships themselves. Mass divided by molar mass is not conceptually hard. The failure is in the ratio step: converting the moles of what you were given into the moles of what you were asked about, using the coefficients of the balanced equation. When the equation is one to one, students get this right without noticing that a step exists. The moment it is one to two, the answer comes out by a factor of two and looks plausible, which is why these errors survive self-marking. A session that makes the ratio step explicit and written, every time, on every question, regardless of how simple the equation looks, is the single most valuable hour available in this subject.

The second layer is dimensional discipline. Concentration in moles per cubic decimetre against volume given in cubic centimetres is the most common unit trap in 0620, and it produces answers out by a factor of a thousand which students accept because the method felt right. The habit that fixes it is mechanical: write the conversion before substituting, never during. Significant figures sit alongside it, since an otherwise perfect calculation stated to six figures loses the final mark. None of this is chemistry and all of it is chemistry marks, which is why the quantitative sessions spend their time on setup and layout rather than on the arithmetic itself.
bullets: Write the ratio step explicitly even when the equation is one to one
Convert cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres before substituting, not during
Treat limiting reagent questions as a two-answer comparison, not a guess
Check significant figures and units on the final line as a fixed habit

sections.heading: The language a chemistry mark scheme actually rewards
paragraphs: Chemistry is marked on wording to a degree that surprises families. Two answers can describe the same event and score differently, not because one is wrong but because one contains the element the scheme is looking for. This is not examiner pedantry: the required phrasing almost always encodes the mechanism, so a student who can produce it has demonstrated understanding and a student who cannot has demonstrated something less.

The commonest divide is observation against explanation. A question asking what you would see wants the observation: a white precipitate forms, the solution turns from orange to green, effervescence occurs. A question asking why wants the mechanism in particle terms. Students routinely answer both with a mixture of the two, which collects partial credit at best. The second divide is between everyday and chemical register. It goes clear is not accepted where the solution becomes colourless is; clear and colourless mean different things and the scheme knows it. The third is causal completeness: explain questions need the chain, so bonds are broken, which requires energy, so the reaction is endothermic scores where endothermic because of bond breaking does not.

All of this is teachable in a handful of sessions and it transfers to every paper afterwards, which makes it among the best value work in the subject. The method is simple and unglamorous: take real past-paper questions, write the answer, compare it line by line with the published scheme, and name which element was missing. Do that twenty times and the pattern becomes automatic. The table below sets out the pairs we work through most often with Dubai students.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: four families and a short list of conditions
paragraphs: Organic chemistry has a reputation among Dubai students that its 0620 question style does not justify. At this level it is four homologous series, their general formulae, how to name and draw members of each, a limited set of reactions, and the conditions those reactions need. The questions are among the most predictable in the syllabus, which makes the topic a poor candidate for anxiety and a good candidate for efficient revision.

What students actually lose marks on is conditions and specificity. The reaction is usually identified correctly and the catalyst, temperature or reagent is vague or absent. Fermentation needs yeast, an absence of air and a warm temperature, and students write it needs yeast. Oxidation of an alcohol to a carboxylic acid needs an acidified oxidising agent, and students write it is oxidised. Addition across a double bond needs the bond to open, and a structure drawn with the double bond still intact collects nothing regardless of how clearly the intention is visible.

Drawing is the other reliable loss, and it is a convention problem rather than a chemistry one. Structures need every bond shown where the question asks for a displayed formula, including the bonds to hydrogen. A functional group drawn ambiguously is marked as wrong rather than generously. Polymer questions need the repeat unit with the continuation bonds drawn through the brackets, which students omit constantly. These are precisely the marks a shared screen is good for: the structure gets drawn, corrected, redrawn and saved, and the convention sticks because it was practised rather than described.
