sections.heading: Electrochemistry and redox: electrons, not labels
paragraphs: Electrolysis produces the most confident wrong answers in 0620. The reason is that students learn anode and cathode as labels attached to products rather than as destinations for electrons, so the rules hold until a question changes the electrolyte or the electrode material and then collapse. A student who can say that the cathode is where reduction happens because electrons arrive there will get every variant right. A student who has memorised that chlorine comes off at the anode will get the familiar case right and the unfamiliar case wrong.

Half equations are the second recurring loss and they are mechanical. Electrons go on the side that balances the charge, the species is written correctly with its state, and the numbers must balance on both counts. Students routinely balance the atoms and leave the charges unbalanced, which is a visible and avoidable error once the check becomes habitual. Predicting products at each electrode then follows a short decision sequence that can be written out and rehearsed: what ions are present, which is preferentially discharged, what is formed, what is observed.

Redox more broadly is where the oxidising and reducing agent language trips students up, because the agent is the opposite of what intuition suggests. The oxidising agent is itself reduced, and students reverse this under pressure with great consistency. Oxidation states help when taught as bookkeeping rather than as theory: assign, compare before and after, and the direction of change tells you which process happened. For Extended candidates this sits behind a significant number of marks across several topics, which makes it worth the two or three sessions it takes rather than the single mnemonic it usually gets.
bullets: Teach the cathode as where electrons arrive, not as a product list
Balance half equations for charge as well as for atoms, every time
Rehearse the product-prediction sequence as a written decision chain
Assign oxidation states as bookkeeping before reasoning about agents

sections.heading: Core and Extended: where the depth difference actually sits
paragraphs: Families are often told that Extended is harder without being told where. In chemistry the difference is concentrated rather than spread, and knowing where it sits matters because it determines whether a tier change is realistic and what work would support one.

Broadly, the descriptive topics differ least. States of matter, the tests for gases, the names and uses of materials and the environmental content are recognisable across both tiers. The quantitative topics differ most: Extended expects multi-step mole work, limiting reagents, percentage yield and purity, and calculations built on energy changes. The explanatory topics sit in between, with Extended requiring causes in terms of electronic structure where Core accepts a stated trend. Organic chemistry extends further into reaction conditions and polymer structure.

The decision has an administrative deadline rather than an academic one. Tier forms part of the entry the centre submits, and final entries close months before the examination period: Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Apply the same arithmetic to a June entry and the tier conversation belongs in the autumn term. If it is live in your household, the evidence that supports it is a marked Extended paper section showing the student can access the higher grades, which is a more persuasive document than a request. Where the window has already closed, the realistic choices are the next series or a different post-16 route, and both are better discussed in November than discovered in May.

sections.heading: The chemistry practical paper: tests, observations, conclusions
paragraphs: The written alternative to practical is a paper about experiments rather than an experiment, and that distinction is what makes it entirely preparable online. It asks a student to read apparatus and scales, record results in a properly constructed table, plot and interpret, identify what a set of observations indicates, name a specific source of imprecision and propose a change to the method. None of that requires a laboratory; all of it requires conventions nobody has usually taught as conventions.

Half the marks are available before any chemistry is applied. A results table with consistent decimal places and headed columns with units scores; one with inconsistent precision does not. A graph whose points fill more than half the grid in both directions scores the scale mark; one occupying a corner does not. A line of best fit drawn through the trend scores; one drawn between the first and last points does not. These are the cheapest marks in the whole syllabus and they are lost routinely by students who know the chemistry perfectly well.

The chemistry half of the paper is the qualitative analysis, and it rewards exact memorisation of a short list. Flame colours, the precipitate colours formed with sodium hydroxide and which dissolve in excess, the halide precipitate colours with acidified silver nitrate, the sulfate test with acidified barium salts, the carbonate test, and the gas tests with their named reagents and observations. It is a finite list, it recurs every series, and it is examined in a predictable way. A student who learns it properly and writes observations rather than conclusions picks up marks in both the practical component and the theory paper, where the same tests appear inside structured questions.
bullets: Consistent decimal places and headed columns with units, before any chemistry
Choose a scale that fills more than half the grid in both directions
Learn the analysis tests as named reagent plus exact observation
Name one specific source of imprecision, not a general wish for care

sections.heading: How a one-hour online chemistry session is built
paragraphs: An hour holds less than families expect and more than most sessions deliver. The structure that works puts the student's writing at the centre rather than the tutor's explaining, because chemistry marks are awarded for what gets written and a session where the student only listens tests nothing.

The shape is roughly: ten minutes on last week's set questions, with the student explaining their own working rather than being told where it went wrong; twenty-five minutes on one idea, built on the shared board in equations and structures rather than described in sentences; fifteen minutes with the student writing a full answer to a real past-paper question under something close to exam pace while the tutor watches the working appear; and ten minutes agreeing the set work and updating what the next session targets. The watching is the part that online delivery does well. On a shared board a tutor sees the ratio step go in wrongly as it happens, which a completed answer never reveals.

What an hour cannot do is cover a topic. Acids, bases and salts is weeks of content; a session is one idea taken properly, such as why a titration calculation needs the ratio step written out even when the equation looks simple. A parent judging value by ground covered will prefer the tutor who races through four topics, and that race is why the same marks go missing in April. One idea, secured, with an answer written to mark-scheme standard, is the correct output of sixty minutes, and the saved board means it is still available in the revision folder months later.
bullets: Student explains their own working before the tutor corrects it
One idea per session, built in equations rather than in sentences
A full answer written under pace while the tutor watches it form
Set work that can be completed without the tutor present

sections.heading: What a session cannot fix, and what is not a chemistry problem
paragraphs: Three things that arrive as chemistry problems are not chemistry problems, and buying chemistry sessions for them wastes a term. Naming them is more useful than another table of features.

The first is mathematics. If every lost mark traces to ratio, rearrangement, standard form or unit conversion, the cheaper and faster intervention is in mathematics, and the chemistry grade moves as a consequence. We will say so after a diagnostic rather than teaching chemistry around a hole in 0580. The second is supervision. A student who will not sit down to work for a parent generally will not for a tutor on a screen either, and since IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes, we are the wrong purchase in that case and would rather say it on the call. The third is reading. Where a student's errors are concentrated on long question stems in every subject, the issue is comprehension under time pressure, and chemistry sessions will treat the symptom.

Two further honest limits belong here. No grade can be promised for any series, by us or anybody else: nobody controls the paper, the cohort or the boundaries, and a page offering a specific score should be treated with scepticism. And academic-honesty boundaries do not move with money. For 0620 there is no coursework, so the question barely arises; at Diploma level, where chemistry carries an internally assessed investigation, a tutor may teach method, explain criteria and respond to a student's own draft, and may never write, complete or redraft it. Providers selling finished internal assessments operate in this market, and the student carries the consequence.

A supervision problem needs an adult in the room, which we do not provide here

process.title: Confirm the specification and the tier
process.description: Cambridge 0620 or another board, Core or Extended, and which practical route the centre enters. Three questions to the head of science that change every subsequent decision, including which past papers are worth your child's time. Families are wrong about at least one of the three often enough to always ask.

process.title: Identify which of the three demands is failing
process.description: Multiple-choice speed, written precision, or experimental judgement. A short diagnostic drawn from all three shows which one is costing marks, and they need different sessions. This runs as the free first session, with no card details requested.

process.title: Start with whatever is upstream
process.description: Where mole work is insecure, that comes first regardless of what the school is teaching, because at least six topic areas depend on it. Where the arithmetic is sound, written precision usually comes first, since it pays on every paper afterwards.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written output
process.description: A fixed hour on Gulf Standard Time, one idea per session, with the student producing a full answer under pace each week. Equations and structures are built on the shared board and saved, so the revision folder fills as the term goes on.

process.title: Close each area on marked questions
process.description: Each repaired area ends with past-paper questions filtered to it alone, marked against the published scheme with the wording quoted. If the marks have not moved, the approach changes rather than the schedule continuing unexamined.

whyPoints.title: The three demands are diagnosed separately
whyPoints.description: Speed on multiple choice, precision in writing and judgement on the practical component are different skills carrying thirty, fifty and twenty per cent of the grade. A single chemistry grade hides which one is failing, and the work for each is genuinely different.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme wording is taught, not implied
whyPoints.description: Colourless rather than clear, bond breaking requires energy rather than energy is used up, collision frequency rather than particles moving faster. Students do not infer this from textbooks, and it is worth marks on every paper once it is explicit.

whyPoints.title: The mole is treated as infrastructure
whyPoints.description: Stoichiometry is listed as one topic of twelve and sits underneath at least six of them. Securing the ratio step and the unit discipline is the highest-return work in the subject, which is why it is sequenced ahead of whatever the school is currently teaching.

whyPoints.title: The practical component gets its own block
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade with the most consistent mark scheme in the syllabus, and the component most students revise last. Tables, scales, named sources of imprecision and real method improvements are taught as conventions, because that is what they are.

whyPoints.title: The limits are stated on the page
whyPoints.description: Mathematics problems, supervision problems and comprehension problems are not chemistry problems, and a term of chemistry sessions will not fix them. We would rather name that in the first conversation than discover it in a termly review.

faqs.question: What does Paper 4 in 0620 actually ask my child to do?
faqs.answer: Produce precise written chemistry at pace. It is eighty marks in seventy-five minutes at Extended level, worth half the grade, in structured questions that often combine two ideas in one part: a balanced equation then a mole calculation then an explanation of an observation. The working rate is just over a mark a minute, so a four-minute detour on one part costs the last question. What it rewards is specific wording and shown method; what it punishes is a correct idea expressed in everyday terms and an answer with no visible working.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks when his chemistry answer looks correct to me?
faqs.answer: Usually because the answer is right in everyday register and the scheme wants chemical register. It goes clear scores nothing where the solution becomes colourless scores, because clear and colourless describe different properties. Energy is used up scores nothing where bond breaking requires energy does, because the scheme is awarding the mechanism rather than the outcome. These are not traps; the required phrase almost always encodes the understanding being tested. Twenty comparisons between a written answer and the published scheme usually makes the pattern automatic.

faqs.question: How do you teach mole calculations over a video call?
faqs.answer: On a shared board, with your child writing. The tutor sets out the framework once, then the student works a question while the tutor watches each line appear, which is the whole advantage: the ratio step going in wrongly is visible as it happens rather than inferred from a wrong final answer. The habit being built is written setup before arithmetic, with the conversion of cubic centimetres and the ratio from the balanced equation both on the page. Every worked example is saved, so the method is available in the revision folder months later.

faqs.question: Is organic chemistry really as hard as students say?
faqs.answer: Its reputation outruns its 0620 question style. At this level it is four homologous series with their general formulae, naming and drawing, a limited reaction set and the conditions each needs. The questions are among the most predictable in the syllabus. Where marks actually go is conditions left vague, fermentation described as needing yeast with the warmth and absence of air omitted, and drawing conventions: a double bond left intact after an addition reaction, or a polymer repeat unit without continuation bonds through the brackets.

faqs.question: What are the qualitative analysis tests my daughter has to memorise?
faqs.answer: A finite and recurring list, which is good news. Flame colours for the common metal ions. Precipitate colours with sodium hydroxide, and which of them dissolve in excess. Halide precipitates with acidified silver nitrate, distinguished by colour. The sulfate test with an acidified barium salt. The carbonate test with acid. And the gas tests with their named reagents: limewater turning milky, a glowing splint relighting, damp red litmus turning blue. Learned as reagent plus exact observation, these pay in both the practical component and the theory paper.

faqs.question: How much of 0620 is calculation rather than recall?
faqs.answer: Less than students fear and more than they prepare for. Calculation is concentrated in stoichiometry, energetics, electrochemistry quantities and the titration and purity work in acids and bases, with the Extended tier asking considerably more multi-step work than Core. The rest of the syllabus is description, explanation and pattern reasoning. The practical effect is that a student can be strong across most topics and still lose a grade on the calculating ones, which is why a diagnosis that separates calculation from description is more useful than a percentage.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an observation and an explanation in a chemistry answer?
faqs.answer: An observation is what a person in the room would see, hear or measure: a white precipitate forms, effervescence occurs, the orange solution turns green. An explanation is the mechanism behind it, in terms of particles, bonds, electrons or position in a reactivity series. The mark scheme asks for them separately and awards them in different places, so an answer blending the two collects partial credit at best. Separating them deliberately on real past-paper questions is two sessions of work and pays on every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: Do Core candidates study less organic chemistry than Extended candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the pattern holds across the syllabus. The descriptive content differs least between tiers, while the quantitative and explanatory content differs most. In organic chemistry specifically, Extended goes further into reaction conditions and polymer structure, and expects drawing to full convention. Elsewhere, Extended adds multi-step mole work, limiting reagents, yield and purity, half equations with charge balanced, and explanations of periodic trends in terms of electron arrangement. Confirm the content for your child's tier on the syllabus document rather than from a revision site.

faqs.question: How do you handle state symbols and ionic equations in a session?
faqs.answer: As a habit rather than a topic. State symbols are mark-bearing and routinely omitted, so every equation written in a session carries them from the start, which is less effort than adding them under exam pressure. Ionic equations are built by writing the full equation, identifying what actually changes, and removing the spectator ions, with the charge balance checked separately from the atom balance. Done on a shared board the intermediate steps stay visible, which is what makes the method reproducible rather than remembered.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge supply a Periodic Table in the 0620 exam?
faqs.answer: Treat the question as one to verify for your child's specific series on the syllabus and specimen materials at cambridgeinternational.org rather than taking any tutoring page's word for it, including this one. What matters practically is the same either way: a student who can locate a group, read a relative atomic mass and reason from position will use whatever is provided effectively, and a student who has memorised isolated facts will not. Sessions therefore practise using the table as a reasoning tool rather than relying on recall of its contents.

faqs.question: Can one session fix my child's redox problem?
faqs.answer: One session can fix the labelling problem; the full picture takes two or three. The quick win is replacing anode and cathode as product labels with the electron-destination model, after which unfamiliar electrolytes stop being frightening. What takes longer is oxidation states as bookkeeping, half equations balanced for charge as well as atoms, and the counterintuitive language where the oxidising agent is itself reduced. For an Extended candidate this sits behind marks in several topics, which makes the two or three sessions better value than the mnemonic it usually receives.

faqs.question: How is the Pearson chemistry specification different from Cambridge 0620?
faqs.answer: Mainly in architecture rather than in content. Cambridge examines through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a separate practical component. The Pearson International GCSE carries practical skills inside its written papers instead, and its formula and data provision follows its own conventions. Content coverage is broadly comparable. The practical consequence is that past papers do not cross over usefully: confirm the specification code with the school, then revise from that board alone. Mixing boards is the most common avoidable revision error we see in Dubai.

faqs.question: What does the chemistry alternative to practical paper look like?
faqs.answer: A written paper about experiments. It asks for readings taken from drawn apparatus, results recorded in a properly headed table with consistent decimal places, points plotted on a scale that fills the grid, a trend drawn and interpreted, an unfamiliar set of observations identified using the standard tests, one specific source of imprecision named, and a method improvement proposed. Half the available marks sit in conventions rather than chemistry, which is why four to six sessions on it is the most efficient block in the subject.

faqs.question: My daughter is strong in biology and weak in chemistry. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the two subjects reward different habits. Biology at IGCSE is predominantly recall precision: the exact term, the complete definition, the named structure. Chemistry adds a quantitative layer that biology barely touches, and the mole work is where most of the difficulty concentrates. A student with excellent recall discipline can carry biology and still stall in chemistry on the ratio step. That is diagnosable in one session, and the repair is arithmetic and layout rather than more chemistry content.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 chemistry student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of the three demands is failing, and that is what a diagnostic establishes. A written-precision problem is two to four sessions plus checking on each marked script. A practical-component gap is four to six. An insecure mole framework is four to six, and it is upstream of several topics so it pays back across the paper. A student with genuine content gaps in several areas needs a term rather than a block, and anyone quoting a total before seeing marked work is guessing.

intro.heading: The price question, answered before anything else
paragraphs: A Dubai parent looking for chemistry help wants two numbers: what an hour costs and how many hours this will take. The market is unusually bad at supplying either. Of the most visible providers ranking for these searches, three publish no price whatsoever, one asks the price in its own list of questions and then declines to answer it, and two quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. So here is the range in dirhams, with sources: a university student or recent graduate online runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject teacher online AED 150 to 300, an independent tutor visiting a Dubai home AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the number, an IGCSE or A Level subject specialist AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and named premium tutors above AED 500. Every one of those bands is attributed in the tables further down.

The second number is harder and more honest to break into parts. A Year 10 student consolidating as the school teaches needs a different quantity of hours from a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series with stoichiometry unsecured. A single topic repair in chemistry can genuinely be four sessions. A two-year programme of weekly support is around seventy. Anyone quoting you a total without first seeing a marked paper is guessing, and the guess will be generous in the direction of their invoice.

What makes chemistry particular, and worth paying attention to on cost, is that its difficulty is concentrated rather than spread. Twelve topic areas sit in the 0620 syllabus, and one of them, stoichiometry, is load-bearing for at least six of the others. A student who cannot move confidently between moles, mass, concentration and volume will lose marks in acids and bases, in electrochemistry, in energetics, in the Periodic Table questions and in the practical paper, and will appear to have a general chemistry problem. Fixing that one area is usually four to six sessions and lifts marks across half the syllabus. Reteaching twelve topics is a term and a half. The difference between those two purchases is several thousand dirhams, and it is decided by whether anyone looked at the script first.

Delivery and the honest limits, stated plainly. Chemistry lessons for Dubai students run live online, one to one, over video, with a shared screen for equations, mechanisms and graph work. IB Gram does not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The cost consequence of that is straightforward and in your favour: you are not paying for a drive across the city inside an hourly rate, and the tutor you get is chosen for knowing the 0620 mark scheme rather than for living near your community.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tut.programmesIntro: Four routes a Dubai chemistry student may be on, described here by what each one costs a family in hours as well as in content. Where a programme carries internally assessed work, the tutoring brief narrows and the boundaries tighten, which changes the price of help as well as its shape.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Twelve topic areas examined across three components with no coursework. Core candidates sit the Core multiple-choice and theory papers and are capped at grade C; Extended candidates sit the Extended versions and can reach A*. A practical component, either the laboratory test or the written alternative, carries a fifth of the grade in both tiers.
programmes.countryNote: The most commonly tutored science in Dubai after mathematics, and the one where requests cluster most tightly on a single topic. Stoichiometry and the mole are named in the majority of first enquiries we receive from Dubai families, which is why a four to six session topic repair is the most frequently bought chemistry package in this city.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering all three sciences in two IGCSEs, with the chemistry content reduced from the separate syllabus. Students sit combined papers, which means the chemistry sections appear interleaved with biology and physics and require recall switching the separate papers do not test.
programmes.countryNote: Often the cheaper route in tutoring terms simply because there is less content to support, but the saving is not automatic. Past papers from the separate 0620 syllabus contain material a 0654 candidate will not be examined on, so a tutor who does not check the code can bill hours teaching content that will never be assessed.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation most Dubai British schools offer. AS Chemistry assumes mole calculations as reflex rather than as content, and adds organic mechanisms with curly arrows, equilibrium treated quantitatively and a formal practical skills assessment. Students who reached a high 0620 grade by memorising worked examples meet the wall in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Entry commonly sits at grade A or B at Extended 0620 in Dubai schools, and the subject is a prerequisite for medicine and most engineering routes. That makes a 0620 grade more expensive to get wrong than most: a missed threshold can mean a year's resit or a changed degree plan.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Standard or Higher Level, with an internally assessed investigation that the student designs, performs and writes up, marked at school and moderated by the IB. The written papers weight data analysis and experimental reasoning more heavily than 0620 does, and the internal assessment introduces a strict academic-honesty boundary.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of Dubai's international schools run the Diploma, and the internal assessment is where parents most often ask what help is allowed. The answer is narrow and it does not change with price: a tutor may teach method, discuss a plan and give feedback on the student's own draft, and may never write, complete or redraft it.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tut.subjectsIntro: The Cambridge codes Dubai families most often buy support in alongside Chemistry 0620, with what each one assesses and a note on how heavily it is tutored in this city. Demand drives availability, and availability drives price.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Twelve topic areas from states of matter to organic chemistry. Assesses calculation, pattern reasoning and precise description. Stoichiometry is load-bearing for six other topics, which is why it is the single most requested chemistry repair in Dubai and the one with the best return on hours paid.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Twenty-one topic areas and the heaviest recall load of the sciences. Assesses definitional precision over calculation. Tutored heavily in Dubai at Year 11 rather than Year 10, because its problems surface late, when the volume of recall finally outruns a student's revision method.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Six topic areas assessed through calculation, graph work and experimental reasoning. Shares the practical paper's skills with chemistry almost exactly. Specialist availability is tighter than in chemistry or biology, which is the one place in the sciences where scarcity visibly moves the rate.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: All three sciences to reduced depth in combined papers. Assesses the same core chemistry relationships with fewer multi-step calculations. Cheaper to support per grade point, provided the tutor filters past papers to the double-award content rather than working from separate-science papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Assesses number, algebra, geometry and statistics. Ratio, proportion and rearrangement are examined again inside every chemistry calculation without being labelled as maths. The most common hidden cause of a chemistry grade that will not move, and often cheaper to fix than the chemistry itself.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Functions, calculus and trigonometry above 0580 level. Taken by stronger Dubai sets, and a reliable signal that a chemistry problem is conceptual rather than numerical. Students holding both need session planning around whichever subject has the heavier assessment week.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Assesses reading, writing and response to text. The command-term discipline it builds is the same discipline chemistry mark schemes demand: describe, explain, suggest, state and compare are not interchangeable, and in chemistry that distinction is worth marks on every paper.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Assesses data response, diagram work and extended written reasoning. Frequently paired with chemistry by Dubai students keeping both science and commerce routes open, which produces the heaviest Year 11 workloads and the tightest session scheduling.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Assesses practical software skills and theory across coursework-style tasks and written papers. Its deadlines frequently land in chemistry revision season, which is worth mapping in September so a practical submission week does not eat the stoichiometry block.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Assessed in Arabic, and for Arab students in Dubai it sits alongside the international curriculum as a mandatory subject under KHDA's requirements. Its timetable position and separate class organisation affect when science support can realistically be scheduled.

paragraphs: A single hourly number hides most of what you are actually deciding. Six variables move a quote in this emirate, and only two of them are about the tutor. Knowing which ones you control is the difference between negotiating and being quoted at.

Tier is the first. Extended Paper 4 work requires someone fluent in multi-step calculation and mark-scheme wording, and that is a narrower pool than Core support, which prices accordingly. Proximity to a series is the second, and it is the one families underestimate: in the eight weeks before June, every centre's candidates want the same evenings, and scarcity in that window is real rather than manufactured. Specialism scarcity is the third. Chemistry sits in the middle of the sciences on availability, easier than physics and tighter than biology.

The three you control are session length, frequency and timing in the year. Ninety minutes usually costs less per minute than sixty and delivers more than sixty for calculation-heavy topics, because moles work needs a run-up. Frequency compounds: two sessions a week in the final stretch costs more per month and less in total than three months of weekly sessions started too late. And timing is the largest lever of all. Support bought in Year 10, while the school is teaching the topic, costs a fraction of the same marks recovered in Year 11 under deadline. The comparison nobody puts in writing is between starting early and rescuing late. sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: A tutoring budget is set against a school fee, and in Dubai that number has just stopped moving. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family that set a tutoring budget last year on the assumption of a fee rise this year, that is real headroom, and it is the single most useful piece of financial context on this page.

The scale of the market around you explains the rest of the pricing. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for the largest share of enrolment at thirty-seven per cent, Indian curricula next, then American, with the International Baccalaureate taking a smaller slice. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment grew by six per cent.

Those two facts together explain why IGCSE chemistry tutoring prices in Dubai behave the way they do. A growing UK-curriculum population means more 0620 candidates every year chasing a specialist pool that does not grow at the same rate, which is why the squeeze in the eight weeks before a series gets tighter rather than easier. Frozen fees mean the household budget that absorbs tutoring is more stable than it has been. The practical conclusion for a family planning a Year 11: book the specialist in the autumn term at the ordinary rate rather than in the spring at the scarcity rate.

sections.heading: Which 0620 marks are cheapest to recover
paragraphs: If you are spending by the hour, the question that matters is which hours return the most marks. Chemistry has an unusually clear answer, because its difficulty is concentrated rather than evenly spread across the twelve topic areas. Stoichiometry is the centre of gravity. Moles, mass, concentration, volume and the balanced equation are not one topic among twelve; they are the machinery that acids and bases, electrochemistry, energetics, metals and the analysis questions all run on. A student who is insecure there looks generally weak in chemistry and is actually weak in one place.

After stoichiometry, three areas return marks fast. The first is equation writing and balancing, including ionic equations, which is mechanical and drillable. The second is the practical component, which carries a fifth of the grade with the most predictable mark scheme in the syllabus: tabulating with consistent precision, plotting, identifying a specific source of imprecision, proposing a change to the method rather than an exhortation to be careful. The third is command-term discipline, where state wants a fact without reasoning, describe wants the observation, explain wants the cause in particle terms, and suggest invites applied reasoning. Those three are a handful of sessions each and they transfer to every paper afterwards.

The expensive marks are the ones that need understanding rebuilt: organic chemistry for a student who never secured bonding, or electrochemistry for one who cannot track electrons. Those are weeks, not sessions, and a provider promising them quickly is selling a timeline rather than a method. The ordering follows from the arithmetic: buy the cheap transferable marks first, then decide whether the expensive ones are worth the remaining budget. Grade outcomes are never promised here, and nobody in this market can honestly promise one.

sections.heading: The extras that change the figure you were quoted
paragraphs: An hourly rate is not a total, and the gap between the two is where most Dubai families get a surprise. Six things routinely sit outside the quoted number, and all six are answerable in one message before you pay anything.

Materials are the first. Ask whether past papers, worked sets and marking are included or billed. Marking in particular is where value sits in a chemistry package: a session is an hour, but a marked Extended paper with mark-scheme wording quoted back takes a tutor longer than the lesson did, and providers differ on whether that is inside the rate. Cancellation terms are the second. In a Dubai school year interrupted by mock weeks, half terms, travel and Ramadan schedule changes, a policy requiring forty-eight hours' notice behaves very differently from one requiring a week.

The third is tax. Do not take any page's word on how UAE VAT applies to tuition, including this one; ask the provider directly whether the figure they quoted includes it, and ask for that in writing. The fourth is travel, which only arises for in-home arrangements and is usually inside the rate rather than added, which is precisely why those rates sit higher. The fifth is the minimum commitment: some providers quote an attractive hourly figure attached to a ten-session minimum, which is a different purchase from four sessions on stoichiometry. The sixth is the trial. Where a trial is offered free, the conditions should be visible on the same screen as the word free. Ours is one session, with no card details requested, and you keep the marked diagnostic work whether or not you continue.

sections.heading: How to spend less without buying less
paragraphs: There are legitimate ways to reduce the total and there are ways that only look like savings. Worth doing: start earlier, buy a diagnostic before buying a term, choose ninety minutes over sixty for calculation topics, and let the plan end when the named problem is fixed rather than rolling forward by default. Each of those reduces hours rather than reducing quality.

Shared sessions are the saving most often proposed and the one that most often disappoints. Two students genuinely at the same point, same tier, same topic, same week, can work well together and the discussion between them adds something. Two students a year apart or on different tiers produce a session that is slightly wrong for both, and the chemistry case is worse than most because the mole work is sequential: one student waiting while the other catches up is paying to watch. Where two of your children need chemistry, two shorter separate sessions generally move more marks than one longer shared hour at a lower per-head rate.

The false economy worth naming is the band gap. Hiring budget-band support for Extended Paper 4 work in the final term is not cheaper, it is a different product bought for the wrong job, and the usual outcome is a term of hours followed by specialist hours anyway. The honest version of this advice runs the other way too: for a Year 9 student consolidating general science before the IGCSE option choice, the budget band may be entirely sufficient and the specialist band is simply money spent on precision nobody needs yet. Match the band to the job and the bill looks after itself.

sections.heading: When we would tell you not to spend the money
paragraphs: A page about cost is incomplete without the cases where the answer is not to buy. There are four we see regularly in Dubai, and in each one a term of chemistry tutoring is money that will not produce marks.

The first is a supervision problem presented as a chemistry problem. A student who will not sit down to work for a parent will usually not sit down for a tutor on a screen either. For that case an adult physically present has a genuine advantage, and because IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai, the honest answer is that we are the wrong purchase and we will say so on the call. The second is a timing problem: a student whose topic knowledge is sound and whose paper marks are poor needs timed practice and a triage rule, which is two to four sessions, not a term. Paying for a term in that situation buys content the student already has.

The third is a maths problem wearing a chemistry coat. If every lost mark traces back to ratio, rearrangement or standard form, the cheaper and faster intervention is mathematics, and the chemistry grade will move as a side effect. The fourth is the regulatory false alarm. Tutoring is not required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency. For the record, the British-track equivalency requirement is published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competitor page states six IGCSE subjects are required. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae rather than taking either figure from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Why does a 0620 specialist cost more than a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Because you are buying mark-scheme fluency rather than subject knowledge. A good general science tutor can teach the mole concept. A 0620 specialist can look at your child's Extended Paper 4 answer and say which phrase earned the mark, which one the examiner would not accept, and what the two-mark version of that answer looks like. That is a narrower skill, held by fewer people, and the pool tightens further in the eight weeks before a series when every Dubai centre's candidates want the same evenings.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute chemistry session better value than sixty minutes?
faqs.answer: For calculation topics, usually yes. Stoichiometry needs a run-up: recall the relationship, set up the ratio, work an example, then have the student produce one unaided while the tutor watches the working. Sixty minutes often ends in the middle of that cycle. Ninety also tends to cost less per minute than sixty at the same band. For recall-heavy topics the reverse holds, and two shorter sessions a week beat one long one because the spacing is what fixes recall. Match the length to the topic rather than booking one pattern for the year.

faqs.question: Does 0620 chemistry support cost more in the eight weeks before a June series?
faqs.answer: Effective prices do, and the mechanism is availability rather than a published increase. In the six to eight weeks before a June or November series, the specialist pool is fully booked at the hours families want, which are weekday evenings and Saturday mornings. What you actually face is not a higher advertised rate but a narrower choice: the specialist you wanted is unavailable and the alternatives sit in a different band. The fix is calendar rather than negotiation. Booking in the autumn term secures the slot at the ordinary rate.

faqs.question: Will the chemistry rate I was quoted be the figure on the invoice?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, and treat any page that states the UAE tax treatment of tuition as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation with caution, including this one. What you are entitled to know before paying is simple: whether the figure quoted to you is the figure you will be invoiced, and if not, what will be added. faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly budget for Year 11 chemistry in Dubai?

faqs.question: Can a small group bring the cost of 0620 support down?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, under narrow conditions. Two students at the same tier working on the same topic in the same week can share a session productively, and the discussion between them adds something a one-to-one hour does not. A year's difference, or a tier difference, produces a session slightly wrong for both. Chemistry suffers more than most subjects here because the mole work is sequential, so one student waiting while the other catches up is paying to watch. faqs.question: Which part of 0620 gives the most marks back per hour paid?
faqs.answer: Stoichiometry, with no serious competition. Moles, mass, concentration, volume and the balanced equation are the machinery that acids and bases, electrochemistry, energetics, metals and the analysis questions all run on, so securing it pays marks back across at least six of the twelve topic areas. After that, equation and ionic-equation writing, which drills mechanically; the practical component, which is a fifth of the grade with the most predictable mark scheme in the syllabus; and command-term discipline, which is two sessions and transfers to every paper.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start chemistry support in Year 10 than to rescue it in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it is the largest saving available anywhere on this page. A Year 10 student supported fortnightly while the school is teaching a topic only needs consolidation, which is mid-band work at a fortnightly frequency. The same student rescued in the April of Year 11 needs two or three sessions a week at peak-season availability, doing excavation rather than consolidation, and paying specialist rates for it. The cheapest chemistry plan in Dubai is almost always the one that began before anybody in the household was worried.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying a deposit for a term of chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Is marking of past papers inside the hourly figure or billed separately? What is the cancellation window, and how does it handle mock weeks and travel? Does the quoted figure include any applicable tax? Is there a minimum session commitment attached to the rate I was quoted? And what specifically will be different, on paper, after the first five sessions? The last one matters most. A provider who cannot answer it with a named topic and a form of evidence is selling hours rather than outcomes.

faqs.question: We only need stoichiometry fixed. Can we buy four sessions and stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most sensible purchase in this subject. Four to six sessions on the mole, with a marked set of questions on that area before and after so the gain is visible, is a defined block with an end date. If the marks move, you have what you came for. If they do not, you have spent a fraction of a term finding that out and the diagnosis changes. Blocks that roll forward by default are how families end up paying for a year they never decided to buy.

The written alternative to practical has the most predictable mark scheme in the syllabus: tabulating with consistent precision, plotting with a sensible scale, reading an instrument correctly, identifying one specific source of imprecision and proposing a method change. intro.heading: The arithmetic behind a home-tutor search
paragraphs: An in-home tutor is the default mental picture for most families and it is a legitimate service. Somebody arrives, sits with your child for an hour or two, and leaves. You supervise nothing, there is no screen to police, and a teenager who will put their head down for a visitor does not always do the same for a laptop. For a younger child those advantages are real and worth paying for, and plenty of Dubai families do exactly that.

The reason this page starts with arithmetic rather than with that picture is that the published numbers tell a story families rarely see laid out. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE support from AED 150. Monthly packages make the gap starker: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions works out near AED 100 a session, while AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions works out near AED 200 an hour. All of those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers who published them, not to us.

The difference is not profiteering. It is travel. Somebody has to pay for the drive, and in a city where a weekday evening run between two communities can take forty minutes each way, that cost is either inside the hourly rate, inside a minimum booking length, or inside the quality of tutor who is willing to accept the booking at all. The last of those three is the one that costs a 0653 family most, because it quietly narrows the search from tutors who know the syllabus to tutors who live nearby.

IB Gram delivers tutoring for families in Dubai and across the Emirates one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or in any other emirate; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this page will suggest otherwise. The case for that is not that screens are better than people. It is that for a single-award science course, the binding constraint is finding one tutor who is genuinely comfortable moving between osmosis, mole calculations and circuit diagrams inside the same hour, and that person is rarely the nearest available option.

What follows is the practical detail. The travel arithmetic by community. The extras that appear on a second invoice. What the 0653 syllabus asks a single tutor to hold. The four ways of buying an hour in this city compared on teaching time rather than headline rate. The permit and invoicing position. And what to agree before you need to cancel, pause or change tutor, because those conversations go better when the terms were set in week one.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.programmesIntro: Where a student sits in the sequence changes both the hours required and the sensible format. These are the four stages a Dubai family planning combined-science support is usually choosing between.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science before options
programmes.description: Science is still taught as one subject by one teacher, often a specialist in only one of the three strands. The habits that decide a combined-science grade form here: whether a student writes units on an answer, whether they can rearrange a simple relationship, whether they read a graph or guess at it. Support at this stage is cheap and preventative.
programmes.countryNote: This is also when the Dubai options conversation happens, and it is the point at which a family can still influence whether a child is put on the single award, the double award or three separate sciences. Ask the head of science what the school's criteria are for each route before the form arrives.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core entry covers the core content of all three sciences with a lower grade ceiling than the Extended entry. Support here is mostly content coverage and confidence, and it is the cheapest version of 0653 to tutor because the body of material is narrower and the paper technique less demanding.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Core entry is frequently used for students carrying a heavy timetable including mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams. Confirm the tier from the statement of entry rather than assuming, because the grade ceiling it sets affects sixth-form applications.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended candidates sit different papers and carry supplement content on top of the core material across all three sciences. A wider body of material for one tutor to hold, which is why Extended support needs either longer sessions or a short specialist block on whichever strand the marked paper shows as weakest.
programmes.countryNote: Extended 0653 is the common entry where a Dubai school expects students to progress to sixth form but has judged three separate sciences too heavy. It is the version where a family most often ends up paying for a second tutor for a limited period.

programmes.name: November series retake
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, so a student who misses a required grade in June can sit again in November. A retake plan is short, intensive and entirely paper-technique led, built around the specific components where marks were lost rather than a fresh pass through the syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing before results day, because the November entry has its own deadline and the summer is the only available preparation window. A Dubai family travelling in July and August should plan continuity before they leave rather than after they return.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.subjectsIntro: A single-award science course asks one tutor to be credible across a wide range. These are the codes we are asked about, described from the point of view of what a tutor has to be able to do rather than what the syllabus says.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade, three sciences. A tutor needs to move from a food-web question to a reacting-mass calculation to a series-circuit problem without losing the thread, and to know which of the three the student is actually losing marks in. Test that in a trial lesson rather than assuming it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: The same three sciences with more content and two grades. A tutor comfortable with 0653 is usually comfortable here, but the volume means the weekly session has to be longer or the plan has to be more selective about what gets covered.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Recall-heavy and the strand most 0653 students feel safest in. A tutor who allows a student to spend the hour on biology because it feels productive is being pleasant rather than useful.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The strand that most often forces a family to buy a second, specialist tutor for a few weeks. Moles, relative formula mass, reacting masses and concentration are maths problems wearing chemistry clothes, and they take several sessions to rebuild before any marks move.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Formula selection, unit conversion and graph interpretation under time pressure. The marks are volatile rather than missing: students who can do these calmly at home lose them in a timed paper until the method is reflexive, which needs short repeated drilling.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science (Double Award, 4SD0)
subjects.description: Used by some Dubai centres instead of the Cambridge route. Different papers, different practical arrangements and a different series calendar, so a tutor must confirm the board from the statement of entry before preparing anything.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The subject hiding inside most combined-science losses. Rearranging relationships, converting units, handling ratio and reading values off a graph are all maths, and a student who cannot do them loses the same science marks in every paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Long-answer science marks are awarded for precise wording. A second-language writer can hold the science and still miss the credited term, which is visible on a marked script and cheaper to fix than more content teaching.

subjects.name: A Level and IB Diploma sciences
subjects.description: Where the single-award decision shows its cost. Post-16 science entry conditions are set school by school in Dubai, and some sixth forms ask for a separate-science grade for a given subject. Confirm in writing while the options form is still open.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question for 0653, answered without a pitch
paragraphs: Taken literally, a Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 home tutor in Dubai is a person who travels to your address and teaches at your table. That market exists and the published rate for it is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. What you are buying at the upper end of that band is partly teaching and partly logistics taken off your hands, and for some households that is the right purchase. It is worth saying so plainly rather than arguing against a service a lot of families are happy with.

IB Gram does not provide it. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a fixed position across every country page on this site rather than a policy invented for this one, and it means no sentence here will promise anyone arriving at a Dubai address.

The argument for making that trade is specific to a single-award science course. 0653 produces one grade from biology, chemistry and physics, so the tutor you want is one person who can hold all three credibly. That is a narrower population than it sounds. Most science tutors are specialists in one strand who are serviceable in a second and vague in the third, and the strand they are vaguest in is usually the one carrying your child's lost marks. Searching within driving distance of your community makes an already narrow search narrower.

There is a second, duller argument that matters more over a year. A video session starts when the student sits down. An in-home session starts when the tutor arrives, which in this city is a variable rather than a time. Over thirty weeks the difference between a lesson that reliably begins at half past five and one that often begins at six is several hours of teaching, which is worth more than the hourly saving most families are shopping for.

sections.heading: What travel actually costs in a Dubai in-home booking
paragraphs: The published in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. What that phrase conceals is that the travel is paid for in one of three currencies, and only the first is visible on an invoice. It can be billed, usually as a surcharge or a longer minimum booking. It can be absorbed by the tutor, in which case they will accept only bookings near where they already are. Or it can be absorbed by your child, in the form of a session that starts twenty minutes late and finishes on time.

The table below works through the arithmetic in the way a family never does. It takes an indicative evening drive each way, as families in these communities report it, and shows what a nominally reasonable hourly rate becomes once the tutor's travel is counted as part of the hour you are paying for. The point is not that in-home tutoring is bad value. It is that the comparison most parents make, between a quoted in-home rate and a quoted online rate, is not comparing the same thing.

The second effect is less obvious and more damaging. A tutor who has to drive will take the booking that fits their route, which means the available slots in a given community cluster together and the tutors available are the ones already working nearby. If your child needs the chemistry arithmetic rebuilt and the nearest willing tutor is a biologist, the geography has made a teaching decision for you. That is the mechanism by which a lower hourly rate ends up costing a term.

None of this applies to a two-hour weekend booking in a community where the tutor lives, which is the one case where in-home arithmetic looks good. If that is your situation and you have found a person who genuinely knows 0653 at your child's tier, the format is not the thing to change.

sections.heading: The extras that appear after the first invoice
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the part of tutoring families compare and the part that varies least. The variation is in everything around the hour, and most of it is invisible until the second month. It is worth asking about all of it before the first session rather than discovering it in an awkward message.

The commonest extras are structural. A minimum booking length, usually two hours for an in-home visit, which turns a reasonable hourly rate into a fixed evening commitment. A travel surcharge for communities outside a stated radius. A different rate for weekends or for sessions after a certain hour, which is exactly when a Year 11 student in Dubai is available. A charge for the first diagnostic session, which is reasonable in itself but should be stated. Materials or workbook fees, which deserve a question about what is being supplied, since examination board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published free on the board's own website and may not lawfully be sold on to you as a bundle.

Then the cancellation terms, which cause more friction than anything else. Twenty-four hours notice is the usual standard, and the question worth asking is what happens in the specific situations a family actually meets: a child off sick, a school trip announced at short notice, a family trip over a long weekend, an exam timetable that was published after the block was booked. None of these are unusual and all of them are cheaper to agree in advance.

Finally, the word free. If a trial is advertised as free, the conditions attached to it belong in the same place as the word: how long the session is, whether card details are required, whether it obliges you to anything. The trial lesson offered here is one full-length one-to-one video session, at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue, and that is the whole of the condition.

sections.heading: What one tutor has to hold in their head for 0653
paragraphs: The financial case for a single tutor only works if the tutor is genuinely credible across the whole award, so it is worth being concrete about what that means. Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 draws material from biology, chemistry and physics and awards one grade. It is tiered, with Core and Extended candidates sitting different papers, and the assessment follows the familiar Cambridge science pattern of a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component. Check the current syllabus and the component details on the Cambridge International website, and check the paper numbers and the practical choice on your child's statement of entry, because centres make the practical decision themselves.

In a single hour a 0653 tutor may need to explain why water moves across a membrane, then calculate the mass of a product from a balanced equation, then work out the current through a resistor. Those are three different kinds of thinking. The biology is recall organised into mechanism. The chemistry is proportional reasoning with units attached. The physics is formula selection followed by arithmetic under pressure. A tutor who is strong in one and weak in another will unconsciously steer the hour towards their own comfort, and the student will let them, because the alternative is harder.

This is testable in about four minutes and it is the single most useful thing to do with a trial lesson. Ask for a mole calculation worked aloud. Then ask for an explanation of why a food chain rarely has more than four or five links. Then ask for a worked example on series and parallel resistance. Fluency on all three is what you are buying. Hesitation on one is not disqualifying, but it tells you where a short specialist block may be needed later.

The other half of holding the course is knowing where the loss is. One grade averages three sciences, so a marked paper broken down by strand is the only honest basis for a plan. Without it, a tutor is guessing, and the guess is usually that the student needs more of whatever the tutor teaches best.

sections.heading: Four ways to buy the same hour in Dubai
paragraphs: Comparing formats on headline rate is how families end up disappointed. The useful comparison is hours of teaching received per hour paid for, and whether the teaching reaches the thing that is actually wrong. The table sets out the four options available in this city on both measures.

The group row deserves a note, because it is the option families dismiss too quickly and also the option that fails most often for 0653 specifically. Group classes are genuinely cheaper, at AED 45 to 150 per student at the budget end on published rates. They are set by year group rather than by tier, and in a combined-science class the students in the room are losing marks in different sciences. A group works for content coverage and does not work for a specific arithmetic weakness in the chemistry strand.

The centre row is a different kind of thing altogether. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a licensed business, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. The fee reflects that overhead and the premises. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no premises in the UAE, which is why a centre is not a format we offer rather than a format we criticise.

The last column is the one to read first. For a 0653 student the question is whether the hour can be aimed at the specific strand carrying the loss, and only one-to-one formats can do that. Everything else in the table is a judgement about how much that precision is worth to your household this term.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and the admin of paying a tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated and most families do not know it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted, and anyone quoting one to you is improvising.

The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Because the permit costs nothing and takes two days, there is no reasonable excuse for a tutor charging commercial rates not to hold one, and no basis for charging a premium because they do.

One further rule is worth knowing if the tutor you are considering teaches at your child's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK publication before relying on it, but the direction of travel is clear enough that marketing a child's own teacher privately is not something to arrange.

On invoicing, two practical points. Ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT, in writing, because an exclusive quote changes the comparison you believed you were making; we will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees here, as that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption. And keep a record of what was paid for what, particularly with an informal in-home arrangement, because there is no other paperwork in the relationship if something goes wrong.

sections.heading: Scheduling a 0653 session into a Dubai evening
paragraphs: The limiting factor on a weekday lesson is almost never the tutor's diary. It is the gap between a school's final bell and a fifteen-year-old being fed, settled and capable of thinking about reacting masses. Dubai school days finish early, but bus routes serving several communities can take an hour, and a parent collecting from a Jumeirah school to a southern community at half past three is making a journey nobody can time.

The pattern that works for most Dubai families is one weekday session between 17:00 and 19:00 for teaching and repair, and one weekend morning session for anything requiring full-length timing. A ninety-minute paper attempted at eight in the evening after a full school day produces a score that is not a fair baseline, which means the diagnostic you are paying for is wrong. Saturday mornings consistently produce the most useful scripts, and for an exam-term cadence two shorter sessions beat one long one for the calculation-heavy strands.

Ramadan changes the shape and should. School timetables compress, less new content is taught, and the month is better spent on retrieval, command-word technique and short papers than on starting mole calculations from scratch. Families who prefer it move sessions to post-iftar slots. We would not schedule a Year 11 science lesson in the pre-dawn hours even if asked.

One scheduling fact sits outside anyone's control. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. If you are planning travel near the exam period, work from your school's own timetable rather than a generic one found online, and tell your tutor the dates so the final sessions are scheduled around the actual papers.

sections.heading: Cancelling, pausing and what to agree before you need it
paragraphs: Most of what goes wrong in a tutoring arrangement is administrative rather than academic, and all of it is cheaper to settle in week one. The table below lists the situations Dubai families actually meet, what is worth agreeing before each one happens, and what no provider can honestly promise about any of them.

The hardest case is the one at the bottom. A tutor can be competent, prepared and perfectly pleasant, and a particular fifteen-year-old can still refuse to engage with them. That is not a failure of either party and it is not fixed by persistence. It is fixed by changing the match, quickly and without a negotiation, which is why the arrangement here is that you say so and we change it rather than asking you to justify the request.

The second hardest is the plan that is not working despite the sessions happening. The protection against that is measurement rather than goodwill: a baseline paper, a plan with dates, and a second comparable paper six weeks later marked the same way. If the score has not moved, buying more hours of the same plan will not move the third paper either. That conversation is ours to start, and starting it is the only honest use of the evidence file.

What is not on offer, from us or from anybody who is being straight with you, is a grade guarantee or a refund tied to an outcome. Nobody controls the paper, the marking or a sixteen-year-old's morning. A provider who offers that is either not honouring it or pricing it in, and in either case it is a reason for scepticism rather than reassurance.

process.title: Decide what you are really buying
process.description: If the requirement is supervision and logistics taken off your hands, an in-home arrangement may genuinely suit you better, and the published Dubai band for that is AED 180 to 500 an hour. If the requirement is a tutor who knows 0653 at your child's tier, the geography stops helping. Worth being honest about which it is.

process.title: Get the tier and the board from the entry
process.description: Core or Extended, Cambridge 0653 or a Pearson equivalent, and which practical component. Extended covers a wider body of material, so any quote given before the tier is known is a guess. The exams officer at your child's school can confirm all three in one email.

process.title: Free trial, and test all three strands in it
process.description: One full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken. Use four minutes of it to ask for a mole calculation, a food-chain explanation and a resistance problem, back to back. Fluency across all three is the thing that makes a single tutor cheaper than three.

process.title: Measure at six weeks, then decide again
process.description: A second paper of the same format under the same timing, marked the same way, with the strand breakdown repeated. The comparison is the review. If nothing has moved, the plan or the tutor changes rather than the hours increasing, and that is a conversation we start rather than wait for.
