faqs.question: Will you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for Combined Science 0653?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is consistent across every country page on this site rather than a position taken for this subject. The in-home market in Dubai does exist and the published rate for it is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. The reason we do not compete in it for a single-award science course is that the tutor you want is one person credible across all three sciences, and searching within driving distance narrows that search considerably.

faqs.question: What does an in-home science tutor charge in Dubai once travel is counted?
faqs.answer: The published band is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The figure you should work with is cost per hour of teaching rather than the headline rate. A tutor driving thirty-five minutes each way who bills travel at their own rate turns a nominal AED 250 into roughly AED 450 for one hour taught. The better in-home arithmetic is a two-hour weekend booking with a tutor who already lives nearby, which lands close to AED 225.

faqs.question: How much teaching time does a cross-city tutor visit actually lose?
faqs.answer: It depends who absorbs the drive. If the tutor bills it, you pay more per hour taught. If the tutor absorbs it, they will only accept bookings on their existing route, which shrinks your choice of tutor to whoever is already working nearby. If nobody absorbs it formally, it comes out of the lesson, in the form of a session that starts twenty minutes late and still finishes on time. The third version is the common one and the hardest to argue about, because nothing on the invoice records it.

faqs.question: Is a two-hour home session better value than two one-hour online sessions?
faqs.answer: For the calculation-heavy strands inside 0653, almost certainly not. Chemistry arithmetic and physics formula work respond to short frequent repetition until the method is reflexive under time pressure, which is why two separate hours beat one block of two. A two-hour minimum also exists mainly to justify a tutor's drive rather than because two hours is the right length for a Year 11 evening. The exception is full-length paper practice, which needs an uninterrupted stretch and is best placed on a weekend morning.

faqs.question: What extras should I expect on top of the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask about six things before the first session: minimum booking length, travel surcharges outside a stated radius, different rates for weekends and late slots, whether the first diagnostic session is charged, materials or workbook fees, and the cancellation notice period. Materials fees deserve particular scrutiny, because examination board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published free on the board's own website and should not be resold to you as a bundle. Anything advertised as free should carry its conditions in the same place as the word.

faqs.question: Can one tutor genuinely cover biology, chemistry and physics for 0653?
faqs.answer: Some can and many cannot, and it is testable in four minutes. In a trial lesson ask for a mole calculation worked aloud, then an explanation of why food chains rarely exceed four or five links, then a worked example on series and parallel resistance. Those are three different kinds of thinking: recall organised into mechanism, proportional reasoning with units, and formula selection under pressure. A tutor weak in one will steer the hour towards their strength without meaning to, and the student will happily let them.

faqs.question: How do I check a private tutor is permitted to teach in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The official route is MoHRE's private tutor licensing service, applied for through the MoHRE app, website or e-services, with a stated completion time of two working days. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no good reason not to hold one.

faqs.question: Should I pay a tutor in cash, and should I expect an invoice?
faqs.answer: Keep a record either way, because with an informal arrangement there is no other paperwork in the relationship. Ask in writing whether the quoted figure includes VAT; an exclusive quote changes the comparison you thought you were making, and providers in this market are inconsistent about saying so. We will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees here, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption, and IB Gram publishes no tax registration number on this page.

faqs.question: What notice do I need to give to cancel a session?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four hours is the common standard in this market, but the useful conversation is about the specific cases rather than the headline figure. A child off sick that morning. A school trip announced at short notice. An exam timetable published after a block was booked. A family trip over a long weekend. Agree what happens in each of those before you need to, because every one of them is ordinary and all of them are cheaper to settle in week one than in the message where you are asking for a favour.

faqs.question: Can we pause 0653 sessions over the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a Year 10 student a summer pause is usually sensible. For a Year 11 student in the exam term it is a trade worth thinking about, because the calculation strands lose fluency quickly and rebuilding them costs more hours than maintaining them. Where a family is travelling, video delivery means sessions can continue from anywhere with only the time zone to renegotiate, which is the quiet reason it suits Dubai families who spend part of the summer elsewhere.

faqs.question: My son shares a bedroom - where should an online session actually happen?
faqs.answer: A room with a door that closes matters more than the hardware. In an apartment that often means the dining table with everyone else out of the room for an hour, which is a scheduling negotiation rather than a technical one. Headphones help considerably, both for concentration and because the tutor's voice is then not competing with a television. What the student needs on the desk is modest: a device with a working microphone, paper, pencil, ruler and calculator, because much of the work is handwritten and then shown or typed onto the shared screen.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if my daughter gets home at half past four?
faqs.answer: Five o'clock is realistic and half past four is not, because a fifteen-year-old needs to eat and put a bag down before thinking about reacting masses. Most Dubai families settle on one weekday session between 17:00 and 19:00 for teaching, plus a weekend morning slot for anything needing full-length timing. A ninety-minute paper attempted at eight in the evening after a school day produces a score that is not a fair baseline, which makes the diagnostic you paid for misleading.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start 0653 support in Year 10 or to wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper in total and considerably cheaper per unit of improvement, because it is teaching rather than repair. Roughly thirty weekly sessions across Year 10 removes the need for an intensive block later, and tutors in Dubai have open diaries in October in a way they do not in March. A Year 11 family starting after winter mocks typically needs eighteen to twenty-five sessions before a June series, bought at the point of peak demand. Waiting is a decision to pay more for triage.

faqs.question: What do I do if the tutor is good but my son will not engage with them?
faqs.answer: Say so and the match changes, without having to justify the request. A tutor can be prepared, competent and pleasant, and a particular teenager can still refuse to work with them, and that is not fixed by persistence or by a conversation about attitude. The free full-length trial lesson exists partly to catch this before money changes hands, but fit sometimes fails in week three instead. What is never on offer here is a grade guarantee or a refund tied to a result, because nobody controls the paper or the marking.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.closingHeading: Compare the formats on teaching hours, not on headline rates
dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.closingBody: A Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 home tutor in Dubai is what families type, and the published rate for that service is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. Before you compare that against anything, work out what each option gives you per hour of actual teaching, and whether the hour can be aimed at the one science your child is losing marks in. Get the tier from the statement of entry, get a recent paper marked by strand, and test a prospective tutor on all three strands in the trial. That trial is a full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken.

intro.heading: One number, three problems
paragraphs: Combined Science has a reporting problem that single-subject courses do not. A student comes home with 48 per cent and that number is the average of three separate performances. It could mean solid biology, collapsed chemistry and middling physics. It could mean the opposite. It could mean competent knowledge across all three with every long-answer question answered in the wrong register. Those four situations need four different plans, and none of them is distinguishable from the mark on the report.

What follows from that is the whole method on this page. Before any teaching happens, a past paper is sat under exam timing and scored three ways, with the marks attributed to biology, chemistry and physics questions separately and then to topics within each strand. The result is not a grade, it is a diagnosis. It usually surprises families, and the surprise is normally in the same direction: the strand the student complains about is not the strand losing the most marks.

The second half of the method is repetition under controlled conditions. A score only means something next to another score from the same paper format, the same length and the same timing. So an eight-week block begins and ends with comparable papers, with the diagnostic work in between, and the only claim anybody makes about progress is the movement between those two numbers. That claim belongs to your child. It is not a marketing figure, it has no sample size behind it and it is not transferable to anybody else's child.

Live video delivery matters here for a reason that has nothing to do with convenience. An online session leaves artefacts: the annotated script, the saved whiteboard working, the running mark log, and the recording where a family wants one. An in-home session leaves a parent's impression of how it went, plus a notebook that will not be found in May. If the point of the arrangement is evidence rather than reassurance, the format that produces documents automatically is the format that supports it. This also removes the awkward conversation most families eventually have with a visiting tutor, where neither side can point to anything concrete and the discussion becomes about effort and attitude instead of about marks.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform. Tutoring for families in Dubai and across the Emirates is delivered one-to-one over live video; we do not make home visits in Dubai, as that is a service we run only in India. Nothing here claims a regulator approval or an examination-board affiliation, and no grade outcome is promised, because a provider who cannot show you the method behind a number should not be publishing the number. What is on offer is a marked script you can read against the board's own published mark scheme.

sections.heading: Scoring one paper three ways
paragraphs: The first piece of work is mechanical and it takes about ninety minutes of marking. A released past paper is scored question by question against the board's published points. Every question is then tagged to biology, chemistry or physics, and the marks are totalled three times. Within each strand the losses are tagged again, this time to topic, so the output is not a percentage but a short list of places where marks went.

What this surfaces is the thing a single grade is incapable of showing. The table below is a worked example rather than a published statistic, included to show the shape of the output rather than to claim anything about any cohort. Read down the fourth column rather than across the rows: the useful information is what kind of error produced the loss, because knowledge gaps, arithmetic failures and technique failures need different weeks of work.

The pattern that recurs often enough to be worth naming is a mismatch between where a student feels weak and where the marks actually go. Students report the strand they find unpleasant. A breakdown reports the strand that costs them. Those are frequently different, because the unpleasant one gets revised and the other one gets quietly avoided. Having the breakdown in a document rather than in an argument is what makes the following eight weeks possible.

The second thing it gives you is a baseline that can be beaten honestly. A school mock mark is not a baseline, because mocks are often shortened, marked against a different standard, or sat under conditions that vary between schools. A paper sat at full length under exam timing and scored against the published points is comparable with another one of the same format later. That comparability is the only reason the exercise is worth the ninety minutes.

sections.heading: What live video adds to the record
paragraphs: Online delivery is usually sold on convenience. The reason it matters for an evidence-led plan is duller and more useful: it produces documents automatically. Every session happens on a shared screen, so the working the tutor and the student produce is already a file. It gets saved and sent rather than left on a kitchen table in a notebook that will not be found in May.

The running mark log is the central artefact. It records, for each paper attempted, the date, the paper format, the total, the three strand totals, and a one-line note on the dominant error type. After four or five entries it stops being an administrative record and becomes the thing that drives decisions, because trends are visible in a way that individual marks are not. A chemistry line that has been flat for three papers while the physics line climbs is telling you to change the plan rather than to add hours.

Recordings are optional and worth more than families expect in the fortnight before a paper. A student can watch the explanation of reacting masses three times at eleven at night without anybody else being awake for it, which is not possible with a lesson delivered in a living room. The saved whiteboard files do similar work: a student revising from ten of their own worked calculations is in a different position from one revising from a textbook page they have already read and not absorbed.

There is a limit worth stating. The record shows what happened in sessions and on papers. It does not show what happened in class, it cannot measure effort between lessons, and it is not a prediction. A mark log that has moved from one comparable paper to another is evidence about the past eight weeks and nothing more. Anybody turning that into a forecast, including us, would be inventing something.

sections.heading: Teaching a student to read the mark scheme themselves
paragraphs: The most durable thing a 0653 tutor can hand over is not content. It is the ability to look at a question and know what the marks are for. Cambridge awards marks against specified points, and the number of marks printed beside a question tells a candidate how many separate credited statements are expected. A student who internalises that stops writing four lines where one word scores, and stops writing one line where three points were available.

Command words carry the rest of it. State wants a fact. Describe wants what happens, in sequence, without reasons. Explain wants why, with a mechanism connecting cause to effect, which is the single commonest place marks are lost in a combined-science theory paper. Compare wants both sides in the same statement. Suggest wants known principles applied to an unfamiliar situation, and a blank answer there guarantees zero where a plausible attempt may score. Calculate wants the working, the units, and a number that is physically sensible.

The teaching method for this is specific and repetitive. The student marks their own work before the tutor comments, using the published mark scheme for the paper, and says out loud why each mark was or was not awarded. It is uncomfortable for about three sessions. After that students start predicting the mark scheme before they see it, which is the point at which the technique problem stops being a problem and the remaining losses are genuine content gaps.

We reference and link the board's published syllabus and mark schemes on the Cambridge International website rather than reproducing or supplying them, because that material belongs to Cambridge. A provider offering you a download bundle of mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables is distributing material they have no right to distribute, which tells you something about how they will handle the rest of the arrangement.

sections.heading: Eight weeks of progress, written down
paragraphs: An evidence-led block has a shape, and publishing it is the point. A family should be able to see at the start what will exist at the end, so that the arrangement is accountable rather than open-ended. The table below is the standard eight-week structure for 0653 support, with the artefact each week produces and the decision that artefact is supposed to drive.

Two features of it are worth drawing out. The first is that week four is a decision point rather than a progress report. Four sessions into a plan there is enough information to know whether the weakest strand was correctly identified, and the commonest mid-course correction is discovering that what looked like a chemistry problem is a maths problem. Catching that at week four rather than week eight saves four sessions of the wrong work.

The second is that the practical component gets its own protected slot. It is worth a fifth of the grade and it is the component households never revise, partly because it feels like something only a school can prepare. It is not: identifying variables, building a results table with units in the headings, choosing axes so a trend is readable, spotting an anomaly and suggesting a method improvement are all paper skills, and they can be taught on a shared screen the student writes on.

What the block cannot do is also worth stating in the same place. Eight weeks of weekly sessions is eight hours of teaching. That can rebuild two topics properly, fix command-word technique across all three strands and prepare the practical component. It cannot replace a year of content that was never learnt, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked to explain how.

sections.heading: Why physics marks swing and chemistry marks stay flat
paragraphs: Once a family has four entries on a mark log, the same two questions always arrive. Why does the physics figure jump around, and why has the chemistry figure not moved at all? Both have specific answers and both are reassuring once understood, which is the main argument for keeping the log in the first place.

Physics swings because the skills it tests are performance skills rather than knowledge. Selecting the right relationship, rearranging it, converting units and finishing the arithmetic under time pressure either happens fluently or does not, and a student who can do all four calmly at home will still lose the marks in a timed paper until the sequence is automatic. The remedy is short, frequent and extremely boring: the same calculation types, repeatedly, until no thought is required. Twenty minutes twice a week beats an hour once a fortnight, which is why exam-term sessions get shorter and more frequent rather than longer.

Chemistry stays flat because the repair happens below the surface. Mole work, reacting masses and concentration are proportional reasoning with units attached, and if a student cannot reliably rearrange a relationship then no amount of chemistry revision will fix the chemistry marks. The first three or four sessions go to the arithmetic, during which the chemistry line on the log does not move at all. Families read that as the tutoring failing. It is the only order in which the work can be done, and saying so in advance is more useful than explaining it afterwards.

Biology usually sits highest and moves least, for a reason that is about human nature rather than science. It is the strand that feels productive to revise, so it is the strand that gets revised, which keeps it healthy and consumes the hours the other two needed. The least popular and most valuable thing a tutor does is insist the hour goes where the breakdown says it should.

sections.heading: Using the record at a Dubai parents' evening
paragraphs: A marked script with a strand breakdown is useful outside the tutoring arrangement, and families underuse it. A ten-minute parents' evening slot is normally spent on a general exchange about effort and attitude. Arriving with a specific question changes what you get out of it, and the specific question is in the breakdown.

The questions worth bringing are narrow. Has this topic been taught yet, and when is it scheduled. Is my child entered for the Core or the Extended tier, and is that still under review. Which practical component has the centre chosen. Does the department's own marking of the long-answer questions match this, because if not, one of the two standards is out and it matters which. Teachers generally welcome this, because it is a conversation about their subject rather than a complaint.

What a tutor's script is not is an authority that overrides the school. The school knows the student in a classroom, holds the entry, and sees work the tutor never sees. If the department's reading of a student differs from ours, that is information rather than a dispute, and the useful response is to ask what they are seeing that we are not. Occasionally the answer is decisive: a student who performs on paper and will not speak in class has a problem no amount of paper marking will show.

One boundary belongs here. We do not contact your child's school, send reports to teachers or represent a family in a school conversation, and nothing on this page should suggest a relationship with any school named on it. The record is yours to use as you see fit. Schools are named on this page as context for families comparing provision, with no affiliation implied in either direction.

sections.heading: The honesty line on papers, mark schemes and coursework
paragraphs: This market contains operators selling things a tutor must not sell, and the boundary is worth setting out as a table rather than as a reassurance. One provider in this space sells completed internal assessments outright, which is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student rather than the seller at risk. A family paying for tutoring is entitled to know exactly where the line sits before the first session.

The principle is simple. A tutor teaches, explains, demonstrates on examples that are not the assessed work, and gives feedback on work the student has produced themselves. A tutor does not supply text for submission, does not edit a piece of assessed work into something the student could not have written, and does not provide board material they have no right to distribute. All three of those are refusals that protect your child rather than restrictions that inconvenience them.

On board material specifically, syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, specimen material and grade-boundary information are published by Cambridge International and by Pearson on their own websites. We reference them and link them. We do not reproduce them, bundle them or sell them, and a provider who hands you a drive full of them is distributing somebody else's copyright. For unreleased material the exposure is worse than copyright, because it reaches into malpractice.

The last row of the table is the one families ask about most delicately, and the answer is a straightforward yes. A tutor can read a practical write-up the student has already written and say what a mark scheme would credit, what is missing and what a stronger version would contain. The student then rewrites it. That is teaching. The distinction between that and the thing we will not do is the student's hand on the work.

process.title: Send what already exists
process.description: The statement of entry for the syllabus code and tier, a photograph of the most recent marked science assessment with marks visible, and the school's scheme of work if you have it. Those three documents turn a first session from a conversation into a diagnosis, and they take about five minutes to gather.

process.title: Free trial lesson over live video
process.description: One full-length one-to-one session at no charge, with no card details taken. Part of it is diagnostic. Use some of it to ask the tutor for a worked mole calculation, a food-chain explanation and a resistance problem, because a single-award course needs someone fluent in all three strands.

process.title: Baseline paper, scored three ways
process.description: A released past paper at full length under exam timing, marked against the published points, with the marks totalled separately for biology, chemistry and physics and then tagged to topics. The output is a list of places marks went, not a percentage, and it is what the plan is built from.

process.title: Eight-week block with the log sent weekly
process.description: Weekly sessions with the mark log updated and shared after each one, the saved whiteboard working sent the same evening, and a formal review of the target strand at week four. Most mid-course corrections happen at that review, usually because a chemistry problem turns out to be an arithmetic one.

process.title: Second comparable paper, then decide
process.description: Same format, same length, same timing, same marking standard. The movement between the two scores is the only claim anybody makes about the block. If it has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does; buying more hours of a plan the evidence has already contradicted is how money gets wasted.

whyPoints.title: One grade is split back into three
whyPoints.description: Every paper is scored separately for biology, chemistry and physics and then tagged to topics, because a single combined-science percentage averages three different problems. Without that split a plan is a guess, and the guess is usually that the student needs more of whatever the tutor teaches best.

whyPoints.title: The mark log is the product
whyPoints.description: Date, paper format, total, three strand totals and a one-line note on the dominant error type, updated after every paper. After four entries the trends drive the decisions, which is how a flat chemistry line gets caught at week four instead of being discovered in May.

whyPoints.title: The student marks their own work first
whyPoints.description: Self-marking against the published points, out loud, before the tutor comments. It is uncomfortable for about three sessions and then students start predicting the mark scheme, at which point technique stops being the problem and the remaining losses are genuine content.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts stay with your child
whyPoints.description: Saved whiteboard working, annotated scripts, the mark log and session recordings where a family wants them. A student revising in May from ten of their own worked calculations is better placed than one rereading a textbook page. An in-home lesson leaves none of this behind.

whyPoints.title: The claims stop where the evidence stops
whyPoints.description: Progress means the movement between two comparable papers and nothing further. No predicted grades, no improvement percentages, no star ratings, no success statistics, because none of those could be published here with the sample size, date and method that would make them honest.

faqs.question: How will I actually know whether the 0653 sessions are working?
faqs.answer: By comparing two papers of the same format, sat at the same length under the same timing, marked against the same published points. The first is sat in week one before any teaching, the second at week eight. The movement between those two numbers is the claim, and you see both scripts with the annotations on them. Anything else offered as proof of progress, including a tutor's impression of how sessions are going and a student's own report, is weaker evidence than two comparable scripts marked the same way.

faqs.question: Can you tell me which of the three sciences my son is losing marks in?
faqs.answer: That is the first piece of work rather than something that emerges later. A past paper is marked question by question, every question is tagged to biology, chemistry or physics, and the marks are totalled three times, then tagged again to topics inside the weakest strand. The output is a list of where marks went rather than a percentage. It regularly contradicts what the student believes, because students report the strand they find unpleasant while the breakdown reports the strand that costs them marks.

faqs.question: Why is your marked score lower than my daughter's school mock mark?
faqs.answer: Because the two are not measuring the same thing. School mocks are often shortened, sat under varying conditions, and marked to a standard that is deliberately encouraging at that point in the year. A baseline here is a full-length released paper under exam timing, scored strictly against the board's published points. The lower number is not a judgement on the school; it is a measurement designed to be comparable with another measurement in eight weeks. A generous baseline would make the second paper meaningless.

faqs.question: What exactly do I receive after each online session?
faqs.answer: The saved whiteboard file from the session, which contains the working your child and the tutor produced rather than a textbook page. An updated mark log where a paper was marked that week, showing date, paper format, total, the three strand totals and a one-line note on the dominant error type. The session recording where your family has asked for recordings. And, at week four and week eight, a short written review. All of it is sent to you rather than described to you.

faqs.question: Do you mark past papers using the official Cambridge mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, against the board's published points, which is why the marking is sometimes stricter than a student expects. We reference and link those documents on the Cambridge International website rather than reproducing or supplying them, because the material is Cambridge copyright and is already free to download there. Any provider handing you a bundle of mark schemes, subject guides or grade-boundary tables is distributing material they have no right to distribute, which is worth noticing before you trust them with anything else.

faqs.question: Can my child's school use your marked scripts at a parents' evening?
faqs.answer: The record is yours and plenty of families take it in, which usually improves a ten-minute slot considerably. The useful questions are narrow: has this topic been taught and when is it scheduled, is the entry Core or Extended and is that under review, which practical component has the centre chosen, and does the department's own marking of long answers match this. We do not contact schools, send reports to teachers or represent families in school conversations, and we claim no relationship with any school.

faqs.question: How long before a marked paper shows real movement?
faqs.answer: It depends which strand you are watching. Technique changes show up fast, often within two or three papers, because fixing a describe answer written for an explain question is a habit change rather than a knowledge build. Chemistry arithmetic shows up slowest, typically not before the fourth or fifth session, because the repair happens in the maths underneath before any chemistry marks can move. That lag is the single most common reason families conclude too early that a plan is not working.

faqs.question: Why do physics marks go up and down while chemistry stays flat?
faqs.answer: Physics tests performance skills. Choosing a relationship, rearranging it, converting units and finishing the arithmetic under time pressure either runs fluently or does not, so the same student scores well and badly on consecutive papers until the sequence becomes automatic. The remedy is short, frequent repetition rather than long sessions. Chemistry stays flat because the first sessions go to the proportional reasoning underneath the mole work, during which the chemistry line genuinely does not move. Both patterns are normal and both are visible on the log.

faqs.question: Are the 0653 session recordings available afterwards?
faqs.answer: Where your family asks for recordings, yes, and they earn their keep in the fortnight before a paper. A student can rewatch an explanation of reacting masses three times late at night without anybody else being awake, which is not available from a lesson delivered in a living room. The saved whiteboard files do similar work. The practical value is that revision material in the student's own handwriting and the tutor's own words is used, whereas a textbook chapter already read tends not to be.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on a practical write-up my son has already written?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is exactly where the line sits. A tutor can read what the student wrote, say what a mark scheme would credit, name what is missing and describe what a stronger version would contain. The student then rewrites it themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply text for submission or edit a piece of assessed work into something the student could not have produced. The distinction is the student's hand staying on the work, and it protects your child rather than inconveniencing them.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes as downloads?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. Cambridge International and Pearson publish syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and specimen material on their own websites, free, and that material is their copyright. We link to it and work from it in sessions. A provider offering a drive or folder of board material is redistributing somebody else's property, and where unreleased material is involved the exposure moves from copyright into malpractice. It is a useful early signal about how a provider handles rules generally.

faqs.question: What happens if the second comparable paper shows no improvement?
faqs.answer: The plan changes or the tutor changes, and that conversation is ours to start rather than yours to chase. Buying more hours of a plan the evidence has already contradicted is the most common way money is wasted in this market. In practice there are three usual causes: the wrong strand was targeted, the sessions were happening but nothing was practised between them, or the real obstacle is not academic at all. The log usually distinguishes between them, which is why it exists.

faqs.question: How do you decide which 0653 topics get session time?
faqs.answer: From the breakdown rather than from preference. Marks lost are tagged to topics inside each strand, and the hours go to the topics carrying the largest measured loss that can realistically be rebuilt in the time available. That last clause matters: six weeks before a paper, two topics rebuilt properly beats six topics touched. The target strand is formally reviewed at week four, and the most common correction at that point is discovering a chemistry problem is actually an arithmetic problem.

faqs.question: If we change tutor mid-term, does the record carry over?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the record is kept as documents rather than in a tutor's head. The mark log, the strand breakdown, the topic audit and the saved working all transfer, so a new tutor starts from the evidence rather than from a fresh baseline paper. That is the practical reason the written artefacts are worth the time they take to produce. Changing tutor is something you can ask for without having to justify it, and it should not cost your child four weeks of re-diagnosis.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.closingHeading: Ask for the breakdown before you buy the hours
dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.closingBody: A Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 online tutor in Dubai should be able to hand you something readable after the first paper: marks totalled separately for biology, chemistry and physics, the losses tagged to topics, and a one-line statement of what kind of error produced them. That document is what a plan is built from, and without it any number of hours is a guess. Send the statement of entry and the most recent marked assessment, and the trial lesson can start from a diagnosis rather than a conversation. The trial is a full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken.

intro.heading: Starting with the number, because nobody else will
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai pricing science tutoring is working almost blind. Of the competitor pages examined for this market in October 2026, three publish no hourly figure anywhere on the page, one publishes a figure that contradicts its own structured data, and two quote in US dollars to families who pay for everything else in dirhams. One of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The effect is that the first quote a family receives becomes their only reference point, whether it is AED 120 or AED 500.

So this page leads with rates, with each figure attributed to the source that published it. The headline bands for Dubai as of October 2026 are these. Budget online tutoring, usually a university student, runs from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE support from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel runs AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting 200 to 500. Exam specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Premium named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650.

None of those are IB Gram's prices and none of them are quoted here as ours. They are the market, published so you can judge whether a quote you have received is ordinary or unusual. IB Gram is an independent matching platform that delivers tutoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video; we do not make home visits in Dubai, as that is a service we run only in India. For our own arrangement the honest route is the free trial lesson and the conversation that follows it, because the sensible number depends on the tier, the number of sessions and how close the exam is.

The second half of the pricing question is the one families ask less often and regret more: what are you buying per hour. Combined Science 0653 awards a single grade covering biology, chemistry and physics, which means one tutor can cover the whole subject if they are genuinely comfortable across all three strands. A family paying three separate specialists for a single-award course is usually paying for coordination they do not need. Equally, a tutor who is a biologist pretending to be comfortable with moles and with circuit calculations will cost you more in a wasted term than the hourly difference ever saves.

There is a useful piece of context for budgeting. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are the fixed part of an education budget; tutoring is the part that moves. A family that plans a year of weekly support deliberately in September spends less than one that buys an intensive block in panic in April, and the earlier version works better.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.programmesIntro: The science route a Dubai school puts a student on decides both the tutoring bill and the post-16 options, and the decision is usually made on a Year 9 options form. These are the four routes, framed by what each costs to support and what each leaves open.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science, single award
programmes.description: One qualification and one grade covering biology, chemistry and physics. Fewer guided learning hours than the double award or separate sciences, with a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, tiered Core and Extended. The cheapest route to support because one competent tutor can hold the whole syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is often the route a school recommends for a student carrying a heavy subject load or finding three separate sciences unmanageable. Ask what it does to the sixth-form options at your own school before agreeing, because the answer varies between Dubai schools rather than following a national rule.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences, double award
programmes.description: Two grades from one course, with more content than 0653 across the same three sciences. Costs more to support than the single award because there is more syllabus to cover, and less than separate sciences because the papers are shared rather than tripled.
programmes.countryNote: The most common compromise route in Dubai British-curriculum schools. Two science grades on the certificate also help with the Ministry of Education equivalency count, where five accredited subjects at grade E or 3 or better are required on the British track.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 taken as three qualifications with three grades. The most content, the most papers and the most expensive to support, because a student needing help in two of the three realistically needs two specialists rather than one generalist.
programmes.countryNote: The standard route in Dubai's selective British-curriculum schools and the expected preparation for A Level sciences. A family supporting two of the three subjects weekly is looking at roughly double the tutoring budget of a 0653 family at the same hourly rate.

programmes.name: Post-16 science progression
programmes.description: A Level sciences or IB Diploma sciences. Entry conditions are set by the individual school, and some Dubai sixth forms specify a grade in a separate science rather than accepting a combined award for a given A Level. This is the real cost of the 0653 decision, and it is not an hourly one.
programmes.countryNote: Check the published sixth-form entry criteria at your own Dubai school, in writing, before the Year 9 options form is signed. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 places, so provision is changing and last year's criteria are not a safe guide.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.subjectsIntro: What a tutor charges depends partly on how specialised the subject is. These are the science and supporting codes we are asked about across Dubai, with a note on where each sits in the market's pricing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade across three sciences. Sits in the general-science band of the market rather than the specialist band, which is why rates for 0653 support tend to come in below separate-subject physics or chemistry. One tutor covering all three strands is the normal and sensible arrangement.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: More content than 0653 for two grades rather than one. Support costs more in hours rather than in hourly rate, because the syllabus is wider and the practical component carries the same weight across a larger body of material.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: The separate-science biology route. Priced in the market much like 0653 because content recall dominates, though Extended-tier specialists who have marked a full series charge toward the upper band.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Consistently the most expensive of the three separate sciences to support in Dubai, because moles, stoichiometry and electrolysis need a tutor comfortable with the arithmetic as well as the chemistry. This is the strand inside 0653 that most often forces a family to pay for a second tutor.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Priced similarly to chemistry and for the same reason. Formula rearrangement, unit handling and graph interpretation are mathematical skills, and a biologist teaching physics inside a combined course tends to run out of depth at exactly the questions carrying the marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science (Double Award, 4SD0)
subjects.description: The Pearson counterpart used by some Dubai centres. Different paper structure and a different series calendar, so Cambridge past papers are not interchangeable. Check the board on the statement of entry before paying for any preparation material.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science (Single Award)
subjects.description: The Pearson single-award route, broadly equivalent in scope to 0653. The practical arrangements and the paper layout differ enough that a tutor needs to confirm the board rather than assume Cambridge.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The hidden cost inside a combined-science bill. A student losing 0653 marks on rearranging equations, unit conversion or reading a graph has a maths problem appearing in a science exam, and fixing it there is cheaper than fixing it twice.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Relevant because long-answer science marks are awarded for precise wording. Students writing in a second language lose marks to vocabulary rather than to science, which is diagnosable from a marked script and cheaper to address than more content teaching.

subjects.name: A Level and IB Diploma sciences
subjects.description: Where the 0653 decision shows its real price. Post-16 science entry conditions are set school by school in Dubai, and a single combined award sometimes does not satisfy them for a given subject. Worth confirming in writing while the Year 9 options form is still open.

sections.heading: What a 0653 tutor costs in Dubai, in dirhams
paragraphs: The table below is the thing this market does not publish. Every figure is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, and all of it was read in October 2026. It describes the market rather than IB Gram, and it is here so a parent can tell an ordinary quote from an unusual one. If a tutor quotes you AED 650 an hour, that is a real band in this city, but you should know you are at the top of it and ask what you are getting for the position.

The shape of the market is worth reading before the numbers. The budget tier is mostly university students teaching online, and for a Year 10 student needing content coverage it can be perfectly adequate. The qualified-tutor tier is where most Year 11 work sits. The specialist tier buys someone who has marked a syllabus to the published points through a full series, which matters most in the eight weeks before a paper and matters least in October of Year 10. The premium tier is where examiner claims appear, and that is where scepticism is most warranted, because current examiner status is rarely evidenced and never confers access to marking or boundaries.

The in-home band sits higher than the online band at every tier for one reason, which is travel. Somebody pays for the drive, either inside the hourly rate or as a minimum booking length. In a city where a cross-town evening run takes forty minutes each way, a nominally cheaper in-home rate can work out dearer per hour of actual teaching, and the pool of tutors willing to make the drive at five in the afternoon is small.

Monthly packages are where comparison gets hard, and that is sometimes deliberate. The figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide before you compare: the first works out near AED 100 a session and the second near AED 200 an hour. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number in Dubai
paragraphs: Five things change a 0653 quote in this city, and only one of them is the tutor's qualifications. The first is format, which is really travel, and it is the largest single factor. The second is how close the exam is: demand for science tutoring in Dubai concentrates between the January mock results and the June series, and a tutor with a full diary in March has no reason to discount. Booking the same tutor in September usually costs less per hour for the same person.

The third is session length and commitment. Hourly rates quoted for a single session are routinely higher than the same tutor's rate inside a ten-session block, and ninety-minute sessions often price below two separate hours. The fourth is how many strands you need covered. A family needing only the chemistry inside 0653 is buying a narrower service than one needing all three, and a tutor who has to prepare across the full syllabus every week will price for that preparation whether or not they say so.

The fifth is tier, and it is the one parents never ask about. Extended-tier preparation requires the tutor to be fluent in supplement content as well as core, which is a genuinely larger body of material. A quote given before anyone has established whether your child is a Core or Extended candidate is a guess. Establish the tier from the statement of entry and then ask for a number.

What does not legitimately move the price is a claimed approval. Nobody in this market is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson to tutor your child privately, and a tutor charging a premium for implying otherwise is charging for nothing. The one credential that exists is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge, so it cannot honestly be used to justify a higher rate either.

sections.heading: One grade for three sciences: what 0653 actually is
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 is a single award. The student studies material drawn from biology, chemistry and physics and receives one grade covering all three. It is tiered, so Core candidates and Extended candidates sit different papers, and the assessment has the familiar Cambridge science shape of a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component. Always confirm the exact paper numbers and the practical choice against your child's statement of entry, and check the current syllabus on the Cambridge International website, because centres make the practical choice at their own level.

What a parent needs to understand about the single award is that it is not a reduced version of one science; it is a reduced version of three. Coverage of each strand goes less deep than a separate-subject syllabus, which makes the course manageable, and that reduction is exactly what post-16 admissions tutors are looking at when they set entry conditions. The content is real and the grade is real. The question is whether one science grade is enough for what your child wants next.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that 0653 rewards a generalist in a way separate sciences do not. A tutor needs to be genuinely comfortable moving from osmosis to mole calculations to circuit diagrams inside a single hour, which is a less common skill than it sounds and is the thing worth testing in a trial lesson. Ask a prospective tutor to explain a mole calculation and then a food-chain question. Hesitation on either is useful information.

The other consequence is that the loss is harder to locate. A student with three separate science grades knows which subject is weak. A 0653 student has one number that averages everything, so a marked paper broken down by strand is the only way to find out whether the problem is the biology recall, the chemistry arithmetic or the physics reasoning. That diagnostic is worth an hour before any teaching happens.

sections.heading: 0653, 0654 or three separate sciences: cost against certificate
paragraphs: This is the decision that costs real money, and it is usually made on a Year 9 options form by a thirteen-year-old. The table compares the three routes on the two axes a family actually cares about: what supporting it costs across two years, and what the certificate leaves open afterwards.

The arithmetic on the left of the table is straightforward. At the same hourly rate, a family supporting one weekly session for a single-award course spends roughly half what a family supporting two weekly sessions for separate sciences spends. Over two years at AED 200 an hour, that difference runs into five figures in dirhams, which is not trivial even against Dubai school fees. The double award sits between the two, usually needing one longer session rather than two.

The column on the right is the one that matters more. Post-16 science entry conditions in Dubai are set school by school. Some sixth forms accept a combined or co-ordinated award for entry to a given A Level science and some ask for a grade in the separate subject, and the only reliable way to find out is to read your own school's published criteria or to ask the head of sixth form in writing. Dubai's provision is expanding quickly, with seven new private schools and 16,846 new places arriving for the 2026-27 intake, so a criterion that applied two years ago is not a safe guide.

Where a family has a genuine choice, the useful question is not which route is hardest but which route your child can carry alongside everything else on the timetable. A student taking three separate sciences and scraping passes has a worse certificate than the same student taking the double award and doing well, and a worse experience of Year 11. Where there is no choice because the school has made it, the arithmetic above still tells you what to budget.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, the KHDA freeze and a year of support
paragraphs: Tutoring is almost never budgeted against anything. It arrives as a monthly figure with no reference point, which is how a family ends up spending more on panic support in one spring term than on a year of planned weekly sessions. The table below puts a year of 0653 support next to the other education costs a Dubai family already carries, using published market figures rather than our own.

The anchor is the fee position. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For planning purposes that means the fixed part of the budget is known, so the variable part can be planned rather than reacted to.

The pattern across the rows is the familiar one. Weekly support from September costs more in total than an eight-week spring block and costs less per unit of improvement, because the spring block is triage rather than teaching. Two sessions a week is not twice as effective as one; it is the right answer only when a measured diagnostic says two strands both need rebuilding. And the cheapest line in the table is the diagnostic itself, which is an hour that regularly saves a family from buying the wrong plan.

One honest caveat on everything in this section. The market figures are published rates read in October 2026 and they move. The structure of the comparison is the durable part: price per hour of actual teaching, not per hour booked; plan from a baseline rather than from a worry; and do the arithmetic on monthly packages before comparing them with hourly quotes.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences inside 0653 costs the most to fix
paragraphs: A single grade hides where the loss is, so the first useful piece of work is a marked paper broken down by strand. Across the 0653 scripts we see from Dubai students, the pattern is consistent enough to be worth stating: the biology marks are usually the most secure, the physics marks are the most volatile, and the chemistry marks are the most expensive to recover.

Chemistry is expensive because the losses are arithmetic rather than recall. Mole calculations, relative formula mass, reacting masses and anything involving concentration require a student to rearrange a relationship and carry units through it, and a candidate who cannot do that reliably loses the same marks in every paper regardless of how much chemistry they revise. Rebuilding it means going back to the maths, which takes several sessions before any chemistry marks move. Families often interpret that lag as the tutoring not working, when it is the only order in which it can work.

Physics is volatile for a related reason. Formula selection, unit conversion and graph interpretation are skills that either fire under exam pressure or do not, and a student who can do them calmly at home will still lose the marks in a timed paper if the routine is not automatic. The remedy is short, frequent and boring: the same calculation types repeated until the method is reflexive. It is cheap in hours and unpopular with teenagers.

Biology is usually the most secure strand, which creates its own trap. A student who feels competent in biology will choose to revise biology, because revision that feels productive is the revision people do. A tutor's least popular and most valuable contribution is to insist that the hour goes to the strand carrying the loss. That is also why the marked breakdown matters: it takes the argument out of the room and puts it in a document.

sections.heading: How many hours a 0653 student actually needs
paragraphs: This is the second half of the pricing question and the one that decides what you spend. The honest answer is that it depends on when you start and on what the diagnostic finds, but the ranges are not mysterious and anybody quoting a fixed package without seeing a marked paper is guessing.

A Year 10 student with no particular crisis, working weekly in step with the school, is looking at something like thirty sessions across the year. That is the cheapest effective pattern available, because it is teaching rather than repair, and it removes the need for an intensive block later. A Year 11 student starting after poor winter mocks typically needs eighteen to twenty-five sessions between February and the June series, weighted towards the strand carrying the measured loss, with the practical component taking four to six of those as its own protected strand.

A student six weeks out needs triage, and it is worth being blunt about what that can achieve. Six weeks at two sessions a week is twelve hours. Twelve hours can rebuild two topics properly, fix command-word technique across all three strands, and prepare the practical component. It cannot teach a year of unlearnt content, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling you something. The right use of a short block is to concentrate it on the highest-yield weaknesses the baseline paper identifies, and to leave the rest alone deliberately.

The number to watch is not hours booked but movement between two comparable papers. If the second paper has not moved, more hours of the same plan will not move the third one. That is the point at which the plan changes or the tutor does, and it is a conversation we would rather start than have you chase. There is no refund promise tied to an outcome here, because an honest provider cannot offer one, and no grade guarantee, because nobody can.

sections.heading: Paying for tutoring in the UAE: permits, invoices and what free means
paragraphs: Three administrative points are worth knowing before money changes hands, and they are all things competitor pages in this market skip. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can be quoted honestly. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The second is tax. Ask every provider in writing whether a quoted figure includes VAT, because a quote that turns out to be exclusive changes the comparison you thought you were making. We will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption, and IB Gram publishes no tax registration number here. What a parent can reasonably insist on is a clear statement of whether the number quoted is the number payable.

The third is what free means. The trial lesson offered here is one full-length one-to-one session over live video, at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. That is the entire condition, stated in the same place as the offer, which is how any free claim should be made. If another provider's free trial requires a card, a minimum booking or a sign-up to a monthly plan, those conditions should appear next to the word free rather than three clicks away.

One last disclosure belonging in this section. IB Gram is an independent matching platform with no premises anywhere in the UAE and no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with physical premises and annual renewal requirements. We are not approved, accredited or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and no school named on this page has any relationship with us. Those bodies appear here because understanding them helps a parent spend sensibly.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates as of October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, an exam specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and an in-home visit including travel at AED 180 to 500. Budget online options start around AED 45, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Because 0653 is a single award covering all three sciences, it usually sits in the general-science band rather than the specialist band.

faqs.question: Is one tutor for 0653 cheaper than hiring three separate science tutors?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and that is the main financial argument for the single award. 0653 awards one grade across biology, chemistry and physics, so one tutor who is genuinely comfortable across all three strands can hold the whole syllabus. You pay for one session a week rather than two or three, one diagnostic rather than three, and no coordination between tutors. The caveat is real: a tutor who is a biologist pretending to be at ease with mole calculations and circuit questions will cost you a wasted term, which is far more expensive than the hourly difference.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutors quote AED 150 and AED 450 for what sounds like the same thing?
faqs.answer: Five factors move the number and only one is qualifications. Format and travel is the largest, because somebody pays for the drive. Proximity to the exam series is second: March demand in Dubai is heavy and tutors with full diaries do not discount. Then session length and block commitment, how many of the three strands you need covered, and the tier, since Extended preparation is a wider body of material than Core. A quote given before anyone has checked whether your child is a Core or Extended candidate is a guess rather than a price.

faqs.question: Do science tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: In practice, yes, because demand concentrates between the winter mock results and the exam period while the supply of experienced tutors does not change. A tutor with a full March diary has no reason to discount, and the hours left available at that point tend to be the awkward ones. Booking the same person in September or October usually costs less per hour and buys teaching rather than triage. If you are already in the spring, the sensible response is to scope the block tightly from a marked baseline rather than to buy open-ended hours.

faqs.question: Is a small group class at the budget end worth it for Combined Science?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the problem is. Group teaching at AED 45 to 150 per student is genuinely cheaper and genuinely less targeted, and for a 0653 student that matters more than it would for a single subject. A group is usually set by year rather than by tier, and the single grade means different students in the room are losing marks in different sciences. If your child needs content coverage, a group can work. If the loss is concentrated in chemistry arithmetic, a group will not reach it.

faqs.question: What is the practical difference between Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654?
faqs.answer: 0653 is a single award giving one science grade; 0654 is a double award giving two grades from one course, with more content across the same three sciences. In cost terms the double award needs more hours rather than a higher hourly rate, usually one longer weekly session rather than two. In certificate terms the double award puts two science grades on the record, which helps both with sixth-form entry conditions and with the Ministry of Education equivalency count of five accredited subjects on the British track.

faqs.question: Will a single combined science award limit my daughter's A Level options in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It can, and the answer is school-specific rather than national. Some Dubai sixth forms accept a combined or co-ordinated award for entry to a given A Level science and some ask for a grade in the separate subject. The only reliable way to find out is to read your own school's published entry criteria or ask the head of sixth form in writing, ideally before the Year 9 options form is signed. Dubai provision is changing quickly, with seven new private schools and 16,846 new places arriving for 2026-27, so older criteria are not a safe guide.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 0653 student usually need before the exam?
faqs.answer: Starting after the winter mocks, eighteen to twenty-five sessions between February and a June series is the usual range, weighted towards the strand the marked paper shows is weakest, with four to six of those protected for the practical component. A Year 10 student working weekly in step with the school is looking at around thirty sessions across the year, which is the cheapest effective pattern because it is teaching rather than repair. A student starting six weeks out has twelve hours and should spend them on triage.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences inside 0653 takes the longest to fix?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, almost always, because the losses are arithmetic rather than recall. Mole calculations, relative formula mass, reacting masses and concentration all require rearranging a relationship and carrying units through it, so rebuilding them means going back to the maths before any chemistry marks move. Families often read that lag as the tutoring failing. Physics marks are the most volatile, needing short repeated drilling until the method is automatic under time pressure. Biology is usually the most secure strand, which is why students choose to revise it.

faqs.question: Are tutoring fees in Dubai quoted with VAT included?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, every time. A quote that turns out to be exclusive of tax changes the comparison you believed you were making, and providers in this market are inconsistent about stating it. We will not assert the VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption, and IB Gram publishes no tax registration number here. What you can insist on from any provider is a plain statement of whether the figure quoted is the figure payable.

faqs.question: Should I buy a monthly package or pay by the hour for 0653 support?
faqs.answer: Divide before you decide. Packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 a session, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which works out near AED 200 an hour. A package is good value when the sessions will definitely be used and poor value when the plan is still unclear. For a first month, hourly or a short defined block keeps the decision reversible, which matters more than the small discount.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a UAE licence, and does that make the lessons more expensive?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it does not justify a higher price. Private tutoring in the UAE falls under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years to eligible applicants, who include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor using it to justify a premium is charging for paperwork.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutor to get an accurate quote for 0653 support?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take five minutes to gather. The statement of entry, which shows the syllabus code, the tier and the practical component. A photograph of the most recent marked science assessment with the marks visible. The school's scheme of work or a note of which topics have been taught. And the date of the exam series your child is entered for. With those, a quote is a calculation. Without them, every number you are given is a guess dressed as a price.

faqs.question: If we stop 0653 sessions after a fortnight, what happens to the money?
faqs.answer: You should never be in a position where that question is expensive to answer, which is why the first step here is a free full-length trial lesson with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. Beyond that, agree in writing how sessions are paid for and what notice applies before you commit to a block. We publish no refund promise tied to an outcome and no grade guarantee, because neither would be honest. What exists instead is a documented plan and a second comparable paper that shows whether it worked.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-combined-science-0.closingBody: The cheapest hour you will spend on Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 support in Dubai is the one that establishes where the marks are going. A single grade covering three sciences hides the loss, and a plan built without that breakdown is how families end up paying for twenty hours of biology revision while the chemistry arithmetic stays broken. Get the tier from the statement of entry, get a recent paper marked by strand, then decide how many hours you are buying and from whom. The trial lesson is a full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken.
